# Requirements: music-dj-tools

**Defined:** 2026-04-16
**Core Value:** Own your DJ library - no walled garden, no lost work when a vendor changes their DB format.

## v1 Requirements

Requirements for initial usable release - the **Library Hygiene** milestone. Each maps to a roadmap phase.

### Reconciliation (RECON)

Fix the current library's broken state so every downstream tool works on accurate data.

- [x] **RECON-01** (shipped Phase 1): List all Rekordbox tracks whose `FolderPath` points at a file that doesn't exist on disk, with full metadata for each (title, artist, album, BPM, key, duration, original path, file size).
- [x] **RECON-02** (shipped Phase 1): For each missing-file entry, automatically locate the most likely candidate file on disk and **triple-validate** the match using at least three independent signals (e.g. filename similarity, duration ±0.5s, size match, audio fingerprint, ID3-tag title/artist match, path-rewrite heuristic). Emit a `confidence` score and a short rationale per candidate.
- [x] **RECON-03** (shipped Phase 1): Dry-run Rekordbox path-updater: generate a patch description (track id → old path → new path) for every high-confidence match, without touching `master.db`.
- [x] **RECON-04** (shipped Phase 1): Cautious live-write pass: after user approval of 2-3 specific tracks, stop Rekordbox, back up `master.db`, apply those 2-3 path updates to the live DB, verify the rows read back correctly, and produce a reversibility log.
- [x] **RECON-05** (shipped Phase 1.1): Unrecoverable files either re-sourced and re-linked, or explicitly removed from Rekordbox with a logged decision; audit reports MISSING=0.
- [x] **RECON-06** (shipped; follow-on to META-09, Thu 1 Oct 2026):
  A track whose file moved is relinked by its audio, not only by its name. The
  fingerprint the duplicate scan recorded for the track (by `stable_id` or old
  path, in the dedup database) is evidence for `locate` and the relocate
  candidates page: a candidate with the same audio gains `fingerprint_match`
  (weight .35, counts toward triple validation), a fingerprinted file at a new
  path with the same audio is offered even when it was renamed, and a
  candidate with clearly different audio under the same name carries
  `fingerprint_mismatch`, which rules it out of automatic apply. Read-only
  towards the music: candidates are decoded, never written.
  - [if] the recorded audio is found under another name [then] that file is a
    candidate with `fingerprint_match` [⛔️ if a renamed move is not offered].
  - [if] a same-named file has different audio [then] it is never
    triple-validated, whatever else fired [⛔️ if it would auto-apply].
  - [if] another library track owns the matching file [then] it is not offered
    (a duplicate, not this track's file) [⛔️ if two tracks would share a file].
  - [if] no scan fingerprinted the track, or a candidate cannot be measured
    [then] no fingerprint signal fires and the count of unmeasured candidates
    is reported [⛔️ if unmeasured reads as a mismatch].
  - [if] a row from `broken.csv` (which names no stable_id) has a moved file the duplicate scan recorded under the same track [then] that file is still seeded by its audio, the track resolved from the scan's own record of its old path; a file another track owns stays out ⛔️

- [x] **SYNC-01** (shipped Phase 2): Enumerate djay Pro playlists + track memberships (extends the current read-only TSAF parser).
  - [if] an agent calls `GET /api/v1/rb-djay-sync/djay/playlists` or `python -m apps.sync djay-playlists` [then] djay playlist enumeration is reachable [else] ⛔️
- [x] **SYNC-02** (shipped Phase 2): Match djay tracks ↔ Rekordbox tracks using ISRC + fingerprint + title/artist fuzzy match.
  - [if] an agent calls `POST /api/v1/rb-djay-sync/match` or `python -m apps.sync match --help` [then] the rb-djay matcher surface is reachable [else] ⛔️
- [x] **SYNC-03** (shipped Phase 3): Bi-directional playlist sync (RB-canonical) with conflict policy + dry-run.
  - [if] an agent calls `POST /api/v1/rb-djay-sync/playlists/plan` or `python -m apps.sync playlist-diff --help` [then] the rb-djay playlist sync surface is reachable [else] ⛔️
- [x] **SYNC-04** (shipped Phase 4): Bi-directional cue point + beatgrid sync, RB-canonical.
  - [if] an agent calls `POST /api/v1/rb-djay-sync/cues/plan` or `python -m apps.sync cue-diff --help` [then] the rb-djay cue sync surface is reachable [else] ⛔️
- [x] **SYNC-05** (shipped Phase 4): Analysis metadata sync (BPM, key, energy, custom tags).
  - [if] an agent calls `POST /api/v1/rb-djay-sync/metadata/plan` or `python -m apps.sync apply-analysis --help` [then] the rb-djay analysis sync surface is reachable [else] ⛔️
- [x] **SYNC-06** (shipped Phase 4): Sync 0-5 star ratings between Rekordbox and djay Pro, RB-canonical. Includes dry-run preview and conflict reporting when both sides have changed since last sync. (Primitives landed Phase 2; write path + safety rails in Phase 4.)
  - [if] an agent calls `POST /api/v1/rb-djay-sync/ratings/apply` with `dry_run: true` or `python -m apps.sync apply-ratings --help` [then] the rb-djay ratings sync surface is reachable [else] ⛔️

- [x] **META-05** (shipped Thu 3 Sep 2026): Cross-service Spotify-to-SoundCloud playlist transfer through official user-authorized APIs, with numeric confidence and pass provenance per match, separate matched / unmatched / ungradable buckets, a mandatory batched LLM web-search and track-length check below the configured threshold, and a terms-cited decision not to ship TIDAL access.
  - **Scope note - this is TRANSFER, not PLAYBACK.** The Out of Scope row
    "DRM-protected streaming playback" still binds: cataloging Spotify/TIDAL
    URIs is in scope, decoding their DRM audio is not. `apps/shared/platform_paths.py`
    already classifies `spotify:` / `soundcloud:` / `tidal:` rows as a distinct
    streaming bucket (per `apps/reconcile/match.py`), so the transfer target is
    metadata that already has a home.
  - **Do not duplicate:** CAT-01 (Spotify playlist importer) and SYNC-02
    (ISRC + fingerprint + fuzzy matching) are the primitives this builds on.
    This requirement is the cross-service X-to-Y direction plus the confidence
    contract, not a second matcher.
  - **Shipped implementation:** `apps/streaming_transfer/` reuses CAT-01's
    scoring primitive, searches and writes through SoundCloud's official OAuth
    API, requires official OpenRouter usage and citation proof for the exact
    below-threshold batch, compares durations deterministically, and writes the
    full report atomically. The agent-native
    entrypoint is `python -m apps.streaming_transfer spotify-to-soundcloud`;
    setup, safety flags, output contract, and the TIDAL terms decision are in
    `docs/streaming-library-transfer.md`. The production parsers and decision
    path are locked by captured provider metadata in
    `tests/streaming_transfer/test_transfer.py`.
  - [if] a transfer runs from one streaming service to another [then] every
    matched track carries a confidence figure, and matched / unmatched /
    ungradable are reported as separate named buckets [⛔️ if a bare
    "transferred N tracks" figure is quoted with no confidence and no
    unmatched bucket].
  - [if] a candidate match scores below the configured confidence threshold
    [then] it is escalated to the cheap batched LLM pass (web search + a track
    length match requirement) rather than accepted silently, and the stored
    result records which pass produced it.
  - [if] the Tidal question is answered [then] the answer cites Tidal's actual
    API terms and says plainly whether a partnership deal is required [⛔️ if a
    Tidal path ships on undocumented or ToS-breaking access].

- [x] **META-06** (shipped Thu 10 Sep 2026): Cross-vendor terminology glossary as a markdown document plus a
      machine-readable JSON synonym map: what each vendor calls a thing, and what we
      call it in code and UI.

  - **Partial today, so this is a consolidation not a greenfield build:** the
    per-adapter capability documents `open-dj/adapters/rekordbox.md`,
    `djay.md`, `serato.md` and `traktor.md` already hold much of the mapping
    data. What is missing is the single consolidated artifact and the JSON map
    a tool can load.
  - [if] a vendor term is looked up in the glossary [then] it resolves to our
    canonical code/UI term and to the equivalent term in every adapter we ship
    (rekordbox, djay, Serato, Traktor) [⛔️ if the glossary covers only
    rekordbox].
  - [if] the JSON synonym map is loaded by a tool [then] it parses with a
    standard JSON reader and every entry names its canonical term, so the map
    is usable programmatically and not only by a human reading the markdown.
  - [if] a new adapter or a new canonical field lands [then] the glossary and
    the JSON map gain the matching entry, so a shipped adapter can never sit
    with no glossary coverage.

META-07..08 recorded Sun 6 Sep 2026: analysis pool workers
died on the CI host at a NULL instruction pointer (`segfault at 0 ip
0000000000000000`), which the parent could only report as a bare
`BrokenProcessPool`.

- [x] **META-07** (shipped Sun 6 Sep 2026): Analysis pool workers
  are SPAWNED, never forked, and each worker pins `OMP_NUM_THREADS`,
  `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS`, `MKL_NUM_THREADS` and `NUMBA_NUM_THREADS` to 1 before
  its backend import chain runs. Forking a parent that has already imported
  librosa/numba/OpenBLAS copies only the calling thread, so the child inherits
  native state whose owning threads do not exist in it and jumps through a NULL
  function pointer on the next native call.
  - [if] the analysis CLI runs with `--workers 2` [then] each worker process is
    a fresh interpreter that imported the native stack itself [⛔️ if a worker
    is a fork of the parent].
  - [if] a worker begins its first task [then] all four thread-count variables
    read `1` and numpy has not yet been imported in that process, so the pin
    still precedes the import that reads it [⛔️ if numpy is already imported].
  - [if] the platform default start method is `fork` [then] the pool still
    spawns, because the context is explicit rather than inherited.
  - [if] `--workers` is given a value [then] that many workers are started, so
    the flag's meaning is unchanged by the context switch.

- [x] **META-08** (shipped Sun 6 Sep 2026): A pool worker that dies
  from a signal is reported to the operator by that signal, with the executor's
  own teardown distinguished from the initiating crash, and with a fatal trace
  claimed only when one was actually produced.
  - [if] a worker dies from SIGSEGV [then] the CLI exits 5 and names `SIGSEGV
    (signal 11)` [⛔️ if it reports only `BrokenProcessPool`].
  - [if] the crash is reported [then] the pool has been shut down first, so the
    worker exit codes are reaped rather than read as `None` [⛔️ if a real crash
    reports the "died before its exit signal could be read" fallback].
  - [if] one worker crashes while another is still running [then] the survivor's
    executor-sent SIGTERM is labelled cleanup [⛔️ if it is listed as a second
    independent cause].
  - [if] SIGTERM is the only signal seen [then] it is reported as the cause, not
    as cleanup, because nothing broke the pool before it.
  - [if] the terminating signal has no `signal.Signals` member (a real-time
    signal) [then] its number is rendered [⛔️ if a `ValueError` replaces the
    crash diagnosis].
  - [if] the terminating signal is one faulthandler does not trace [then] the
    message does not claim a trace was printed [⛔️ if the operator is sent
    looking for output that does not exist].
  - [if] a worker dies while the queue is still being submitted [then] the same
    diagnostic is raised [⛔️ if a bare `BrokenProcessPool` escapes from
    `submit`].

- [x] **META-09** (shipped this PR; Thu 1 Oct 2026,
  third-party gaps audit item 6): Duplicate detection works in a shipped build,
  on the device, with no outside service. The Rust engine fingerprints audio
  (`odj-audio fingerprint FILE...`, rusty-chromaprint, MIT) into the same
  string chromaprint's `fpcalc` prints, so the packaged app no longer needs
  `fpcalc` or pyacoustid; the AcoustID web service is never called. The
  duplicate review page's "Find duplicates" (`POST /api/v1/dedup/scan`, progress
  at `GET /api/v1/dedup/scan`) fingerprints every live library track whose file
  is on this device, caches each by path, size and mtime under the track's own
  `stable_id`, and rebuilds the duplicate groups over this library's
  fingerprints. Groups are proposals for review only: no audio file is ever
  written, moved or deleted.
  - [if] the packaged app runs (`ODJ_AUDIO_BIN` set) [then] fingerprints come
    from the bundled engine [⛔️ if a shipped build reports no backend].
  - [if] the same audio is encoded twice (another sample rate, gain or codec)
    [then] the two fingerprints score at least 0.92 and land in one group, and
    different music scores below 0.8 [⛔️ if different music groups together].
  - [if] one copy starts later than the other (leading silence, encoder delay)
    [then] it is scored at the offset its shared sub-fingerprints agree on.
  - [if] two fingerprints overlap by fewer than 32 sub-fingerprints (about 4 s)
    [then] they score 0 [⛔️ if near-silent or very short files match anything].
  - [if] a fingerprint came from `fpcalc` (an older cache) [then] it decodes and
    compares against the engine's, because the compressed format is chromaprint's
    own [⛔️ if the decoder reads the compressed bytes as raw words, as the
    pre-fix fallback did].
  - [if] a track's file is missing or is a cloud placeholder [then] it is
    counted as not on this device and skipped, never downloaded.
  - [if] one file cannot be decoded [then] it is counted and named in the scan
    status and the scan continues [⛔️ if one bad file stops the scan].
  - [if] a scan is already running [then] another start answers 409 and starts
    nothing.
  - [if] the library holds thousands of tracks [then] candidate pairs come from
    an index of shared sub-fingerprints, not an all-pairs loop.

### Catalog (CAT)

- [x] **CAT-01** (shipped Phase 9): Spotify playlist importer - given a Spotify playlist URL, download (via user's own purchased channels), auto-tag, and create the matching playlist in RB + djay.
- [x] **CAT-02** (shipped Phase 10): USB sync + verify - keep external drives up to date with the canonical library; detect drift.
- [x] **CAT-03** (shipped Phase 8): Track-pairing memory - maintain hand-curated "these two flow well together" + "X flows into Y" lists.
- [x] **CAT-04** (shipped Phase 11): Cloud sync of the full library (master.db + MP3 files) using existing iCloud/Dropbox, a cheap paid provider (B2/R2), or an OSS alternative (Syncthing/Seafile). Provider chosen during the phase.
- [x] **CAT-05** (shipped Phase 11): Web UI supports cloud-synced browsing and edits, including immutable selected-pair deck snapshots with timestamps and live EQ adjustments.
- [x] **CAT-06** (shipped Phase 10.1): Pioneer/CDJ USB export - generate valid `export.pdb` + ANLZ + OneLibrary (`exportLibrary.db`) for CDJ/XDJ hardware from our canonical library. Three write paths: OneLibrary overlay (CDJ-3000X + OPUS-QUAD + OMNIS-DUO + XDJ-AZ; own SQLCipher handle `apps/sync/usb/pioneer/onelibrary.py` since Thu 1 Oct 2026, replacing `rbox`, which is GPL-3.0-only from 0.1.6; appended playlists and tracks now take the next free sequence number instead of repeating the last sibling's, and stick value verify reads OneLibrary loudness, which was always UNREAD under rbox), `rekordcrate` (classic `export.pdb`, experimental), agentic UI automation (drives Rekordbox.app). Fixture-backed validation via two-parser cross-check; hardware HITL deferred.

### Pairing Capture (PAIR)

- [x] **PAIR-01** (shipped Sun 6 Sep 2026): Pairing sync snapshots and alignment marks use a versioned durable SQLite repository that adopts compatible archive-era live tables without data loss.
  - [if] a live state database already contains compatible pairing capture tables [then] migration records the capture schema version and preserves every existing row [⛔️ if adoption recreates a table or loses a capture].
  - [if] the migration runs again after adoption [then] it returns the recorded version with no duplicate schema metadata or rows [⛔️ if a restart changes durable capture data].
  - [if] an existing capture object is a view or lacks a repository-required column [then] migration raises a named shape error before recording adoption [⛔️ if capture writes are redirected or fail later with opaque SQLite errors].

- [x] **PAIR-02** (shipped Sun 6 Sep 2026): `/api/v1/pairings/sync-snapshots` and `/api/v1/pairings/alignments` GET+POST routes expose the PAIR-01 durable repository with request/response validation, registered in the app; no UI in this part.
  - [if] a POST body names the same track for both sides of a snapshot or alignment [then] the route responds 422 `PAIRING_CAPTURE_INVALID` and persists nothing [⛔️ if an invalid capture is written or a 500 leaks a raw SQLite error].
  - [if] a POST body carries an out-of-enum `master_side`/`sync_mode`/`anchor_*_kind` or a negative position/anchor value [then] request validation rejects it with 422 before the repository is called [⛔️ if a malformed capture reaches storage].
  - [if] the state database predates the PAIR-01 migration (no capture tables yet) [then] the list routes return an empty array rather than a 500 [⛔️ if a pre-migration database 500s instead of reporting zero captures].
  - [if] state.db is absent [then] every route responds 503 `PAIRING_CAPTURE_DB_UNAVAILABLE` [⛔️ if a missing database silently 200s or 500s].

- [x] **PAIR-03** (shipped Mon 7 Sep 2026): Create-pairing sheet's Align hotcues and Reload sync wire onto the PAIR-02 routes through the typed client, reading live deck state and reusing the existing tempo/master/seek performance commands rather than a new composite one.
  - [if] both selected decks are loaded with two distinct tracks and share at least one hot-cue slot letter [then] Align hotcues POSTs one alignment per matching slot and reports the count [⛔️ if a match is skipped or a non-matching slot is POSTed].
  - [if] a sync snapshot for the pair was captured with the two tracks on the opposite decks from the current selection [then] Reload sync still finds and correctly re-maps it, since the repository's snapshot match is directional [⛔️ if a reversed-order capture is silently missed or replayed onto the wrong deck].
  - [if] no sync snapshot exists for the selected pair, or a replay command fails [then] the action reports the failure via toast and never a false "reloaded" success [⛔️ if a failed seek or tempo change is still reported as success].

- [x] **PAIR-06** (shipped Sat 26 Sep 2026; renumbered Sat 3 Oct 2026 from PAIR-04 because main shipped unrelated PAIR-04 for Create-pairing persistence): HTTP pairings persist in sqlite and paired partners show purple underlines in the library for the reference master across playlists. A failed pairing lookup shows an error toast and clears the underlines instead of reading as "no pairings", and switching master clears the previous master's underlines at once (Fri 2 Oct 2026). Deleting an HTTP pairing leaves a graph pairing it does not own in place with its notes: one that existed before it, such as one added through the pairing CLI, or one that graph tooling recreated or rewrote after the capture. Ownership is an explicit marker on the HTTP pairing (Sat 3 Oct 2026).
  - [if] capture pairing succeeds on /performance [then] POST /api/v1/pairings persists and survives SqliteBackend restart [else stop]
  - [if] a partner stable_id is paired with the reference master [then] its library row shows a purple pairing indicator in any playlist pane [else stop]
  - [if] the reference master changes while the previous master's pairing lookup is in flight [then] only the current master's partners are underlined (apps/webui/frontend/tests/unit/pairing-index-stale.test.mjs) [else stop]
  - [if] capture pairing fails [then] the UI surfaces an error toast and keeps the sheet open [else stop]
  - [if] a pairing create reuses a stored pairing_id for different endpoints or direction [then] it is refused with 409 already_exists and neither http_pairings nor the pairings graph changes (Fri 2 Oct 2026) [else stop]
  - [if] a create reuses pair-1 (A->B) for C->D while C->D already exists as pair-2 [then] the id check runs before the same-edge merge, so it is refused with 409 and neither pairing gains notes or a snapshot (Fri 2 Oct 2026, tests/webui/test_pairings_id_collision.py) [else stop]
  - [if] `state_authoritative_backup restore --table pairings` runs [then] http_pairings is restored with the pairings graph, a backup without http_pairings leaves the live table untouched, and a live state.db without it gets it created first [else stop]
- [x] **PAIR-04** (shipped Fri 2 Oct 2026): A pairing saved from the Create pairing sheet, or added on /pairings, is stored in the state database's `pairings` table (the same rows the `apps.pairings` CLI and the suggester's stage-2 rerank read), with its deck snapshot, so it survives a daemon or app restart. /pairings lists each pairing by artist and title, and shows the stable id with a "not in the library" tooltip only when the track cannot be found. Saving a pairing the CLI already holds the other way round (an `out_of` or `either` edge) merges into that row rather than duplicating it, and the suggester's stage-2 rerank (including suggest-next) and the `paired_with` smartlist rule read such reverse-stored edges for the track they follow. A local authoritative backup taken before pairings kept a deck snapshot still restores its pairings, with no snapshot.
  - [if] a pairing is captured and the daemon restarts [then] GET /api/v1/pairings and the PAIRED row for the deck-1 track still show it, with its snapshot [⛔️ if the pairing lived only in process memory and vanished].
  - [if] the same pairing is captured again [then] new notes append and the first snapshot is kept [⛔️ if a recapture overwrites the frozen snapshot or adds a duplicate row].
  - [if] a pairing was added with the CLI [then] the UI lists it, an `out_of` edge reading as its reverse `->` [⛔️ if CLI and UI pairings live in separate stores].

- [x] **PAIR-05** (shipped Fri 2 Oct 2026): Create pairing is reachable on laptop-width windows and opens on any two loaded decks.
  - [if] the performance window is 1161px to 1740px wide [then] the top bar shows the button as a compact PAIR label with the same title [⛔️ if it is hidden on every Mac laptop width].
  - [if] beat sync max is on but a loaded deck has no beat at or before its position (no beatgrid yet, or a fresh load at 0 ms) [then] the sheet still opens and stamps every deck in real time, with the snapshot's `beat_sync_max` false [⛔️ if the sheet refuses to open, or mixes beat and time units].
  - [if] Capture succeeds [then] a "Pairing saved" toast shows and the PAIRED row appears without reloading the deck [⛔️ if the save is silent until the next deck load].

### Lyrics (LYR)

- [x] **LYR-01**: Word-onset lyric alignment is measured in track seconds by a versioned scorer reporting median absolute error, PCO at 300 ms, and catastrophe rate; the committed timing-only fixture set must meet Ship-tier thresholds of medae_s <= 0.15, pco_300ms >= 0.90, and catastrophe_rate <= 0.03.
  - [if] a predicted word onset is within 300 ms of its index-aligned reference onset [then] it counts toward `pco_300ms`, including exactly 300 ms [⛔️ if a floating-point representation of the boundary changes the result].
  - [if] a predicted onset is more than 2.0 seconds from its reference [then] it counts toward `catastrophe_rate`, while exactly 2.0 seconds does not [⛔️ if the boundary is treated as a catastrophe].
  - [if] an aligner leaves a reference word unplaced [then] it is excluded from accuracy denominators but reported through `words_unplaced` and recall [⛔️ if missing predictions can read as accurate].

- [x] **LYR-02**: The karaoke batch pipeline (`python -m apps.lyrics batch run|resume`, `jobs work`, `register-stems`, `stems push --missing`, `stems hydrate`) runs on main against the v10 storage: verdicts through `apps.lyrics.store`, word timings as `karaoke_words` artifacts, stem parts as content-addressed R2 assets recorded only in the bundle manifest.
  - [if] the ingest stage starts in cloud mode with no `sync_policies` row for `karaoke_words` [then] the driver fails at stage 0 naming the missing policy, before any GPU or Modal spend ⛔️
  - [if] `register-stems` registers a schema-v3 bundle [then] its manifest gains `files_sha256` per part and no local file is moved or deleted; a v1 manifest is left byte-identical ⛔️
  - [if] `stems push --missing --dry-run` runs [then] it prints the work set and uploads nothing; a live run verifies every upload by re-listing and journals it ⛔️

- [x] **LYR-03**: The app serves word-level karaoke data (`GET /api/v1/tracks/{stable_id}/lyrics/words[?include=lines]`, summary, triage, override, config, jobs, purge routes) and renders it as a word lane on the performance waveform behind the `lyrics_waveform_overlay` pref, with listing enrichment (lyrics verdict, remix, radio-edit) served by one bulk query per page.
  - [if] a track has a live verdict row and a readable words artifact [then] the words route returns 200 with words and derived lines; [if] either is missing or tombstoned [then] 404 with a detail naming which ⛔️
  - [if] `lyrics_waveform_overlay` is on and the track has words [then] the word lane renders and main's line lane does not; otherwise main's line lane renders exactly as before ⛔️
  - [if] main's `GET /api/v1/tracks/{stable_id}/lyrics` is called after the change [then] its response is byte-identical, pinned by a regression test ⛔️
  - [if] `/performance` is at the compact `max-height: 799px` wavestack and LYR is on [then] the TopBar shows a compact waveform-lyrics suppression cue instead of silently hiding the word lane while LYR still appears fully active ⛔️

- [x] **LYR-04**: A branch-era state.db moves to schema v10 through a scripted, dry-run-first runbook that backs up first, renames the legacy `lyric_verdict` and `lyric_word` tables aside, drops the stale `idx_lyric_verdict_red`, runs the ladder and converts legacy words into artifacts with honest counts; the live run on the user's Mac is a separate machine-bound step.
  - [if] the script runs `--dry-run` [then] it prints the plan and counts and changes no byte of the file ⛔️
  - [if] the stale index is still attached to the renamed table when the ladder would run [then] the script stops before the ladder naming the index ⛔️
  - [if] `--live` runs twice [then] the second run is a no-op that says so ⛔️

  - [if] the batch driver is pointed at one real library track on a fresh main checkout [then] it ends with a live `lyric_verdict` row and a words artifact for that track, run log attached ⛔️
  - [if] the app opens that track with the overlay on [then] the word lane renders the words in time, captured as an exact-SHA screenshot on the PR ⛔️
  - [if] the track page opens [then] the lyrics panel shows verdict, source and word/line counts matching the row ⛔️

- [x] **LYR-06**: A library-scale, resumable `python -m apps.lyrics verdicts backfill` command and its `POST /api/v1/lyrics/verdicts/backfill` HTTP parity fill or refresh a stem-coverage-only `lyric_verdict` row for every track with a loadable demucs4/roformer2 stem bundle, deriving vocal coverage from the existing `apps.vocals.from_stems`/`vocal_region_worker` maths (never reimplemented) and writing only through `apps.lyrics.store.upsert_stem_coverage_verdict` -- a dedicated, atomically-guarded writer for this coverage-only path, distinct from the shared `apps.lyrics.store.upsert_verdict` every other lyrics writer (ASR/aligner, legacy migration) uses; see ADR-0025. Depends on the v1 bundle loader for MP3/FLAC parts by their own container landing first; this work must not merge before it.
  - [if] a candidate stable_id is listed in `state/stem-order-reserved-100.json` [then] it is skipped, reported under a "reserved" reason, and never processed unless `--include-reserved`/`include_reserved` is explicitly set ⛔️
  - [if] an existing row carries a human `override` or a `words_content_hash` (word-level data) [then] the backfill never overwrites it, only fills/refreshes coverage-only rows -- enforced both at scan time (`SKIP_HAS_OVERRIDE`/`SKIP_HAS_WORDS`) and, against the same race a scan-then-write gap allows, inside `upsert_stem_coverage_verdict`'s own atomic conflict guard (`SKIP_PROTECTED_ROW_RACE`) ⛔️
  - [if] a bundle fails to load (corrupt/missing parts), or a present vocal-cache entry cannot be read/parsed [then] it is reported as a FAILURE with a reason, never silently skipped or folded into a "no cache" recompute ⛔️
  - [if] the backfill is re-run with no bundle or row change [then] it is a no-op (0 processed), and a replaced or re-separated bundle (new stem-artifact identity, `apps.vocals.from_stems.bundle_stem_identity` -- not merely a new source-track `sha256`) forces recompute ⛔️

- [x] **LYR-07** (shipped Sat 26 Sep 2026; e2e `lyrics-words.spec.ts` LYR-07 karaoke-words deck strip + LYR-07 line-cache fallback deck strip against real `/lyrics` API): The deck hot-cue region shows one to three rows of synced lyrics beside the hot-cue bank when `lyrics_deck_line` is on; never shows "no lyric data" when word or line-cache lyrics exist; layout compacts when vertical space is tight. The hot-cue bank and the lyric strip split the cue row's width 3:2 (Fri 2 Oct 2026: before this the bank's `width: 100%` left the strip 0px wide, present and loaded but invisible); pad labels ellipsize inside their pad instead of spilling into the next column.
  - [if] lyrics exist for the loaded deck track [then] the deck shows lyric text beside the hot-cue bank instead of NO LYRIC DATA [else stop]
  - [if] the cue row is tall enough [then] up to three lyric preview rows render [else stop]
- [x] **LYR-08**: Producing a karaoke words artifact drops phantom tail words so the waveform word lane never shows them, and the envelope keeps its honest `source` attribution. Only two narrow rules drop words: a word whose start is at or past the track's actual duration (no shortening margin), and a trailing span after the last sung line that is exactly one or more known Whisper silence phrases ("thank you", "thanks for watching", ...) where every word has a weak ASR witness (contradict/lost/unheard) AND the span begins at least 2 s after the previous word ends. Repetition alone is never evidence, and a gap that cannot be measured keeps the words.
  - [if] produce writes words for a track whose aligner output ends in a weak-witness "thank you" span after a silence gap, or holds words starting past the track duration [then] those words are absent from the written artifact [else stop] ⛔️
  - [if] the aligner output has real lyrics inside the duration, including a repeated chorus or outro after the last line, a sung agree-witness "thank you", or a word in the final quarter-second [then] every word is kept unchanged [else stop] ⛔️

**Shared prerequisite, verified Mon 31 Aug 2026 - the recorder does not watch
Open DJ.** SET-01..03 (record, classify, replay) are shipped and `apps/sets` is
mounted, but the only two timeline sources that exist are
`apps/sets/sources/rb_source.py` (`RekordboxHistorySource`, which polls
rekordbox HISTORY playlists and records `deck=None` because "rb history does
not carry a deck label") and `apps/sets/sources/djay_source.py` (djay history
items). NOTHING observes Open DJ's own decks, and the rail REC glyph is inert.
Every recording ask here is about the user's OWN Open DJ set, so SET-06 and
SET-08 both sit behind a missing Open DJ deck observer. That is a real build,
not a mounting fix, and no acceptance test below can pass while the timeline
for an Open DJ performance does not exist.

**Correcting the record, Tue 1 Sep 2026 - the observer now exists.** The
paragraph above is accurate as of Mon 31 Aug 2026 and is kept for the record.
Since then `apps/sets/sources/opendj_source.py` plus
`POST /api/sets/deck-observations` landed, and the browser emitter
`apps/webui/frontend/src/lib/sets/deck-observer-emitter.ts` now feeds it from
/performance while REC enables the `opendj_decks` source. An Open DJ set
therefore produces a real timeline: measured on a 40s audible play, 43
snapshots accepted and a `track_loaded` row with deck='1' and audible_s 41.35
in data/sets/sets.db. The live performance rail REC control now queries
`GET /api/sets/recorder`, prompts for the required ffmpeg input index, then
starts `POST /api/sets/recorder/start` with `djay_monitor` and `opendj_decks`.
While it owns an active session, the same control finalizes that session through
`POST /api/sets/recorder/{session_id}/stop`; an externally owned recording is
refused with its owning process rather than stopped implicitly.

This requirement is a ruling on how autoplay should treat a sorted library view.

"this way" = autoplay consuming the LIVE sorted library view, so re-sorting
mid-session silently re-plans what plays next. The ruling is SNAPSHOT-AT-
ACTIVATION. A separate UI placement amendment is recorded
separately as FB-07, not here.
- [x] **PLAY-04**: Autoplay takes a SNAPSHOT of the library order at activation, starts a new snapshot when the active playlist changes even if its ordered members match, adopts a new sort only when turned on or toggled off and back on after sorting, and never silently re-plans when the live view changes underneath it.
  - **Status Thu 3 Sep 2026:** shipped. The activation freeze, frozen-while-running
    behavior, and re-toggle snapshot are covered by
    `autoplay-feed-snapshot.test.mjs`. This closed the empty pre-hydration
    snapshot hole (see PLAY-06). The final acceptance gap remains closed:
    the browser now plainly identifies when the running snapshot differs from
    the visible order and tells the user how to adopt that order.
  - **Status Fri 2 Oct 2026:** the activation
    snapshot waits until a progressively loaded playlist has finished
    filling (`pane.load_progress` is null). Before, turning AutoPlay on while a
    big playlist was still streaming in froze the candidate set at the first
    page. While the fill runs the feed tracks the growing view unsnapshotted.
  - **Why PLAY and not LIBUX/DECKUX.** The question is WHEN the autoplay order
    is planned, which is PLAY-02's subject (`PLAY IT` auto-generates a
    play-order). The sorted library view is the INPUT to that decision, not the
    thing being specified, so this extends the Play Orders family rather than
    the library-layout one.
  - [if] the user sorts the library while autoplay is already running [then]
    the currently planned order is unchanged and continues to play [⛔️ if
    sorting silently re-plans what plays next].
  - [if] the user sorts the library and then turns autoplay on, or toggles it
    off and back on [then] autoplay adopts the new sorted order from that
    moment.
  - [if] the user changes or clears an active library filter while autoplay is
    running [then] autoplay immediately uses only the newly visible rows, or
    the restored full list, without serving the prior chain [⛔️ if a filtered-
    out track can be scheduled or clearing needs a reload].
  - [if] a user manually loads a track from the library [then] autoplay derives
    the chain from that loaded track rather than the first row in the view
    [⛔️ if a double-click resets the next-track decision to the list top].
  - [if] autoplay is running against a snapshot that no longer matches the
    visible sort [then] the UI makes that plainly visible rather than implying
    the two agree [⛔️ if the user has to guess which order is live].
  - [if] the user switches playlists while autoplay is running [then] the new
    playlist becomes a new feed scope and can re-arm an uncommitted exhaustion
    even when its stable IDs and order match the prior playlist [⛔️ if autoplay
    remains exhausted against the prior playlist scope].
- [x] **PLAY-05** (shipped): A user-viewable autoplay queue, created when autoplay is started,
      showing what is planned to play next. **Flagged as a LATER requirement**
      ("Later, we'll have a queue user can view"), so it is recorded now and
      deliberately not scheduled into the current work; it depends on PLAY-04's
      snapshot existing as a real object first.
  - **Note the note.** This feature was separately flagged from the other
    direction and parked: rekordbox's auto mix queue is judged cumbersome
    and little used, so this feature is deliberately placed in the backlog.
    The ruling above revives a lighter version of it (view the queue
    autoplay already built), not rekordbox's editable queue. Build the
    viewer before any editor.
  - [if] autoplay is started [then] a queue object is created that the user can
    open and read, listing the planned upcoming tracks in order.
  - [if] the autoplay snapshot is re-taken per PLAY-04 (toggled off and on
    after a sort) [then] the visible queue reflects the new snapshot [⛔️ if
    the queue and the actual playback order can disagree].
  - [if] an AutoPlay guard clears the charted order and its inputs recover unchanged [then] the next poll republishes the visible queue [⛔️ if rank badges remain blank until a different input changes].

PLAY-06..07 recorded Tue 1 Sep 2026 from the morning's live incident (first
track played, then silence) and that day's rulings.

- [x] **PLAY-06** (shipped): An EMPTY library view never arms the
      autoplay activation snapshot. auto_play_enabled defaults true and persists,
      and the panel effect observes (enabled, zero rows) before the first rows
      fetch resolves; freezing that locked autoplay out for a whole session while
      83 eligible tracks sat in the playlist.
  - [if] autoplay is enabled while the visible view has zero rows [then] no
    snapshot is taken; the feed keeps tracking the live view and the FIRST
    observation with rows takes the activation snapshot [⛔️ if an empty feed
    is frozen for the session].
  - [if] the autoplay picker dead-ends because the candidate feed is EMPTY
    [then] the toast names the empty feed as its own diagnosis [⛔️ if it is
    reported as a key/BPM dead end, which sends the operator reading key
    wheels while the real fault is a pre-hydration freeze].
  - [if] the view is genuinely empty and stays empty [then] repeated
    observations keep waiting and never half-arm the snapshot.
- [x] **PLAY-07** (shipped): The autoplay trigger window clamps to
      min(16s, duration/2). Rule decided Tue 1 Sep 2026: a track shorter than
      the constant window used to be in-window at t=0, so pressing play armed a
      handoff instantly and the next track started over its own first beat.
  - [if] a 12s track starts playing [then] no handoff arms before 6s have
    played, and the handoff arms after that point [⛔️ if play start arms
    immediately].
  - [if] a track's duration is unknown [then] no window exists and no handoff
    ever arms from it (scenario row 3 preserved).
  - [if] a track is 32s or longer [then] the window is the constant 16s,
    unchanged.
- [x] **PLAY-08** (shipped): Every terminal AutoPlay branch - the
      remaining rows are all missing/stub audio, no next track in play order, no
      key/BPM-compatible track, a handoff that failed its attempt budget or died
      after the commit point - leaves a PERSISTENT, visible state naming the
      cause and the way back to sound, not only a toast. Rule from the Wed 9 Sep
      2026 incident: the exhaustion toast fired at 18:23:39.614Z, cleared itself
      after `TOAST_DEFAULT_MS`, and the app then sat with a loaded deck and a
      blank screen until 20:53Z. the report was that it "randomly stops
      playing", which is exactly what a five-second explanation looks like.
      Stopping when nothing playable remains is CORRECT; being quiet about it is
      the defect.
  - [if] autoplay exhausts the queue [then] the app says so and keeps saying so
    until sound is actually back [⛔️ if the only trace expires in five
    seconds].
  - [if] the stalled track then ENDS and every deck goes idle [then] the state
    is still displayed [⛔️ if the explanation vanishes at the exact moment the
    room goes quiet].
  - [if] every remaining playlist row is a missing or stub file [then] those
    tracks are nameable from the UI, with an exact total even when the list is
    capped [⛔️ if a library-integrity fault surfaces only as silence].
  - [if] the same missing file occupies several playlist positions [then] it is
    named ONCE and the total counts DISTINCT tracks [⛔️ if the keyed render
    hits duplicate keys and the banner fails to draw at all; the operator
    relinks files, not positions].
  - [if] a compatible candidate already failed to LOAD for this source [then]
    the state blames the files [⛔️ if a quarantined candidate leaves a
    remainder that merely looks incompatible and the operator is sent to widen
    a pitch range that was never the problem], and NAMES the candidates that
    failed [⛔️ if it names the surviving incompatible rows, which is where the
    remainder points once the failures are quarantined out of it].
  - [if] the operator opens a different playlist after a load failure [then]
    the next dead end does not claim the NEW playlist's candidates failed to
    load [⛔️ if attempt state outlives the feed it was measured on and the app
    reports a failure that never happened].
  - [if] a candidate failed to load AND every unquarantined row left is a stub
    [then] the load failure is the reported cause [⛔️ if the stub remainder
    wins: it is already visible in the library, while the failed candidate is
    visible nowhere else once its toast expires].
  - [if] the attempt budget is spent [then] the state NAMES the three files
    that failed [⛔️ if their identities survive only in expiring toasts], and
    says THREE DIFFERENT
    tracks failed [⛔️ if it says one track failed three times: a candidate is
    claimed before its dispatch, so a retry can never pick the same id twice,
    and the singular sends the operator hunting a flaky file that does not
    exist].
  - [if] AutoPlay is switched off, or /performance unmounts, while a handoff is
    still awaiting [then] the late rejection records nothing [⛔️ if a stop
    banner sits over a switched-off feature, and module-level state carries it
    into the next mount]. It is checked against the ARMING the handoff started
    under, not against "is AutoPlay on now" [⛔️ if a toggle off and on lets a
    dead handoff restore its stale state into the session that replaced it].
  - [if] the operator expanded one stall's track list [then] a LATER stall
    starts collapsed [⛔️ if an unrelated stop springs 30vh of list over the
    decks unasked], and it opens on the FIRST click [⛔️ if the carried-over
    open flag inverts the toggle and the operator has to click twice]. Every
    recorded stall carries a per-OCCURRENCE revision and
    the expansion is keyed on it [⛔️ if a key made of the stall's CONTENT
    reads a second stop with the same reason and source track, over a
    different playlist, as a continuation of the first].
  - [if] a different track is playing as master [then] the state is retired
    [⛔️ if a stale stop banner sits over a playing set].
  - [if] AutoPlay is switched off [then] the state is retired: a disarmed
    feature is not a stalled one.
  - [if] the condition is recorded [then] it is reported at `error` severity
    and reaches `/api/v1/client-errors`, and it is published on the ui-mirror so
    an agent reads the same cause a person does.
  - [if] a stall is raised while /performance is already open [then] the
    banner becomes VISIBLE without a reload, and leaves the DOM when the stall
    is retired [⛔️ if it renders but is clipped by the topbar's `overflow:
    hidden`, painted behind the waveform stack, or merely hidden rather than
    removed]. Proven in a real browser
    (`playwright.autoplay-stall-gate.config.ts`), because visibility, stacking
    and hit-testing are not answerable from markup.
  - [if] a REAL exhaustion happens in the shipped app - a real playlist, a real
    deck load, real transport, and the production controller's own poll [then]
    the banner appears with the cause on it [⛔️ if only an INJECTED stall is
    ever proven to render, which passes while the controller has stopped
    publishing one].
  - [if] the track list is expanded [then] neither it nor the banner covers the
    control that closes it, nor the deck controls beneath [⛔️ if the operator
    cannot dismiss the list or reach a deck].
  - [if] a late handoff rejection arrives from a dead arming [then] NOTHING it
    would have done runs: no toast, no `/api/v1/client-errors` row, no
    quarantine, no re-arm [⛔️ if a stale session files a server-side failure
    against the session that replaced it, or makes it skip a candidate it
    never tried].
  - [if] the deferred MASTER handover for a track AutoPlay just started is
    refused [then] that is recorded durably too [⛔️ if it stays an expiring
    toast: the follower is playing and unmastered, `pickSourceDeck` only ever
    arms off the master, so nothing queues after it and the set ends in silence
    when it finishes].
  - [if] a refused master handover is recorded [then] it is retired only when
    the REFUSED deck is itself the audible master [⛔️ if ANY audible master
    clears it: a rejected setDeckMaster leaves the OUTGOING deck master and
    still playing, so the very next poll would erase a banner whose fault is
    still true]. This inverts the retire rule every other reason uses, and is
    the only reason that inverts it.
  - [if] a stop is recorded [then] the toast and the durable state are built
    from ONE derivation of the cause [⛔️ if the incident row in
    `webui-client-errors-*.log` names a different cause from the banner on
    screen; the log is what an audit reads months later].
  - [if] the banner wraps to more than one row at a narrow width [then] its
    track list still sits below it [⛔️ if a hard-coded offset covers the
    wrapped instructions and the toggle needed to close the list].

- [x] **PLAY-09** (shipped Fri 11 Sep 2026): AutoPlay disarms once every deck has been stopped

  - [if] AutoPlay is armed and decks 1 and 2 (the hunt's scope) have both been

    [then] the pref reads disarmed [⛔️ if aria-pressed stays true and the hunt records

  - [if] idle disarm fires while a PLAY-08 stall is displayed [then] the stall

Post-playback idle raises `no-deck-playing` after 30s and disarms after 31s; arming AutoPlay with no deck playing keeps the pref for 3 minutes before auto-disarm without a silent stall; when AutoPlay is on the `>|` split shows accent highlight and hover-blue icon.

- [x] **PLAY-14** (shipped Sat 26 Sep 2026): AutoPlay arm/run failures are observable in frontend error capture with timestamp and reason.
  - [if] AutoPlay is enabled but cannot arm or run [then] a console `error` or documented stall reason is emitted and is collectable by the autoplay error hunt [⛔️ if the UI sits silent with no diagnosable reason].

- [x] **PLAY-10** (shipped Mon 14 Sep 2026): AutoPlay commits at most one load per master track per threshold pass. Arm and claim happen before dispatch; a commit-phase handoff failure never re-arms; claimed stable_ids stay unpickable for the session even across feed-epoch rolls; master promotion waits until the follower is audible.
  - [if] the master is in-window with a pickable next row [then] at most one follower receives a new load for that source track [⛔️ if two distinct stable_ids load before the source changes].
  - [if] load succeeded on the follower and a later handoff step fails [then] AutoPlay does not pick another candidate [⛔️ if a second deck loads].
  - [if] a stable_id was claimed earlier this session [then] it is excluded from future picks even if its deck was unloaded [⛔️ if the same id loads twice].
  - [if] master promotion is waiting for audibility [then] later polls promote without starting a new handoff [⛔️ if promotion failure re-arms the trigger].

  - [if] the transition ends, aborts, or the outgoing deck unloads [then] the outgoing loop is released and LOW EQ duck is restored
  - [if] the transition completes or aborts [then] the outgoing deck fader command changes nodes.fader.gain

### Smart Playlists (SMART)

Rule-based auto-populating playlists (Lexicon-style). Materialized into static playlists on sync to RB + djay; re-evaluated when underlying data changes.

- [x] **SMART-01** (shipped): Rule schema supporting predicates on genre, BPM range, key (Camelot), rating, energy, custom tags, added-date, last-played, color-tag. AND/OR/NOT composition.
- [x] **SMART-02** (shipped): Materialization engine evaluates a rule against the current library and pushes the resulting track list as a static playlist to Rekordbox and djay Pro.
- [x] **SMART-03** (shipped): Re-evaluation triggers - on new track added, on tag edit, on user-requested refresh. Debounced.
- [x] **SMART-04** (shipped Fri 11 Sep 2026): Web-first smartlist create + rule editor UI; POST /api/v1/smartlists then /smartlists/{id} editor save; launcher integration later.
- [x] **SMART-05** (shipped Sat 12 Sep 2026, part 1 of 2): Genre, rating, and BPM autolist groups compile to a smartlist rule (OR within a group, AND across groups) and evaluate on a fixture DB without persisting bucket rows.
  - [if] one genre bucket is selected [then] evaluate returns only that genre's tracks [⛔️ if other genres leak in].
  - [if] two buckets in one group are selected [then] the result is their union; selections from different groups intersect.
  - GET/POST /api/v1/autolists, Autolists-tab headers, worker index, and virtualized multi-select UI shipped as **SMART-06**.
- [x] **SMART-06** (shipped Sat 12 Sep 2026, part 2 of 2): Autolists tab lists Genre / Rating / BPM group headers that expand without blocking the UI; multi-select is union within a group and intersection across groups; the stacked row set stays virtualized; first click uses the worker index or paged POST /api/v1/autolists/query so an 8k library does not freeze the main thread.
  - [if] user opens the Autolists tab [then] Genre, Rating, and BPM headers are on screen from static markup (no await before paint) [⛔️ if tab open waits on GET /autolists or GET /tracks]
  - [if] two buckets in one group are selected [then] the pane rows are their union; selections from different groups intersect; TrackTable stays the only row list
  - [if] the user first-clicks a bucket in a large library [then] page-1 rows arrive from the worker index or paged query without a synchronous 8k BrowserRow map on the main thread

### Library Management (LIBM)

Library CRUD, membership, hygiene and UI conventions. Full 129-leaf tree; only leaves with a filed build issue are listed here; add the rest as they are scheduled. Blocking decisions LIBM-D1..D5 are all answered (ADR-0019..ADR-0023 in `docs/decisions/`).

- [x] **LIBM-01** (shipped Sat 12 Sep 2026, via LIBM-20; row shape from schema v13): Playlist membership is an addressable row (item id + fractional order_key string); a one-track add is O(1) writes, not a delete-and-reinsert of the whole playlist.
- [x] **LIBM-02** (shipped Sat 12 Sep 2026): order_key is a fractional index STRING using a base62 alphabet (never a float); v13 backfill preserves original position order as 8-digit digit strings in that alphabet.
- [x] **LIBM-03** (shipped Sat 12 Sep 2026; per-container forbid Sat 12 Sep 2026): duplicate policy is allow-in-playlist by default (LIBM-D2); a per-playlist forbid_duplicates flag rejects extra copies; add/remove/move enforce it in one place and key remove/move on item id.
  - [if] a track is added to a playlist that already contains it and duplicates are not forbidden [then] both memberships are stored and both are independently removable
  - [if] a container has the "forbid duplicates" setting on and the track is already a member [then] the add is a no-op, never a silent second row
  - [if] duplicate copies of a track are inspected [then] all copies resolve to the same underlying file/stable_id
- [x] **LIBM-04b** (shipped Sat 12 Sep 2026): container uniqueness is a per-playlist forbid_duplicates flag (default off). Ordered lists allow repeats; the flag forbids them. This is not a second crate type. Live query remains smartlists; live folder-mirror is not this issue.
- [x] **LIBM-08** (shipped Sat 12 Sep 2026): membership uniqueness is item_id, not (playlist_id, stable_id); a tombstone cannot block re-adding the same track.
- [x] **LIBM-09** (shipped Mon 14 Sep 2026): Per-track local availability (`track_availability`) is owned and refreshed by the engine through a bounded, resumable stat-only probe at startup and after ingest or relink; `tracks_available` is populated without a manual MIK audit. `python -m apps.mik availability` remains the explicit full-library parity and repair tool.
  - [if] a fresh data dir has N tracks whose paths exist on this machine [then] after engine start and probe completion `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tracks_available` equals an independent `os.path.exists` count over live `tracks.file_path` values
  - [if] a path does not resolve on a mounted volume [then] the row is `absent`, not `present`, and is excluded from `tracks_available`
  - [if] a path is under `/Volumes/<name>` and that volume is not mounted [then] the row is `awaiting_volume` and is reclassified on later probe passes when the volume is attached
  - [if] a library listing is requested while a probe is still running [then] the listing answers without waiting for probe completion
  - [if] an agent triggers `POST /api/v1/availability/probe` [then] the same status is readable via `GET /api/v1/availability/status` and `opendj api`
  - [if] another in-process engine writer briefly holds the state.db write lock during a background availability batch [then] the worker waits/retries and the round's rows are not dropped to a terminal failed phase
  - [if] a background availability batch exhausts its database-lock retries [then] the worker logs the give-up at error, requeues that batch, and keeps draining until every unchecked row has been probed [else stop]
- [x] **LIBM-11** (shipped Fri 11 Sep 2026): Raw CLI escape hatch `opendj api METHOD PATH` so every HTTP endpoint is agent-reachable from the CLI the day it ships.
  - [if] the engine is not running [then] `opendj status`, `opendj open performance`, and `opendj api GET /api/v1/health` all exit 2 with a message naming the lock file or unreachable origin [else stop]
  - [if] `opendj api` is called with an unknown HTTP method [then] it exits 1, never 2 [else stop]
  - [if] `opendj api` is called with an invalid path [then] it exits 1 and `--json` reports `error.code: invalid_path` [else stop]
- [x] **LIBM-112** (decided ADR-0022): webui-only data with no vendor equivalent (`notes`/`tags`/`pairings`/`smartlists`/`play_orders`) is genuinely backed up rather than derivative; `hub_backup.py` covers synced rows; local per-machine backup via `apps/shared/state_authoritative_backup.py` (`docs/ops/state-authoritative-backup.md`).
- [x] **LIBM-113** (decided ADR-0022): library backup and restore keeps N dated versions, restores selectively, and covers external volumes via `--dest`; local module + hub backup together satisfy the requirement.
- [x] **LIBM-122** (shipped Sat 26 Sep 2026): Large libraries render through DOM virtualization with honest non-broken health counts (not raw state_db.tracks).
  - [if] All Tracks has thousands of rows [then] TrackTable virtualizes DOM while the pane holds hydrated rows [else stop]
  - [if] the library health dot quotes a total [then] it uses non-broken reconcile counts [else stop]
  - [if] the non-broken reconcile count is not yet known after a library refresh [then] no total quotes the raw state_db row count in its place [else stop]
- [x] **LIBM-138** (shipped Sat 26 Sep 2026; renumbered Fri 2 Oct 2026 from LIBM-135 because main shipped unrelated LIBM-135 for context menus; renumbered Thu 1 Oct 2026 to LIBM-135 after main claimed LIBM-132 through LIBM-134): Admin diagnostics links to library tidying routes without file deletion.
  - [if] Admin diagnostics is open [then] reconcile, dedup, and remove-from-library guidance is linked [else stop]
- [ ] **LIBM-129** (v2): Folder watcher auto-import from configured paths (config placeholder only in v1; no background watcher).
  - [if] library_watcher_folders is saved in prefs [then] paths are validated and stored with a v2-not-active label [else stop]
  - [if] library_watcher_folders is saved on disk [then] a fresh browser profile hydrates the same list from GET /api/v1/ui-prefs [else stop]
  - [if] the watcher-folders PUT fails (HTTP error or no daemon) [then] Settings shows the failure, not "Saved", and keeps the previous folders [else stop]
  - [if] a watcher folder is a Windows drive-letter (C:\Music, C:/Music) or UNC (\\server\share) absolute path [then] the client syntax check accepts it like a POSIX absolute path, while relative and drive-relative (C:Music) forms are still rejected [else stop]
- [x] **LIBM-130** (shipped Fri 25 Sep 2026): Library listing and playlist detail hydrate their rows with a fixed number of state.db connections, and each batched read issues one SELECT per 500-id bind batch (`ID_BIND_BATCH`), so statements grow with ceil(rows / 500), never once per row; a track with no rekordbox mapping never opens its own connection, and the page's rekordbox meta read seeks the page's ids rather than walking the library.
  - [if] `GET /api/v1/tracks` lists 20 tracks with no rekordbox mapping [then] it opens the same connections and issues the same statements as a 4-row page
  - [if] a 20-member playlist opens via `GET /api/v1/playlists/{id}` [then] it opens the same connections and issues the same statements as a 4-member one
  - [if] a batched path read spans 501 or 1001 ids [then] it issues 2 or 3 SELECTs per table (one per 500-id batch) and every id resolves as the per-id reader does
  - [if] the artwork lookup is batched [then] every row's `artwork_available` / `artwork_status` equals the per-row `local_artwork_available` verdict the rb-meta route serves
  - [if] a page's `djmdContent` read (`bulk_rb_meta`, the library wheel's genre read) runs on a real rekordbox schema [then] its plan seeks the ID key, never the `rb_local_deleted` index that walks every live row
- [x] **LIBM-131** (shipped Fri 25 Sep 2026; superseded Tue 29 Sep 2026 by LIBM-132, which reads no existing member at all): Adding tracks to a playlist reads each existing member once (the response `items` and undo snapshots), never once per lookup; the neighbors' order_keys and the duplicate check are bounded reads.
  - [if] one track is added to a 400-member playlist [then] exactly one more member row is read per extra member than for a 40-member playlist, append or positioned
  - [if] a position is given [then] the new row's neighbors are the same two order_keys the full ordered member list gives

- [x] **LIBM-137** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026, found on the preview's All Tracks boot): A page of the track listing reads each rekordbox-mapped row's preview strip, vocal regions and cover-art verdict off disk once, then answers later pages from memory for as long as every file it looked at is unchanged. Before, every request re-walked the share root for every row, many file opens a row, and built the page's models three times; a warm page took hundreds of milliseconds and a full-library walk took several seconds in process. What is remembered is file CONTENT that was read through the descriptors of the share-root containment walk itself (round 3, after an independent review): no path is reopened, no containment verdict is reused, and a row is remembered only when nothing on its paths was refused. A remembered row is served only while the share root has the same identity, every directory on its paths is the same real directory, and every file it looked at has the same type, inode, device, size, modification time and change time; an error while checking is a miss for that row, never a failed page. The memory is bound to one share root, emptied when the share root is recomputed or re-anchored, and holds at most 40,000 rows (least recently used goes first; about 1 KB a row measured). The wire format is unchanged. Round 4 (second independent review): an analysis file that cannot be decoded (empty, garbage, truncated, a changed PVDI header) is that one source having nothing, so the row falls through to its next source and is logged by stable id, never by path, and the page answers; a file with more than one hard link, or larger than 16 MiB, is not read and its row is not remembered (typical export trees hold no hard links, and their analysis files are well under that cap); a row that cannot be keyed on its own vendor strings (any row where the descriptor walk is unsupported, a `/PIONEER/` path with an empty, `.` or `..` component or a trailing dot, a path outside `/PIONEER/`) is read by path on every request and neither reads nor fills any memory. The page's `lyrics_available` flag is one `lstat` of `<stable id>.json` in the lyrics cache per row: letter case follows the volume exactly as the lyrics read's own lookup does, a symlinked entry is no lyrics wherever it points, an id that is not one file name is no lyrics, and any error (the cache path is a file, the directory is unreadable) is no lyrics for that row, never a failed page.
  - [if] a 500-row page of a 10,000-track rekordbox-mapped library is asked for a second time, at the start of the library and 7,000 rows in [then] the request opens at most 40 files and returns the same rows as the first time [⛔️ if the count of opens grows with the number of rows, or a remembered row differs from a freshly read one].
  - [if] pages of 100 and 500 rows are read at the start and deep in the library [then] every page uses the same number of database statements and connections, and the page's bytes stay under 1,900 a row on the test library [⛔️ if statements grow with page size or offset, or the payload budget is passed].
  - [if] between two requests an analysis file is rewritten, a cover file is deleted, or an analysis file appears where there was none [then] the next page shows the new preview, `file_missing`, and the new strip, while an untouched row is unchanged [⛔️ if a remembered row outlives a change to a file it was read from].
  - [if] a directory on a remembered row's path is replaced by a symlink pointing outside the share root [then] the next page serves no preview and no artwork for that row [⛔️ if bytes read before the swap are served after it].
  - [if] a directory on a remembered row's path becomes unreadable, a symlink loop, or a name too long to open [then] that one row shows no preview and the page still answers; the row reads again once the path is readable [⛔️ if the page fails, or the errored row is remembered].
  - [if] a file or directory is swapped for a symlink to a look-alike outside the share root at the instant the row is being read, and the swap is later undone [then] no request, then or later, shows the outside bytes [⛔️ if a race that was lost is served or remembered].
  - [if] the share root is switched to another library that uses the same vendor path strings [then] the next page shows the other library's rows [⛔️ if a row read under the old root is served].
  - [if] a row's `.2EX` is zero bytes, garbage, truncated, or carries a PVDI header that is not the known one [then] the page answers 200, that row shows the preview of its next source (or none) and `not_analyzed` vocals, and every other row on the page is intact, on the first request and on the next [⛔️ if the page fails, or the log line names the file's path instead of the track's stable id].
  - [if] a vendor path holds a NUL or a character no file name can hold [then] that row has no preview and no cover and the page answers [⛔️ if the page fails].
  - [if] a row takes the by-path read (a doubled slash in its vendor path) [then] it is read from disk on every request and the path-keyed preview and vocals memories are neither read nor filled [⛔️ if anything it read is remembered, or a value already in those memories is served].
  - [if] an analysis file inside the share root is a hard link to a file outside it [then] it is not read, the row is not remembered, and the row's other sources still answer [⛔️ if the outside bytes are served].
  - [if] the lyrics cache path is a file, or the directory cannot be read, or an entry is a symlink [then] `lyrics_available` is false for the rows concerned and the page answers [⛔️ if the page fails, a symlinked entry counts, or the flag lists the cache directory].
- [x] **LIBM-139** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026, second independent review of LIBM-137; narrowed the same day by a third review): A rekordbox share root that became a different directory is trusted again only when its owner asks, and without restarting the engine. The engine refuses to read below a share root that is no longer the directory it first trusted, whatever made it different: a volume unplugged and mounted again at the same path, a directory swapped in by rename, a symlinked share root pointed somewhere else, or a directory ABOVE the share root replaced by a symlink to another tree. A track listing never re-trusts it on its own, because a listing is a read that any page can cause and each of those changes is also what an attack looks like: the page answers 200 with those rows carrying no preview and no cover, and the refusal is logged. `POST /api/v1/library/share-root/reanchor` is the only way back (a deliberate reset): it opens every directory above the share root from the filesystem root without following a symlink, records the identity of the directory it opened under both names the root is reached by (the configured path and its resolved form), empties the row memory, and answers `exists: true`. It answers `exists: false` and changes nothing when the share root is not there. It answers 409, changes nothing, and names the directory in `detail` when a directory above the share root is a symlink; the share root itself may be a symlink, since calling the route is its owner vouching for where it points now. The route has no UI; it is the agent and operator surface.
  - [if] the share root directory is moved away and another real directory is put at the same path [then] every listing page answers 200 with no preview and no cover from it, however many times it is asked, until the re-anchor call; after the call the next page shows the new directory's rows [⛔️ if a listing trusts the new directory on its own, fails the page, or serves a row read under the old directory].
  - [if] the directory above the share root is replaced by a symlink to another tree that holds a directory of the same name [then] the listing serves nothing from it, and the re-anchor call answers 409 with a `detail` that names that directory and says it is a symbolic link, leaving the recorded identity alone [⛔️ if either one serves the other tree, or the call refuses without saying why].
  - [if] `POST /api/v1/library/share-root/reanchor` is called after a symlinked share root was re-pointed [then] it answers 200 with `exists: true`, the next page shows the new target's rows, and reads through the resolved form of the root work too [⛔️ if a symlinked root is trusted without the call, or the call leaves the resolved-form identity stale].
  - [if] `POST /api/v1/library/share-root/reanchor` is called on a platform with no descriptor-anchored walk (Windows) [then] it answers 501 naming why and opens nothing, never a 500 [else stop]

- [x] **LIBM-140** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026, ADR: NEW deletes-stay-deleted): A track the user removed stays removed. `tracks.deleted_reason` (schema v23) is the durable record of that intent: `user` for Remove from library, `missing` for a watched-folder rescan that found the file gone, and a tombstone with no reason (written before v23) reads as `user`. A vendor no longer listing a file is availability, never deletion. Re-running any ingest (rekordbox, folder, Spotify placeholder) does not restore a removed track: the row is left untouched, kept out of every imported playlist, and counted in the ingest summary as `skipped: deleted by user: N`. The only restore of a user removal is the explicit undelete (`POST /api/v1/tracks/{id}:undelete` or `python -m apps.shared.state.cli undelete <stable_id>`), which stamps `tracks.restored_at` (schema v23); a `missing` tombstone is lifted by the ingest that finds the file again. `GET /api/v1/tracks/deleted` and the `deleted` CLI verb list what is removed and why. `StateWriter.upsert_track` raises `TrackRemovedError` on a removed row instead of reactivating it. Same recording under a new path or id: a file whose `content_hash` or `audio_hash` equals a removed track's, with no live row holding that identity, is the same recording and stays removed; different audio bytes are a new track; ISRC alone is not used. Proof: `tests/shared/state/test_deletes_stay_deleted.py`, `tests/shared/state/test_folder_rescan.py`, `tests/webui/test_track_deleted_listing.py`.

### Library Health Lights (HEALTH)

The six dots at the bottom of the browser panel. Each light has one rule for green, every count names its denominator (`present` = audio resolves on this machine right now), and the engine works toward green on its own. Rule text for the dots lives in `apps/webui/frontend/src/lib/rb/library-health-dots.ts`; the server measurement in `apps/webui/server/library_playable.py` and `apps/webui/server/routes/ingest_coverage.py`.

- [x] **HEALTH-01** (verified Sat 3 Oct 2026): The Library health light is green when every track whose audio is expected on THIS machine resolves. Rows on another machine, awaiting an unmounted volume, streaming, or without a path are reported in the hover detail and never make the light amber. Supersedes the LIBM-105 "non-broken" wording for this dot (tree badges keep it).
  - [if] every row this machine recorded as available still resolves [then] the light is green, whatever the count of off-machine rows [else stop]
  - [if] a row lives on another machine [then] the playable predicate counts it off_machine, never broken here [else stop]
  - [if] a file this machine recorded as available no longer resolves [then] the light is amber, the detail counts it as a broken link here, and the playable predicate counts it broken here [else stop]
  - [if] the detail quotes a total [then] it is tracks expected on this machine (present + broken here), named as such, never the raw row count [else stop]
  - The shared hover names the present + broken_here denominator and all four excluded buckets; empty expected sets and failed measurements are grey. Real production API/browser green, owned-missing amber, restored green and stopped-endpoint grey were captured against an immutable 18-file library source; versioned inputs and checksum manifest are in `apps/webui/frontend/tests/unit/fixtures/health01-real-protocol-v1*` (nine focused production-mapper tests pass).
- [x] **HEALTH-02** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026): One playable predicate (`library_playable.scan_playability`) classifies every live row into present / broken_here / off_machine / awaiting_volume / streaming / pathless, and both `GET /reconcile/summary` (`availability`) and `GET /ingest/coverage` (`availability`, `on_disk`) read it.
  - [if] the two endpoints are read against the same library [then] their `availability` blocks are equal and `present == on_disk` [else stop]
  - [if] the buckets do not sum to the live row total [then] the scan raises instead of answering [else stop]
- [x] **HEALTH-03** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026): The coverage endpoint is fast and its lights cannot show a stale or invented verdict. Stem-bundle validation is cached per bundle on (directory mtime, manifest mtime, manifest size); the dots refetch every 60 s and on the `library.changed` event a CloudSync pull publishes; coverage and summary requests time out; an endpoint that cannot answer, or answers with counts that do not add up, renders grey "unknown".
  - [if] coverage is requested twice with no bundle changed [then] no bundle is re-validated on the second request [else stop]
  - [if] a bundle's directory or manifest changes [then] it is re-validated [else stop]
  - [if] the coverage request fails or times out [then] the three coverage lights are grey with the reason, never green, amber or red [else stop]
  - [if] a CloudSync round pulls rows [then] `library.changed` is published; a round that pulls nothing publishes nothing [else stop]
- [x] **HEALTH-04** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026): "Nothing to make" is a recorded, finished state. Per step every present track is exactly one of done / terminal / failed / pending. Lyrics are terminal on an `instrumental` or fresh `no_source` fetch verdict; stems are terminal when the outcome ledger records `no_source` for that audio file or when no stems executor exists on this install; vocals are terminal when their stems are. A light is green when pending and failed are both zero, and the hover detail shows the done / terminal / pending (and failed) counts.
  - [if] a track has no lyrics available [then] it counts as terminal and the lyrics light can reach green [else stop]
  - [if] a track has never been tried [then] it is pending, never terminal [else stop]
  - [if] the audio file is replaced [then] a recorded `no_source` or failure for it no longer applies [else stop]
- [x] **HEALTH-05** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026): The engine drains missing coverage work on its own until the lights are green: one job at a time, vocals from existing stem bundles (CPU) first, then lyrics. Stems are never generated on this machine by the drain; tracks needing the remote farm are reported in the drain status. Parity: `GET /coverage-drain/status`, `POST /coverage-drain/start|stop|retry`, `PUT /coverage-drain/config`, and `python -m apps.webui.coverage_drain_cli status|start|stop|enable|disable|retry`. The setting defaults on (`state/coverage-drain.json`); `MUSIC_DJ_COVERAGE_DRAIN=off` leaves the loop unarmed.

  - [if] a deck is playing, or a track landed on a deck in the last 20 s [then] no job starts [else stop]
  - [if] a user-ordered job is running [then] analysis waits, and vocals and lyrics do not [else stop]
  - [if] an analysis job fails on a track [then] it is retried after 60 s, then 120 s, and never again on the same audio file after the third failure until `retry` is called [else stop]
  - [if] the analysis CLI exits with a code about the machine (no backend, usage, internal error) [then] the analysis step stops until `retry` and no track's attempts are spent [else stop]
  - [if] analysis is pending and the drain owns an analysis job [then] the drain does not report green [else stop]
  - [if] the drain has no analysis job [then] vocals and lyrics behave exactly as HEALTH-05 states [else stop]
- [x] **HEALTH-07** (Thu 1 Oct 2026): Stems coverage knows about bundles evicted to R2. Per present track the state is one of: local (a valid bundle on disk), in cloud (no local bundle, the cached R2 stem index lists it with a manifest, and a hydration source is armed), terminal (HEALTH-09), failed, or pending (needs the farm). Local and in cloud both count as done for the Stems light; `GET /ingest/coverage` adds `local.stems`, `in_cloud.stems`, `awaiting_stem_download` and `stems_index {state, reason}` and the hover reads "N local, N in cloud, N no stems source, N pending of N present tracks". The index is read from its local cache only, memoized on the file's mtime and size (`coverage_cloud`, `stem_index.load_cached_index_memo`). Supersedes: the local-only stems count of HEALTH-03/04, which reported every evicted bundle as needing the farm.
  - [if] a track has no local bundle and the index lists its bundle [then] it counts as done and as in cloud [else stop]
  - [if] a track has no local bundle and is not in the index [then] it is still pending [else stop]
  - [if] the index cache is missing or unreadable, or hydration is configured but not armed [then] `stems_index.state` is `unknown`, nothing counts as in cloud, and the Stems light is grey while any track lacks a local bundle [else stop]
  - [if] the machine has no hydration source at all [then] `stems_index.state` is `off` and a missing bundle is pending, as before [else stop]
  - [if] the coverage response is read [then] `local.stems + in_cloud.stems` equals `done.stems` [else stop]
- [x] **HEALTH-08** (Thu 1 Oct 2026): The drain makes vocals for tracks whose stem bundle is in the cloud by fetching ONE bundle per job (`stem_hydration.hydrate_one`), deriving the vocal-cache entry, and leaving the bundle to normal eviction (`coverage_cloud_vocals`). It holds at most `transient_bundle_cap` fetched bundles (default 2, 0 switches it off, max 16; `PUT /coverage-drain/config {"transient_bundle_cap": n}`, CLI `transient-cap --value n`): before the next fetch it removes its own oldest, only when R2 confirms that bundle byte for byte and no deck has it open. It fetches nothing while the stem cache has less room above the free-disk floor than 256 MiB per transient slot, and nothing for a track whose vocals are valid. Local-stems vocals and lyrics run before any fetch. A hub or network failure pauses cloud vocals for 300 s and spends no attempt.
  - [if] several tracks need a bundle fetched [then] each drain job fetches exactly one [else stop]
  - [if] the drain has fetched `transient_bundle_cap` bundles [then] no more than that many of them are on disk at any time [else stop]
  - [if] the evictor removes every bundle between jobs [then] each bundle is still downloaded exactly once, and the drain goes green [else stop]
  - [if] free disk is under the floor plus headroom [then] no bundle is fetched and the drain status says why [else stop]
  - [if] a track's vocals are valid [then] its bundle is never fetched for vocals [else stop]
  - [if] a fetched bundle is open on a deck, or R2 does not confirm it [then] the drain never removes it [else stop]
- [x] **HEALTH-09** (Thu 1 Oct 2026): "This track can never have stems" is recordable for stems. The drain classifies pending-stems tracks (20 per tick) and records `no_source` when the file is itself a stem (it sits in a directory named `vocals` or `instrumental`, or its file name or title ends in `-vocals`, `_vocals` or ` - vocals`), when ffprobe reads no duration from it, or when it is shorter than 10 s (`coverage_stems_terminal`). A file that cannot be opened, or a host with neither ffprobe nor ffmpeg, is unknown and never terminal. Without ffprobe (the packaged app ships only its bundled LGPL ffmpeg) the same read goes through `ffmpeg -i`, with the same two demuxer refusals as damage (Fri 2 Oct 2026). Parity: `GET`/`POST /coverage-outcomes/stems/no-source`, `DELETE /coverage-outcomes/stems/no-source/{stable_id}`, CLI `no-source-list | no-source-mark --stable-id --reason | no-source-clear --stable-id`. A cleared mark is kept in `state/coverage-stems-keep-pending.json` so the automatic check does not restore it. Concurrent marks and clears are serialized and each writes its own temp file, so none loses another's id. Marked tracks count as finished and show as "no stems source" in the hover.
