  - [if] a marked track later gains a bundle [then] it counts as done and local, not terminal [else stop]
  - [if] the audio file is replaced [then] the mark no longer applies [else stop]
  - [if] the cloud stem index is unknown [then] nothing is classified and nothing is reported as needing the farm [else stop]
  - [if] the duration probe is inconclusive (a timeout, a refused open) [then] a later tick probes the unchanged file again after a backoff that starts at 2 min and doubles to 1 h, a backed-off file is not counted as work and does not hold back later tracks, and a conclusive verdict is not re-probed [else stop]
- [x] **HEALTH-10** (Thu 1 Oct 2026): The drain has a switch per step. `PUT /coverage-drain/config {"steps": {"vocals"|"lyrics"|"analysis": bool}}` and CLI `step-on | step-off --step <name>`; all default on, stored in `state/coverage-drain.json`, and updating one key keeps the others. ### Licence-clean audio tag I/O (TAGIO)

mutagen (GPL-2.0-or-later) is replaced in this Apache-2.0 project: tinytag (MIT) reads every allowlisted container, and in-house ID3v2 / FLAC / MP4 / Ogg writers cover the write paths. ADR: `docs/decisions/ADR-NEW-permissive-audio-tag-io.md`.

- [x] **TAGIO-01** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026): Folder import reads title, artist, album, genre, comment, BPM, key, ISRC and duration from MP3, FLAC, M4A, AIFF, WAV, OGG and Opus files in every build, including the packaged app; tag BPM and key are recorded with `inferred` provenance only where the track has no value yet.
  - [if] an MP3/FLAC/M4A/AIFF/OGG/Opus file carries artist and genre tags [then] the imported row carries them [else stop]
  - [if] the track already has a bpm or key from analysis or an edit [then] a rescan leaves it unchanged [else stop]
  - [if] a file cannot be parsed [then] it is still imported, titled from its filename, and counted in `files_without_tags` [else stop]
- [x] **TAGIO-02** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026): MP3 tag writes (Serato GEOB, unified tags, analysis write-back) go through the in-house `apps.shared.id3v2`, which preserves every frame it did not touch and the audio bytes exactly.

### Control Latency (LATENCY)

Contract for the `/performance`
real-time control surface: which controls must be instantaneous (Class A) versus
deliberately deferred and opt-in (Class B), with hard budgets and a measurement
mandate. LATENCY-01 (Class A), LATENCY-02 (Class B QUANTIZED LAUNCH) and LATENCY-03
(instrumentation) all shipped Sat 12 Sep 2026.

- [x] **LATENCY-01** (shipped Sat 12 Sep 2026): Class A - immediate controls (play/pause, cue and hot cues,
      EQ knobs and kills, filter, stem mutes, channel faders, crossfader) must never
      wait on a network round trip, an IPC hop, or a store refetch. Budget: visual
      feedback <=16ms (one frame at 60Hz, control reflects input on the next frame);
      audible effect <=30ms p99 from input event to audible change. The local
      WebAudio graph is authoritative - apply the change to the AudioContext first,
      then inform the engine asynchronously and reconcile on the next push. Never
      await a response before the audio changes.
  - [if] a transport play or pause is applied [then] `deckStates[deck].playing` is written
    before the first `await` in `_scheduleDeck`, and the play/cue buttons are not
    `disabled` by `pending` [⛔️ if the glyph waits on the worklet ack, or `pending`
    grays the button for a frame].
  - [if] a plain play, pause, cue, or seek is scheduled [then] the launch instant is
    `currentTime + processorLead + TRANSPORT_IMMEDIATE_SAFETY_S` and that margin is
    <= 30ms [⛔️ if `SYNC_SCHEDULE_SAFETY_S` returns to those paths].
  - [if] an EQ, filter, fader, or crossfader change is applied from UI or MIDI with a
    press stamp [then] mixerState is written in the same synchronous turn as the
    AudioParam call, the command is unscoped (`performanceCommandQueueScopes` is
    null), and a mixer-apply or eq-apply ring row carries `press_to_apply_ms`
    [⛔️ if `_execute` or MIDI drops the stamp, or the command waits on a deck
    scope].
  - [if] a stem mute or stem solo is applied with a press stamp [then] it is unscoped,
    `st.stems.controls` updates in the same turn as `setControls`, the chip is not
    `disabled` by deck `pending`, and a `stem-mute-apply` / `stem-solo-apply` row
    carries `press_to_apply_ms` [⛔️ if mute waits behind play/load, or the chip
    blinks grey].
  - [if] a hot-cue pad is triggered with BeatSyncMax off [then] the jump is immediate
    (`planHotCueTrigger` kind `immediate`), `pressT0Ms` reaches `quantizedSeek`,
    and the pads are not `disabled` by deck `pending` [⛔️ if the pad grays out, or
    the jump pays the beat-sync 100ms margin].
  - [if] `press_to_apply_ms` for a stamped mixer Class A apply is compared to
    `ops/quality/baseline.json` `latency.input_to_applied_ms` [then] a 5ms delta
    is under the floor and a 20ms delta is over it [⛔️ if the test hardcodes 16
    instead of reading the JSON, or wiring loss does not fail the quality gate].
  - **PROVISIONAL (the 30ms figure, not the requirement).** The device output
    floor is a CHOICE, not a fixed property of the machine. Measured on this
    Mac, the floor moves between 24.0ms and 48.0ms depending on the
    `latencyHint` passed to the AudioContext. So "what does the hardware
    allow" has no single answer until we pick a hint, and the budget has to be
    read against the hint we choose.
    The most aggressive hint measured a 26.9ms floor. That was REJECTED: it
    leaves 3.1ms of headroom inside a 30ms budget, and a buffer that tight
    risks audible dropouts under load, which is a worse failure than a slightly
    late kick. The rejection is a dropout-risk judgement.
    Recorded explicitly because the earlier reasoning here was wrong: it read
    as "32 > 30, therefore infeasible", as though the floor were fixed and the
    budget simply unreachable. It is not. The budget is reachable at some
    hints and the question is what we are willing to pay for it. Revisit when
    round 2 lands the stretch-processor work, since that changes what headroom
    is actually needed.
- [x] **LATENCY-02** (shipped Sat 12 Sep 2026; deferred-by-decision, evidenced Sat 26 Sep 2026): Class B - deliberately deferred, opt-in by modifier only.
      The feature name is QUANTIZED LAUNCH (also: beat-phase-locked start; Ableton
      calls the general mechanism global quantization) - use that exact name
      consistently. Cmd+Space (and Cmd+click on play) starts playback at the next
      point where this deck's beat 1 aligns with the master deck's beat 1. Deferred
      by design, not slow: it must render a visible armed/waiting state with a
      countdown to the launch point, so a pending launch is never mistaken for a
      hung button. Plain Space / plain play stays Class A: immediate and ungated.
      v2 Instance Link (LINK-01, LINK-04, LINK-09) uses this as the
      primitive that hides remaining WAN RTT for transport start; the session
      clock is the alignment target, not only the local master deck..
  - [if] Cmd+Space or Cmd+click on play starts a paused loaded deck while a playing master has a trusted beatgrid [then] playback is scheduled at the next point where this deck's beat 1 aligns with the master's beat 1, and the play control shows an armed/waiting countdown until that instant [⛔️ if it starts immediately, or the wait looks like a hung button]
  - [if] Space or a plain play click, or a play command with no quantize flag, starts a paused loaded deck [then] playback uses the Class A immediate path, ungated by QUANTIZED LAUNCH [⛔️ if the default play waits for a grid boundary]
  - [if] the AGENT-03 play command carries quantize: true [then] it takes the same QUANTIZED LAUNCH path as Cmd+Space, including the armed countdown in query() [⛔️ if agents can only get immediate play]
  - [if] a QUANTIZED LAUNCH cannot be planned (no playing other-deck master, or either deck lacks a trusted grid) [then] the command refuses with a named error that includes QUANTIZED LAUNCH and the play button does not stay busy [⛔️ if it hangs or silently falls through to immediate play]
- [x] **LATENCY-03** (shipped Sat 12 Sep 2026): Measurement mandate - "instant" must be instrumented, not
      asserted: log input event timestamp vs `AudioContext.currentTime` at the
      applied change, regression test with a hard floor, floor lives in the quality
      ratchet (`ops/quality/baseline.json`). EQ changes may ramp
      (`linearRampToValueAtTime` over ~5-10ms avoids zipper noise) but the ramp
      must start immediately - a ramp is not an excuse for latency. The existing
      `?muted=1` startup master mute silences only the final node before
      destination while the full graph keeps running, so latency can be measured
      on a muted instance without listening.
  - [if] a transport play, pause, cue, or hotcue is applied with a press stamp
    [then] the perf ring row carries `press_to_schedule_ms` against the
    `AudioContext.currentTime` read at schedule [⛔️ if the stamp is dropped
    before `_scheduleDeck` or the delta is taken from a later clock].
  - [if] an EQ change is applied with a press stamp [then] a perf ring row of
    kind `eq-apply` carries `press_to_apply_ms` against the
    `AudioContext.currentTime` read at the AudioParam call [⛔️ if `_execute`
    or MIDI drops the stamp, or setEq still calls `_setParam` with no log].
  - [if] an EQ change is applied [then] the AudioParam ramp starts at
    `AudioContext.currentTime` via `setValueAtTime` plus
    `linearRampToValueAtTime` over `PARAM_SMOOTH_S` (5-10ms)
    [⛔️ if the ramp is delayed, or setTargetAtTime stays on the EQ path].
  - [if] `ops/quality/baseline.json` has no `latency.input_to_applied_ms`, or
    the EQ apply wiring listed in `scripts/quality_latency.py` is gone
    [then] the quality gate fails [⛔️ if the floor is decorative, or
    `--update-baseline` can drop the key].
  - [if] the instance is started with `?muted=1` [then] EQ and transport apply
    logging still run [⛔️ if mute bypasses the graph or skips the instrument].

Focused buttons, range sliders, library rows, and page chrome do not suppress them; Space is consumed outside text entry so the browser scroll default never runs there.

A11Y-02 added Sun 6 Sep 2026: the 'm' comment-pin
hotkey (and every other performance hotkey) silently stopped firing once a
click left focus on WaveRow's waveform-seek canvas, because
`isNativeInteractiveTarget` treated ANY negative `tabindex` as proof the
element owns no keyboard behavior. That is wrong in general - a negative
tabindex only means "not Tab-reachable", not "keyboard-inert" - so an early
fix attempt that keyed the exception off tabindex sign alone was caught
before merge: it would have swallowed real keystrokes on
any programmatically-focused input, button, contenteditable node, or
roving-tabindex ARIA widget carrying `tabindex="-1"`. A11Y-02 records the
corrected, narrower contract that shipped instead.

- [x] **PERF-PAINT-01** (shipped Sat 5 Sep 2026): Waveform rows cache the immutable band image by waveform, zoom, width, height, and palette, then translate that image under the fixed playhead. A row repaints only after a one-CSS-pixel scroll or a visual input change; inactive, unhovered rows schedule no rAF. `tests/live/wave-row-raf-attribution.mjs` wraps `requestAnimationFrame` before loading a real performance page and rejects four playing rows whose 3s callback share reaches 15% of the main thread.
  - [if] one deck plays and the playhead moves less than one CSS pixel [then] no band rescan happens that frame [⛔️ if the band cache rebuilds before one CSS pixel of scroll].
  - [if] four decks play [then] the WaveRow rAF callback share over three seconds is below 15% of the main thread [⛔️ if `pnpm test:live:wave-raf` reports 15% or more].

- [x] **PERF-STEMDEC-01** (shipped Thu 10 Sep 2026, issue Q18 rung 1): A stemmed deck decodes its FLAC parts in real Web Workers on the engine where that is faster, chosen by measurement rather than by engine name. The first two stemmed loads of a session each run one whole lane uncontended - main thread first, since that is what ships - normalized to encoded bytes per wall millisecond, and the faster lane holds for the session. Every part that does not take the worker path reports WHY on the `deck-stems` ring row (`stem_decode`, `stem_decode_workers`, `stem_decode_lane`, `stem_decode_refused`), so a load that lost its speed-up says so instead of reading as a slow machine. A decode the decoder itself reported errors on is refused and its worker destroyed; a decode refused for the BUNDLE's shape leaves a healthy worker parked.
  - [if] a stemmed deck loads FLAC parts on an engine whose measurement chose the workers [then] every part reports `viaWorker` with no refusal [⛔️ if the ring row says `main-thread` on an engine that measured workers faster].
  - [if] the decoded sample rate differs from the audio context's [then] the part falls back to `decodeAudioData` with `sample-rate-mismatch` and no buffer is built at the wrong rate [⛔️ if a buffer right in samples and wrong in seconds is published].
  - [if] the parts are not FLAC [then] each reports `not-flac` and the deck still loads [⛔️ if a v3 bundle in another codec fails a deck load].
  - [if] `decodeFile` resolves with a nonempty `errors` array [then] the part is refused as `decode-failed`, the worker is destroyed rather than pooled, and `decodeAudioData` supplies the audio [⛔️ if partial frames from a damaged stream are published as the stem].
  - [if] a decoder rejects while becoming ready or while resetting [then] it is freed before the failure propagates [⛔️ if a worker thread and a wasm heap are stranded per failed load].
  - [if] a second stemmed load overlaps a calibration load [then] neither is recorded as a lane trial and the overlapping load reports `awaiting-calibration` [⛔️ if a contended timing settles the session lane].
  - [if] the bundle in a would-be calibration load is not FLAC [then] the trial slot is not claimed and no main-thread throughput is recorded [⛔️ if a FLAC lane is settled from another codec's number].
  - [if] the `decodeAudioData` fallback rejects after a worker refusal [then] the media error it raised is what the deck load reports [⛔️ if a retry of the same fallback on the buffer it already detached replaces the real cause].
  - [if] a part's STREAMINFO discloses a sample rate the audio context does not run [then] no worker is taken for that part and it is decoded once, natively, reporting `sample-rate-mismatch` [⛔️ if every part is decoded twice, once in a worker that is thrown away and once through the fallback].
  - [if] a rate mismatch surfaces only after a worker decode, because the header did not disclose the rate [then] the session settles on the main-thread lane [⛔️ if every later stem load repeats the discarded worker decode because the refused trial never settles a verdict].
  - [if] the worker lane's calibration trial is the load that first builds the decoder pool [then] the workers are spawned and their wasm compiled BEFORE the trial's clock starts [⛔️ if a one-time cold start that no later load pays settles the session on the slower lane].

- [x] **PERF-STEMDEC-04** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026, rounds 0 to 2 of `ops/perf/stem-decode-under-playback-round-N/report.md`): While any deck is audible, a stem bundle's parts decode at most `STEM_DECODE_WIDTH_WHILE_PLAYING` = 2 at a time; on a silent rig they decode all at once, as before. The width is read again before each part starts, so a transport change mid-bundle applies to the parts not yet started. Measured with a deck playing on a loaded host: four at once made the audio callback late 0.47 times per bundle against 0.13 two at once and 0.14 one at a time (36 interleaved decodes, host background 0.107 per second), and two at once decodes in about the time four does. Local bundles reach stems ready in 1.8 s (mp3) and 2.4 s (FLAC) median, worst 3.1 s, with a deck playing. Zero late callbacks across 5 runs is NOT achieved and is not measurable on a host that is late every 10 s when idle; the remaining stem-attributable cost was the 0.31 per bundle measured in the bench's create segment. Amended Thu 1 Oct 2026 (round 3): that segment was first read as WebAssembly instantiation on the audio thread, and that reading was wrong; creating four processors with no PCM measured 0 late callbacks in 30 bundles, and the cost is the main-thread PCM copy that follows creation (see PERF-STEMDEC-05).

  - [if] no deck is audible [then] every part starts at once and the load is labelled `decode_width=4` [⛔️ if a silent rig decodes narrower, which slows the control load].

- [x] **PERF-STEMDEC-05** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026, round 3 of `ops/perf/stem-decode-under-playback-round-N/report.md`): A decoded stem part is handed to its stretch processor by transferring the AudioBuffer's own channel storage, not by copying it on the main thread, on engines where a runtime probe shows the storage really moves; anywhere else, and for any buffer whose channels are not whole unshared buffers, the part is copied as before. The deck mix always copies, because the mix AudioBuffer is still read after the load. The stem load's perf event carries `pcm_handoff=transfer` or `pcm_handoff=copy`, so a log shows which path a load took. Measured with a deck playing, built-in Chromium 152, 70 interleaved bundles under host load: copying made the audio callback late in 14 of 70 bundles (20 late callbacks, worst gap 41 ms), transferring in 3 of 70 (6, worst 13 ms), against 2 of 140 idle windows; stem processor creation dropped from roughly 70 to 150 ms to 16 to 42 ms per bundle. Not measured on WKWebView: the probe decides there at runtime and the copy path is the fallback. Audio continuity at the live handoff was not listened to.
  - [if] the engine moves channel storage and a stem part's channels are whole unshared buffers [then] the worklet receives the same storage, the AudioBuffer is left detached and the load is labelled `pcm_handoff=transfer` [⛔️ if the part is copied, or if a transfer is reported while a copy was made].
  - [if] the probe finds the storage does not move, a channel is a view into a larger or shared buffer, or two channels share one buffer [then] every channel is copied and the load is labelled `pcm_handoff=copy` [⛔️ if a partial transfer leaves some channels detached and others copied, or if the load throws].
  - [if] the deck mix is loaded [then] it is copied and its AudioBuffer stays readable [⛔️ if the mix buffer is detached].
  - [if] a load is narrowed at any point [then] it is not a lane trial and records no lane measurement [⛔️ if the workers-versus-main verdict is settled on a narrowed load's wall time].
  - [if] one part fails to decode [then] the parts after it still decode and the failure is reported [⛔️ if a failure stalls the queue].

- [x] **PERF-DIAG-01** (shipped Sat 5 Sep 2026, hardened Sun 6 Sep 2026, narrowed Sun 6 Sep 2026): The installed diagnostics probe reads its existing JSONL with `trend --since <ISO>`, reports per-process footprint slope, deck-load-normalized footprint, orphan count and engine RSS, and returns RED with a nonzero exit when retained unload footprint, orphaning, or growth crosses an explicit threshold. The 30-minute sufficiency floor gates only the slope-derived RED signal - a window shorter than 30 minutes cannot extrapolate a growth rate, so a steep slope alone reports UNKNOWN with exit 0 and stays an observation rather than a finding - but a suspected orphan or a failed unload check is a direct observation rather than an extrapolation, so either still returns RED regardless of window length, with any steep slope in that same sub-floor window reported alongside as an observation explicitly not counted toward the verdict. The player records all four initially-empty decks in the perf ring, so the first four-deck load/unload cycle has a measured baseline. Deck-load-normalized footprint covers only samples with at least one loaded deck, and counts the zero-deck samples it omitted rather than dividing them by a substituted denominator of one. A RED trend POSTs into the engine client-error log and exits 3, separately from RED's own exit 1, when that POST cannot be written, naming the error. `--pid` and `--match` select a Chrome renderer or dev engine process family for SAMPLING; trend reads process rows already written to JSONL, so it refuses `--pid`, `--match`, `--shell-pid`, `--bundle-id` and `--summary` instead of accepting and ignoring them, and `--since` is refused outside trend mode.
  - [if] 30 minutes of samples exist [then] trend prints every PID's slope and a GREEN, AMBER, or RED verdict [⛔️ if RED exits zero].
  - [if] fewer than 30 minutes of samples exist [then] trend reports UNKNOWN naming the shortfall and exits 0, even when a two-sample slope crosses the RED threshold [⛔️ if it reports RED from a sub-floor window].
  - [if] four decks load and then all unload [then] footprint returns within 256 MB of the post-boot baseline [⛔️ if the verdict names retained delta].
  - [if] a process previously associated with the app outlives its shell [then] the next sample lists it as an orphan [⛔️ if the orphan count stays zero].
  - [if] a sample records zero loaded decks [then] it is absent from the deck-load-normalized series and counted in `deck_load_normalized_excluded_zero_deck_samples` [⛔️ if its whole-app footprint appears as a per-deck value].
  - [if] a RED trend's client-error POST is refused or answered with anything but 202 [then] the command prints the error against `client_error_posted` and exits 3 [⛔️ if it exits 1 with no explanation of the missing record].
  - [if] the engine answers the identity check or the client-error POST slower than the old 1.5 s but inside `TREND_REPORT_BUDGET_SECONDS` (30 s, one wall-clock budget for both) [then] the report succeeds and the engine holds exactly ONE row for it [⛔️ if a loaded host loses its RED trend, or a retry records it twice: the engine does not dedupe on `client_event_id`, and a CI run once timed out on a POST the engine had already written].
  - [if] the engine never finishes a reply, silent or one byte at a time [then] the command stops waiting at the budget, prints how long it waited and how many attempts it made (`TREND_REPORT_ATTEMPTS`, 1), says for a sent POST that the engine may still record it, and exits 3 [⛔️ if the wait is unbounded, or the POST is sent a second time].
  - [if] nothing listens on the engine port [then] the command still fails on the refused connection, in seconds, with exit 3 [⛔️ if a stopped engine costs the caller the whole budget].
  - [if] `trend` is given `--summary`, `--pid`, `--match`, `--shell-pid` or `--bundle-id` [then] the command exits with a usage error naming the argument [⛔️ if it prints a summary, or a verdict computed over processes the caller did not select].

      a reading whose threshold depends on cache state is tagged `cold` or
      `warm` in its note. S12 records hello/push/pull, the spoke's local

      through `apps.sync_hub.sync_timing.PhaseTimer` with the library track
      count as denominator.

### CloudSync Runtime (CLOUDSYNC)

Recorded Sun 13 Sep 2026: best-practice sync must parallelize when
the machine is idle, back off under CPU/RAM pressure, and never run during
Gig / a playing deck unless the DJ clicks Force sync. Faster is better unless
it affects the audible or visible experience. Default disk budget versus
on-demand fetch must share one believed-state with `sync_policies`,
`track_locations`, and `jobs.db`. Battle-tested engine replacement, Turso
revisit, and R2/CDN edge streaming as a first-class playback option are
CLOUDSYNC-11..13 (v2).

Live gaps verified Sun 13 Sep 2026:
`apps/sync_hub/scheduler.py` documents that it does not pause for a playing
deck; PERFMODE-04's shed controller is armed with `jobs: []`;
`resolve_playback_source` / `apply_policy_after_produce` / `evict_cache` are
reached only from tests; hydration is not
a `jobs.db` kind (chassis ships zero kinds until registered; stems and setup
import are the production kinds today); `transfer_status` is process-local
ephemeral progress, not durable presence.

- [x] **CLOUDSYNC-14** (shipped in stages: gating plus the force override on HTTP/CLI/UI, shipped across several PRs; the CLI's own `deck_playing` visibility -- it always passed `ui_mirror=None` before this -- was fixed, which also added the `engine_mirror_unreachable` defer reason for an inconclusive live-engine probe; a later review round found the mirror probe itself still fail-open on a non-loopback `ConnectError` and a stale-but-200 mirror body (both closed the same day, see `apps.sync_hub.maintenance._refused_by_loopback_engine` / `_ui_mirror_is_fresh`), and found `python -m apps.sync_hub sync` did not actually share single-flight protection with the scheduler/HTTP route across processes despite this requirement's own acceptance line below claiming it did -- closed the same day with `apps.sync_hub.single_flight.sync_flock_for`, a cross-process `fcntl.flock` (the same pattern `apps.engine_core.lock.EngineLock` uses) that `apps.sync_hub.maintenance.sync` now holds around `client.run_sync`, reached by the scheduler, the HTTP route, AND the CLI since all three funnel through that one function; parts 3-5 -- PERFMODE-04 pressure defer, hydration parallelism, `resolve_playback_source` wiring -- listed PARTIAL here Mon 14 Sep 2026, were carved off to CLOUDSYNC-09 and CLOUDSYNC-10 (both shipped) rather than remaining under this id; flipped Thu 24 Sep 2026): oDJ does not auto-sync metadata or hydrate/evict
      assets during Gig or while any deck is playing, unless the DJ clicks
      Force sync. User-facing copy: `Force sync (oDJ won't sync during
      performance unless this is clicked)`. The scheduler
      (`apps.sync_hub.scheduler`) skips the round; `POST /api/v1/cloudsync/sync`
      and `python -m apps.sync_hub sync` without `--force` refuse with a named
      reason (`CLOUDSYNC_SYNC_DEFERRED` with `gig_posture`, `deck_playing`, or, CLI-only,
      `engine_mirror_unreachable` when a live engine's own mirror cannot be read conclusively);
      `--force` / `{ "force": true }` is the only override of the Gig/deck-playing
      gate, and never overrides single-flight: every caller (scheduler, HTTP route,
      and the CLI's own separate process) shares protection against a second
      concurrent round via the pre-existing in-process lock (`apps.sync_hub.
      single_flight.sync_lock_for`, scheduler + HTTP route only) layered with a
      cross-process flock (`sync_flock_for`, all three) that `maintenance.sync`
      holds for the duration of `client.run_sync`. Prep with every deck stopped
      runs as today. Mixxx/Ableton rule: no sync I/O or SQLite write burst on the
      audio/presentation path.

- [x] **CLOUDSYNC-15** (shipped Mon 14 Sep 2026, fixing an ERROR-log flood):
      A set of rows held back from the sync set is reported at ERROR ONCE PER
      PROCESS, grouped by table and cause with a count and example pks, not
      once per row or per held parent on every scheduler tick. Children held
      only because their parent is held share one group per parent table
      (`sync_set.hold_group`); every other reason, including an offending
      stored value, is its own group. A group reports again when its
      membership changes (a newly held parent, a swapped one) or when it is
      released and returns; each pass that held anything writes one INFO
      summary line with the total. The inconclusive-digest ERROR in
      `client._settle_digest` follows the same rule per hub and digest pair.
      Measured on a snapshot of a real library's `state.db`: tens of
      thousands of ERROR lines logged per tick before the fix, a handful on
      the first tick after, and none on every tick thereafter.
  - [if] 60 identical sync ticks hold the same rows [then] exactly one ERROR
        per group is logged [⛔️ if every tick logs again]
  - [if] a new parent is held, or one held parent is swapped for another
        [then] that group logs at ERROR again [⛔️ if the change is silent]
  - [if] a held set is released and later returns [then] it logs again
        [⛔️ if it stays remembered as reported]

      concurrent GET/Range fetches up to a named cap). Under
      `KERNEL_ELEVATED_LEVEL=2` or `PRESSURE_CHURN_EARLY_WARNING=500` or
      session xruns > 0, concurrency falls to 1 and non-forced rounds defer
      rather than drop. Class A controls and track-select never wait on a
      sync lock. The audio/presentation thread never does HTTP or SQLite
      sync writes.

  - [if] pressure and xruns are clear and posture is Prep [then] a metadata

  - [if] a sync or hydration lock is held [then] Class A mixer/hot-cue

### Library-Processing Wait Time (PERFBATCH)

Directive Tue 1 Sep 2026.

User wait-time for processing their library (stems generation, lyrics
fetch/align) is a PERFORMANCE surface: track it in the perf program alongside
interactive latency. HARD GATE on all of it: quality first.

- [x] **PERFBATCH-01** (shipped Fri 11 Sep 2026): Stems and lyrics pipeline wait-time KPIs (per-track wall time, queue throughput, end-to-end library ETA) tracked in the perf KPI ledger and register, with honest denominators (present-audio rows only). Capture via ``just perf-library-wait`` / ``python -m scripts.perf.library_wait``.
- [x] **PERFBATCH-02** (shipped Fri 11 Sep 2026): DO-NOT-TOUCH rule: no optimization lands in either pipeline while it is still actively processing the user's library (both are up as of Tue 1 Sep 2026). Observation/measurement only until the runs complete. Enforced by ``python -m scripts.perf.perfbatch_gate`` and ``.github/workflows/perfbatch-gate.yml`` (missing jobs.db / farm-logs / state.db is LIVE).
- [x] **PERFBATCH-03** (shipped Fri 11 Sep 2026): Quality-loss guard: any throughput/latency change to stems or lyrics processing REQUIRES (a) requirements solidified first, (b) a locked quality signal per the quality-signal-calibration rule (stems precedent: the -dB measure calibrated against the user's taste, J01 0.2 dB SI-SDR bar in ``scripts/bench/judgement-calibration.json``), and (c) before/after on the same scorer+fixtures showing no quality regression. Speed wins that cost quality are refused (precedent set earlier). Enforced by the same gate's ``perfbatch-03: quality-ok reqs= signal= before_after=`` marker.
- [x] **PERFBATCH-04** (shipped Fri 11 Sep 2026): On-device stems executor behind the same ``stems.separate`` job contract as the farm, selected by CloudSync policy (local-only -> ``scripts/stems_local_worker.py`` + ``stem_bundle_worker`` PEP 723); PERFMODE tier floor + ``local_stems.executor`` feature flag gate with explicit tooltip; farm path unchanged when remote processing is allowed.
- [x] **PERFBATCH-05** (shipped Fri 11 Sep 2026): User-ordered stems and lyrics jobs from the library. Enqueue from selection at the head of a persistent per-lane queue, reorder, cancel, and live status.
  - [if] the user selects N tracks and chooses "Stems: do next" [then] N stems jobs exist at the head of the stems lane in selection order; the queue API returns them in that order; nothing already running is interrupted
  - [if] the user does the same for "Lyrics: do next" [then] lyrics jobs are enqueued the same way; stems and lyrics are separate lanes and one never blocks the other
  - [if] a track already has a fresh stem bundle (or lyrics cache) [then] the job is a no-op reported as skipped: up to date, not re-run and not silently dropped
  - [if] the user drags (or API PATCHes) a queued job to a new position [then] the queue order changes and the next dispatch honours it
  - [if] the user cancels a queued job [then] it leaves the queue; cancelling a RUNNING job stops it at the next safe point and reports cancelled
  - [if] the daemon restarts [then] queued order survives; running jobs resume or restart per the queue's lease rules
  - [if] any job changes state [then] the in-app status (bottom ribbon or job panel) updates without reload, and the per-track LHS status column reflects it
  - [if] the INSTALLED app (the packaged engine, `apps.engine_core.app.create_app`) boots with `MUSIC_DJ_LIBRARY_JOBS` unset [then] the drain thread `webui.library-jobs` runs and claims queued jobs; an invalid value refuses to boot (status Mon 14 Sep 2026: before this, only the standalone webui daemon armed the drain, so every job queued in the installed app stayed pending forever)
  - [if] the UI can do it [then] the same is possible over HTTP and the CLI; missing endpoints fail the PR
- [x] **PERFBATCH-06** (shipped Sat 12 Sep 2026): Design-time performance envelope for unbuilt live stems (realtime on-device generation during playback, not the PERFBATCH-04 local batch executor). CPU/RAM budgets, PERFMODE-04 shed-list position, PERFMODE-01 x LATENCY-04 tier gating, and PERFBATCH-03-style quality rules are locked in the live-stems performance envelope. Implementation remains blocked until that document plus a quality-ok citation exist.
  - [if] a live-stems generator PR is opened [then] it cites the live-stems performance envelope and a perfbatch-03 quality-ok marker with reqs=PERFBATCH-06
    [⛔️ if live-generation ships without the envelope or without a locked quality signal].
  - [if] PERFMODE-01 resolved tier is LOW or LATENCY-04 quality is disabled [then] live stems are not offered
    [⛔️ if the feature appears and only fails mid-set].
  - [if] live-generation runs [then] its working set stays at or under 512 MiB (low) or 1024 MiB (high), uses only LATENCY-04 lookahead windows, and is visible to the memory meter
    [⛔️ if it retains whole-track PCM or hides RSS].

### Desktop Install (INSTALL)

Packaging and first-run contract for the Tauri desktop shell.

- [x] **INSTALL-01**: The desktop shell MUST render a setup screen naming the engine address, the failure and the fix whenever the engine is unreachable at startup; a blank window, an indefinite spinner or fabricated data is a defect.
- [x] **INSTALL-02**: The shell MUST NOT depend on the engine-served SPA for any state in which the engine is unreachable.
- [x] **INSTALL-03**: `just dmg` MUST verify the artifact it produced (mount, structure, bundle identifier) and MUST NOT report a stale artifact as fresh.
- [x] **INSTALL-04**: macOS signing identity and notarization profile MUST come from `.env` and MUST NEVER be committed; a resolvable-identity failure MUST fail the build rather than degrade to unsigned; `just dmg` MUST notarize and staple the source `.app` before rebuilding its dmg and updater archive, then notarize and staple the dmg, and MUST validate staples on the mounted dmg app and extracted updater app before publication.
- [x] **INSTALL-05**: Desktop artifacts MUST state architecture (arm64 only for v1) wherever they are described.
- [x] **INSTALL-06**: Per-lane bundle identifier and productName MUST derive from `MDT_LANE_LABEL`; an unsafe label MUST be refused, not sanitised.

INSTALL-07..13 turned the shell from a window onto somebody else's engine into
an app that boots its own. The bar they encode is a single sentence: the
artifact must run on a Mac with no repo and no developer toolchain, and must
be able to say what it is.

- [x] **INSTALL-07**: Every artifact MUST state its own build identity (git sha, branch, dirty flag, build timestamp, lane) at runtime over `GET /api/v1/build-info` and on the main UI surface; a build whose identity is unreadable MUST render a visible fault, never a blank or a default. A git checkout without a payload manifest MUST also carry `app_version` from `tauri.conf.json`, the semver the updater compares.
  - [if] no payload manifest is set and the engine runs from a git checkout [then] `/api/v1/build-info` carries `app_version` from `tauri.conf.json`, [else stop]
  - [if] a git checkout cannot read that version [then] build-info refuses with a named fault, [else stop]
  - [if] the engine runs from a git checkout and the update channel cannot be read [then] `/api/v1/update/check` answers HTTP 200 with a named fault status, [else stop]
  - [if] the engine runs from an installed payload and the update channel cannot be read [then] `/api/v1/update/check` answers HTTP 502 with a named fault status, [else stop]
  - [if] the update channel reports `same_version_different_build` true [then] the build chip's label is plain, non-warning wording and `prominent` is false, with the full explanation kept in the hover title, [else stop]
- [x] **INSTALL-08**: The payload builder MUST refuse a missing or stale SPA build and MUST NEVER rebuild the frontend silently.
- [x] **INSTALL-09**: The shipped payload MUST carry exactly one `SignalsmithStretch.*.mjs` worklet asset and the bundled engine MUST serve it as immutable JavaScript.
- [x] **INSTALL-10**: No Mach-O file in the payload may link a path outside the bundle, `/usr/lib` and `/System`; a `/opt/homebrew` or `/usr/local` reference MUST fail the build.
- [x] **INSTALL-11**: Every `ctypes` runtime library load reachable in the payload MUST be classified as bundled, OS-provided or provably unreachable, with the reason recorded in the manifest; an unclassified site MUST fail the build. A line-keyed classification whose file ships but whose line no longer holds a load site MUST fail the build too (stale), so a dependency bump that moves a site cannot leave its reason attached to other code.
- [x] **INSTALL-12**: The payload MUST install the LOCKED dependency closure, and excluding a dependency MUST also drop the packages that existed only to serve it.
  - [if] the payload build never requests an optional `[extras]` group [then] the omission is recorded in `OMITTED_OPTIONAL_EXTRAS` with its reason, and the build fails loudly if that package ever appears in the locked export anyway (a stray direct dependency, an extra requested elsewhere without updating the record) [⛔️ if a listed extra ships silently different from what this record claims]. Added Wed 2 Sep 2026: the omission itself is a licensing decision for a human, not this build's to make silently. The `[tags]` extra (mutagen) was removed Sat 3 Oct 2026 (ADR-0122): GPL, removed for Apache-2.0 release. Tag reads, embedded artwork included, use the shipped `tinytag` reader.
- [x] **INSTALL-13**: The installed app MUST default to its own Application Support data directory, MUST NEVER read the repo `data/` or a real rekordbox library, and MUST actively unset `MDT_REKORDBOX_WRITEBACK_ENABLED` before spawning the engine.
- [x] **INSTALL-14**: The desktop shell MUST start the bundled engine itself on an OS-assigned free loopback port, MUST NOT bake any default engine origin, MUST raise a native error dialog instead of opening a window when the engine does not become healthy within the boot timeout, and MUST kill the engine's whole process group on exit.

INSTALL-15 is the placement and content contract for the readout INSTALL-07
requires. INSTALL-07 says the identity must exist and must never fake an
answer; this one says where it sits, what it carries and how it opens, because
the first version satisfied INSTALL-07 while floating on top of the sidebar and
while still leaving a tester unable to find the app's own address.

- [x] **INSTALL-15**: The build identity chip MUST be an ordinary member of the
      bottom tray of whichever surface is on screen, at the BOTTOM-RIGHT of that
      tray, overlapping no other control; it MUST NOT be a fixed-position overlay
      floating above the app. Exactly one instance is on screen at a time (the app
      shell's tray, or the browser panel's bottom bar on /performance).
  - CONTENT. The compact line carries lane, short sha, dirty marker and
    built-at. Clicking it opens a foldout carrying, for both engine and shell:
    product name, bundle identifier, app version, full sha, branch, dirty flag
    and built-at in local time AND UTC, plus THIS APP'S ENGINE BASE URL.
  - PLACEMENT is load-bearing, not cosmetic: a permanent readout that covers
    other controls trades one defect for another.
  - BEHAVIOR. Click to fold out, click to fold away. The foldout opens UPWARD
    and is anchored to the tray's right edge, so it never resizes the tray row
    and never runs off the window.
  - ENGINE URL. The address MUST be derived at runtime (the page's own origin
    when the engine served it; the configured API base in a dev build), MUST be
    rendered as selectable text with a copy control, and MUST render a NAMED
    FAULT rather than a plausible-looking address when neither source is
    available. Rationale: the packaged engine binds an EPHEMERAL port, so the
    app's URL differs every launch and is written down nowhere. A tester who
    wanted to open the app in a browser guessed the dev port and reached
    nothing. Printing a guessed `127.0.0.1:8585` would reproduce exactly that
    failure with more confidence.

    names the Chrome dev loop in a browser, or the DMG app version in the
    packaged shell, while the existing engine-shell drift warning still fires
    when their commits disagree [⛔️ if the reader cannot tell which surface
    produced the stamp].

- [x] **INSTALL-21** (Mon 14 Sep 2026; capability grant and observability fixed Tue 15 Sep 2026): Cmd-Q asks before quitting. The Tauri shell intercepts the close and quit requests (`CloseRequested` and the app menu Quit) and shows an in-app dialog titled "QUIT: are you sure?" with a small dim helper line "cmd q again or enter to confirm" and two buttons, Cancel and Confirm. A second Cmd-Q or Enter confirms; Escape or Cancel dismisses. The dialog is skipped when no deck has a track loaded and nothing is playing, and it is never skipped while any deck is playing. The ship flow's clean quit (OPS-07) uses the engine's quit endpoint and is not blocked by the dialog. Confirming Cmd-Q and the ship-flow quit share one code path (`confirmQuit()` in `quit-gate.ts`) that calls the Tauri process plugin's `exit()`, which requires `process:allow-exit` granted to the main window's loopback remote origin (`capabilities/updater.json`) -- without it the ACL silently refuses the call and neither path actually quits. A failed exit is reported through the client-error pipeline under the `unhandled-rejection` kind with `source: quit-gate` rather than surfacing only as a generic uncaught-promise accident.

  - [if] Escape or Cancel [then] the dialog closes and focus returns to where it was.
  - [if] no deck is loaded and nothing plays [then] Cmd-Q quits immediately.

One missed health check on an engine whose pid is alive MUST NOT count as a death: the supervisor restarts only after `UNRESPONSIVE_AFTER_MISSES` consecutive misses, logs that as `engine-unresponsive(...)` rather than an exit code, and never blocks waiting on a live child. The quit path MUST NOT wait on the supervisor lock for more than `SHUTDOWN_LOCK_WAIT`; past that it stops the engine's process group without it. The engine's SIGTERM grace (`SHUTDOWN_GRACE`) MUST cover its own worst-case shutdown (uvicorn's bounded graceful window, the refresh job's CLIs being stopped with their descendants, and the job runner settling jobs still forking and then reaping its worker groups), and analysis pool workers MUST exit when the process that started them is gone. Only a platform quit (Cmd-Q, the Dock, an Apple Event) is held for the INSTALL-21 quit gate; the gate's own confirmed `exit()` MUST be let through, or `POST /api/v1/lifecycle/quit` returns 200 while the app keeps running. Before this, a single missed health check put up the fatal page over a serving engine, the reap then waited forever on it while holding the lock, every quit (Cmd-Q, AppleScript, `lifecycle/quit`) hung behind it, and the analysis workers left behind blocked the DMG installer.

- [x] **ELECTRON-06** (shipped this PR): Chromium grants `midi`, `midiSysex`, `media` and `speaker-selection` to loopback pages only, which gives the UI Web MIDI and `setSinkId` output choice that WKWebView lacks. Web MIDI in the page is a stopgap: MIDI moves into the Rust audio engine, and the shell adds no MIDI path of its own.

  - [if] the payload has no audio engine but the launching terminal set `ODJ_AUDIO_BIN` [then] the engine sees it unset ⛔️

### First-Run Setup (SETUP)

First-run contract for the /setup wizard. SETUP-01..04 are numbered in the
order given.

- [x] **SETUP-01**: A fresh install reaches a populated library without a terminal: /setup detects rekordbox, imports as a job, and streams progress over the WS bus.
- [x] **SETUP-02**: Every wizard step has an HTTP endpoint an agent can drive in the same order with the same refusals.
- [x] **SETUP-03**: A tester with no rekordbox can point at a folder; the result is honestly labelled unanalysed (no BPM/key/beatgrid written or guessed).
  - [if] `apps.shared.state.ingest.folder` is imported in a clean process [then] `pyrekordbox` is absent from `sys.modules` [⛔️ if the no-rekordbox path loads Rekordbox code].
  - [if] the setup folder-import worker starts [then] it emits `detect: preparing folder import`, then one `detect: loading ...` line before each deferred import, `detect: probing N folder(s)` before the filesystem probe, and `detect: checking N folder(s)` after that probe [⛔️ if a stall in that window cannot name the import or the probe it is inside].
- [x] **SETUP-04**: A folder macOS has blocked never reads as an empty one: denied is distinct from readable, and no count is quoted for a denied root.
- [x] **SETUP-16**: Folder import rejects corrupt, truncated, empty and non-audio payloads before they become library rows, and reports them separately from untagged-but-valid files.
  - [if] a folder contains zero-byte, header-only, truncated, prose-in-.wav, riff-garbage or corrupt-container fixtures alongside a valid control wav [then] only the control becomes a track row [⛔️ if any corrupt file imports].
  - [if] corrupt files are skipped [then] the import report exposes `files_rejected_unplayable` distinct from `files_without_tags` [⛔️ if callers cannot tell valid untagged from rejected].
  - [if] mutagen is absent or present [then] the same corrupt fixtures are still rejected [⛔️ if fabricated metadata lets a corrupt file through].
- [x] **SETUP-08**: Folder import refuses the filesystem root before queuing a job, so a folder-picker mis-click cannot start an unbounded whole-disk walk.
  - [if] `POST /api/v1/setup/import/folder` receives `/`, or an absolute path resolving to `/`, as a folder root [then] it returns a clean 400 before enqueueing [⛔️ if the detect worker begins traversing the filesystem].
- [x] **SETUP-09**: The folder-import path field renders its placeholder as a dim italic hint while typed text stays normal and full-contrast.
  - [if] the folder input is empty and unfocused [then] the placeholder renders dimmer and italic via `.folder-form input::placeholder` [else stop].
  - [if] the user types any character into the folder input [then] the typed text renders at full contrast, non-italic [else stop].
  - [if] an empty field screenshot is compared to the same field with `/Users/you/Music` typed [then] the two are visibly distinguishable [else stop].
- [x] **SETUP-10**: The first-run folder-import step offers a native directory picker in the desktop shell and keeps manual path entry as the browser fallback.
  - [if] a user is on the folder-import step in the Open DJ desktop shell [then] a folder icon beside the path field opens the OS-native directory picker [⛔️ if the user must type or paste an absolute path by hand].
  - [if] the user selects a folder in the native picker [then] the path field is populated with the chosen absolute path [⛔️ if manual typing is still required].
  - [if] the same step is opened in a browser tab against the dev server [then] the text input remains editable and no Tauri dialog import is attempted [⛔️ if the page throws or the field is unusable].
- [x] **SETUP-11**: The folder step offers the user's own existing music folders as one-click suggestions via `GET /api/v1/setup/detect/music-folders`, never fabricating a path that does not exist on disk, and never hiding a folder macOS has denied access to.
  - [if] `GET /api/v1/setup/detect/music-folders` runs on a machine where only `~/Music` exists among the candidate list [then] only that path is returned [⛔️ if a nonexistent candidate path appears in the response].
  - [if] a candidate folder exists but macOS refuses to list it [then] it is still returned with `readable=false`, `denied=true`, and a non-empty `detail` [⛔️ if denied candidates are silently omitted].
  - [if] the operator clicks a readable suggestion chip [then] the path is filled and `GET /api/v1/setup/detect/folder` runs for that path [⛔️ if the chip only fills the field without scanning].
- [x] **SETUP-13**: The folder step's folder-picker affordance is never a fake or dead click. Where the native picker is unavailable (browser context, or a shell that does not provide one), the control is visibly disabled with a tooltip stating why, rather than present-but-inert.
  - [if] the folder step renders the path input [then] a folder icon button sits beside it [⛔️ if there is no visible picker affordance].
  - [if] the operator is in a browser context or shell without a native picker [then] the folder icon is visibly disabled and its tooltip explains the unavailable native-picker context and the working manual-path alternative [⛔️ if the tooltip is empty or references PARITY-TODO].
  - [if] the native picker is unavailable and the operator clicks the folder icon [then] nothing happens because the control is `disabled` [⛔️ if it opens a dialog or pretends to browse].
  - [if] the native picker is available and the operator clicks the folder icon [then] the OS-native directory picker opens and the selected path populates the field [⛔️ if manual typing is still required, as already specified by SETUP-10].
- [x] **SETUP-14** (Wed 16 Sep 2026, after an onboarding run): a FOLDER import ends by putting Open DJ's own analysis to work, and says so. The last screen reads the live `GET /api/v1/analysis-queue` rather than the frozen import record, starts the drain once through `POST /api/v1/analysis-queue/run` instead of waiting out the daemon's reconcile interval, and reports four distinguishable states: not yet read, nothing to analyze, working with live counts, and FAILED carrying the engine's own error text.

  - [if] the drain has FAILED [then] that state is reported with the engine's error verbatim, even though a failed drain leaves every track pending [⛔️ if `pending > 0` is read as "working", so a build that cannot analyze at all shows a progress line forever].
  - [if] a drain is already running, or has already failed, or there is nothing queued [then] the screen does not request another one [⛔️ if the poll relaunches a drain every interval].
  - [if] the analysis queue cannot be read [then] the screen says so [⛔️ if a failed read renders as a library that needs nothing].
  - [if] an agent drives setup over HTTP [then] the stored folder-import record names the queue and run endpoints and reports `analysis_available` MEASURED on this engine [⛔️ if it is a hardcoded `false` that reads the same whether or not analysis can run].
- [x] **SETUP-15** (Wed 16 Sep 2026, same run): starting stem separation in first-run setup is ACKNOWLEDGED on the step that started it. The wizard does not advance on enqueue; the step reports that separation started and names the job, and the last screen repeats it.

  - [if] the operator declines separation [then] the wizard advances immediately [⛔️ if a "no" is made to wait for a confirmation of nothing].

- [x] **SETUP-12** (Wed 16 Sep 2026, from onboarding notes): the first-run wizard can be walked FORWARDS AND BACKWARDS. Every step renders a Back control, and a step already visited is a clickable link in the breadcrumb. Back is refused in exactly two cases, each stating its own reason on the control: the first step has nothing behind it, and a LIVE import cannot be un-started by walking away from it. The breadcrumb and the "step N of M" counter list only the steps the selected branch will actually visit, so a folder import never shows or walks into the rekordbox confirmation step.
  - [if] the operator is on any step after the first with no import running [then] a Back control is present and enabled and returns them to the previous step of THIS branch [⛔️ if Back is absent, inert, or lands on a step this branch skips].

The engine creates and migrates its own `state.db` before it chooses a backend, so it never serves an in-memory library, and `/api/v1/tracks`, `/api/v1/health` and `/api/v1/library/readiness` read the same store.

- [x] **SETUP-19** (found Fri 25 Sep 2026 by the LIBM-120 10k measurement): The engine keeps answering while a folder import runs. Worker progress is written at most every 0.25 s per job (`PROGRESS_WRITE_INTERVAL_S`), in a worker thread rather than on the event loop, and every progress line still reaches its kind's observer.
  - [if] a worker emits hundreds of progress lines against a disk that charges 10 ms per commit [then] the engine loop never goes 0.5 s without running [⛔️ if progress writes serialize on the loop].
  - [if] a folder import runs [then] `GET /api/v1/health` answers 200 within 1 s throughout, and `GET /api/v1/library/readiness` answers 200 on every probe with no gap longer than 5 s [⛔️ if any probe times out, health stalls past 1 s, or readiness goes silent]. Measured at 10k tracks on a CI runner: health max 0.14 s; readiness max 2.05 s and max gap 3.0 s, against a 172 s silence before. The readiness query ITSELF takes up to about 2 s at 10k rows while the loop keeps answering health. Making that query sub-second is outside this requirement, and it is recorded in the performance register row for this work. The 40-file test holds both routes to 1 s.

  - [if] `playwright.preflight-gate.config.ts` or `playwright.onboarding.config.ts` goes red [then] the e2e gate is red [⛔️ if either config runs only when a human remembers it].

"Skip for now", "Continue without importing" and "Start playing" dismiss engine-side and then re-read `GET /api/v1/preflight`, so the root layout's empty-library gate judges the library as it is now rather than as it was at boot; the Done step re-reads `GET /api/v1/setup/status` once the wizard's own import job settles; a FAILED detection is never painted as a scan still in progress; and the Confirm step offers "Continue without importing" beside Back.
  - [if] the library is empty and the user clicks "Skip for now" [then] the wizard closes into the incomplete note and stays closed across preflight polls [⛔️ if it bounces back].
  - [if] a folder import succeeds and the user reaches Done [then] Done reports the imported count, matching `GET /api/v1/setup/status` [⛔️ if it says no import was recorded].
  - [if] the engine's fresh preflight still reports no library after a dismissal [then] the wizard stays open with a plain sentence saying why [⛔️ if it closes into an invisible reopen].
  - [if] detection failed with nothing on screen [then] the detect step does not show the scanning sentence [⛔️ if "Looking for your music" sits beside an error].

  - [if] the status or detection read gives no answer for 20 s (`SETUP_READ_TIMEOUT_MS`) [then] the request is aborted and the detect step says the search did not finish, with Look again, Choose a folder instead and Continue without importing enabled (Mac check, Fri 2 Oct 2026) [⛔️ if "Looking for your music on this machine..." stays up with no end].

  - [if] a status or detection read fails with the server's own words (a plain-string `detail`, a path) [then] the visible copy is a fixed plain sentence and the raw message rides only on `data-agent-error` [⛔️ if the server's words render on Welcome or the detect step].
- [x] **SETUP-27** (shipped Fri 2 Oct 2026, follow-up to an earlier fix): A first-run import that fails says why in plain words, and the folder field's hint is a path the import accepts. The failure sentence is chosen from the worker's error code (`[ERROR] <code>:` in the job's error tail); the raw tail stays in "Details for agents". A failed or cancelled job no longer shows its last progress line. The folder placeholder reads `/Users/you/Music`, because the import refuses a path that starts with `~`.

  - [if] the import is still running [then] its sanitized progress line still shows (control) [⛔️ if the progress line disappears while it runs].

SETUP-05..07 are the way BACK IN. The first-run overlay is a one-shot: the
engine records the dismissal in the data dir and never offers it again, so a
tester who had skipped setup, or who had imported once and wanted to import
again, had no route to the wizard from inside the running app at all.

- [x] **SETUP-05**: A settings surface MUST be reachable by the standard
      preferences accelerator (Cmd+, on macOS, Ctrl+, elsewhere) from EVERY route
      including /performance and inside the packaged shell's webview, and MUST
      offer a "Run setup" action that lands on /setup. The action MUST be visible
      as soon as the surface opens, without the user typing a search term first.
- [x] **SETUP-06**: The admin panel MUST carry a tab strip with a Setup entry
      routing to /setup, so the operator surface has a route into setup that does
      not depend on knowing the URL.
- [x] **SETUP-07**: Every entry point into the wizard MUST clear the
      engine-side dismissal BEFORE navigating, and MUST NOT navigate when that
      write fails: the wizard on screen while the engine still records "dismissed"
      is two truths about one decision. Every entry point MUST also await the
      daemon capability probe before deciding it is refused, because an unfinished
      health GET is "not yet", never "you may not". Agent parity: the same flow is
      `POST /api/v1/setup/dismiss {"dismissed": false}` followed by the documented
      /api/v1/setup/* sequence, with no UI-only step.

### Standalone analysis, no rekordbox (STANDALONE)

Thu 17 Sep 2026.

Recorded because the existing criteria cannot express that requirement, let
alone enforce it. An audit of this block found that every beatmapping and key
criterion is either conditioned on `own` being the selected source, which no
shipping configuration does, or scored against rekordbox as reference data:

* SETUP-03 certifies the ABSENCE of analysis as a pass ("honestly labelled
  unanalysed"), so it cannot fail when analysis never appears.
* NATIVE-01 and NATIVE-04 open every acceptance line with "[if] own is
  selected", and `apps/analysis/selection.py` sets `DEFAULT_SOURCE = "rbx"`,
  so those lines are vacuously satisfiable.
* BEATMAP-01 and PARITY-01 define beatmapping quality as agreement WITH
  rekordbox, which is unmeasurable on a machine that does not have it.

The gap that leaves: nothing in this document states that BPM, key or genre
must be VISIBLE to a user with no rekordbox. All of the above pass on a
rekordbox-equipped machine while the standalone path is entirely broken. The
ids below are written to fail in that exact situation.

This block deliberately does not restate NATIVE-14's promotion gates. Those
govern overriding a rekordbox grid on a rekordbox library. A library rekordbox
has never touched has no grid to override, and that distinction is the whole
subject here.

- [x] **STANDALONE-01**: The test suite can run with no rekordbox artifact anywhere, and proves it could tell if one were present. (shipped Sat 19 Sep 2026)
  - [if] the library and analysis suites run against a data dir holding no `master.plain.db` and no ANLZ cache [then] every listing, deck-load and analysis test passes [⛔️ if any test needs a rekordbox artifact to exist].
  - [if] that run is repeated with `pyrekordbox` absent from the environment [then] `create_app()` imports and `GET /api/v1/tracks` answers 200 [⛔️ if any module-scope pyrekordbox import is reachable from app startup].
  - [if] the isolated data dir is deliberately given a `master.plain.db` [then] the isolation marker test goes RED [⛔️ if the probe cannot detect its own violation, because an isolation check that cannot fail is not measuring isolation].
- [x] **STANDALONE-02** (shipped Fri 25 Sep 2026): A computed BPM reaches the user without a promotion step.
  - [if] a track is folder-imported with no vendor mapping, the native beatgrid backfill writes an `ok` lane, and no lane has been promoted [then] `GET /api/v1/tracks/{sid}` returns a non-null `bpm` sourced from `own_beatgrid.` [⛔️ if `bpm` is null, or its source is `rekordbox`].
  - [if] the same library is opened on a machine that DOES have rekordbox installed, for tracks rekordbox has never seen [then] the result is identical [⛔️ if the presence of an unrelated rekordbox install changes what an unmapped track serves].
- [x] **STANDALONE-03** (shipped Fri 25 Sep 2026): An empty analysis cell always states why it is empty.
  - [if] a track has no `track_fields.bpm` and no own beatgrid record [then] the row carries a `bpm_status` and a non-empty `bpm_reason` [⛔️ if the cell renders blank with no status, which is indistinguishable from a measured zero].
  - [if] a computed own record exists for a lane whose effective source is `rbx` [then] the row reports `available-not-selected` naming that lane [⛔️ if a value has been computed and the interface says nothing about it].
- [x] **STANDALONE-04**: Running the better analyzer never degrades the deck.
  - [if] an unmapped track serves a beatgrid before the native backfill runs [then] after the backfill it serves a grid of at least the same beat count [⛔️ if the own lane settling disables the legacy row while the own overlay is still gated off].
  - [if] the own record is `failed` [then] the grid goes inert with the named reason [⛔️ if a superseded pre-v1 result is resurrected in its place].
- [x] **STANDALONE-05** (shipped Sat 19 Sep 2026): Genre does not require rekordbox, and never fails silently.
  - [if] a folder-imported file carries a GENRE tag and no rekordbox is present [then] the Library Wheel places it in a genre family [⛔️ if it counts as unclassified, which `apps/library_wheel/query.py` does today for every unmapped track].
  - [if] the optional `tags` extra is not installed [then] the genre column states that reason by name on hover (LIBUX-36: the cell itself stays blank) [⛔️ if genre is silently empty, because a missing dependency and an untagged file are different facts].
  - SUPERSEDED Fri 2 Oct 2026 (tinytag now reads file genres, so a missing `tags` extra is no longer a missing genre reader): [if] the optional `tags` extra is not installed [then] the genre column states that reason by name [⛔️ if genre is silently empty, because a missing dependency and an untagged file are different facts].

### Own Cue Store (CUES)

Thu 1 Oct 2026. Until then cues lived only in rekordbox's `djmdCue`, so a
track rekordbox never saw could not keep a single cue (PARITY-05 made that
honest; this replaces it).

- [x] **CUES-01** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026): Hot cues, memory cues and loops live in Open DJ's own store, for every track.
  - [if] a track has no rekordbox mapping [then] hot-cue SAVE, CLEAR and RESTORE succeed and the cue is served back by `GET /tracks/{sid}/hot-cues` and `/anlz` [⛔️ if the pad is inert, or the write 404s, for want of a rekordbox row].
  - [if] a hot cue is saved at a measured fractional-millisecond position
    [then] the selected nonnegative finite position is serialized to the
    existing integer wire contract at the nearest millisecond, retaining beat
    quantization preference and the presentation read model; negative or
    nonfinite selected positions remain refused (repaired).
  - [if] a rekordbox-mapped track is edited in Open DJ for the first time [then] its own set is seeded from its rekordbox cues, so every cue the user did not touch survives [⛔️ if editing slot B drops rekordbox's hot cue A or a memory cue].
  - [if] any hot-cue write runs [then] rekordbox's `djmdCue` is unchanged [⛔️ if an Open DJ edit writes a vendor database; write-back is a separate, explicit node].
  - [if] the user runs a rekordbox import [then] each track's rekordbox cues are copied into the own store, and re-importing refreshes them while nobody has edited them in Open DJ [⛔️ if a re-import overwrites cues the user edited in Open DJ, or stops refreshing cues nobody edited].
  - [if] the own store holds a set for a track [then] `/anlz` serves that set rather than `djmdCue` [⛔️ if the deck shows rekordbox's cues after the user changed them].
  - [if] another machine holds the CloudSync writer lock, or the lock probe is down [then] `GET /tracks/{sid}/hot-cues` still answers, since it only reads; PUT, DELETE and RESTORE are refused with 503 ⛔️

### Beat Mapping (BEATMAP)

Accuracy contract for the engine's own beat-grid analyzer against rekordbox's
stored grid. Applied verbatim from a separate beat-mapping bench
specification, written separately and deliberately not edited into this file
itself.

Deliberately a NEW line rather than an extension of LATENCY-02 QUANTIZED LAUNCH:
that requirement governs the latency and phase behaviour of a live sync action at
playback time, this one governs whether an offline analyzer reproduces the stored
grid at all. Different question, different evidence, different failure mode.

- [x] **BEATMAP-01** (shipped Sat 12 Sep 2026): Beat-grid agreement
      with rekordbox. For tracks
      rekordbox has already analysed, the engine's own beat-grid analyzer must
      agree with rekordbox's ANLZ PQTZ grid, measured by
      `scripts/beatbench/scorer.py` (versioned; round 0 used v1.0.0, round 1
      v1.1.0) over a
      stratified fixture set, and reported SPLIT fixed-tempo versus dynamic-tempo
      with denominators named. The KPI is threefold: BPM agreement at 0.01 (the
      `djmdContent.BPM` int-x100 storage granularity), 0.1 and 1.0 BPM with
      half/double octave errors counted separately; beat-position F-measure at
      +/-70 ms with one-to-one matching, plus nearest-beat p50/p95 offsets both
      raw and median-offset-removed (a lower bound on the best achievable
      shift, not the F-maximizing one); CMLt and AMLt continuity at the
      standard 17.5 percent tolerances, whose gap is CONTINUITY RECOVERED BY
      THE ALLOWED METRICAL VARIANTS and is NOT an octave-error rate (both are
      fractional continuity scores rather than track counts, and AMLt also
      maximizes over an off-beat phase variant, so a nonzero gap can be pure
      phase recovery with no octave error at all); the half and double columns
      remain the classified octave rate an acceptance decision uses; and
      downbeat agreement against rekordbox bar-1 beats, reported N/A for
      analyzers with no downbeat concept.
      Round 0 (Wed 19 Aug 2026) established the harness, the denominators
      (2161 gradable rows of 9986: 2023 fixed, 138 dynamic), honest serial
      runtimes (beat_this 33.8x realtime on CPU, roughly 20 h for a 10k-track
      library serially) and the first accuracy table, on which beat_this leads
      decisively on fixed grids at F 0.857 and a 16 ms raw median offset against
      0.46-0.48 and 106-137 ms for every classical tracker.
      Round 1 (Tue 8 Sep 2026) corrected that estimator: scorer v1.1.0 fits
      tempo by least squares over beat times, adds CMLt/AMLt and a
      shift-corrected F, and rescored round 0's identical committed beat times
      on the identical fixture set. beat_this on the 200 fixed-tempo fixtures
      reads BPM exact 33.5 percent (was 13.5), within 0.1 BPM 75.0 percent (was
      14.5), within 1.0 BPM 82.5 percent (was 52.0), F 0.857 unchanged,
      shift-corrected F 0.942, CMLt 0.816, AMLt 0.896, downbeat 73.0 percent.
      Round 3 (Sat 12 Sep 2026, producer 1.2.0 `lock_bar_phase`):
      converter-only on the same committed round-1 raw arm; `bar_length_anomaly`
      0/90; subset90 `ok` 72/90; fixed served downbeat 0.705; F 0.876 unchanged;
      floors `BAR_PHASE_AGREEMENT_FLOOR` 0.50 and `BEATMAP01_FIXED_DOWNBEAT_MIN`
      0.705 locked in `ops/beatbench/round-3/bar-phase-gate.json`; runtime locked

      Round 6 (Tue 29 Sep 2026, BEATMAP-02): floors re-measured after the bar

### Beat Sync Uneven Grid Warning (BEATSYNC-GRID)

Shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026, beside the NAE-19 continuous phase lock. Tests: `apps/webui/frontend/tests/unit/beat-sync-uneven-grid-warning.test.mjs`.

It returns null for a grid with neither, and for a grid too short to have an interval (that state keeps its own gridless tip). A real clean grid and constant grids stored to the millisecond stay quiet; one 12 ms interval in an otherwise clean grid warns.
- [x] **BEATSYNC-GRID-02**: The deck header shows that warning on the BEAT SYNC control whenever the loaded track's grid raises it, sync on or off: an orange `!` badge on the button (hover `title` carries the counts), the same sentence appended to the button's tooltip, and the warning line of its explainer. Nothing is shown on a clean grid, and the badge sits in the button's corner so the header does not move.
- [x] **BEATSYNC-GRID-03** (amended Thu 1 Oct 2026 by BEATSYNC-JITTER-01..03): On the real uneven grid from the mix that fell out of sync, driven through the Web Audio phase lock, no scheduled follower tempo leaves base x (1 +- 0.3%) where base is the tempo the lock holds at that tick (on an uneven grid it follows the grid's smoothed local tempo, inside the pitch range), the cap is reached when an offset pushes on it (so the bound is exercised), the grid's jitter costs no re-join over 90 s (before the amendment it was re-joined), the lock keeps the followed base, and a deck Beat Sync no longer owns is neither trimmed nor seeked while the same error on an owned deck is corrected.

### Beat Sync Phase Lock On Jittered Grids (BEATSYNC-JITTER)

Shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026, round 1. Why: ADR deck-beatgrid-source Amendment 1 measured the NAE-19 lock re-joining a median 82.6 times a minute (7 to 771) and trimming 78.7% of the time on the 19 uneven rekordbox grids, and found that straightening the grid makes beat alignment worse; so the grid stays as stored and the lock stops chasing its jitter. Tests: `apps/webui/frontend/tests/unit/phase-lock-jitter.test.mjs` (synthetic grids through `phase-lock-workload.mjs`, the ADR's simulation ported to drive the shipped decision, with the lock as it was kept as the "before" instrument), plus the amended NAE-19 suites. Real-grid before and after, the alternatives rejected and the 27 guard mutations: `ops/beatbench/phase-lock-jitter-round-1/report.md` (runner `apps/webui/frontend/tests/live/phase-lock-jitter-workload.mjs`, GET-only).

- [x] **BEATSYNC-JITTER-01**: The phase lock reads a grid the shared grid rule calls uneven (`classifyGrid`: suspect or variable_tempo, the rule the deck badge reads) through `smoothedBeatTimes` (pure, `src/lib/rb/phase-lock.ts`): each beat replaced by a least-squares line through the beats within 8 of it, read at that beat; no beat added or dropped; cached per beat array and rebuilt when the array's length or end times change. An even grid is read as stored: over 1600 random inputs the decision on even grids equals the previous lock's bit for bit, and on the 64 even library grids of the ADR's control every per-track figure is unchanged. On 7 synthetic steady grids stored in 5 or 10 ms steps with stray beats, re-joins go from a median 5.2 a minute to 0 and time trimming from 70.5% to 0.0%, with the median audio error within the 2 ms deadband of before.
- [x] **BEATSYNC-JITTER-02**: With either deck's grid read smoothed, the lock's base tempo follows the smoothed local tempo (master tempo x normalization x follower beat period / master beat period) whenever it differs from the base by more than 0.05%, clamped to the deck's pitch range; the 0.3% trim, its release and the tempo handed back when a lock drops are relative to that base, which both engines keep on the lock. A real tempo change is followed within 9 beats with no seek: through a 2.5% ramp over 32 beats the audio error stays within 5.0 ms and through a 1.7% one-beat step within 17.0 ms, where the previous lock re-joined 223 and 127 times. On steady jittered music the base is retuned fewer than 120 times a minute. With an even grid on both decks the base never moves.
- [x] **BEATSYNC-JITTER-03**: A re-join (a seek) is asked for only when the error has been past the line (a quarter beat or 15 ms, whichever is smaller) on 3 consecutive ticks AND at least 8 s have passed since the lock's join; until then the capped trim works on the error, and 8 s of capped trim covers more than the 15 ms line. One reading past the line never seeks; a tick back under it restarts the count; a genuine large offset is re-joined exactly once; a 20 ms error right after a join is trimmed back without a seek. Both engines carry the count and the join's age on the lock (`joinedAtContextTime` on the audio clock in Web Audio, `joinedAtSec` in Rust mode).
- [x] **BEATSYNC-JITTER-04**: The lock does not fight an offset the DJ dialed in: `userOffsetMs` on the decision input (default 0) is part of the phase the lock holds, wrapped like the phase, and a non-finite one throws. The Web Audio lock exposes `nudge(deck, deltaMs)`, which throws for a deck with no lock: after a registered 8 ms nudge nothing is trimmed or seeked and the offset stands, while the same 8 ms nobody registered is trimmed back. No control feeds `nudge` yet (the jog dial is a readout and a seek on a synced follower re-runs the join); the Rust lock carries the field at 0.
- [x] **BEATSYNC-JITTER-05**: On the 19 uneven library grids, in the ADR's simulation, re-joins fall from a median 82.6 a minute (7.3 to 771.4) to 0.9 (0.0 to 7.3) and mean time trimming from 78.7% to 31.5%. The 9 whose tempo stays inside the +-8% pitch range of their mean: 0 re-joins on all 9, trimming 81.3% to 1.7%. The 10 with a section outside that range cannot be held by any in-range tempo against a mean-tempo master; the minimum interval bounds them to at most 7.3 seeks a minute. Not verified: any of it by ear, or in the running app.

### Boot Preflight (PREFLIGHT)

A blank landing page on app start that requires correct functional
permissions to continue, shows per-check green/red status, has a
click-to-re-request-permissions button, surfaces any relevant
health/diagnostic info BEFORE the main app, and auto-progresses the moment
everything is green -- the standard preflight gate most desktop apps have.
Same screen also reachable from the admin area for reference. Context: a
packaged build shipped with three boot-path failures hit in one session (an
unmigrated state.db, a revoked Media Library permission hanging every audio
open, and masked error bodies); this turns all three into a labeled red
light instead of a broken deck.

- [x] **PREFLIGHT-01**: one canonical `GET /api/v1/preflight` returns overall
      status plus an ordered, cheap-first list of checks (engine-alive,
      state-db, audio-access, library-attached), each `{id, label, status:
      pass|fail|pending, detail, remediation}`; the UI, the CLI, the RC-QA
      lane and the ship flow's OPS-05 probe all consume this ONE endpoint,
      never a second UI-only computation of the same verdict. The frontend
      boot gate holds on any `fail`, auto-advances the instant none remain
      (a `pending` row never blocks it), polls the endpoint on a Re-check
      click and every few seconds while red, and the same component mounts
      read-only and live-polling in the admin area for post-boot reference.
      "Re-request permissions" is the identical GET: the audio-access check
      already performs the real gated read every time, which is what
      prompts macOS if it has never asked before, so a click after granting
      the permission is both the recheck and the re-request -- there is no
      separate mutating route to keep in sync with this one. A prior-deny
      grant that macOS will not re-prompt for gets a deep link straight to
      the Media & Apple Music privacy pane alongside the retry, so the
      button is never dead.
  - [if] `state.db` opens but `schema_meta`'s version is below `SCHEMA_VERSION` [then] the `state-db` check is `fail` and its `detail` names both the found and the expected version, [else stop]
  - [if] the audio-access check's sampled track has no working file, or the read blocks past the hard timeout [then] the check is `fail` with the real error/timeout named, never a hang, [else stop]
  - [if] audio-access times out on a blocked open [then] no in-process worker thread remains wedged and a subsequent preflight request completes within the same timeout budget, [else stop]
  - [if] engine lifespan shuts down after a blocked audio-access attempt [then] shutdown finishes within the existing watcher join timeout (5s), [else stop]
  - [if] a library resolves zero tracks with a playable file across the check's whole sample [then] audio-access reports `pending` with the sample size and the total, never a fabricated `pass` [else stop]
  - [if] every check is `pass` (or `pending`, which never blocks) [then] the response's overall `status` is `pass` and the boot screen auto-advances well under ~300ms of added latency, [else stop]
  - [if] any check is `fail` [then] overall `status` is `fail`, the boot screen holds with no skip/continue-anyway control, and there is no route around it, [else stop]

- [x] **PREFLIGHT-02**: a fresh install where the operator clicks "Continue
      without importing" lands in the main app with an empty library and
      stays there after a reload and after a full app relaunch (adversarial
      UX round 2). `library-attached` reads the engine-side
      setup-dismissed flag (`apps.engine_core.setup.record`) so a dismissed,
      empty library is `pending` (non-blocking) with a "Run setup"
      remediation, never `fail`; a library that is empty and NOT dismissed
      stays `fail` exactly as before, because that state is the setup
      wizard's to own, not this gate's. `GET /api/v1/preflight` and `GET
      /api/v1/health` resolve `state.db`'s path through the one shared
      `resolve_state_db_path` function instead of two independent
      module-level guesses, so the two can no longer disagree about whether
      the identical file exists. The frontend boot gate's per-row markup
      (`PreflightCheckRow.svelte`) renders a real, clickable "Run setup"
      control on that dismissed-empty row.
  - [if] setup was dismissed and the library has 0 tracks [then] `library-attached` is `pending` with a remediation naming "Run setup", overall `status` is `pass`, [else stop]
  - [if] setup was NOT dismissed and the library has 0 tracks [then] `library-attached` stays `fail` and the setup wizard (not this gate) is what the user is shown, [else stop]
  - [if] `state.db` exists and health reports it [then] no preflight check's detail says "no state.db" for that same path, [else stop]
  - [if] the engine-side setup record cannot be parsed [then] `library-attached` is `fail` with the real parse error, never a silent "not dismissed" guess, [else stop]

- [x] **PREFLIGHT-03**: On a fresh engine (empty library, setup
      not dismissed), the Setup wizard opens automatically within one health

      silently blocks first-run when the engine offers setup. The boot
