      Import path for empty libraries; overlay stacking prevents interactive
      surfaces (setup, settings) from rendering behind the boot gate.
  - [if] library-attached is fail, engine-alive pass, setup not dismissed
    [then] Setup overlay visible without manual intervention [else stop]
  - [if] resolveFirstRun cannot complete within timeout [then] a visible
    retry/error state appears, never silent false [else stop]
  - [if] library-attached is fail or pending-empty [then] boot gate offers
    clickable Import / Run setup, not prose-only Cmd+, remediation [else stop]
  - [if] setup overlay and boot gate are both logically open [then] setup
    is the topmost interactive layer [else stop]
  - [if] the setup wizard's lazily loaded chunk cannot be fetched (stale
    client after a deploy, dropped connection) [then] an `alertdialog` named
    "Setup failed to load" states the rejection on the wizard's backdrop with
    one "Reload and retry" action that loads a fresh document at `/setup`
    (a second `import()` of the same URL retries nothing: the browser keeps
    the failed module fetch), and an error toast reaches the client-error
    log; never a yielded boot gate with nothing on screen [else stop]
    (Thu 24 Sep 2026; proof `tests/e2e/lazy-chunk-failures.spec.ts`)
- [x] **PREFLIGHT-04** (Wed 16 Sep 2026): the boot gate speaks in three colors, not one. Every check
      carries a `severity` (`blocking` or `advisory`) and a plain-language
      `explainer`, and `GET /api/v1/preflight` returns `status: fail` only
      when a check whose severity is `blocking` failed; an advisory failure
      is reported in a new `advisories` count and does NOT hold the gate.
      Severity is a property of the OUTCOME, not of the check id: the same
      `library-attached` check is advisory when the library is merely empty
      and blocking when the setup record is unreadable or media permission
      was denied. The row UI paints green for pass, red for a failed
      blocking check, and orange for everything else (a failed advisory
      check, or one that could not be exercised), and every row shows its
      explainer on the row and in the hover title, so the user can learn
      what a row means and what to do about it without breaking anything.
      Painting every non-pass row red taught the user that red does not mean
      stop, which cost the color its meaning on the one row where it does.
  - [if] the library is empty and setup was dismissed, or empty with nothing
    else wrong [then] `library-attached` is `advisory`, `advisories` is at
    least 1, and overall `status` is `pass` so the user reaches the app,
    [else stop]
  - [if] the engine-side setup record cannot be parsed, or media permission
    was denied [then] that same check is `blocking` and overall `status` is
    `fail` exactly as before, [else stop]
  - [if] a check is `engine-alive` or `state-db` [then] it is `blocking`
    whatever its outcome, because the app cannot run without either,
    [else stop]
  - [if] a check arrives with no `severity` at all (an older engine, or a
    check nobody classified) [then] it is read as `blocking` and paints red,
    never silently downgraded to a color the user ignores, [else stop]
  - [if] any row renders [then] it carries a non-empty explainer in its
    hover title saying what the row is and what the color means, [else stop]

### API Schema Fidelity (SCHEMA)

From the Tue 1 Sep 2026 strong-typing audit. `src/lib/api.ts` held
eight hand-written response interfaces and 17 `as unknown as` double-casts, one
per place a hand-written shape had drifted from the schema the daemon actually
publishes. A double-cast is the one assertion TypeScript cannot argue with: a
single `as` still demands the two types overlap, while routing through
`unknown` erases the source type and asserts anything onto anything. That is
how `PlaylistDetail` came to promise a non-optional `updated_at: string` the
server has never sent, with a green build the whole time.

- [x] **SCHEMA-01**: Frontend response types are aliases of the generated OpenAPI schemas, never hand-written copies, and `as unknown as` is a ratcheted quality-gate metric burning down to zero.
  - [if] a frontend module names a daemon response type [then] it is
    `components['schemas'][...]` from `src/lib/api-types.ts`, so a schema
    change reddens the compiler at every call site [⛔️ if a hand-written copy
    can drift from the contract with a green build].
  - [if] a PR adds an `as unknown as` anywhere under
    `apps/webui/frontend/src` [then] the gate fails on
    `frontend.unknown_casts` against its baseline allowance [⛔️ if type
    erasure can be added for free].
  - [if] a double-cast is replaced by a generated alias [then] the gate prints
    RATCHET and still passes, and the allowance may be re-recorded lower.
  - [if] the double-cast scan finds no frontend files at all [then] it raises
    [⛔️ if a broken path config reports as a clean tree].
  - [if] a converted call needs a response header as well as the body [then] it
    reads both through `requireBody`, which applies the same empty-body check
    `unwrap` does [⛔️ if an undefined body reaches UI state because the call
    site wanted an ETag].

- [x] **SCHEMA-02** (shipped): Rekordbox API failures preserve their HTTP status and a useful body excerpt when an unhandled server error returns non-JSON text.
  - [if] an rb API request receives a `text/plain` 500 response such as Starlette's
    `Internal Server Error` [then] the client throws `RbApiError` with code
    `HTTP_500` and the first 200 body characters [⛔️ if JSON parsing hides the
    HTTP status behind a `SyntaxError`].
  - [if] an rb API request receives the `{detail: {code, message}}` error
    contract [then] the client preserves that explicit code and message in its
    `RbApiError` [⛔️ if valid coded daemon errors are reduced to `HTTP_<status>`].

    reproduce that track and cue directly in this sandbox; this pins the
    same code paths against a synthetic fixture instead.

    main scrolling waveform at their cue positions.

    failure is in the cue source, not the palette - ruled out here by
    `test_hot_cue_waveform_source_agreement.py`, which fails loudly if a
    future change reintroduces the divergence.
  - [if] two hot cues in different slots are visible and differ in kind
    (loop vs non-loop) [then] they paint different colors, and each color

    itself does not assign a distinct hue per letter A-H, so neither does
    the waveform).
  - [if] a cue is a loop (`is_loop`, `out_ms` set) [then] it renders as a
    band spanning `in_ms`..`out_ms` in the top marker strip, not a point
    triangle [⛔️ if a loop still reads as a single tick].
  - [if] loops use the orange hue [then] non-loop hot cues and memory cues
    never use it, so the two are separable at a glance.
  - [if] any cue marker's fill is measured against `--rb-bg` [then] it may
    fail the 4.5:1 WCAG AA floor bpm-heat.ts enforces for the BPM column
    (`--rb-red` alone measures 3.85:1) - every marker is additionally
    stroked with `--rb-text` (`cueOutline`), which measures 11.99:1 and
    guarantees the floor regardless of fill hue or future theme edits;
    pinned numerically in `tests/unit/wave-cue-contrast.test.mjs`.
  - **Second divergence found in review**: `refreshHotCues` (audio-engine, the handler behind every `hot_cue_save`
    /`hot_cue_clear`/`hot_cue_restore` IPC command) fetches a fresh `/anlz`
    for its own deck state but never wrote that result back into the shared
    `anlz-cache.svelte.ts` module - `fetchAnlz` bypasses `ensureAnlz`/
    `fetchAnlzForDeckLoad` entirely. A later `load()` of the same track (this
    deck or another) reused the pre-mutation cached entry via
    `isAnlzEntryUsable`, so the bank (always a live fetch) and the waveform
    (stale cache) disagreed again after a save-then-reload - the same
    symptom as the original bug, reached through a different trigger.
    Fixed by `refreshAnlzCacheEntry`, a new export that overwrites the
    shared cache entry in place with no fetch of its own; `refreshHotCues`
    calls it right after its own fetch resolves.
  - [if] a hot cue is saved, cleared or restored on a loaded deck, and that
    same track is later reloaded on any deck [then] the waveform shows the
    post-mutation cues, matching the bank [⛔️ if the waveform still shows
    the pre-mutation cue set after such a reload] - pinned in
    `tests/unit/anlz-cache.test.mjs` ("refreshAnlzCacheEntry overwrites a
    stale published entry without fetching").
  - **Third finding in review**: that same
    refresh's `/anlz` fetch could be satisfied straight out of the browser's
    HTTP cache (`_CACHE_ANLZ`, then `"public, max-age=3600"`, `rb_assets.py`;
    since tightened to `"private, no-cache"` plus an ETag, see PARITY-02), so
    within that hour the "fresh" fetch was not guaranteed to hit the network
    at all. Fixed by `fetchAnlzBypassingHttpCache` (`api-rb.ts`, `cache:
    'reload'`), used by `refreshHotCues` in place of the ordinary `fetchAnlz`.
  - [if] `refreshHotCues` fetches `/anlz` inside the hour after a prior fetch
    of the same track [then] it still reaches the network rather than
    replaying the pre-mutation HTTP-cached response [⛔️ if the refresh reuses
    a cached response older than the mutation] - pinned in
    `tests/unit/api-rb-base.test.mjs` ("fetchAnlzBypassingHttpCache forces
    cache: reload, unlike ordinary fetchAnlz").
  - **Fourth finding in review** (fixed since it is cheap and lands in
    this PR's own new paint code): a loop cue's spanning band is opaque across the full
    `MARKER_BAND_PX` strip, and the original single-pass `drawCues` painted
    it AFTER the beat grid and phrase chevrons, blanking out whatever fell
    under the loop's span. Split into `drawLoopCueBands` (background, now
    painted before `_drawBeatGrid`/`_drawPhrases`) and `drawPointCueMarkers`
    (foreground, unchanged position after them).
  - [if] a stored loop cue's span overlaps a beat tick or phrase chevron
    [then] that beat/phrase mark still paints on top of the loop band, not
    blanked out by it [⛔️ if a loop band ever paints after the beat grid or
    phrases] - pinned in `tests/unit/wave-cue-render.test.mjs` ("a loop cue's
    band paints before the beat grid and phrases, not over them").
  - **Fifth finding in review** (fixed rather than deferred): `refreshHotCues`'s `Promise.all([
    fetchAnlzBypassingHttpCache, fetchHotCueSlots])` rejected wholesale if
    either GET failed, skipping `refreshAnlzCacheEntry` even when the mutation
    had already committed server-side - the shared cache stayed on its
    pre-mutation entry, `isAnlzEntryUsable` kept serving it, and a later
    `load()` could reach the same stale-waveform symptom via a failed-refresh
    path. Fixed with a new `invalidateAnlzCacheEntry` export (deletes the
    cache entry outright) called from a `.catch()` on that `Promise.all`,
    which rethrows after evicting so the caller still observes the failure.
  - [if] one of `refreshHotCues`'s two post-write GETs fails after a hot-cue
    mutation has committed [then] the shared ANLZ cache entry for that track
    is evicted rather than left serving the pre-mutation payload [⛔️ if a
    later load of that track still reuses the stale entry after such a
    partial failure] - pinned in `tests/unit/anlz-cache.test.mjs`
    ("invalidateAnlzCacheEntry evicts a ready entry so a later ensureAnlz
    refetches it").

- [x] **DECKUX-13** (shipped Tue 8 Sep 2026): a double-click on a selected row's title smart-loads and plays, instead of silently hitting the quick-load box's own deck button underneath the pointer.
      TrackTable.svelte's `.deck-btns` box reveals on
      `tr.rb-row-selected:has(.c-art:hover, .c-title:hover)`, which can turn
      true on the FIRST click of a double-click, with the pointer already
      resting where a click must be. The buttons' pointer-events used to go
      `auto` on that same instant, so the gesture's second click landed on a
      deck button instead of the row - that button's own `ondblclick` calls
      `stopPropagation()`, so the row's smart-load handler never even ran.
      Fixed with a JS-timed guard: every row click arms a `DBLCLICK_GUARD_MS`
      (500ms) timer for that row via `_armDblclickGuard`, which drives a
      `.dblclick-guard-active` class the select-driven reveal's pointer-events
      rule requires the ABSENCE of; the box itself stays `pointer-events:
      none` throughout, so a click inside the guard window passes straight
      through to the row. A CSS-only `transition-delay` guard was tried first
      and reverted: `pointer-events` is a discrete property, so a browser only
      honors `transition-delay` on it with `transition-behavior:
      allow-discrete` (Chrome 117+/Safari 17.4+), which does nothing on this
      app's packaged WKWebView floor (macOS 11). The corridor-travel
      (`.deck-btns:hover`) and keyboard-focus (`:focus-within`) reveals are
      unchanged and stay instant.

### Transition indicator (TRANS)

Recorded from a transitioning-indicator investigation. The performance UI already
has the mixer and transport read model a blend detector needs; this family
names the blend so TopBar, IPC, and a future status light share one signal.
Voice-assistant talkback deferral during a blend is a separate consumer and is not this family.

- [x] **TRANS-01**: `/performance` classifies a dual-deck blend from the live mixer + transport read model as `idle | approaching | transitioning`, renders that state as a live TopBar pill immediately to the right of the vibe meter, and publishes the same object on `queryPerformanceState().transition` and the UI mirror. Parking the crossfader or dropping the incoming fader clears `transitioning` on the next snapshot. A pluggable `TransitionStatusLight` adapter is documented; with no device registered the light control stays inert and its tooltip says so.
  - [if] decks 1 and 2 are both active and the default mixer is at xfader 0.5 with faders at 1 [then] `query().transition.state === 'transitioning'` and the TopBar pill shows `transitioning`
  - [if] the xfader then parks at 0 and only bus A remains heard [then] state is not `transitioning` on that snapshot
  - [if] no `TransitionStatusLight` is registered [then] the light control is inert and its tooltip contains `no device` and `not implemented`
- [x] **TRANS-02**: the TopBar blend pill explains itself on hover. The whole pill carries a hover text that says what the state means, which deck is going out and which is coming in, and that the pill is status only with no settings. A press on the pill cannot move keyboard focus off the decks, and the pill stays out of the tab order.
  - [if] the pill reads `transitioning` and is hovered [then] the text says two decks are audible on the master and names both decks
  - [if] the pill reads `approaching` and is hovered [then] the text names the audible deck and the deck that looks about to come in
  - [if] the pill is pressed while a deck has keyboard focus [then] focus does not move

### Mixer Dials & Color FX (MIXUX)

Context for MIXUX-01/02: on current main the channel FILTER dial is
an inert visual stub (`ChannelStrip.svelte` renders
`<Knob ... label="FILTER" value={0.5} tone="rainbow" inert />`) - there is no
filter law on main at all; a separate branch, blocked on
audio sign-off, introduces the first real one
(`apps/webui/frontend/src/lib/rb/color-fx/` kernels incl. `filter.ts` +
`svf.ts`, `dial.ts`, `ColorFxRack.svelte`).

- [x] **MIXUX-01**: Filter dials are wired to real audio -- shipped Thu 3 Sep 2026.
  - Equivalent wiring (not that branch): a paired lowpass/highpass `BiquadFilterNode`
    per channel, inserted after the EQ stack in `audio-engine.svelte.ts`'s
    `_ensureGraph`, swept exponential-in-Hz per `docs/research/filter-taper-laws.md`'s
    L2 law (main-tree research, independent of that other branch). Constants and
    law in `player/constants.ts` (`FILTER_*`) and `_filterFreqsFromKnob`. Command
    plumbing mirrors `trim`/`eq`/`fader` exactly: `PerformanceCommand` `filter`
    variant, `AudioEngine.setFilter`, `ChannelStrip.svelte`'s FILTER `Knob` now
    live (real `value`/`onchange`, `inert` and the `tone="rainbow"` stub marker
    removed). Agent-native parity is automatic: browser UI and any automation
    agent already dispatch through the one `runPerformanceCommandFromUi` /
    `window.musicDjToolsPerformance` surface, same as every other mixer control.
  - **Deliberately NOT included:** dynamic Q/resonance shaping (onset/edge
    tapers, the "warppy" character) -- that is MIXUX-05, explicitly flagged
    non-blocking and needing the user's ear calibration before it is built (QUALITY
    SIGNAL CALIBRATION); this ships a fixed Butterworth Q. MIDI hardware
    mapping for FILTER stays out of P0 per the existing `midi-types.ts` scope

### Headphone Cue Output (CUEOUT)

Recorded Fri 11 Sep 2026 from a research note on headphone-cue practice mode. When no monitor output device is selected, MIX is no longer inert: it blends the PFL cue bus into the main output on one clock so Bluetooth headphones can beatmatch. Selecting a monitor restores master-only main. Sibling ids CUEOUT-02..06 are out of scope here.

- [x] **CUEOUT-01** (shipped this PR): Practice mode blends PFL into the main output via the MIX dial when no monitor is selected; `output_mode` is `practice` or `two_outputs`; unknown modes fail fast; a selected monitor restores master-only main. A single click on the headphone MIX knob steps by one third of the range in the current direction and reverses at 0 and 1 (from 0: 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1, 2/3, 1/3, 0); double-click keeps its reset behavior with no stray step from the first click; drag is unchanged; agents use the existing `headphone_mix` IPC/HTTP command.
  - [if] no monitor device is selected and a channel's CUE is on [then] turning MIX toward cue makes that channel audible pre-fader in the main output, with master attenuated by the equal-power law
  - [if] no monitor device is selected and no channel has CUE on [then] MIX at full cue produces silence in the main output rather than passing master through
  - [if] a monitor device is selected [then] the main output is master-only again and MIX affects only the monitor, no cue bleed into the room
  - [if] `output_mode` is set outside the enum via IPC [then] the command throws and state is unchanged
  - [if] Bluetooth headphones are the sole output in practice mode [then] cue and master stay sample-aligned (same path); the mode never routes cue to a second device
  - [if] the operator single-clicks the headphone MIX knob at 0 [then] MIX advances to 1/3 via the existing `headphone_mix` command path
  - [if] repeated single-clicks from 0 [then] MIX follows 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1, 2/3, 1/3, 0 with direction reversing at each endpoint
  - [if] the operator double-clicks the headphone MIX knob [then] the delayed single-click step does not fire and only the double-click reset runs

LIBUX-04..06 extend LIBUX past the library panel proper to
whole-UI panel and overlay layout, which is where they fit best; the section
name is read as "Library & Panels Layout", panels included.

- [x] **LIBUX-04** (shipped Sat 12 Sep 2026): Hotkeys overlay on "/" and "?", with a searchable list view, live
      type-to-filter with yellow match highlighting, and Esc or an X button always
      hiding it.

  - **The two keys are DIFFERENT gestures, not aliases.** "/" is hold-to-show
    (it hides again on release); "?" toggles the overlay on and off. Building
    both as the same toggle loses half the requirement.
  - [if] "/" is held down [then] the overlay shows for as long as it is held
    and hides on release, while pressing "?" toggles the same overlay on and
    leaves it up until toggled off [⛔️ if both keys behave identically].
  - [if] the user types while the overlay is open [then] the keystrokes go
    straight into the search box and filter the hotkey list as they type, with
    the matched part of each word highlighted yellow, in BOTH the overlay view
    and the list view.
  - [if] Esc is pressed or the X button is clicked [then] the overlay hides,
    from either view and from any filter state [⛔️ if a filtered or list-view
    state can trap the overlay open].

- [x] **LIBUX-05** (shipped Thu 3 Sep 2026): "Technically-working mode" - every component becomes an
      edge-revealed overlay so the user can DJ while working. Ctrl+R toggles (press) or
      peeks (hold; the chord was cmd+R until LIBUX-29 and LIBUX-31), cmd+E raises the EQs mid-screen, Opt held reveals the controls with
      no obvious home over a translucent background, and each region reappears by
      mousing to its own edge.

  - **Hold versus press is load-bearing throughout** ("hold = doesn't stay,
    press = toggle"), the same split LIBUX-04 draws between "/" and "?". Build
    one gesture primitive for both requirements rather than two.
  - **Do not build a second hide mechanism.** LIBUX-02 already covers
    hide-able Next / recommended panels with a collapsed state that does not
    persist across sessions. This is the whole-UI generalization of the same
    idea and should share its machinery.
  - [if] Ctrl+R is pressed [then] the components animate into overlay mode and
    stay there, while holding Ctrl+R brings them back only for as long as it is
    held [⛔️ if press and hold do the same thing].
  - [if] the UI is in overlay mode and hidden, and the mouse moves to a given
    edge [then] only the part belonging to that edge appears (deck 1&3, deck
    2&4, library, waveforms at the top), and only for the decks actually in use
    [⛔️ if mousing to one edge reveals the whole UI].
  - [if] Opt is held [then] the controls with no obvious home appear over a
    full translucent background so they stay readable against whatever is
    behind them, and a config option selects a smooth fade rather than an
    instant appear/disappear.

      genre's culture, "overplayed-ness", playlist membership, which set it was played

  - **Two axes are PREREQUISITES, not free options.** the user marks both themselves

  - [if] the Library Wheel is opened [then] it renders the real library grouped
    by genre from `state.db` [⛔️ if it renders demo or sample nodes; an empty

The test also fails on the banned text-symbol glyphs (including the small down-pointing caret), and it reads each file with HTML entities (decimal, hex and named) and JS escapes decoded, so an encoded spelling is caught like the literal character; a named entity it cannot decode fails the test instead of passing unread. The pad-mode menu caret is a CSS triangle. The test also bans ordinary action symbols (undo and redo arrows, window-control squares and dashes, close crosses, back and collapse arrows, expand and stop marks) where they are a button's content, while the same characters in prose, in attributes, or joining two words or numbers (a dimension like 1280×800) still pass. - [x] **CHROME-07**: MIDI connect is reachable from settings and the audio I/O view; a dim MIDI chip in the bottom-right tray sits 20px left of Preview and opens the I/O view on click. That tray Preview button stops a playing library preview; while nothing previews it is disabled, with a tooltip saying to click a mini-waveform to start one. The mixer's two MIDI entries (the headphone-cluster MIDI button and the MIDI entry inside the audio I/O menu) both open the MIDI drawer and unpin the I/O view, so the pinned I/O popover never covers the drawer; the headphone-cluster button no longer opens the I/O view. A control explainer pinned by its parent closes when the parent unpins it, without reporting that close back to the parent, and a hover or click pin the user made is left alone. Turning the MIDI setting on requests WebMIDI access at once through the same path as the page-load auto-enable (a denial turns it back off); turning it off detaches the controller input listeners and action glue and leaves the browser's permission state as it is. While MIDI is turned off, both mixer MIDI entries read gray with a tooltip saying MIDI is off and to turn it on in Settings, even though the browser still holds its grant or its permission prompt is still open (a request turned off while pending is superseded, so it is not shown as pending); a pending request for MIDI that is on reads amber, and the MIDI drawer's Request MIDI access button turns MIDI on the way the Settings toggle does; with MIDI on and no mapped controller connected they stay red with a cross and a reconnect tooltip. Both entries draw that cross (and the green state's tick) as the same inline SVG mark beside the MIDI label, so the I/O-menu entry never shows the bare word while the cluster button shows the mark. A settings AI proposal for MIDI names the rb.midi_enabled setting, the id the settings overlay applies. The action glue attaches only once access is granted, and a request still pending when MIDI is turned off is superseded: its late grant attaches nothing and does not turn the choice back on. The settings toggle displays the stored choice live: it flips on the click and again when a request settles (a denial turns it back off) or a disk-backed choice arrives. If the MIDI runtime fails to load after the toggle is used, the choice is restored to off, both in the browser and in the disk-backed prefs (so the next page load does not turn MIDI back on, and a failed enable never writes on), and an error toast says MIDI could not load. The drawer's device list and the learn-log pop-out load when the drawer opens. The MIDI drawer, its device list and learn-log pop-out, and the track row's Show in playlists and Relocate popovers are lazy chunks: if one fails to load, an alert says so in place with the error and a Reload button (the drawer, pop-out and popover alerts also have Close). Each chunk is fetched once per page, because the browser keeps a failed module fetch, so reopening in the same page cannot recover it; only Reload, a fresh page the user asks for, does, and nothing reloads on its own. Clicking the tray MIDI chip acquires the audio devices inside that click, as the mixer's I/O button does, before opening the I/O view.
- [x] **CHROME-08**: The MIDI panel can expand to 70% viewport width and can return to a non-oversized floating drawer with a close affordance.
- [x] **CHROME-09**: Refresh analysis uses exactly one hover treatment (the repo standard explainer/popover path).
- [x] **CHROME-10**: Refresh analysis click shows running progress or an explicit WIP/not-working state, never an inert control. Each click's own outcome (already running, or the WIP/not-working reason) renders first in the popover, ahead of a hover fetch error or a previous run's finished state; a live running status still shows its progress. Every click, whether it starts a refresh or is refused, opens the popover the way a hover does, from the keyboard too, as the click happens rather than when the request settles, so a blur, Escape or mouseleave while the request is pending keeps it closed (a run that started is still followed until it ends, for its badges and done toast): it polls the status, so a click that starts a run, or finds one already running, shows that run's live progress, and it opens only once when the pointer already has it open. Blur or Escape closes a popover the pointer did not open, and closing stops the polling once no refresh is running. A status response that arrives out of order cannot replace a newer one: a status request sent before the click started a run and answered after it leaves the run followed, and a running status of a run delivered after that run's end neither revives it nor toasts its end twice. Statuses are ordered by the engine's own stamps (a run's end, else its start); a newer status of the run already shown still applies, so progress keeps updating. A status with no stamps (a restarted backend) applies only when it was asked for after the shown status arrived. If the popover's code fails to load, the popover shows the load error with Reload and Close instead.

### Performance Rekordbox listing (PERF-RB)

- [x] **PERF-RB-01**: Rekordbox library availability for playlist summaries and hydrated rows is served from a persisted, resolver-namespaced path index with per-request stat budgets (0 for tree summaries, 16 for row hydration); cold rows surface `AVAILABILITY_PENDING` on the wire and refresh in the background.
  - [if] the tree summary is requested with an all-stale index [then] zero filesystem stats occur (count via a stat spy)
  - [if] a playlist detail is requested with 500 stale rows [then] at most 16 stats occur in-request and the rest are scheduled
  - [if] the server restarts [then] the previous availability answers are served from the index before any probe
  - [if] a row is pending [then] the response marks it AVAILABILITY_PENDING, never present/absent
  - [if] one request probes primary paths AND `track_locations` alternates [then] both draw on ONE budget, so row hydration never exceeds 16 stats
  - [if] a row's primary path is empty, streaming or gone but an alternate location is on disk [then] the row is present; a row with an alternate still pending is pending, never absent
  - [if] the tree summary serves a stale index answer [then] it still does zero stats but queues that path for background refresh, so the index TTL bounds the lag
  - [if] an API can only answer a boolean (reconcile broken-link scan, rb-meta `file_exists`) [then] it runs a FULL scan and never maps pending to missing
  - [if] `file_exists` is null [then] `file_availability` is AVAILABILITY_PENDING; every settled status (present, absent, streaming, awaiting_volume) carries a boolean
  - [if] the background refresher runs where no state.db exists yet [then] it never creates one (answers go to the in-process cache only), so a request gating on the file's existence can never see a half-migrated database

- [x] **PERF-RB-02**: The library browser (table, column view, smartlists, autolists, All Tracks) loads rows whose availability is `AVAILABILITY_PENDING` and shows them as their own state, never as missing.
  - [if] a playlist has more than 16 pending rows [then] it loads; the row mapper accepts `file_exists: null` only together with AVAILABILITY_PENDING and still rejects null on a settled row
  - [if] a pending row is double-clicked, dragged or previewed [then] it is not refused: the load or preview runs and is itself the disk probe, and no "availability still checking" toast appears (Thu 1 Oct 2026; supersedes the earlier pending refusal) ⛔️
  - [if] a row is known absent (`file_exists` false) [then] load, drag and preview are still refused as "audio file missing on disk" ⛔️
  - [if] Hide broken links is on [then] pending rows stay visible and only confirmed-missing rows are hidden
  - [if] a row is pending [then] it is neither grayed as broken nor fed to AutoPlay as playable, and carries a hover title saying availability is still being checked

- [x] **PERF-RB-03** (Thu 1 Oct 2026): A playlist or smartlist pane whose rows loaded with availability pending re-asks on a 1.5 / 3 / 6 / 12 s backoff and writes each settled answer onto the rows already on screen, so the rows shown with broken links hidden converge on the non-broken count the playlist tree shows. All Tracks, autolists and Stick panes are not re-asked.

### Performance Rescue (RESCUE)

On-disk rolling buffer for Gig view crash recovery.

- [x] **RESCUE-01** (Mon 14 Sep 2026): The Gig view keeps a
      small rolling buffer of state snapshots on disk so a crash, force quit,
      accidental Cmd-Q or power loss can be recovered. A snapshot is the deck
      layout and per-deck: loaded track id and source path, play state,
      position expressed as a BEAT STAMP (beat index plus fractional beat from
      the track's beatgrid, alongside the sample position for tracks without a
      grid), tempo and pitch settings, key lock, loop state, hotcue arm, EQ and
      fader values, the master/cue sink selection, and the crossfader.
      Snapshots are written by the engine (not the page) to
      `<data-dir>/state/rescue/ring-<n>.json` at most every 2 s while any deck
      is playing and on every transport or load event, kept as a ring of 8, each
      under 32 KiB, written atomically (temp file plus rename). Writing a
      snapshot never touches the audio thread and never blocks a request.
  - [if] a deck starts playing [then] a snapshot lands within 2 s carrying that
    deck's beat stamp and play state [⛔️ if the ring is empty 5 s into playback].
  - [if] the engine is killed with SIGKILL mid-write [then] the newest complete
    snapshot is still parseable and the partial one is ignored (atomic rename).
  - [if] nothing is playing and no transport event happens [then] no snapshot
    is written (no idle disk churn).
  - [if] the ring has 8 entries [then] the oldest is overwritten and
    `rescue/index.json` names the newest.
  - Test: unit tests on the ring writer (atomic write, size cap, cadence gate,
    index update) and on beat-stamp encode/decode against a fixture beatgrid
    (round trip within 1/64 beat, and sample fallback when the grid is absent).

Depends on the rescue snapshot ring.

Recorded Sat 26 Sep 2026 from a Windows CI gate:
the restore replayed a saved master sink id, the relaunched window did not
enumerate it, and the uncaught "is not an enumerated headphone output" aborted
the whole restore at boot.

- [x] **RESCUE-05** (Sat 26 Sep 2026):
      A saved audio output survives a relaunch whose page origin changed. The
      desktop shell serves the page from a fresh loopback port every launch,
      and Chromium (so WebView2) salts `MediaDeviceInfo.deviceId` and `groupId`
      per origin (measured with `apps/webui/frontend/scripts/probe-device-id-salting.mjs`
      on Edge 153: id differs across two ports, is stable for one origin across
      a restart, label identical). So each rescue snapshot saves the selected
      master and cue sink LABEL beside its id, and restore re-enumerates, then
      resolves each sink by exact id, else by exact label when exactly one
      output carries it, else selects nothing and names the output the sink is
      actually routed to. Decision record:
      `docs/decisions/ADR-NEW-output-device-descriptor-survives-origin-change.md`.
  - [if] the saved id is enumerated [then] that output is selected by id, even
    when a different output carries the saved label.
  - [if] the saved id is gone but exactly one output carries the saved label
    [then] that output is selected under its new id, with no warning.
  - [if] neither id nor label resolves [then] no select is sent, the rest of
    the restore continues, and the toast names the saved output AND the one in
    effect, read back from the mixer: `Saved master output 'X' not found; using
    'Speakers (Realtek(R) Audio)'` when the enumeration policy auto-pinned a
    speaker, `...; using the system default output` when nothing is pinned
    (cue: `no cue output selected (pick one in I/O)`), never an assumed default.
  - [if] two outputs carry the saved label [then] neither is guessed; the toast
    says `matches 2 devices` and names the output in effect.
  - [if] the output list cannot be read, or one sink's select is refused
    [then] only the affected sink is reported `refused` with the reason; the
    other sink and every deck still restore.
  - [if] a snapshot written before this change (id only, no label) is restored
    on a new origin [then] nothing throws; the sink is reported `not_found`
    naming the id prefix.
  - [if] a master or cue output is picked (select or I/O acquire) in gig
    posture while nothing plays [then] that pick alone writes a ring snapshot,
    because the periodic snapshot only runs while a deck plays.
  - Test: `apps/webui/frontend/tests/unit/rescue-restore-output-device.test.mjs`
    (resolution, orchestration and the ring trigger, over captured device
    labels with the production headphones.ts reconciliation), and end to end
    on real hardware `apps/webui/frontend/tests/live/rescue-output-device-origin.mjs`
    (pick an output in the app on one origin, the production ring writer
    captures it, the app booted on another origin auto-restores it; exit 2
    UNAVAILABLE when no suitable labeled output exists or the engine does not
    salt).



### Rekordbox Parity Metrics & Source Toggle (PARITY)

Split into two ids because they fail differently. PARITY-01 is a MEASUREMENT
contract (is our analysis as good as theirs, per lane, against named
denominators?). PARITY-02 is a RUNTIME AFFORDANCE (can the user switch source and
hear the difference on demand?). A toggle with no metric is a vibe check; a
metric with no toggle cannot be sanity-checked by ear.

- [x] **PARITY-01** (shipped Sat 12 Sep 2026): Every rekordbox-derived analysis lane we re-implement is scored against rekordbox's own analysis of the user's real library as reference data, per lane, with the denominator named on every figure (round 0: apps.parity scorer 1.0.0 scores BPM and Key on a committed library-shaped fixture; round 1: apps.parity scorer 1.1.0 scores waveform preview PWAV/PWV2, detail PWV3/PWV4/PWV5 with unreadable_ext excluded, tri-band PWV6/PWV7, phrase (PSSI), cues_db, cues_anlz, and Vocal on committed library-shaped fixtures; vocal uses apps.vocals.cli.pvdi_present fourcc probe and SPIKE-B2 IoU; beatgrid and downbeat delegated to BEATMAP-01; phrase ungradable missing_pssi; cues_db ungradable missing_djmd_cue; cues_anlz and waveform_detail ungradable unreadable_ext (cues_anlz drops PCO2 only); vocal ungradable missing_pvdi; no lane matching a calibrated threshold; live library not measured this host).
      The lanes are enumerated below from what rekordbox actually holds for
      this library, not from what it is assumed to hold.
  - **Ground truth actually extractable today.** Measured read-only against
    `data/master.plain.db` (the decrypted working copy), the ANLZ files
    rekordbox stores alongside it reached via `djmdContent.AnalysisDataPath`,
    and `data/state/state.db`. Per the honest-denominator rule in
    `docs/library-availability.md`, RE-MEASURE these; never cite them from
    memory. The lanes measured are BPM, Key, Beatgrid, Downbeat, Waveform
    preview, Waveform detail, Waveform tri-band, Phrase, Cues (DB), Cues
    (ANLZ), and Vocal, each against its own denominator (library rows with
    audio present on disk, or a sampled subset of those with a resolvable
    ANLZ directory).

    Reading the table:
    - `present` counts live rows that have audio that resolves on disk right
      now, distinct from a raw row count or a vendor-mapping count, so a
      figure that does not say which denominator it divided by is not a
      figure.
    - The sampled rows are drawn from rows that have BOTH present audio AND a
      resolvable ANLZ directory; an ANLZ file for a track whose audio is gone
      cannot be scored against anything, so `present` is the working
      denominator for every parity lane.
    - PARSE FAILURE IS REAL AND UNEVEN. A minority of sampled tracks have at
      least one unreadable ANLZ sibling, every one of them an `.EXT`, which is
      why the waveform-detail and ANLZ-cue lanes read lower than the full
      sample. None lost their analysis entirely, matching the GUARD-01
      contract.
    - PHRASE IS NOT UNIVERSAL. `PSSI` is present for a majority but not all of
      the sample, so a phrase parity score carries its own sub-denominator
      and can never be quoted against the beatgrid pool.
    - CUES DISAGREE BETWEEN STORES. `djmdSongHotCueBanklist` is EMPTY. The
      repo reads cues from `djmdCue` per the CLAUDE.md house rule, and that
      store covers a small minority of tracks, so DB-side cue ground truth is
      thin and a cue parity claim must name its own count, not "the library".
    - `PVDI` is written by rekordbox 7 but pyrekordbox 0.4.4 refuses it
      (`Tag 'PVDI' not supported!`), so `apps/vocals/cli.py` seek-walks the
      `PMAI` section headers for the fourcc instead; that module records a
      majority of the library as lacking rekordbox 7 vocal analysis at all.

    analyzer abstraction with a portable `librosa` default and a dev-only

    already serves an own-analysis grid in the EXACT `/anlz` shape. What does

  - [if] a track's `file_path` is stale, unresolvable, or otherwise not materialized on disk (regardless of whether the optional `mutagen` reader is installed) [then] `GET /artwork` 404s `ARTWORK_NOT_FOUND`, since residency is checked before reader availability [⛔️ if a mutagen-less build reports 503 `ARTWORK_READER_UNAVAILABLE` for a file that was never there to begin with].
  - [if] an unmapped track's embedded artwork response is cached publicly [then] it includes a byte-derived ETag and returns 304 for a matching `If-None-Match`, so retagged artwork revalidates before its 24-hour max-age expires [⛔️ if a client must serve stale image bytes and mime type until max-age elapses].
  - [if] an unmapped track has a resolvable embedded picture and the client reads both the library listing and `GET /tracks/{stable_id}` [then] the listing row's `artwork_available` and the detail `TrackOut.artwork_available` are identical (both `true` when mutagen is installed, both `None` when the optional reader is absent) [⛔️ if detail disagrees with the listing].
- [x] **PARITY-05** (shipped Tue 1 Sep 2026; superseded Thu 1 Oct 2026 by CUES-01, which gives unmapped tracks a real cue store): Cue writeback target for unmapped tracks - hot-cue SAVE on a deck with no live rekordbox mapping goes inert-with-tooltip ("cues need a rekordbox mapping") instead of firing a write that would 404, since `djmdCue` is keyed by a `djmdContent.ID` a locally imported track never has (PARITY-TODO.md line 134).
  - [if] `GET /tracks/{stable_id}` or `PATCH /tracks/{stable_id}` resolves a track with no live rekordbox mapping (no `track_vendor_ids` row, its `djmdContent` row is soft-deleted, its `track_vendor_ids` mapping row is itself soft-deleted (`deleted_at` set) even though the old `djmdContent` row is still live, or it is mapped only under a non-rekordbox vendor) [then] the response's `has_rb_mapping` field is `false`, the same criteria `TrackListItemOut` already uses for the listing row and `resolve_content`'s write path already enforces [⛔️ if the single-track and listing shapes disagree about the same track, or a deck reads `true` for a mapping the write path would refuse].
  - [if] a deck loads a track whose `has_rb_mapping` is `false` [then] clicking an empty hot-cue slot (A-H) does nothing - no SAVE request is sent - and the slot's tooltip reads "cues need a rekordbox mapping" [⛔️ if the click still fires `PUT .../hot-cues/{slot}` and surfaces the resulting 404 to the user].
  - [if] a deck loads a track whose `has_rb_mapping` is `true` [then] empty hot-cue slots behave exactly as before - clicking SAVEs at the current playhead [⛔️ if a mapped track's SAVE path regresses].
  - [if] a hot-cue slot already holds a cue (populated from a prior mapped state or read) [then] clicking it still jumps to that cue regardless of the deck's current `has_rb_mapping` value - only EMPTY slots are gated [⛔️ if a filled slot on an unmapped deck also goes inert].
  - [if] a `hot_cue_save` command reaches `performance-ipc.svelte.ts`'s shared typed dispatcher directly (a browser/CLI/IPC caller, not just `HotCueBank.svelte`'s click handler) for a deck with no live rekordbox mapping [then] `_execute` throws before any network call, the identical guard the component reads to go inert [⛔️ if a non-UI caller can still fire a SAVE the component itself blocks].
  - [if] `queryPerformanceState` serializes a deck snapshot [then] `PerformanceDeckSnapshot.has_rb_mapping` carries the same value `HotCueBank` gates its click on, so a non-UI caller can read the guard state before deciding to dispatch [⛔️ if the query shape omits the field and a caller has no way to predict the guard will fire].
  - [if] a `PATCH /tracks/{stable_id}` with a stale `If-Match` 409s [then] the response's `current` payload (used by the track page's "Take theirs") carries `has_rb_mapping` under the same criteria every other `TrackOut`-shaped response uses [⛔️ if the 409 payload omits the field because it bypassed `_track_to_out`].
  - [if] a deck has nothing loaded (`stable_id === null`, either never-loaded or mid-reload after `unload`) [then] its empty hot-cue slots render inert-with-tooltip ("no track loaded - nothing to save"), the same dimmed treatment as an unmapped deck, and clicking one does nothing - no SAVE request, no thrown error, no lost feedback [⛔️ if the pad renders as a normal live control and the click reaches `onSave`, throwing `hot cue X: deck is not loaded` unhandled]. `has_rb_mapping` alone cannot gate this case: `_emptyDeckState` (`state.svelte.ts`) defaults it `true`, so an empty deck reads as mapped. Fixed Wed 2 Sep 2026: `HotCueBank.svelte`'s `onSlotClick` and the slot's `inert-mapping` class/title now also check `deck.stable_id`.
  - [if] the x-to-clear control on a filled slot is clicked while `deck.stable_id === null` [then] `onClearClick` refuses before calling `onDelete`, the same defensive posture as the SAVE guard, even though the click is not reachable through the UI today (`_emptyDeckState` resets `hot_cues` to `[]`, so the x never renders on an empty deck) [⛔️ if the guard is removed and a future render path exposes the x on an empty deck without anyone noticing].

- [x] **PARITY-09** (shipped Sat 5 Sep 2026): Genre and comment for an unmapped track come from file tags recorded in the shared state layer during folder import, not from a nonexistent rekordbox row.
  - [if] a folder-imported track has genre and comment file tags but no live rekordbox mapping [then] its hydrated row (playlist detail, smartlist, search) and `GET /tracks/{stable_id}/rb-meta` return those state-layer values [⛔️ if either remains null or the two surfaces disagree]. The `/tracks` listing row is deliberately excluded: genre and comment have never been in that contract, and the browser fills them there from the same lazy rb-meta fetch.
  - [if] rb-meta resolves genre and comment for an unmapped track [then] it reads them through the same `state.db` connection it reads `file_path` and `duration_ms` through, never through the request's `StateBackend` [⛔️ if a local-only library, whose backend may hold no row at all, gets `NotFoundError` for a track the endpoint can plainly see].
  - [if] a folder import reads genre or comment from file tags [then] it writes that value to `track_fields` with `inferred` provenance [⛔️ if metadata is discarded after import].
  - [if] a folder-imported track has no genre or comment tag [then] the corresponding field remains null [⛔️ if the browser invents a value].

- [x] **PARITY-03** (shipped Tue 1 Sep 2026): a track with no rekordbox vendor mapping gets its waveform peaks from OUR OWN decode of its audio, cached like the ANLZ cache, feeding both the deck lane and the browser preview strip, and shows nothing at all until that decode has run.
  - **Why it existed.** A track imported straight into OpenDJ (folder import,
    a generated e2e fixture library, stems written into state.db) has a
    `tracks` row but no `track_vendor_ids` row, so there is no ANLZ file to
    read. `GET /anlz` answered with `empty_anlz_payload` - a valid payload
    with every band empty - so the deck loaded and played over a blank lane
    and the browser row showed the no-preview dash forever. Audio is the one
    thing this repo resolves for itself, so it is also the one honest source
    of peaks for those rows.
  - **Decoder.** ffmpeg, the same external tool `apps/sync/usb/preflight.py`
    already requires, decoding to mono 8 kHz s16le purely to take per-column
    maxima. It reaches every container in `AUDIO_MEDIA_TYPES` without adding
    the opt-in `analysis` extra (librosa/soundfile) to the web server's
    runtime dependencies. Absent ffmpeg is a real, tested state, not a crash.
  - **Where the decode runs.** On the single-track `GET /anlz` fetch, cached
    under `data/state/local-waveform-cache/` afterwards. Library row
    hydration is cache-READ-only on purpose: hydrating 200 rows must never
    fan out 200 ffmpeg processes.
  - **Honest band claim.** The payload declares `kind: "mono"`, the same
    convention a rekordbox PWAV lane uses, and repeats one decoded envelope
    under low/mid/high. Splitting one envelope into three frequency bands
    would be invented data.
  - [if] an unmapped track with decodable audio is fetched from `/anlz`
    [then] its waveform bands carry the peaks of that audio and
    `local_waveform.status` is `decoded` [⛔️ if the bands stay empty while
    ffmpeg could have decoded the file].
  - [if] the decode cannot run (no ffmpeg, undecodable bytes, missing file)
    [then] the bands stay empty and `local_waveform.reason` names the cause
    [⛔️ if any shape at all is drawn for a decode that did not happen].
  - [if] a decoded track's audio file is replaced by a rename-based swap, or
    an in-place overwrite that changes size or mtime [then] the next read
    re-decodes it rather than serving the cached peaks of the old bytes,
    detected on every platform via the source's inode, size, and mtime
    [⛔️ if a stale entry survives its source]. An in-place overwrite that
    also restores the original size AND mtime is additionally caught via
    nanosecond ctime on POSIX; ctime means creation time on Windows, not
    content-write time, so that narrower case is not detectable from cheap
    stat metadata there and is a known, accepted gap shared identically by
    `apps/vocals/cache.py`'s mtime+inode signature.
  - [if] a browser row's track has no local decode yet [then] its
    `preview_b64` and `preview_max` are both null, rendering the same
    explicit dash an unanalyzed rekordbox track gets [⛔️ if hydrating a
    listing triggers a decode per row].
  - [if] a Share-audience request and a local request resolve to different
    playable candidates for the same track [then] each decodes and caches
    its OWN peaks from `resolve_playable_audio`'s audience-scoped pick
    [⛔️ if a Share listener's peaks come from the local-only candidate].
  - [if] a browser row is already rendered before its track's decode has run
    [then] selecting that row adopts the freshly-decoded strip into the
    same row once `/anlz` lands, with no reload [⛔️ if the row stays blank
    until the next listing fetch].
  - [if] concurrent decode demand saturates both the decode slots and the
    admission queue [then] the next request answers `not_decoded`
    immediately, naming the reason [⛔️ if it parks a Starlette worker
    thread instead].
  - [if] the PCM stream is reduced to peaks [then] it is consumed
    incrementally, never buffered whole in memory [⛔️ if an hour-long track
    holds its full decoded PCM in RAM at once].
  - [if] a `not_decoded` answer is caused by transient decoder saturation
    (the admission cap or the queue-wait timeout) [then] the payload marks
    `local_waveform.retryable: true`, the response is sent
    `Cache-Control: no-store`, and the client re-fetches on the next natural
    trigger instead of caching the reject for the session [⛔️ if a momentary
    saturation reads back as a permanent "this track has no waveform" for up
    to an hour].
  - [if] a packaged/GUI-launched app's PATH lookup finds no ffmpeg (it does
    not inherit Homebrew's PATH the way a shell does) [then] setting
    `MDT_FFMPEG` to an ffmpeg executable path resolves the decoder, the same
    escape hatch `scripts/vocal_region_worker.py` and
    `scripts/stem_bundle_worker.py` already use [⛔️ if this decoder alone
    ignores `MDT_FFMPEG` and only those two scripts honor it]. A set-but-not-
    executable `MDT_FFMPEG` fails loud naming the bad path rather than
    silently falling back to PATH.
  - [if] a track's local decode has permanently failed (no ffmpeg, corrupt
    audio, missing file - not a retryable/transient reject) [then] the deck
    lane shows an explicit `NOT DECODED` label with the real reason in its
    tooltip, the same way a rekordbox `ANLZ ERROR` renders [⛔️ if the lane
    renders blank with no label, since `local_waveform` never feeds the
    `waveform` bands the deck paints and the HTTP response is a normal 200].
  - [if] a retryable track's browser row is deselected, or its deck unloads,
    before its ambient retry's cooldown elapses [then] that retry does not
    fire, and a later selection or deck-load revives it with no lost state
    [⛔️ if rapid keyboard/scroll navigation across many uncached rows leaves
    every rejected stable_id retrying every cooldown forever, each holding a
    decode slot the user's actual selection needs].
  - [if] the same track is loaded as a row in more than one browser pane
    [then] a decode triggered by its selection in one pane still fills its
    copy in every other pane, overwriting any strip already there [⛔️ if
    only the pane whose own selection matched the cache lookup gets the
    strip, leaving an identical row in another pane blank until reselected
    there or the listing refreshes; or if a stale, audience-mismatched
    sidecar strip survives the selected track's own fresh
    audience-scoped decode because an existing strip is never replaced].
  - [if] the resolved ffmpeg path is a file the kernel cannot actually
    execute (wrong architecture, a script with a missing interpreter, or the
    file vanishing between resolution and spawn) [then] the decode answers
    `not_decoded` with the launch failure as the reason [⛔️ if the raw
    `OSError` escapes uncaught and `/anlz` answers 500 instead].

PARITY-06 recorded Tue 1 Sep 2026 from the PARITY-TODO board's v1 blocker
"locally imported tracks are second-class citizens". PARITY-01
and 02 assume own-analysis EXISTS for a track; this one is what makes it
exist for a track rekordbox has never seen.

- [x] **PARITY-06** (shipped Tue 1 Sep 2026): Analyze on import - every track that lands without a vendor mapping is queued for apps.analysis and drained automatically, so a local-first library has analysis rows to serve rather than an empty deck.
  - **The gap this closes.** A track imported straight into the local library
    (folder ingest, the first-run setup wizard, a generated e2e fixture
    library, stems written into state.db) gets a `tracks` row and no
    `track_vendor_ids` row, so it has no `djmdContent` twin and no ANLZ file.
    Audio played; beatgrid, waveform, cues, artwork, genre and phrases were
    all empty. `apps/analysis` and the `/beatgrid-fallback` +
    `/auto-cues` endpoints that serve it already existed - nothing ran the
    analyzer on import, so there was never a row to serve.
  - **What the drain actually produces, and what it does not.** The row
    carries tempo, key, energy, onsets and RMS peaks, which is what
    `/auto-cues` reads and what the deck shows for tempo and key.
    `/beatgrid-fallback` is NOT served by it: `synthesize_fallback_beats`
    anchors on `downbeats_s`, and the shipped `DEFAULT_BACKEND` (`librosa`)
    declares `downbeat_tracking = False` and returns no downbeats, so that
    endpoint keeps returning 404 for a locally imported track. The only
    downbeat-capable backend is `librosa+madmom`, which needs madmom from git
    HEAD and is deliberately outside the installable `analysis` extra, so
    draining to it would arm a loop that cannot run on any packaged install.
    Tracked as known tech debt; this requirement does not claim it.
  - **Derived queue, not a queue table.** The backlog is a projection of
    `tracks` + `track_vendor_ids` + `analysis`
    (`apps.analysis.backlog.scan`), so an import through ANY path is visible
    to the next scan with no enqueue call to forget and no second store to
    drift. The daemon RECONCILES on a timer rather than subscribing to the
    in-process event bus, because the CLI and setup-wizard imports run in a
    different process and that bus cannot reach across it.
  - **A failing chunk never blocks the ones behind it.** The drain walks the
    sorted targets in `ANALYSIS_CHUNK` slices. Every chunk is attempted even
    after an earlier one exits non-zero, and the accumulated failures are
    raised once at the end, so the job still reports `error`. Aborting on the
    first failure let a few permanently unanalyzable files (unsupported
    codec, truncated download) starve every valid track sorted behind them:
    nothing later ran, no `analysis` rows appeared, the backlog signature
    never moved, and the reconcile loop then read that unchanged signature as
    "already tried this queue" and suppressed the retry forever - a block
    that survived later imports, because the same chunk sorts first again.
  - **One job slot.** The drain is the existing "Refresh analysis" job under
    a new `scope=unmapped`, so the manual button and the auto-drain can never
    run two analyzers at once, and the existing TopBar progress popover
    renders the auto-drain's progress with no new UI.
  - [if] a track lands with no live `track_vendor_ids` row and no analysis
    row [then] it appears in `GET /api/v1/analysis-queue` and the daemon
    starts a drain for it without a human clicking anything [⛔️ if a local
    import can only be analyzed by hand].
  - [if] a queued track is rekordbox-mapped, already analyzed, a streaming
    URI or has no materialized local bytes [then] it is not a target, and it
    is counted in its own named bucket rather than dropped from the
    denominator [⛔️ if `analyzed + unreachable + pending` stops equalling
    `unmapped`].
  - [if] a track's only `track_vendor_ids` row is for another vendor (djay,
    serato, traktor) [then] it is STILL queued, because only a rekordbox
    mapping implies an ANLZ exists [⛔️ if a non-rekordbox mapping silently
    excludes a track that has no beatgrid to serve].
  - [if] a track's only `analysis` row is from a backend the drain does not
    run (`mik`) [then] it is STILL queued, because the drain's own
    `filter_missing` would analyze it and a mik row can carry no usable
    downbeats [⛔️ if the queue and the drain disagree about "analyzed"].
  - [if] a pending track's file is repaired IN PLACE, same path and same
    `stable_id` [then] the change signature moves and the drain is re-armed
    [⛔️ if bytes that just became decodable are never retried].
  - [if] a drain fails (no analysis extra installed, an undecodable file)
    [then] the job reports `phase=error` with the runner's exit and the
    auto-drain does NOT re-fire until the queue itself changes [⛔️ if a
    failing backend becomes a subprocess retry storm].
  - [if] `MUSIC_DJ_AUTO_ANALYZE` holds anything but `on` or `off` [then] the
    daemon fails to start with that value named [⛔️ if an unrecognized value
    is coerced to a default].
  - [if] the analysis step is disabled in the ingest config [then]
    `scope=unmapped` is rejected 422 rather than starting a job with nothing
    to run.
  - [if] the drain REFUSES to start (analysis step off, or a manual refresh
    claimed the one job slot after the busy check) [then] no attempt is
    recorded, so the next tick over the same queue tries again [⛔️ if a
    refusal retires the backlog until some unrelated import moves the
    signature].
  - [if] a pending track is relinked from an undecodable file to a repaired
    one [then] the change signature moves and the drain is re-armed, even
    though the track's `stable_id` did not change.
  - [if] a repair rewrites a pending file in place with different bytes of the
    same length and then restores the original mtime [then] the change
    signature still moves, because the token carries `ctime_ns` as well
    [⛔️ if a metadata-preserving rewrite - `cp -p` over the original, a tag
    editor that stats first and calls `os.utime` after - leaves the queue
    reading unchanged and the repaired file is never retried].
  - [if] the platform's `st_ctime` is the file's CREATION time rather than the
    inode change time (Windows) [then] the content token digests the bytes
    instead of trusting stat, and the same repair is still visible [⛔️ if a
    same-length in-place repair moves no stat field on that platform at all,
    so the file is suppressed until some unrelated track happens to move the
    queue signature].
  - [if] an unmapped track's stored `file_path` needs `MDT_PATH_MAP` to name
    a file on THIS machine (a Linux build host, or a Windows install reading a Mac's
    library) [then] it is resolved through `platform_paths.resolve_library_path`
    before the residency probe and the queue item carries the RESOLVED path
    [⛔️ if a whole deployment mode reports every track unreachable while the
    mapped files sit materialized on disk, or if the analyzer is handed a path
    it cannot decode].
  - [if] the resolver cannot place a stored path on this machine at all
    (`unmapped:remote`, `unmapped:<platform>`) [then] the track counts
    `unreachable`, which is a real state with a real repair, rather than being
    dropped from the denominators.
  - [if] an unmapped track's `file_path` is an `http://`/`https://` streaming
    URL or is EMPTY [then] the resolver's `streaming` reason excludes it from
    every bucket rather than failing the disk probe [⛔️ if a URL is reported
    as an unreachable file a user is invited to repair, or if `Path("")` --
    the current directory -- is treated as audio to decode].
  - [if] `MUSIC_DJ_AUTO_ANALYZE=on` but the default analyzer backend is not
    installed (the packaged engine ships the `uv export --no-dev` closure and
    librosa/scipy live in the optional `analysis` extra) [then] the reconcile
    loop is NOT armed, and the reason plus the fix are logged once at
    construction [⛔️ if the installed desktop app gives every first import a
    failed job, or if the feature is disabled silently].
  - [if] a queued track leaves the pending set between the watcher's scan and
    the drain worker's own rescan, then returns byte-identical (a vendor
    mapping arriving and being withdrawn never touches the file, so every stat
    field is unchanged) [then] the auto-drain fires again rather than matching
    its recorded signature forever [⛔️ if a track that was never actually
    analyzed is retired until some unrelated import moves the queue].
  - [if] the drain runs at all [then] the attempt is booked against the queue
    snapshot the WORKER read (`_RefreshJob.queue_signature`), never the
    watcher's own pre-start scan, and never before the worker has read one
    [⛔️ if recovery depends on some later polling tick happening to observe
    an empty queue, which a restore inside one interval never produces].
  - [if] the drain a tick started finishes fast enough that another request
    claims the one job slot before the tick's next statement [then] the loop
    still books that drain's own queue signature, because the locked start
    HANDS BACK the job it created rather than leaving the caller to reread the
    registry [⛔️ if the loop books a library job's empty signature over the
    queue its own drain just failed on and relaunches it on the next tick].
  - [if] a drain the watcher did NOT start finishes, such as a manual
    `POST /analysis-queue/run`, and it published a queue signature [then] the
    next tick books that attempt instead of repeating it [⛔️ if the first
    tick after a manual failure relaunches the identical queue the user just
    watched fail, which is what an empty `last_signature` guarantees after a
    fresh daemon start].
  - [if] the job in the one slot is a library or batch job [then] nothing is
    booked and no existing booking is erased, however its signature reads, and
    the same finished job read again on a later tick is not booked twice
    [⛔️ if a scope that never targeted the unmapped backlog retires it or
    forgets an attempt on it, or if re-reading the slot undoes the forget an
    empty queue just performed].
  - [if] a library or batch refresh takes the one job slot AFTER a finished
    unmapped drain that cleared its signature [then] that clear still reaches
    `last_signature`, through the settling path and through the adoption path
    alike, because the newest unmapped drain is kept beside the replaceable
    slot [⛔️ if an unrelated refresh landing later is what silences a drain
    saying its queue was never attempted, and the lost target then sits behind
    `unchanged` for as long as it keeps its content token].
  - [if] a finished unmapped drain published a cleared signature and the
    watcher's own attempt had ALREADY settled [then] that clear still reaches
    `last_signature` and retires the stale booking [⛔️ if the adoption path
    for a drain this loop did not start is qualified on a published signature,
    so the one statement it most needs to hear is the one it skips, and a
    target that returns with the same content token sits behind `unchanged`
    for good].
  - [if] the analysis backend cannot run on this machine at all (the packaged
    engine ships without librosa and scipy, and the TopBar can still start a
    manual refresh) [then] the CLI reports that with its own exit code and the
    drain stops at the first chunk [⛔️ if one subprocess is spawned per chunk
    across the whole library to rediscover a capability fact the first chunk
    already proved].
  - [if] a chunk exits on anything but a PER-TARGET status (an argparse or
    configuration error, an unknown backend, a signal, a crashed worker pool,
    a SQLITE_FULL on the state DB) [then] the step stops there rather than
    continuing [⛔️ if a failure that recurs identically on every chunk is
    met once per chunk across the whole library].
  - [if] a chunk both LOST a target before it could be queued and found the
    backend unable to run for the targets it did admit [then] the admission
    shortfall wins and it exits 3, not 4, because only 3 makes the ingest
    worker clear `queue_signature` [⛔️ if the worker books a snapshot
    containing a target no process ever attempted, so a file that returns
    with the same content token sits behind `unchanged` indefinitely].
  - [if] the analyzer CLI is given a usage error, an unknown backend or a
    malformed handoff file [then] it exits 2, not 1 [⛔️ if a configuration
    mistake is indistinguishable from "some tracks failed" and a chunking
    caller retries it against the same bad configuration].
  - [if] an exception escapes the analyzer run itself, so no track ever got a
    verdict (the state DB cannot be opened, the disk fills mid-write, the
    worker pool dies) [then] the traceback is logged and the CLI exits 5, not
    the 1 CPython would give it [⛔️ if a systemic fault arrives wearing the
    one status a chunking caller is allowed to continue past, and the drain
    meets the same wall once per chunk across the whole library].
  - [if] a backend fails on something that is NOT this file (an analyzer
    config that was never installed, a backend that could not initialize)
    [then] it propagates and the CLI exits 5, because only the failures a
    backend declares to be about the input (`TrackUnreadable`,
    `TrackTooLong`, `TrackVanished`, `BackendNotAvailable`) become a per-track
    error [⛔️ if a
    broad catch around `backend.analyze` relabels a machine-wide fault as a
    failed track and invites the caller to bring it the next chunk].
  - [if] the decode itself fails [then] only exception types measured against
    the real stack to describe invalid input become `TrackUnreadable`
    (`IsADirectoryError`, `EOFError`, `LibsndfileError`, an audioread
    `DecodeError`), and everything else -
    `ImportError`, `MemoryError`, a bare `RuntimeError` from a
    half-initialized decoder - reaches the systemic exit [⛔️ if a broad
    `except Exception` around `librosa.load` turns a dependency or
    decoder-initialization failure into a per-file verdict].
  - [if] a target passes the CLI's admission check and is GONE by the time the
    backend opens it (a library sync, a rename or an unmount inside that
    window) [then] the decode's `FileNotFoundError` becomes `TrackVanished`
    and the run exits 3, not the per-track 1 [⛔️ if the drain books a queue
    it never attempted, so a file restored byte-identically keeps its content
    token and sits behind `unchanged` forever].
  - [if] a manual drain starts and finishes while a tick is inside its scan, having failed per-track so the queue is unchanged [then] the tick still books that attempt and reports `unchanged` [⛔️ if the attempt ledger is read before the scan, so the loop relaunches the identical drain it just watched fail].
  - [if] a drain finishes over this exact queue between the tick's ledger read and its slot claim [then] the start is refused from inside the registry lock and the tick books that attempt instead [⛔️ if a parked watcher thread wakes and launches a second drain over a queue another drain just failed on].
  - [if] shutdown is requested after the tick's last look at the stop event and before it claims the slot [then] the same locked guard refuses the start and the tick reports `stopping` [⛔️ if a parked watcher thread wakes and spawns an analyzer subprocess after the lifespan that owned it has gone].
  - [if] the reconcile-loop tests point the app at a temporary state DB [then]
    they redirect `state.paths.STATE_DB` and leave `open_ro` itself in place,
    so every read runs through the production accessor with its `mode=ro` URI
    and its `query_only` pragma [⛔️ if a fixture substitutes a plain
    read-write `sqlite3.connect`, so the backlog scan is never proved to work
    under the read-only connection it actually gets in the daemon].
  - [if] pytest is launched from a shell that already exported
    `MUSIC_DJ_AUTO_ANALYZE=on`, which is what running the daemon in that shell
    does [then] the suite still forces it off rather than honoring the export
    [⛔️ if entering a TestClient lifespan arms the reconcile loop and spawns
    real analyzer subprocesses against a test's state DB].
  - [if] the decode is denied by permissions - a share mounted without
    credentials, a parent-directory ACL, or a macOS privacy grant that permits
    `stat` and denies `open`, all of which pass the admission check [then] the
    `PermissionError` propagates and the CLI exits 5, because a denial is
    about this process's access and not this file's contents [⛔️ if a
    library-wide denial arrives as the one status the chunk loop may continue
    past, so the drain meets it once per chunk across every track].
  - [if] a bad CONFIG value fails inside `librosa.load` itself, such as an
    `analyzer.sample_rate_hz` of 0 on a file that is perfectly good audio
    [then] it still propagates, because the split is on WHAT the exception is
    and not on WHERE it was raised [⛔️ if a catch keyed on the decode call
    reports the whole library as corrupt one chunk at a time].
  - [if] `audioread.NoBackendError` is raised [then] it counts as being about
    the file, on an ffmpeg-less box as much as on a full one, because librosa
    reads through libsndfile first and reaches audioread only once libsndfile
    has already rejected the bytes [⛔️ if the CI runner, which ships no
    ffmpeg, turns every undecodable file into a systemic stop and the
    "a failing chunk never blocks the ones behind it" contract silently
    inverts there].
  - [if] the unmapped population is larger than the connection's
    `SQLITE_LIMIT_VARIABLE_NUMBER` (999 on pre-3.32 builds, which includes
    the sqlite3 in some system Pythons and the packaged app) [then] the bulk
    location read is split into bounded batches and the scan still returns
    [⛔️ if a big folder import makes `GET /analysis-queue` and every watcher
    tick raise "too many SQL variables" instead of draining].
  - [if] the watcher learns of shutdown DURING its scan, which is the slow
    part of a tick and can outlast the join [then] the tick still stops
    rather than acting on the backlog the scan came back with [⛔️ if a stop
    that timed out still ends in an analysis subprocess spawned after the app
    lifespan shut down].
  - [if] the job holding the one slot has published no queue signature yet
    [then] it is not booked, so the signature it publishes later is still
    adopted [⛔️ if the one-shot adoption is spent on a queue nobody can name,
    leaving `last_signature` stale and relaunching the identical queue that
    just failed].
  - [if] the job holding the one slot is still `queued` or `running` [then] it
    is not booked however real its published signature looks, because that
    value is not final until the job finishes [⛔️ if a CLI that then reports
    a vanished target clears `queue_signature` precisely so the queue is not
    recorded as attempted, and the booking has already happened].
  - [if] a NEWER unmapped drain finished and deliberately cleared its
    `queue_signature` [then] the watcher books that clear rather than falling
    back to its own older signature, because only the job's SCOPE distinguishes
    "no unmapped job here" from "this queue was not attempted" [⛔️ if the
    clearing is undone one job later and the target the newer drain lost sits
    behind a queue nothing has attempted since].
  - [if] the chosen candidate is materialized but its bytes will not decode,
    while another `track_locations` copy on this machine would [then] the drain
    still analyzes only the chosen one - a known, accepted limit,
    because the scan cannot know a candidate is
    corrupt without decoding it and the CLI reports no per-target verdicts to
    retry an alternate against.
  - [if] a lifespan restart finds a reconcile loop that outlived its own
    `stop()` [then] it waits a bounded time for that survivor and starts a
    replacement once it has exited [⛔️ if declining leaves the restarted
    daemon with no reconcile loop at all, so nothing imported afterwards is
    auto-analyzed until some further restart].
  - [if] the content token is taken the way the scan takes it, with no
    capability passed [then] the token really carries what
    `CTIME_IS_INODE_CHANGE` claims for this platform [⛔️ if the selector
    routes Windows through the stat-only path, which the parameterized cases
    cannot see because they name the branch themselves].
  - [if] a `--pairs-json` handoff has the right outer shape but a non-string
    member, such as `[["sid", 1]]` [then] it is a usage error (2) [⛔️ if
    `Path(1)` raises inside the dispatch and the caller reads
    EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR - "stop, this machine is broken" - for a file it
    wrote wrong itself].
  - [if] the daemon lifespan is started again on the SAME app [then] it
    reuses the watcher it left on `app.state` rather than building a new one
    [⛔️ if a thread retained by the previous `stop()` is invisible to the
    next `start()`, which then runs a second reconcile loop beside it and the
    two take turns losing a 409 on the single job slot].
  - [if] the watcher has been asked to stop [then] no later tick starts a
    drain, and a thread that outlived the join keeps its handle [⛔️ if an
    analysis subprocess is spawned after the app lifespan shut down, or if a
    lifespan restart spawns a second reconcile loop beside a live one].
  - [if] the analyzer drops a queued target because it was gone by the time the
    CLI checked [then] it exits with a code that says so and the drain publishes
    no signature at all, so the next tick retries instead of recording the queue
    as attempted [⛔️ if a file evicted between the scan and the handoff, then
    restored, is suppressed forever on the strength of an attempt that never
    happened].
  - [if] a track's `tracks.file_path` is null or stale but this machine has a
    materialized `track_locations` row [then] the drain queues it at the
    location path, because `upsert_track_location` deliberately never writes
    the legacy column and the browser already treats such a track as playable
    [⛔️ if a track the user can play is invisible to the analysis backlog].
  - [if] another job takes the single job slot before the booking tick [then] the
    booking prefers the latest drain that actually published a queue signature,
    and falls back to the one the watcher's own drain read, never to None
    [⛔️ if a library-scope refresh, which publishes no queue signature at all,
    erases the booking and relaunches the failed backlog immediately].

### Native Analysis v1 (NATIVE)

Scope lock: decisions D1 to D7 were recorded the same day, Tue 8 Sep 2026. v1 makes
every analysis value a deck, smartlist or sync path reads producible by our own
code on the user's machine, scored against rekordbox and Mixed In Key with named
denominators, and switchable per lane once it passes an agreed threshold.
Own analysis is canonical INSIDE Open DJ only (D1); write-back to rekordbox and
the USB export are v2, and promotion is a separate persisted per-lane default
source, not the PARITY-02 dev toggle. The lane set is the 8 of D2, producers are
hybrid lane by lane (D3), backfill runs on the user's machine for every lane
except stems and lyrics (D4), lanes live in flat `apps/analysis_<lane>/` packages
(D5), the bench runs on dedicated agent hosts (D6), and a fresh Mixed In
Key run is reference data only (D7). The ids below are section 9 of that spec, plus
NATIVE-13 from its section 13 (cross-platform parity), recorded here at
milestone open; nothing in this block is built yet.
