A review caught six defects across two rounds, all fixed before merge: the candidate answer field was checked as `key_open_key` instead of the repo's real `key_openkey`; `truth_echo` alone could not ceiling the `vs_mik` columns on disagreeing fixtures, fixed by adding `truth_echo_mik`; the DISAGREE-UNRELATED table cell dropped its enumerated stable_ids on the way to the persisted spec log; a test monkeypatched `weighted_score` to fabricate a broken scorer, which AGENTS.md's no-mocks rule prohibits, so it was deleted in favor of the exhaustive real-production-path unit tests already covering that behavior; the constant-key floor answered A minor instead of the C major spec section 5 cites by value, and shipped without the second, most-common-key floor the round-0 brief also names, fixed by correcting the constant and adding `most_common_key`; and a posted round reported only the all-attempted score, discarding the candidate's self-reported failure count and never computing the successful-only score or a named failure-rate denominator spec section 5's baseline contract asks for, fixed by deriving `n_failed`/`vs_rekordbox_successful_only`/`vs_mik_successful_only` per arm. A further review caught four more defects across two rounds, all fixed before merge: an uncaught `NormaliseError` from a malformed Camelot/Open Key candidate string would abort scoring for every arm in the round, now caught and scored as a failed answer; `key_openkey` was never inspected once `key_camelot` was present, even though both are mandatory on a real candidate record, so an internally inconsistent dual-notation answer (the exact bug class this lane exists to catch) scored as correct, now both are parsed and a disagreement between them scores as a failure; a fabricated fallback key (`apps/analysis/backends/librosa.py` emits one at `key_confidence=0.0` on an internal key-estimation failure, with no `error` field) could score as a real answer if it happened to collide with the reference, now checked and scored as a failure regardless of collision; and a disagreement fixture the candidate never answered fell into the enumerated DISAGREE-UNRELATED listening list as if it had actively disagreed with both references, now split into its own `disagree_no_answer` sub-bucket. A fifth finding, that the hand-built synthetic truth bundle itself violates AGENTS.md's no-mocks rule, was REBUTTED and the thread resolved: that rule's own text permits captured/sanitized fixtures consumed through production code paths as input, which this bundle is (checksummed by `seal_bundle`, read through `load_bundle`/`canon.py`), the identical pattern already ships unflagged in the beatgrid lane, and no real rekordbox/MIK data exists on this worker box to substitute (0 of 43 paths resolve) -- replacing it is a blocked deliverable, not an action available in this change. A sixth finding on a further round caught that the `except NormaliseError` from the malformed-value fix above did not cover every uncaught-crash path: MIK's own documented missing-key sentinel (Camelot `"0"`) normalises to a PLAIN `ValueError`, not the `NormaliseError` subclass, so that specific value still aborted scoring; widened to `except ValueError`, which covers both. A seventh finding caught that `render_table` read only three of `_buckets`' five fields (dropping `disagree_no_answer` and `n_no_reference_pair`), and `rounds.append_round` persists only the rendered table, so those two classifications were permanently lost from the retained evidence; both are now rendered, with `disagree_no_answer` enumerated by stable_id like `disagree_unrelated` already was; an eighth, immediate follow-on finding caught that the fix above widened the header row to 17 cells without widening the delimiter row underneath it, which breaks GitHub-Flavored Markdown table rendering entirely, fixed by adding the missing delimiter cell and a structural (not just substring) regression test that mutation-tests true against the pre-fix source. A ninth finding, on the round drawn by that push, caught that `score_bundle` already carried the candidate's own self-reported `payload["n_failed"]` into the report as `n_failed_reported` specifically so it would not be silently dropped, but `render_table` never read that field, so the persisted round showed only this scorer's derived count with no way to see a producer-reported figure that diverges from it; fixed by rendering both counts side by side rather than replacing one or raising on a mismatch (the two count different things: the producer's own aggregate versus this scorer's per-fixture walk). A tenth finding on the same round asked this scorer to preserve producer, device, checkpoint identity, and per-track timing provenance; split on landing, since only part of that list exists in the codebase today: `payload["candidate"]` and `payload["generated_at"]` (written by every control and real candidate CLI already, per `controls.py`) are now carried into the report and rendered as a `producer (generated_at)` column, answering the finding's stated harm ("cannot establish which producer artifact generated the scores"); the `device` and per-track-timing half was REBUTTED and the thread resolved, since neither exists as a field anywhere in `AnalysisRecord` or this harness's payload contract, no candidate in this change emits them, and the CPU-vs-MPS timing/equality comparison the finding cites from `nav1-key-r0.md` item 2 is that lane's own deliverable (built alongside `skey_runner.py`/`profiles.py`, neither of which exists in this change) -- this id's own body never asks for it, so inventing the field here would be scope not owned by this id. An eleventh finding on the round drawn by that push named `payload["candidate_version"]` specifically (present in every key control in `controls.py` and established for real candidates by `scripts/beatbench/_harness.py`), which the ninth/tenth findings' fix had missed alongside `candidate`/`generated_at`; fixed by carrying it into the report as `producer_version` and rendering it in the same cell (`producer/version (generated_at)`), None-safe like the other two. A twelfth finding on that same round caught that `_parse_candidate` accepted a candidate's key label whenever `key_confidence` was nonzero, ignoring `apps/analysis_key/flags.py`'s `no_tonal_center` signal (a low-confidence-but-nonzero or thin-margin estimate on an ambiguous or non-tonal track, the same signal named end to end as `flags.TonalCenterFlag.no_tonal_center`/`LaneResult.reason="no_tonal_center"`/this spec's own key-lane column), so an ambiguous track could inflate MIREX/KSEA/mode-accuracy and the successful-result count instead of scoring as unanswered; fixed by rejecting any candidate result carrying `no_tonal_center` truthy, the same way an explicit `error` already was. A thirteenth finding, surfaced only after `docs/research/beatgrid-and-segmentation-sota-20260906-d-key-detection.md` landed on main mid-change and became citable, caught that `_ksea_match` computed a DIFFERENT metric from that research doc's own KSEA definition (S-KEY paper: 1.0 exact tonic, 0.5 a fifth above/below, ignoring mode entirely): the prior boolean key-signature-equivalence implementation gave full credit to a relative major/minor pair and zero to a fifth, the opposite of the correct scoring; fixed by rewriting `_ksea_match` into `_ksea_score`, returning the partial-credit float the cited paper specifies, and updating `KSEA_DEFINITION` to cite the research doc rather than state the module's own prior, incorrect definition. A fourteenth finding, on the same round, caught that `_buckets` classified DISAGREE-RELATED/DISAGREE-UNRELATED by which reference the CANDIDATE's answer matched rather than by the rekordbox/MIK pair's own relationship (the same research doc, lines 698-710, defines both buckets purely in terms of the two references), so the same disagreeing pair could land in either bucket depending on which arm was scored, and a genuinely related pair (e.g. a fifth apart) fell into DISAGREE-UNRELATED whenever a given candidate's answer matched neither reference exactly; fixed by classifying each disagreeing pair ONCE via `weighted_score(rekordbox, mik)` independent of any candidate, and reporting which side (or neither) the candidate's answer takes only within the related class, adding a `sides_with_neither` count alongside the pre-existing `sides_with_rekordbox`/`sides_with_mik`. A fifteenth finding, on the round drawn by that push, caught that the DISAGREE-RELATED table cell rendered only raw `sides_with_*` counts with no visible denominator, despite the same research doc's own worked phrasing ("sides with MIK on X percent, with rekordbox on Y percent, with neither on Z percent", lines 702-705) and its verification discipline ("measure the size of every bucket and report it every time", lines 713-716); fixed by adding `pct_sides_with_rekordbox`/`pct_sides_with_mik`/`pct_sides_with_neither` (denominator = the bucket's own `n`, so the three rates can legitimately sum to less than 100 when `disagree_no_answer` fixtures exist, rather than hiding that a fourth category exists) and rendering the bucket's `n` beside them. A sixteenth and seventeenth finding, two BLOCKING threads on the round drawn by that push, caught that `load_bundle` accepted a malformed manifest/truth join instead of refusing it: `truth.get(sid, {})` converted a `stable_id` with no truth row at all into an ordinary per-source missing reference rather than flagging the join as broken, and the dict comprehensions building the rekordbox/MIK reference maps silently collapsed a duplicate `stable_id` into one key, shrinking `score_bundle`'s own `stable_ids = list(rekordbox)` denominator without saying so; fixed by a new `_refuse_malformed_join` check in `load_bundle` that raises before either reference map is built, naming the first offending `stable_id` and the count, confirmed by mutation-testing each check away independently and watching only its own new test fail for the right reason.

- [x] **PERFMODE-18** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026, measured on the live preview; amends STEM-47's flat 6 s bound): The hold on a deck's own stem decode is graded by how real the pressure is, and a finished cloud fetch is noticed within a second. With no pressure signal the decode starts at once (unchanged). Under the churn early warning alone (churn score at or over 500, kernel memory pressure below level 2) the hold is at most `EAGER_STEM_DECODE_EARLY_WARNING_DEFER_MS` = 500 ms. Under kernel memory pressure (level 2 or above) it is at most `EAGER_STEM_DECODE_MAX_DEFER_MS` = 2000 ms. An xrun in the current window took that 2000 ms bound too until PERF-STEMDEC-04 (same day) measured it true on 8 of 10 loads on a loaded host with no effect on late callbacks inside the decode; an xrun alone now takes the 500 ms bound. Found because the preview host reads a churn score of 5,820 to 12,933 with the kernel at level 1, so every decode started while a deck played sat out the full 6 s as "STEMS WAITING". The cloud-fetch probe re-asks after 500 ms, then every 1 s for the first minute, then every 5 s; it was 1, 2, 3 then 5 s, which left a finished fetch on screen as "fetching" for up to 5 s (3 s measured).
  - [if] a deck is playing and no pressure signal is raised [then] the decode starts immediately and the deck never shows a waiting state [⛔️ if it is held at all].
  - [if] a deck is playing and only the churn early warning is raised [then] the decode starts within 500 ms [⛔️ if it waits longer, or is dropped].
  - [if] a deck is playing and the kernel reports level 2 or above [then] the decode starts within 2000 ms [⛔️ if it gets the 500 ms bound, or waits longer than 2000 ms].
  - [if] a deck is playing and an xrun landed in the current window with the kernel below level 2 [then] the decode starts within 500 ms [⛔️ if it waits 2000 ms].
  - [if] a cloud fetch finishes within its first minute [then] the deck's next probe is at most 1 s away [⛔️ if the gap can exceed 1 s].
  - [if] a cloud fetch is still running after one minute [then] the deck probes once per 5 s [⛔️ if it keeps probing every second for the whole download].

FB-08 added Wed 2 Sep 2026: a comment pin's lifecycle past drop -
status colors, an agent note, an unread dot, single-pin archive, follow-on,
and marking a pin's status green when the PR that fixed it merges.

- **FB-08**: Pin lifecycle: a pin carries `status` (open/issued/blocked/fixed/merged/archived, defaulting open), an `agent_note`, and an `issue_url`; the widget colors the marker by status, shows an unread dot when `updated_at` is newer than what this viewer last saw, and offers Archive and Follow-on only once a pin is fixed or merged. The widget polls `GET /comments` every 5s once hydrated so an agent's PATCH appears in the same tab without a reload. `POST /comments/{id}/archive` moves one done pin into the newest archive file with its full history and is refused (409) for an open/issued pin even when called directly, not just hidden in the widget; `POST /comments/{id}/follow-on` is refused (409) the same way for an open/issued parent; `PATCH /comments/{id}` cannot set `status: archived` itself, since only the archive endpoint performs the archive-file transaction. Every comments.json read-modify-write (create, PATCH, archive, follow-on, bulk harvest archive) holds one shared lock, so none of them can interleave with another. `just pin-merged <PR>` (called as the last step of every PR merge) auto-discovers every reachable feedback daemon (worktree dev ports, ad-hoc audition servers, the installed app local and on a second machine) the same way `feedback_harvest.py` does, rather than patching only one machine's own loopback engine, and reads `pin <id> -> <sha>` lines and closing keywords out of the merged PR body to PATCH every pin they name to `merged` on every one of them - matching a full issue URL's owner/repo or the `owner/repo#N` shorthand, and scoping a bare `#N` closing reference to the PR's own repository, not just the trailing number. A follow-on draft's Save button disables itself while its request is in flight, and the store replaces rather than duplicates a pin id it already holds, so neither a double-click nor a same-tab poll landing mid-request can leave two pins for one follow-on.
  - [if] Archive is pressed on a fixed/merged pin [then] it leaves comments.json and lands in an archive file with its status, issue_url and agent_note intact [else ⛔️]
  - [if] POST .../archive is called on an open or issued pin, by any client [then] it is refused 409 and neither comments.json nor the archive file changes [else ⛔️]
  - [if] POST .../follow-on is called on an open or issued parent, by any client [then] it is refused 409 and no child pin is written [else ⛔️]
  - [if] a pin is updated twice within the same UTC second [then] `updated_at` still strictly increases, so the unread dot re-raises on the second update [else ⛔️]
  - [if] a merged PR's body closes an issue in a DIFFERENT repository by full URL [then] a pin in THIS repo referencing the same issue number is not marked merged [else ⛔️]
  - [if] a merged PR's body says `Fixes #N` (bare) [then] only a pin whose issue_url points at the PR's OWN repo and issue N is marked merged, never a same-numbered issue in another repo [else ⛔️]
  - [if] a PATCH and a single-pin archive race on the same pin [then] the shared lock serializes them so neither write is silently lost [else ⛔️]
  - [if] an agent PATCHes a pin's status while the reviewer has the app open [then] the marker's color and unread dot update within one poll tick, with no page reload [else ⛔️]
  - [if] `just pin-merged <PR>` runs and the user's pin lives on a worktree dev port, not the main install's default port [then] that daemon is discovered and patched too [else ⛔️]
  - [if] a merged PR's body closes an issue via the `owner/repo#N` shorthand rather than a full URL [then] a pin in that repo referencing issue N is marked merged the same as a full-URL reference [else ⛔️]
  - [if] Save pin on a follow-on draft is double-clicked before the first request settles [then] only one child pin is created, since the button disables itself for the duration of the in-flight save [else ⛔️]
  - [if] a same-tab poll's GET already returned the follow-on's newly created child before its own POST response arrives [then] the pin list keeps one entry for that id, not two, since the store replaces rather than appends a duplicate id [else ⛔️]
  - [if] a comment PATCH explicitly sends `text: null` [then] it returns 422 and OpenAPI does not advertise null as valid [else ⛔️]

### Feedback Pin CloudSync (FBSYNC)

Added Fri 11 Sep 2026: four per-machine `comments.json` stores held 138 outstanding pins (25 duplicated) and each machine saw only its own. Design: `docs/decisions/ADR-0013-feedback-pin-cloudsync.md`. Attachment BYTES are a filed follow-up; FBSYNC-05 covers only the metadata and the explicit gap.

- [x] **FBSYNC-01** (shipped Fri 11 Sep 2026, ADR-0013): Every feedback comment pin on an engine enrolled to a CloudSync hub appears on every other engine on that hub, in `GET /api/v1/feedback/comments`, with no manual step once the engine's CloudSync scheduler is switched on (`MDT_CLOUDSYNC_SCHEDULER=1` plus `MDT_CLOUDSYNC_HUB_URL`). Each pin travels as one row of the synced `feedback_pins` table (schema v12), inside the existing CloudSync sync set rather than a separate channel. The pin's id, text, page, anchor, x/y, status, agent note, issue URL, author, build stamp, environment (including the machine name) and attachment metadata arrive unchanged. The same pin id held by several stores collapses to one pin.
  - [if] a pin is dropped on machine A and A then B sync [then] B lists it with every field identical to A's copy [else ⛔️]
  - [if] two stores hold the same pin id and the machine holding the newer copy syncs first [then] after syncing, both list it once, as the newer copy [else ⛔️]
  - [if] the scheduler switch is off [then] no background sync runs and `POST /api/v1/feedback/sync` is the only trigger [else ⛔️]

- [x] **FBSYNC-02** (shipped Fri 11 Sep 2026, ADR-0013): Lifecycle changes propagate: status issued/fixed/merged, agent note, issue URL and follow-on pins. Conflicting edits resolve by CloudSync's existing row-level last-writer-wins. The later pin `updated_at` wins on every machine, and that stamp is the pin's edit time, never the sync time. An exact tie goes to the greater `origin_device_id`.
  - [if] B marks a pin fixed with a note and opens a follow-on, then B and A sync [then] A shows the status, the note and the follow-on [else ⛔️]
  - [if] A and B both edit one pin before either syncs [then] both converge on the later edit [else ⛔️]
  - [if] both copies carry the identical instant [then] both converge on the copy from the greater machine id [else ⛔️]

- [x] **FBSYNC-03** (shipped Fri 11 Sep 2026, ADR-0013): Nothing is lost: a pin present on either side after a sync exists on both. Archive is an explicit synced tombstone (`deleted_at` plus `status: archived`). It is never inferred from a pin missing from a `comments.json`; a missing pin is copied back instead.
  - [if] B archives a pin and both sync [then] A drops it from the board, holds it in its archive file as `archived`, and a later sync does not bring it back [else ⛔️]
  - [if] a pin disappears from one machine's `comments.json` without an archive [then] the next sync restores it there and nothing tombstones it [else ⛔️]

- [x] **FBSYNC-04** (shipped Fri 11 Sep 2026, ADR-0013): Offline-first and agent-native. The local pin store keeps working while the hub is unreachable. An unreachable hub is never swallowed: it is journaled as a CloudSync `error` result, logged, and answered by `POST /api/v1/feedback/sync` as HTTP 503 `FEEDBACK_SYNC_HUB_UNREACHABLE`. The next successful sync catches up. `GET /api/v1/feedback/sync/status` reports store counts, the CloudSync link, and each pin as `synced`, `pending_push` or `unreconciled` (`?pin_id=` narrows to one). `python -m apps.sync_hub feedback-pins sync|status --engine URL` exposes the same over HTTP.
  - [if] the hub is down when A syncs [then] the answer is 503 with that code, the pin is still listed, and status shows `last_result: error` and the pin `pending_push` [else ⛔️]
  - [if] the hub comes back and A then B sync [then] the pin reaches B and is `synced` on A [else ⛔️]
  - [if] the CLI targets an engine that is not answering [then ⛔️] it exits 1 naming why

- [x] **FBSYNC-05** (shipped Fri 11 Sep 2026, ADR-0013): Attachment metadata syncs. Attachment bytes do not sync yet, and the gap is explicit rather than silent. Fetching a synced pin's attachment whose bytes are absent answers 404 `ATTACHMENT_BYTES_NOT_SYNCED`. The sync status reports `attachment_bytes: missing` per pin and `attachments_missing` per store. The pin card says the screenshot is not on this machine.
  - [if] a pin with a screenshot syncs from A to B [then] B carries the same attachment metadata and fetching it answers `ATTACHMENT_BYTES_NOT_SYNCED` [else ⛔️]
  - [if] the status is read on each machine [then] B reports `missing` and A reports `present` [else ⛔️]
FB-13 added Fri 11 Sep 2026: pin follow-up thread on the same marker.

- **FB-13**: Pin follow-up thread: an open pin card can append a follow-up on the same pin via `POST /api/v1/feedback/comments/{id}/replies` without creating a second pin; `CommentOut.replies` is an append-only list of `{id, author, text, created_at, agent_kind}` and is returned on `GET /comments` so an agent sees the full thread; a PATCH of `agent_note` also appends an agent reply unless it duplicates the last agent turn; the card renders opening text then replies in order (legacy pins with `agent_note` and empty `replies` treat that note as the first agent turn); openapi.json and api-types.ts are regenerated in the same change.
  - [if] a pin's card is open [then] there is a way to add a follow-up without creating a second pin at a different position [else ⛔️]
  - [if] a follow-up is added [then] it is stored server-side and survives a reload, like every other piece of feedback [else ⛔️]
  - [if] a pin has been triaged by an agent and the user replies [then] the reply and the agent's note appear in order, so the exchange reads as an exchange [else ⛔️]
  - [if] an agent reads the pin over the API [then] it sees the full thread, not just the latest text [else ⛔️]
FB-14 added Sat 5 Sep 2026: blocked pins are a narrow, actionable red state.

- **FB-14**: A comment pin may be `blocked` only for credentials/auth, a destructive-action decision, or a genuine product fork that requires the user; unclear instructions are a question in `agent_note`, never blocked. A blocked note begins `auth: the user must ...`, `destructive-action: the user must ...`, or `product-fork: the user must ...`; the red marker displays that first sentence above supporting detail, and a later PATCH to any non-blocked status reuses the same pin and removes red.
  - [if] an agent PATCHes status `blocked` with no agent note [then] it is refused 422 [else ⛔️]
  - [if] an agent PATCHes status `blocked` with an actionable first sentence [then] the marker is red and that sentence appears above the note detail [else ⛔️]
  - [if] an agent PATCHes a blocked pin to `issued` [then] the same pin stays on the canvas without its red marker [else ⛔️]

### Reload Announcement (REFRESH)

Added Wed 2 Sep 2026.

- **REFRESH-01**: A reload announces itself before it lands. While the tab is
  visible, `scheduleReload(reason)` shows a 10s on-top countdown overlay
  before reloading, so a half-read diff or a half-typed comment is not lost
  to a reload landing mid-thought; while the tab is hidden, the reload
  happens at once (a countdown nobody can see is pure latency). This covers
  every reload path in the app, including a Vite dev full reload: the dev
  server (`vite-hold-full-reload.ts`) rewrites the outgoing `full-reload` HMR
  message into a custom event before it reaches the client, so the
  browser-side scheduler - not Vite's own unconditional `pageReload()` -
  owns the actual reload. Agent-native parity:
  `window.__mdtScheduleReload(reason, seconds?)` announces a reload exactly
  the way the app does.
  - [if] `scheduleReload()` runs while the tab is visible [then] a 10s
    countdown overlay renders and counts down before `location.reload()`
    runs [else ⛔️]
  - [if] `scheduleReload()` runs while the tab is hidden [then] the reload
    happens immediately, with no overlay [else ⛔️]
  - [if] a Vite dev full reload fires (a changed file, a cleared tsconfig
    cache) [then] the countdown holds it the same as an in-app reload,
    rather than the page reloading within ~50ms regardless of the overlay
    [else ⛔️]
  - [if] the component holding the countdown is torn down mid-count [then]
    its interval is cancelled rather than left running against a gone
    component [else ⛔️]

### Agent-Native Control (AGENT)

Added Wed 2 Sep 2026. Intent: AI computer-use agents
must be able to control Open DJ in full, headlessly, with a readable state that mirrors
the UI, a CLI that exposes every button and dial, and orders that are sequential,
parallel and transitional in beat time.

- [x] **AGENT-01**: Single command bus. Every performance interaction (UI, MIDI, keyboard, agent) dispatches through `dispatchPerformanceCommand`; queryable command history and per-deck command IDs expose the same bus to observers.
  - [if] a DDJ-400 play press lands [then] it appears in `query()` history and the deck observer sees the same command id as a UI click would ⛔️
  - [if] a browser-panel playlist is selected by mouse [then] `query().browser.active_playlist` changes and the same change is reachable by `dispatch({type:'browser_select_playlist'})` ⛔️
  - [if] master mute is toggled from the TopBar [then] `dispatch({type:'master_mute'})` exists and `query().master.muted` reflects it ⛔️
- [x] **AGENT-02**: UI-mirror state. `GET /api/v1/state/ui-mirror` returns one JSON document a human can read like the screen: per deck title, artist, key, bpm, effective bpm, position as `ms` and as `bars.beats` and `phrase`, playing, audible, context_state, presentation clock trust, loop, 8 hot cues with names, pitch, sync, stems; the elected master deck, which is what a beat-relative order times against and without which an agent cannot resolve its own Duration against the grid the page will use; mixer per channel with labelled positions; master and mute; browser panel (playlist, search, sort, selected row, visible rows count); toasts; open overlays; per-control `available|inert`. Served out of the page over a widened deck-observer push or a WebSocket topic on `engine_core/ws.py`.
  - [if] a deck is playing but master RMS, measured at the master bus upstream of the master mute, is 0 for 2 s [then] `audible:false` and a `silent-while-playing` toast id are both present in the mirror ⛔️
  - [if] the page is not open [then] the route returns 409 with `client_open:false`, never an empty mirror ⛔️
  - [if] a control is `rb-inert` on screen [then] the mirror lists it as `inert` ⛔️
  - [if] the track table shows N > 0 rows intersecting the viewport [then] `browser.visible_rows_count` is N, counting only rows the viewport actually shows, not TrackTable's virtualization overscan pad or the total DOM/playlist count ⛔️ (fixed Tue 15 Sep 2026: the field's selector matched nothing, on every build, at every viewport)
  - [if] the browser panel is `{#if}`-unmounted (library page collapse), scrolled entirely out of the window, or opacity-hidden by LIBUX-05's technically-working mode on `/performance` [then] `browser.visible_rows_count` is 0, since a hidden panel's rows can still report normal on-page rects when the hide is paint-only (opacity), not layout ⛔️ (round 2)
  - [if] an agent types text into the library search box [then] the next mirror publish reports that text in `browser.search` ⛔️
  - [if] an agent clicks a sort header [then] the next mirror publish names the column and direction in `browser.sort` ⛔️
  - [if] an agent selects a track row [then] the next mirror publish identifies that row in `browser.selected_row` ⛔️
  - [if] no search is active [then] `browser.search` is null because nothing is typed, and a test distinguishes that from the field being unwired ⛔️
- [x] **AGENT-03**: Orders. `POST /api/v1/commands` accepts `single`, `sequence` (in order, stop on first error), `parallel` (caller-declared grouping across scopes), and `ramp` (continuous target, from current to value, over a `Duration`). Every order returns a result document with per-step status and the mirror delta.
  - [if] `sequence: [load deck1, play deck1, fader 1 to 0.8]` is posted [then] step 3 does not start before step 2 resolves ⛔️
  - [if] `parallel: [play deck1, play deck2]` is posted [then] both transport schedules share one `commonSyncScheduleTimes` anchor ⛔️
  - [if] `ramp: eq deck2 low to -0.3 over {beats:4}` is posted [then] the EQ reaches -0.3 within 1 beat-grid tolerance of the 4th beat on the clock deck ⛔️
- [x] **AGENT-04**: Beat time. `Duration = {unit: beats|bars|phrases|ms, n, anchor?: next_beat|next_downbeat|next_phrase, clock?: deck|master}` resolves against the named clock deck's PQTZ grid (default master), replans ramp progress after tempo changes, and lifts real `AnlzPhrase` boundaries into the mirror.
  - [if] the clock deck's tempo changes during a 4-bar ramp [then] the ramp re-plans and still ends on the target bar ⛔️
  - [if] a deck has no beat grid [then] a beats order fails with `no_grid`, never silently falls back to seconds ⛔️
- [x] **AGENT-05** (shipped Thu 10 Sep 2026; installed launcher Tue 15 Sep 2026): CLI. `opendj` console script (`[project.scripts]`) in a repo checkout, and the installed payload ships `payload/bin/opendj` with the same environment contract as `opendj-engine`, running `apps.opendj_cli` without manual PYTHONPATH. `opendj install-cli` idempotently symlinks the bundled launcher to `~/.local/bin/opendj` without sudo. Thin client of AGENT-03: `opendj state`, `opendj deck 1 play`, `opendj eq 2 low 0.2 --over 4beats`, `opendj do "load 1 <id>" then "play 1" and "play 2"`. `--json` everywhere. Verb ids seeded from `QuickDrawActionId`. Values are the bus's own control units (0..1, 0.5 flat for EQ/TRIM/FILTER), so an out-of-domain value is refused before dispatch.
  - [if] the engine payload is built [then] bin/opendj exists, is executable, and runs apps.opendj_cli with the payload env contract ⛔️
  - [if] opendj install-cli is run when ~/.local/bin/opendj is absent or already points at the bundled launcher [then] it succeeds idempotently ⛔️
  - [if] ~/.local/bin/opendj exists and points somewhere else [then] install-cli refuses loudly naming both paths ⛔️
  - [if] `opendj` is run through the symlink install-cli made (or any chain of absolute or relative links to a payload launcher) [then] the launcher resolves the link and runs the payload's own runtime and manifest ⛔️ (fixed Tue 15 Sep 2026: an earlier launcher derived its payload from the link's directory and died looking for `~/.local/runtime/bin/python3`)
  - [if] a command exists in the bus [then] `opendj --list-verbs` names it ⛔️
  - [if] the engine is not running [then] the CLI exits 2 with the lock-file path it checked ⛔️
  - [if] a page claims an order and reports `succeeded` while the control it names has not moved in the mirror [then ⛔️] the CLI exits 4 naming the mirror path it read, never `done`
  - [if] the engine is up and no performance page is open [then ⛔️] the CLI exits 3 and says no page is open, rather than holding the order open
  - [if] the mirror names no control the command moves (`slip`, `cue`, a stem command) [then ⛔️] the verdict is `accepted`, never `confirmed`: a deck nothing touched reads `desired_revision == presented_revision` and satisfies the presentation clock without the command having done anything, so a settled clock rules a fault OUT and never rules the effect IN
  - [if] a successful `unload` clears the deck title to null [then ⛔️] the CLI confirms it, rather than reading null as "the control never moved" and exiting 4 on every eject
  - [if] one run writes the same mirrored control twice (`do "play 1" then "pause 1"`) [then ⛔️] only the last write is required of the final mirror, so a sequence that ran perfectly confirms instead of waiting out the settle deadline
  - [if] a `load` reports `succeeded` onto a deck that already holds another track [then ⛔️] the CLI confirms against the `stable_id` the mirror publishes, not the mere presence of a title, so a load that never landed exits 4 instead of confirming the previous track
  - [if] a ramp lasts longer than the request deadline (`--over 120000ms`, 32 bars) [then ⛔️] the deadline grows to outlast the ramp the CLI itself asked for, because the page holds a ramp order open for its whole duration; `--timeout` still floors it for a wedged page
  - [if] a beat-relative ramp is sized (`--over 32bars`) [then ⛔️] the wait is computed from the LIVE grid, the clock deck's published `effective_bpm`, never from an assumed tempo: the pitch fader's ±100% range admits ratios down toward zero, so no constant BPM is an upper bound and a healthy ramp on a slowed deck would exit 5
  - [if] the mirror cannot say what the ramp will travel at (no master elected, the clock deck stopped, no tempo yet) [then ⛔️] `--timeout` stands unchanged, because each of those is an order the page refuses outright rather than holds open
  - [if] `--json` is given and argparse itself refuses the invocation (`--anchor bogus`) [then ⛔️] the refusal is a JSON error document on stdout, not plain usage text on stderr
  - [if] a script runs several groups (`do "play 1" then "unload 1"`) [then ⛔️] each group is confirmed against the mirror it left, so a later command's side effects (an unload clears `playing` as well as the title) cannot invalidate an earlier group's check and exit 4 on a run that did exactly what it was asked
  - [if] a BEAT-RELATIVE ramp names an anchor (`--over 4beats --anchor next_phrase`) [then ⛔️] the request deadline covers the pre-anchor wait as well as the travel, because the page holds the order open for both; an `ms` ramp is not padded for its anchor, because the page measures that one against the wall clock and starts it at once
  - [if] a scripted command quotes a text value containing spaces (`do "hot_cue_save 1 A 100 rev-1 \"cue for the drop\""`) [then ⛔️] the value reaches the bus whole, exactly as the same value does on the command line
  - [if] `--json` reports a dispatch [then ⛔️] the document names `request_timeout_s`, the deadline the CLI actually used, so an agent reads it rather than inferring it from `--timeout`
  - [if] a group in a script does not confirm (`do "load 1 <id>" then "play 1"` where the load never lands) [then ⛔️] the script STOPS there and the remaining groups are reported skipped, because the deck still holds the previous track and playing it puts the wrong music in the room before the CLI can exit 4
  - [if] a script's groups reach different verdicts (`do "play 1" then "slip 1 true"`) [then ⛔️] the run reports the WEAKEST of them, so one confirmed group never speaks for a group only `accepted`, whichever order they ran in
  - [if] a deadline flag is given a value no elapsed time can pass (`--settle nan`, `inf`, a negative) [then ⛔️] it is refused at parse with exit 1, because a NaN deadline loses every comparison and would poll the mirror forever instead of exiting 4
  - [if] a Duration magnitude is not a finite number (`--over infms`, `1e309ms`, `nanms`) [then ⛔️] it is refused at parse with exit 1 naming finiteness, because an infinite duration becomes an infinite request deadline: the same never-expiring wait by another road, and the `ms` path never reached the whole-number check that incidentally caught the beat units
  - [if] the invocation is malformed and no engine is running (`opendj frobnicate` with the app closed) [then ⛔️] the CLI exits 1 with the usage error, not 2, because a typo is not an environmental fault and a caller must be able to validate a command's syntax offline
  - [if] a beat-relative ramp times out AND the clock deck has slowed since the deadline was sized [then ⛔️] the error says so and names both tempos, because a slowed clock and a wedged page demand opposite responses and only the first is fixed by a larger `--timeout`; the deadline itself stays a snapshot, since the engine holds the order request open and exposes no order-status route to poll
  - [if] `--json` reports a ramp [then ⛔️] the document names `ramp_clock_bpm`, the tempo the deadline was computed from, so an agent can see why the deadline is the length it is
  - [if] an agent runs `opendj --help` or `opendj --list-verbs` [then] `install-cli` appears with a one-line description [⛔️]
  - [if] `opendj --json track key-segments <unknown stable_id>` runs [then] exit code is nonzero and `error.code` is `not_found` [⛔️]
  - [if] the lock's `role` is not `opendj-engine` [then] `opendj` and MCP `status`/`command` refuse before dispatch with exit 2 ⛔️
  - [if] lock `boot_id` disagrees with `GET /api/v1/health` `boot_id` [then] refuse with `engine_identity_mismatch`, naming lock path, both ids, and port ⛔️
  - [if] the port answers but health is missing or not an engine JSON document [then] refuse as `engine_not_running` or `engine_identity_mismatch`, never `order_rejected`, and never echo raw HTML ⛔️
- [x] **AGENT-06**: Pixel and AX path. Every interactive control has a deck-scoped accessible name (`play deck 1`), `role`, `aria-pressed`/`aria-valuenow` where applicable, and a `data-testid`; deck and channel containers carry `role="group" aria-label`. The MCP `stateOf` emits pressed and value. Rationale includes the four identical `play` buttons a computer-use agent sees today.
  - [if] an AX-tree agent asks for "play deck 3" [then] exactly one node matches ⛔️
- **AGENT-07**: Shipped-build seam (D4, open). Either the WebDriver seam ships in release behind an explicit opt-in (env var plus a visible banner), or agents are limited to the debug shell. Default proposal: ship it opt-in; the seam is loopback-only. Not queued for build until this is decided.
- [x] **AGENT-08**: Process naming. Every Open DJ process (shell, engine, dev servers, workers, sidecars) is identifiable in `ps` by `opendj-` in `argv[0]` or a `--name opendj-<role>` argument, and writes its role and port into the engine lock file. Shipped.
  - [if] `pgrep -f opendj-` runs [then] every process the app started is listed ⛔️
- [x] **AGENT-09**: Two AGENT-06 gaps closed (shipped): `HeadphoneCluster`'s "I/O" button carries `aria-label="SHOW AUDIO I/O"` so an AX-tree agent can query it by accessible name, and `DeckHeader`'s unload control is gated on `deck.stable_id !== null` rather than on artwork load state, so a loaded deck with missing or failed artwork still exposes a reachable, clickable unload control instead of collapsing to an inert placeholder.
  - [if] the I/O control is queried by accessible name "SHOW AUDIO I/O" [then] it is found ⛔️
  - [if] a deck has a track loaded whose artwork is missing or fails to load [then] the unload control still renders and is clickable ⛔️
  - [if] artwork is present [then] the unload control's rendering is unchanged ⛔️

- [x] **AGENT-10** (Thu 10 Sep 2026): the mirror carries audio health DURABLY. Two defects made a
  live outage invisible to an agent. (1) EPHEMERAL: `ui-mirror.ts` mapped the LIVE toast store,
  and toasts dismiss after ~5s while the mirror publishes every 1000ms, so the operator watched
  several audio errors on screen while the mirror published `toasts: []`. (2) MISSING: the
  `output-health-bar` a human reads at `TopBar.svelte:605` renders `audioOutputHealth.snapshot`,
  and that reading was mirrored nowhere, which is an AGENT-02 parity defect on its own terms
  ("what a human reads off the screen, not a subset"). `audio_health` now carries that snapshot,
  the `describeAudioOutputHealth` class and hover text verbatim so screen and mirror cannot
  disagree, the silence verdict, a meter reading STAMPED with its age, and `recent_faults` read
  from the durable perf-event ring. `master.rms` alone can never answer "is audio leaving the
  machine": it taps `_masterGain` (`audio-engine.svelte.ts:678-679`), upstream of
  `_masterMuteGain -> ctx.destination` (`:689-690`), measured live at 0.4687 while master mute
  was TRUE and the room was silent.
  - [if] an audio fault fired longer ago than the toast lifetime [then] it is still readable in `audio_health.recent_faults` with its age ⛔️
  - [if] no output snapshot exists yet [then] `audio_health.display.cssClass` is `unknown`, never `ok` ⛔️
  - [if] the master RMS reading is older than METER_FRESH_MAX_MS [then] `audio_health.meter.fresh` is false, so a frozen high rms cannot read as live signal ⛔️
  - [if] the meter age is unknown [then] `fresh` is false, because an absent measurement must never render as a good one ⛔️
  - [if] a perf event is stamped in the future [then] the block throws rather than reporting a negative age and silently reordering the timeline ⛔️
  - [if] any module records a perf event at `error` severity [then] it escalates to the server log, whatever its kind: escalation is gated on severity alone and there is no kind VALUE allowlist to drift ⛔️
  - [if] an error toast is pushed [then] it reaches the server log EXACTLY ONCE, through the context-rich report `pushToast` already sends: two reports of one failure cannot merge (`reportClientError` fingerprints on kind:source:message and both halves differ) and the second write can be erased by an in-flight flush, so the richer of the two is the one that goes missing ⛔️
  - [if] a report is raised while a client-error POST is in flight [then] it survives the flush rather than being overwritten by a queue snapshot taken before the await ⛔️
  - [if] unrelated ring traffic follows an audio fault [then] the fault is still in `recent_faults`: audio-health kinds carry their own retention budget instead of sharing the eight-row remainder with toast, timing and SUCCESS rows, or the durability this requirement claims would only have moved the same emptiness one layer down ⛔️
  - [if] the escalator throws [then] the exception is contained and the ring row survives, because the error-reporting path must never take down the code reporting the error ⛔️ ⛔️
  - [if] `scripts/audio_output_probe.py` orders a play/pause toggle [then] it confirms the ENGINE-PUBLISHED `playing`, agreeing presentation-clock revisions, AND the clock source that belongs to that direction (`audio_output` for play, `paused_cursor` for pause) before sampling, refusing the measurement otherwise: the command bus answered `succeeded` while `playing` stayed false during this very outage, and both halves of an A/B pair sampled in one transport state let room noise decide the verdict ⛔️
  - [if] the confirmation is keyed on the mirror's `trust` label [then] it is wrong for a PAUSE: `deckTransportClock` publishes `source: 'paused_cursor'` whenever transport is inactive, so every paused deck is labeled `untrusted` and every OFF sample would wait out its timeout, leaving the probe unable to measure anything at all ⛔️
  - [if] the acoustic sign test is unanimous in NEITHER direction [then] the probe returns UNKNOWN, not NOT AUDIBLE: failing to establish AUDIBLE is not evidence of silence, and 5 of 6 pairs showing signal must not send an outage hunt after a dead output ⛔️
  - [if] the probe moved a deck [then] the deck's entry transport state is restored even when a capture or a later command fails, because it runs against a live app ⛔️
  - [if] an audio-domain row reports HEALTH rather than a failure (`audio-context`, `audio-output-alive`, `audio-output-rebound`, `presentation-clock-recovered`) [then] it is neither published in `recent_faults` nor charged to the audio-fault retention budget: selecting on the `audio-` prefix made a healthy startup publish a nonempty fault timeline, and sixteen recovery rows could evict the one outage the budget was reserved for ⛔️
  - [if] a ring row is read back after a reload [then] the severity its recording site judged is still on the row, so a fault and a recovery remain distinguishable by more than their name; a row written before severity was persisted reports `unknown`, never healthy ⛔️
  - [if] the master analyser is absent during graph initialization or teardown [then] `audio_health.meter` publishes `rms: null` and `fresh: false`: the full-scale value handed to the silence fold is a CONTROL VALUE that keeps a meterless graph from reading as a dropout, and stamping it as a measurement recreated the same misleading healthy-signal diagnosis this requirement exists to remove ⛔️
  - [if] the probe reads a presentation-clock field [then] that field name and the two clock-source literals are the ones `deckTransportClock` and `ui-mirror.ts` actually publish, checked against both production sources, so a rename on either side turns the acceptance red instead of leaving the probe reading `None` forever ⛔️
  - [if] a live engine is reachable [then] the probe's transport reading is exercised over the real `/api/v1/state/ui-mirror` HTTP path; when none is running the acceptance reports UNAVAILABLE rather than standing up a stand-in engine, because a fabricated `succeeded` is the exact input class whose mistreatment is under test ⛔️

- [x] **AGENT-11**: Shipped MCP. `opendj mcp` stdio server in the dmg payload gives agents HTTP control of a running installed Open DJ without a repo checkout. Tools: `status`, `app_state`, `command`, `library`, `ui_url`, `open_route`, `update_check` (AGENT-13, read-only), `update_apply` (AGENT-13). Safety rails enforced server-side: master mute before play, writeback blocked, destructive library and update-apply calls gated.
  - [if] Open DJ is running and an agent runs `opendj mcp` from the bundled binary [then] `status` reports the lock port and healthy engine [⛔️]
  - [if] the engine is not running [then] `status` returns `engine_not_running` naming the lock path and never hangs [⛔️]
  - [if] an agent calls `command` with `master_mute` [then] the result includes a mirror delta [⛔️]
  - [if] an agent calls `library` against a writeback apply path [then] the server refuses before HTTP dispatch [⛔️]
  - [if] an agent calls `play` without prior master mute [then] the server prepends master mute or refuses, never audibly plays unmuted [⛔️]
  - [if] the desktop shell is on library/settings/playlist and an agent needs Performance [then] MCP `open_route` moves the shell to `/performance` and `client_open` becomes true (AGENT-12) [⛔️]
  - [if] `app_state` is called on a path the engine answers 404 or 5xx [then] the tool result has `isError: true` and names the status [⛔️]
  - [if] `tools/list` runs [then] every tool carries `readOnlyHint`, and `library` and `command` carry `destructiveHint` [⛔️]
  - [if] a tool returns a JSON document [then] `structuredContent` is that object, not a string holding it [⛔️]
  - [if] an agent calls `library GET` on a paginated list route with no `?limit=` [then] the result stays under the 20k-token MCP budget via an auto-limited page, with `next_cursor` and an `mcp_note` explaining how to page the rest [⛔️]
  - [if] `library GET` returns a JSON body [then] `body` is embedded as an object, never as an escaped JSON string [⛔️]
  - [if] `library GET` still cannot fit under budget at the caller's own explicit `?limit=` [then] it refuses with `isError: true` naming the measured size, never passing the oversize body through [⛔️]
  - [if] a `library GET` path on a list route carries `?fields=stable_id,title,artist,bpm,key` [then] each row is projected to just those keys [⛔️]
  - [if] `opendj api` is called with a path outside `/api/v1/*` or containing `..` [then] it exits non-zero and `--json` reports `error.code: invalid_path` [⛔️]
  - [if] `opendj api` receives a 2xx body that is not JSON [then] it exits non-zero [⛔️]
  - [if] `library` is called with a path that builds a URL over httpx's length ceiling [then] the tool returns `isError: true` with `error: usage` and a readable message, never an unstructured `UnexpectedToolError` [⛔️]
  - [if] an agent runs `opendj --json status` against a running engine [then] the document matches MCP `status` on the same lock file [⛔️]

- [x] **AGENT-12**: Shell route navigation. `POST /api/v1/shell/navigate` queues a route for the installed desktop shell; only the shell webview (`OPENDJ_ENGINE_ORIGIN`) consumes it. `opendj open performance` and MCP `open_route` post the request and wait for `client_open: true`. Mirror-dependent CLI/MCP calls auto-ensure `/performance` before refusing.
  - [if] cold launch, setup dismissed, agent runs `opendj --json state` [then] mirror within 10 s without human click [⛔️]
  - [if] desktop on library/settings/playlist [then] `opendj open performance` / MCP `open_route` moves the shell to `/performance` and `client_open: true` [⛔️]
  - [if] no performance page after ensure [then] `no_performance_page` names `opendj open performance` [⛔️]
  - [if] bootstrap landing changes [then] `test_desktop_lane_config` pins the navigate target and shell-navigate integration proves mirror registration [⛔️]
  - [if] the shell is idle on `/performance` for 60s [then] the navigate poll (>=5s interval, paused on `document.hidden`, resumed on `visibilitychange`) writes at most 12 `engine.log` lines [⛔️ if ~300 lines appear]
  - [if] the engine is unreachable for 10s [then] the poll logs at most one "failing since T" record and no unhandled rejection reaches the console or client-error log [⛔️ if one record per tick]
  - [if] an agent's navigate moves the shell window [then] the shell shows a toast naming the move and the engine logs the same request [⛔️ if the move is silent]

- [x] **AGENT-14**: UI-mirror control addressability. The `controls` map on `/performance` holds one addressable entry per operable DOM control. Duplicate preferred names (`data-testid`, `aria-label`, or trimmed text) receive deterministic `#2`, `#3`, ... suffixes instead of silently overwriting earlier entries. Mixer channel stem chips use a `channel` testid namespace (`stem-vocal-channel-N`) so deck-panel ids (`stem-vocal-deck-N`) identify exactly one element.
  - [if] the performance screen holds N operable controls [then] the mirror's `controls` map holds N addressable entries, and a test asserts the two counts against each other rather than against a recorded number ⛔️
  - [if] two controls would key to the same name [then] the mirror distinguishes them rather than dropping one, and a test drives that exact case ⛔️
  - [if] an agent operates the control named `stem-vocal-deck-1` [then] exactly one element on screen answers to that name ⛔️

- [ ] **AGENT-13**: The updater is on the installed CLI and the MCP server. `opendj update check` and `opendj update apply` drive the packaged app's own update channel, and MCP `update_check` and `update_apply` drive the same two helpers over stdio, so a machine with only the installed app can be updated by an agent with no repo checkout. Both surfaces call `check_via_engine` and `apply_via_engine` in `apps.engine_core.update_channel`; neither re-implements the apply path.
  - [if] `opendj update check` runs against a running packaged app [then] it prints the channel status, the current version and the available version, and exits 0 only for `up-to-date` or `update-available`; any other status, including `ahead-of-channel` and an unreachable engine, exits non-zero with its `detail` [⛔️]
  - [if] `opendj update apply` runs while the check reports `update-available` [then] it posts `/api/v1/update/apply`, waits for the relaunch, prints the before and after `app_version` and `git_sha_full`, and exits 0 only once both changed to the announced version [⛔️]
  - [if] `opendj update apply` runs in any other state [then] it exits non-zero with the 409 `status` and `detail`, and posts nothing [⛔️]
  - [if] the shell never claims the order, or the relaunch never reports the announced build [then] apply exits non-zero at its own deadline instead of waiting forever or claiming success [⛔️]
  - [if] an agent lists MCP tools [then] `update_check` is read-only and `update_apply` is annotated destructive and refused with `destructive_blocked` unless the destructive environment allows it [⛔️]
  - [if] any refusal is returned over MCP [then] `isError` is true and the body carries the machine-readable status and detail [⛔️]
  - [if] `opendj --help` is printed [then] it lists both update verbs [⛔️]

### Audio Output Liveness (AUDIOLIVE)

Added Wed 9 Sep 2026 (recurrence). The output-rebind path shipped previously
recovers a graph whose device changed under it, but it treats its own
rate-limit as a filter: a request arriving inside `REBIND_COOLDOWN_MS` was
discarded outright. Evidence, from the packaged app's `com.apple.WebKit.GPU`
unified-log stream: at 17:44:43.5Z the system default output flipped
`BuiltInSpeakerDevice` -> a Bluetooth device, and back to
`BuiltInSpeakerDevice` at 17:44:45.4Z. The second edge - the one naming the
device the operator was actually listening on - landed 1.9s into a 10s cooldown
and was dropped with no cycle, no perf row and no toast. The same 1.9s flap
signature appears at 17:16:59Z / 17:17:01Z the same afternoon.

- [x] **AUDIOLIVE-01**: A device-change or output-stall rebind request that arrives inside the rebind cooldown is HELD and re-run when the cooldown expires, never discarded. One pending request at a time, latest reason wins, so the rate limit the cooldown exists for is unchanged: still at most one suspend/resume cycle per `REBIND_COOLDOWN_MS`. Suppression is recorded as an `audio-output-rebind-deferred` perf row rather than being silent.
  - [if] the output device flaps A -> B -> A inside one cooldown [then] the graph ends up re-bound for the LAST edge, not stranded on the middle one ⛔️
  - [if] ten device changes land inside one cooldown [then] exactly one extra suspend/resume cycle runs, coalesced - never ten ⛔️
  - [if] no deck is playing when the request lands [then] it is dropped rather than held: a cycle firing 10s after the operator stopped is noise, not a recovery ⛔️
  - [if] the route unmounts while a request is held [then] `uninstall` cancels it, so a closed context is never suspended ⛔️
- [x] **AUDIOLIVE-02**: A failed output rebind is recorded at ERROR severity and `audio-output-rebind-failed` is in `perf-event-log.ts`'s `ESCALATED_KINDS`, so it reaches `/api/v1/client-errors` and the engine's `webui-client-errors-*.log`. The whole rebind path was previously wired at `info`, which is why the 17:44Z cutout left no server-side trace at all.
  - [if] a rebind's `resume()` rejects [then] the perf row carries `error` severity and the escalator receives it ⛔️
  - [if] a rebind succeeds [then] its row stays `info` and does not spend a round trip ⛔️
- [x] **AUDIOLIVE-03**: The playing gate applies when a rebind request LANDS - at the device-change or stall edge itself, captured by `request()` before its 400ms debounce, not after it - and never again when it runs, and a request that arrives while a suspend/resume is still in flight is held rather than returned on early, so neither the in-flight window nor a mid-cooldown pause can discard an already-accepted request. A rebind is two awaits against the very device that is disappearing, so the cycle routinely outlives the 400ms debounce; nothing downstream repairs a lost request, because `_resumeContext()` only calls `resume()` on a SUSPENDED context and this failure keeps the context `running`. The coalescing and the rate limit are unchanged: still at most one suspend/resume per `REBIND_COOLDOWN_MS`.
  - [if] a device change lands while an earlier rebind is still awaiting `resume()` [then] it is held and re-run once that cycle completes, with an `audio-output-rebind-deferred` row - never dropped in silence ⛔️
  - [if] the operator pauses after a request was accepted but before the cooldown expires [then] the held request still runs ⛔️
  - [if] the operator pauses during the 400ms debounce, after a device change that arrived while a deck was playing [then] the cycle still runs: there are three delays between the edge and the cycle (debounce, in-flight, cooldown) and acceptance is carried through all of them ⛔️
  - [if] no deck is playing when a request LANDS [then] it is still dropped rather than held - relaxing the gate on landing would cycle an idle graph on every device change ⛔️
- [x] **AUDIOLIVE-07** (shipped): `ESCALATED_KINDS` is a SUPERSET of every kind the audio-output modules record at `error` severity, checked rather than curated. `audio-output-dead` (the app's only device-level "no sound is leaving this machine" verdict) and `audio-output-dead-persistent` were both recorded at `error` and both absent from the set, so neither ever reached `/api/v1/client-errors`. AUDIOLIVE-02 added one row of four and the set then drifted below its own modules' severity with nothing to notice.
  - [if] the liveness poll declares the output dead [then] the row reaches `webui-client-errors-*.log` within the escalation window ⛔️
  - [if] an audio-output module records a NEW kind at `error` without adding it to the set [then] the superset guard reds ⛔️
  - [if] an emit site is written in a form the guard cannot decide (a kind held in a constant, a computed severity) [then] it is reported UNCLASSIFIED and the guard reds - a measurement that could not be taken must not render as a clean result ⛔️
  - [if] a row is recorded at `info` (a successful re-bind, say) [then] it still does not spend a round trip ⛔️
  - [if] a sustained dropout re-fires the same kind every poll [then] `ESCALATION_WINDOW_MS` still caps it at one POST per kind per minute ⛔️

- [x] **AUDIOLIVE-04**: The context watchdog's bounded resume schedule is RE-ARMED by outside edges, so running out of attempts is not terminal. `CONTEXT_RESUME_BACKOFF_MS` spans 9,050ms and `statechange` fires only on TRANSITIONS, so a context that went `interrupted` and STAYED `interrupted` fired once, failed six resumes against a device that was still gone, and was then retried by nothing: the liveness poll returns `idle` for any non-`running` context and `_resumeContext()` runs only from an explicit `play()`. Everything that really takes a device away -- a Bluetooth re-pair, a phone call, a screen lock, a backgrounded WKWebView -- outlasts nine seconds. `noteRecoveryOpportunity` is called on `visibilitychange` to visible and on `devicechange`, and each re-runs the SAME bounded schedule. The bound itself is unchanged: still at most `CONTEXT_RESUME_BACKOFF_MS.length` attempts per opportunity, because an unbounded main-thread resume loop is a second way to lose the audio it is trying to save.
  - [if] the resume schedule runs out and the device comes back later [then] a
    visibility or device-list edge re-runs the schedule and audio returns ⛔️
  - [if] one recovery opportunity arrives [then] it buys exactly ONE bounded schedule,
    never an open-ended retry ⛔️
  - [if] the context is already running, or no deck is playing, when an opportunity
    arrives [then] nothing is resumed: `devicechange` fires on every headphone plug ⛔️
  - [if] the route unmounts [then] the watchdog's recovery listener is dropped by
    identity, so a later opportunity never resumes a closed context ⛔️
- [x] **AUDIOLIVE-05**: A slow endurance soak proves the PRESENCE of sound across a MODELED hostile output device, in its own tier. Coverage is of the shipped DECISION path under modeled stimuli, not of a real device or a real processor crash; the two unavailable capabilities are named below rather than recorded as shipped. `just test-audio-soak [minutes]` (default 10) plays real audio through the shipped `installOutputRebind` and `installAudioContextWatchdog` against a real `AudioContext` and a modeled output device, injecting device flaps inside the cooldown, ten-change bursts, a direct `ctx.suspend()` standing in for an OS suspend, an invocation of the shipped `onprocessorerror` handler standing in for a worklet crash (a real one is UNAVAILABLE: only the browser raises `processorerror`), and idle/played transitions. A real `AnalyserNode` downstream of the modeled device samples RMS every 100ms and the suite FAILS when the signal stays under `SILENCE_RMS_FLOOR` for longer than two `REBIND_COOLDOWN_MS` while a deck is playing. The probe is downstream of the device on purpose: the master-bus silence watchdog and the master meter both tap `_masterGain`, upstream of the output, so neither can see this failure class at all. Never on the PR gate -- it is measured in minutes.
  - [if] a run is error-free but silent [then] it FAILS: the assertion is presence of
    sound, not absence of an error ⛔️
  - [if] the cooldown deferral is reverted to the earlier dropped-request behavior [then] the soak goes RED
    on the silence assertion, not on an instrument guard (proven by mutation) ⛔️
  - [if] the probe cannot report silence [then] the NEGATIVE CONTROL test fails first: it
    strands the device permanently and requires a silence run longer than the threshold ⛔️
  - [if] a run never rises above the RMS floor, produces too few samples, fires no hostile
    events, or never records an `audio-output-rebind-deferred` row [then] it FAILS as an
    unmeasured run rather than passing as a healthy one ⛔️
  - [if] hostile events are spaced closer than the failure threshold [then] a later
    event's suspend/resume rescues a stranded graph and the soak cannot tell recovery
    from accident: the gap is three cooldowns for that reason ⛔️
  - [if] a hostile event cannot actually be injected -- the meter does not arm, or the
    shipped `onprocessorerror` handler is absent [then] the soak FAILS naming it, rather
    than skipping that event and reporting a verdict on the rest ⛔️
  - UNAVAILABLE, stated not hidden (1): a real AudioWorklet processor crash cannot be
    provoked from JavaScript at all -- only the browser raises `processorerror`. The soak
    invokes the handler the shipped `attachMeterTaps` installed on the real node, which
    proves that handler runs and does not take the audio with it, and claims no more.
  - UNAVAILABLE, stated not hidden (2): the suite cannot detect Chromium remaining bound to
    a dead PHYSICAL output. Playwright cannot unpair a Bluetooth device or observe a real
    speaker, and the harness's `resume()` re-binds the modeled device by construction.
    What is proven is that the shipped DECISION path keeps a real measured signal arriving
    at the point the output device would sit -- which is where the earlier defect lived --
    not Chromium's own device handling downstream of it.
  - [if] a recovery edge accepted while a deck was playing is held across an operator pause
    [then] the held edge still runs and the context comes back running, or the soak fails
    naming the discarded edge (the `recoveryEdgeAcrossPause` event, AUDIOLIVE-06) ⛔️
  - [if] the sampler stops part way through a run [then] the coverage assertion FAILS: it is
    measured against the REQUESTED duration, never against `elapsedMs`, which the sampler
    writes itself and which therefore freezes with it ⛔️
  - [if] a run is asked for a duration too short to reach every hostile event [then] it
    OVERRUNS to finish one full pass rather than reporting a verdict on the events it
    skipped, and every scheduled event is asserted BY NAME against the harness's own list ⛔️

- [x] **AUDIOLIVE-06**: The context watchdog's playing gate applies when a recovery opportunity LANDS and never again when it runs, and a gesture-driven resume revives an `interrupted` context as well as a `suspended` one. Two halves of one failure. (a) An edge held because a bounded schedule was already running used to be re-gated on `isAnyDeckPlaying()` in that schedule's `finally`, so an operator pausing between the edge landing and the schedule finishing discarded it - and pausing is precisely what an operator does when the sound stops. This is the same defect recurring a third time, after `installOutputRebind`'s held request and its post-debounce gate; the fix is the same rule, that acceptance is decided once at the edge. (b) Nothing downstream repaired the loss, because `_resumeContext()` called `resume()` on a `suspended` context only and fell straight into its throw for `interrupted` - the state WebKit uses when the device is taken away, and the exact state this module exists for. `interrupted` is now attempted too, which is strictly a superset: every state that reached `resume()` still does, and `interrupted` previously reached an unconditional throw. `closed` is still excluded, because `resume()` on a closed context throws `InvalidStateError` and would replace the explicit failure message with a DOMException. The bound is unchanged: still at most `CONTEXT_RESUME_BACKOFF_MS.length` attempts per opportunity.
  - [if] the operator pauses after an edge was accepted but before the schedule holding it
    finishes [then] the held edge still runs - the context never changed state, so no
    further `statechange` is coming and that edge was the only news there was ⛔️
  - [if] no deck was playing when an opportunity LANDED [then] it is still dropped rather
    than held: `devicechange` fires on every headphone plug, and holding those would arm a
    bounded schedule against a graph nobody is listening to ⛔️
  - [if] a held edge finds the context came back on its own [then] it is still dropped -
    the context re-check is the one that cannot lose anything ⛔️
  - [if] the operator presses play on an `interrupted` context [then] `resume()` is
    attempted rather than skipped, so a schedule that ran out is not the last word ⛔️
  - [if] the gesture path is pointed at a `closed` context [then] it still throws the
    explicit "did not enter running state" error rather than a DOMException ⛔️

- [x] **AUDIOLIVE-08** (shipped): A device-level liveness verdict, structurally disjoint from mixer silence. Both existing instruments -- `master-silence-report.ts`'s `silent-while-playing` and the master meter -- tap `_masterGain`, upstream of the actual output device, so during a device-level outage both read a healthy signal for the whole time the room hears nothing; during the Wed 9 Sep 2026 17:44Z Bluetooth flap `silent-while-playing` never fired. `output-device-watchdog.ts` (`foldDeviceLivenessSample`) composes `audio-output-liveness.ts`'s own debounced verdict -- that `outputLatency` read 0 for `LIVENESS_DEAD_POLLS` consecutive polls while a deck played, the same measurement that caught the real Wed 2 Sep 2026 incident -- rather than inventing a new probe or a `sinkId`/`enumerateDevices()` reconciliation (`sinkId` reconciliation has no production evidence for this pipeline and the app never calls `setSinkId` on the master output, so a sink id alone cannot distinguish "still default" from "default changed"). An earlier revision of the fold also required the presentation-clock stall detector (`observePresentedTransportTimeline`'s `contextTime`-vs-`performanceTime` divergence) as a co-signal, but that requirement was found wrong in both directions: a `clock_source !== 'sample'` filter discarded exactly the stalls a dead device produces, and even the unfiltered stall requirement missed the real Wed 2 Sep 2026 incident outright -- `outputLatency` read dead while the HAL clock (`contextTime`) kept advancing. A signal absent from the one production incident this requirement exists to catch cannot be a required co-signal, so `outputLatencyDead` alone is the gate now. `foldDeviceLivenessSample` fires `device-unreachable` only when a deck is playing AND `outputLatency` has read dead AND the master bus is still producing signal at or above `SILENCE_RMS_FLOOR`, so it can never fire on the same reading `silent-while-playing` does -- the two verdicts are structurally disjoint, not merely usually different. Both gate `decks[id].audible` in the UI mirror and each carries its own toast id, so "the room is hearing nothing" and "the mixer is quiet" render as distinguishable states rather than collapsing into one. Exercised in `just test-audio-soak` via a `masterAnalyser` tapped upstream of the modeled `deviceGate` (independent of the harness's existing downstream `analyser`) and the real `ctx.outputLatency` -- NOT a modeled or fabricated latency provider. Playwright cannot actually unbind the browser's output device, so `outputLatencyDead` stays real-but-non-triggering for the whole run and `deviceUnreachableVerdicts`/`longestDeviceUnreachableMs` are asserted to stay at exactly 0, stated as UNAVAILABLE rather than left to look like an unexercised gap; the fold's decision logic is proven separately in `output-device-watchdog.test.mjs` against synthetic `outputLatencyDead` inputs a live browser cannot supply, which is proof of the FOLD LOGIC only, not a validated real-device-loss run -- that capability stays UNAVAILABLE until a harness that can actually take a device away exists.
  - [if] the graph is producing signal but the bound device is gone [then] `decks[id].audible`
    is false and `toasts` carries `output-device-unreachable`, distinct from
    `silent-while-playing` -- proven against synthetic `outputLatencyDead` inputs in
    `output-device-watchdog.test.mjs` (fold-logic proof); UNAVAILABLE against a real device
    loss, which no harness here can produce ⛔️
  - [if] the master bus is genuinely silent [then] `silent-while-playing` fires exactly as
    before and `device-unreachable` does not, because the fold requires signal at or above
    `SILENCE_RMS_FLOOR` ⛔️
  - [if] the per-frame master RMS reading is unavailable when the liveness check runs
    [then] `noteMasterSilence()` does not throw: it substitutes `masterRms = 1` and folds
    `playing = false` into both watchdogs, so the unmeasured frame resets each run rather than
    being counted as either silence or a device outage -- unmeasured is reported as unmeasured,
    never fabricated as a verified-healthy reading ⛔️
  - [if] a device outage is followed by recovery [then] the fold's `reported` flag resets on
    the next sample where `outputLatencyDead` reads false, so a second outage fires a second
    verdict rather than staying silently latched on the first ⛔️
  - UNAVAILABLE, stated not hidden: `just test-audio-soak` cannot make Playwright's real output
    device report a dead latency, the same limitation already recorded against AUDIOLIVE-05's
    `deviceGate` model, so `deviceUnreachableVerdicts`/`longestDeviceUnreachableMs` are asserted
    to stay at exactly 0 rather than left to look like an unexercised gap.

- [x] **AUDIOLIVE-10** (shipped): Unexpected-pause toasts are human-readable while raw diagnostics remain in the perf log and client-error queue. `source-ended-early` names the deck, stop time as `m:ss`, and the track's listed end; the diagnostic row carries both decoded and metadata durations. Formatter unit tests cover all four causes.
  - [if] a deck pauses with cause `source-ended-early` [then] the toast names the deck, stop time as `m:ss`, and the listed length (e.g. `Deck 2 stopped at 0:29, before the track's listed end (4:12). The audio file may be cut short.`) ⛔️
  - [if] any unexpected-pause cause fires [then] the raw `cause=... position_ms=...` line is logged for diagnosis but is not the toast text ⛔️
  - [if] `source-ended-early` fires [then] the logged line carries both decoded buffer duration and metadata duration ⛔️
  - [if] the formatter is unit-tested [then] each of the four causes has coverage and no toast message contains raw diagnostic key/value fields ⛔️
  - [if] a deck is paused and seeked (or cue-jumped, or sync re-anchored) while that pause is still in flight [then] no unexpected-pause row or toast fires: only a stop request onto a deck whose standing intent was to play is a falling edge, so a schedule that re-states `active: false` on an already-paused deck is never classified (found Fri 2 Oct 2026, pause + seek to 0:00 raised "stopped at 0:01, before the decoded audio ends" 3 of 3 times) ⛔️

- [x] **AUDIOLIVE-12** (shipped): Silence watchdog ignores master-bus silence that the mixer explains. Each claimed-live deck's playhead RMS is scaled by its linear gain to the master bus (trim x channel fader x crossfader x master, or 0 when every stem part of a ready bundle is gained to zero), and master silence is content, not a cut, when the sum across those decks is below `SILENCE_RMS_FLOOR`. A deck whose path is closed never has its PCM read; an absent or unreadable gain, or non-finite PCM in the window, never explains silence. EQ is not counted, so a deck killed only on EQ still reads as open.
