- [x] **AUDIOLIVE-11** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026): Deck state does not depend on animation frames. A browser stops firing `requestAnimationFrame` for a hidden, minimized or occluded page while the AudioContext keeps rendering, and the engine's presentation loop published `audible`, `transport_pending`, the position mirror, the natural-end stop, the safety-loop re-arm and Beat Sync phase correction only from a frame. So a deck paused in a hidden tab stayed `audible` for ever, `anyDeckPlaying()` never cleared (stem decode width, background shed and every "no deck audible" gate stayed held), and `unload()` awaited a frame that never came. Frames remain the paint clock. `src/lib/rb/frame-backstop.ts` adds the clocks that do not stop with them: an audio-clock wake (the `ended` event of a muted source stopped at the context time a transport change reaches the output, which page timer throttling does not delay), a 100 ms timer that runs the loop when its pending frame was never delivered, and a presented-stop wait for `unload()` that publishes from the audio clock itself and rejects with `PresentedStopTimeoutError` at 2000 ms (recorded at error severity as `deck-unload-stop-timeout`, after which the deck is still unloaded). The native-engine position mirror and the preset presented/stopped waits use the same module. The audio-Hz meter counts painted frames only, so a hidden tab does not read as a 10 Hz fault.
  - [if] a playing deck is paused while the tab is hidden [then] `audible` and `anyDeckPlaying()` go false once the stop reaches the output, and not before it does ⛔️
  - [if] a deck that has played is unloaded while the tab is hidden [then] `unload()` resolves and the deck is empty, without waiting out its deadline ⛔️
  - [if] the tab is hidden and page timers are throttled away [then] pause still clears `audible` and `unload()` still resolves, both on the audio clock ⛔️
  - [if] a deck keeps playing in a hidden tab [then] it stays `audible` and its published position keeps advancing ⛔️
  - [if] the output never presents a stop [then] `unload()` ends at its 2000 ms deadline with a recorded error and the deck is unloaded, never a silent hang ⛔️
  - [if] the tab is visible [then] the backstop never runs the loop and no audio-clock wake is allocated ⛔️
  - [if] a non-component module references `requestAnimationFrame` outside the allowlist in `tests/unit/raf-non-visual-lint.test.mjs`, or an allowlisted module gains a reference [then] the unit suite fails and names the file ⛔️

### Agent-Native Parity Law (PARITY)

### CloudSync Status (CSSTATUS)

- [x] **CLOUDSYNC-01** (shipped Tue 8 Sep 2026): `apps.cloud.policy.CFG` is one data-only, entitlement-selected CloudSync policy loaded from `data/state/cloudsync-policy.json`, with `MUSIC_DJ_CLOUDSYNC_MODE` as its explicit deployment override. It answers the canonical source, target R2 key scheme, local cache path, per-machine-class default mode, cache budget, and eviction rule for `audio`, `stem_bundle`, `anlz_cache`, `vocal_cache`, `lyrics_cache`, and `karaoke_words`; `just cloudsync-policy` prints that resolved object. No runtime caller may pass or choose cloud versus local: wiring must obtain the entitlement-selected config and consume `CFG` only. Cloud permits remote processing and makes R2 canonical; local forbids remote processing and makes every artifact local and pinned.
  - [if] the selected mode is cloud [then] every listed artifact reports R2 as source of truth and remote processing allowed ⛔️
  - [if] the selected mode is local [then] every listed artifact reports local-machine truth, no R2 key, pinned defaults, and remote processing forbidden ⛔️
  - [if] a caller attempts to select a mode through a policy API [then ⛔️] no such runtime API exists; only the state config and explicit environment override select it

- [x] **CLOUDSYNC-02** (shipped Tue 8 Sep 2026): Every archival stem publish rail derives its R2 key from the exact source-body SHA-256 through `apps.cloud.r2_keys.asset_object_key`, uses the `assets/<sha256[:2]>/<sha256>` layout, and refuses a local source changed after planning; a fresh destination listing must confirm the expected size before success.
  - [if] two archival sources have identical bytes [then] both derive the same R2 key and a rerun skips the verified object ⛔️
  - [if] a local source changes between planning and upload [then ⛔️] the rail refuses it and requires a re-plan
  - [if] a destination object is missing or has a different size after publish [then ⛔️] the rail reports failure rather than success
  - [if] a remote source is swapped for a same-size file during the remote rail's hash-then-upload window [then ⛔️] a post-upload re-hash detects the byte mismatch and the rail reports failure rather than journaling the corrupt mapping

- [x] **CLOUDSYNC-03** (shipped Wed 9 Sep 2026, cloudsync P0 core split; legacy `track_fields` stamp fallback shipped Tue 15 Sep 2026; v15 stamp backfill changelog re-offer shipped Tue 15 Sep 2026; once-only indexed v15 backfill shipped Wed 16 Sep 2026; hub changelog stamp-disagreement repair shipped Wed 16 Sep 2026): A STORED timestamp the sync protocol cannot order quarantines its own row and, transitively, the rows that reference it, and every other row still syncs; the same value arriving OFF THE WIRE is still refused. Legacy `track_fields` rows with NULL `updated_at` order by normalized `modified_at` until migration v15 backfills `updated_at` from it, so value-equal rows that differ only in importer provenance converge after one sync round instead of halting on `SyncDigestMismatch`. Migration v15 and any future stamp backfill append exactly one active-role changelog row per backfilled row (`hub_changelog` when `MDT_IS_HUB=1`, else `local_changelog`), including a one-time re-offer for databases already upgraded previously; the legacy hub-newer case then converges in one sync round with a quiet second round. The v15 repair records completion in `schema_meta_markers`, uses one indexed set-based membership query before acquiring the writer lock, and never rescans `track_fields` on ordinary opens. `hub_changelog` and `local_changelog` carry a `(table_name, row_pk)` index (migration v16). When a hub's latest `hub_changelog` row for a synced key carries a stamp that disagrees with the live domain row (including the EPOCH comparison sentinel), migration v17's one-shot `repair_hub_changelog_stamps` appends a fresh sequence with the live stamp and origin so spokes whose `last_pull_seq` already passed the bad entry still converge; candidate discovery is one set-based join taken before the writer lock, completion is recorded in `schema_meta_markers`, a second sync round is quiet, and LWW still rejects a re-offered hub row older than the spoke's own edit. The count is reported on `SyncResult`, `ApplyResult`, `ChangeBatch` and the `/push`, `/pull` and `/digest` payloads, and the offending value is logged verbatim. Nothing substitutes a value for it: `python -m apps.shared.state.normalize_stamps --live` is the only exit.

  - [if] an incoming playlist would replace a membership bundle whose stored stamps cannot be compared [then ⛔️] the whole playlist is held and the local bundle is byte-identical afterwards

- [x] **CLOUDSYNC-04** (shipped Wed 9 Sep 2026, cloudsync P0 core split): The push fence never steps over a row that did not reach the peer. A row this machine held back keeps its changelog entry above the fence (a full offer re-logs what it held, a fenced offer stops one seq below it), and a peer that decided fewer rows than it was offered holds the fence where it was.

  - [if] every offered row arrives [then] the fence advances to the ceiling, or the fix is a fence that re-offers the library forever ⛔️

Its output reports the repairs and the reset separately.

- [x] **CLOUDSYNC-06** (shipped Wed 9 Sep 2026, cloudsync P0 core split): A staged CloudSync rollout is safe in BOTH orders. A hub answers a caller that has not advertised the `quarantine/v1` capability exactly as `origin/main` would -- HTTP 422 `SYNC_PROTOCOL`, whole batch rolled back -- on `/push`, `/pull` and `/digest`, because an un-upgraded spoke reads `accepted + rejected < offered` as nothing at all and steps its push fence over the held row. The advertisement rides every request that can be answered partially and is never remembered from `hello`, so a spoke rolled back to an older build stops being capable the moment it rolls back.

  - [if] a caller advertises an empty list, an unrelated token or `quarantine/v2` [then ⛔️] it is refused, because an absent or near-miss advertisement is never consent

  - [if] the status headline renders a transport failure [then] it never shows a bare `HTTP 502` with no cause, [else stop]

- [x] **CLOUDSYNC-20** (shipped Tue 15 Sep 2026): The engine CloudSync scheduler (`apps/webui/server/cloudsync_scheduler.py`) exponential-backoffs on hub timeout/5xx/unreachable like it already does for `update_required`; it must not retry at the base interval for hours. Observe-mode missing credential shows a **single** re-enroll notice on status until resolved.
  - [if] scheduled sync fails on hub transport three times [then] wait intervals grow to at least 300s by the third tick, [else stop]
  - [if] the hub reads the credential as missing in observe mode [then] status shows one re-enroll notice and logs warn once per process, [else stop]

- [x] **CLOUDSYNC-21** (shipped Tue 15 Sep 2026): ``POST /api/v1/sync/push`` runs offered ``sync_policies`` and ``playlist_pins`` rows through the same :func:`apps.sync_hub.policy_store.evaluate` gate as ``PUT /api/v1/cloudsync/policies`` before writing; invalid ``cache_budget_mb`` values 422 ``SYNC_POLICY_VIOLATION`` and never enter ``hub_changelog``.
  - [if] a push offers ``sync_policies`` with ``cache_budget_mb <= 0`` [then] the hub 422s naming the ``cache_budget`` violation, [else stop]
  - [if] a push offers ``cache_budget_mb`` while ``mode != cached`` [then] the hub 422s naming the ``cache_budget`` violation, [else stop]
  - [if] a policy row already violates cache-budget rules before this fix ships [then] ``POST /api/v1/cloudsync/policies/validate`` surfaces it, [else stop]
- [x] **CLOUDSYNC-22** (shipped Tue 15 Sep 2026): Sync hub machine registry fields are bounded on the wire; oversize hello/push/enroll input is refused with 422; legacy oversized names in sqlite are clamped in hello/pull/status fleet snapshots.
  - [if] a hello's `machine.name` exceeds a sane bound (e.g. 256 chars) [then] the hub 422s the request, [else stop]
  - [if] a machine row already holds an oversized name from before this fix [then] hello/push/pull responses do not re-inflate on its account, [else stop]

- [x] **CLOUDSYNC-23** (shipped Wed 16 Sep 2026): `prepare_spoke_identity` commits a spoke's local content-identity remap in bounded batches of `IDENTITY_REMAP_BATCH_ROWS` (200) pairs, never as one write transaction spanning the whole backlog, so a 900+ row backlog costs at most one batch's rework on a lock conflict rather than the whole sync round. Each batch takes the write lock with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`; a batch that cannot acquire it within `busy_timeout` retries with backoff (`0.25s, 0.5s, 1.0s`) before raising `apps.shared.state.db.StateStoreBusyError`, whose message is prefixed `STATE_DB_BUSY:` and names the operation, the batch index/count, the attempt count, and the effective `busy_timeout` so it is grep-distinguishable in `cloudsync/status` from a `SyncDigestMismatch`. This is a reliability fix to how an existing remap commits, not a change to CLOUDSYNC-07's identity-merge rules.
  - [if] `prepare_spoke_identity` cannot take the write lock within `busy_timeout` [then] it retries with backoff and the sync round completes rather than raising out of `run_sync`, [else stop]
  - [if] a spoke carries a 900+ row remap backlog [then] it commits in batches of at most `IDENTITY_REMAP_BATCH_ROWS`, never as one transaction across the whole backlog, [else stop]
  - [if] the remap cannot proceed after its retries are exhausted [then] the raised `StateStoreBusyError` names the lock holder (self-contention, same process) and the operation, and its `STATE_DB_BUSY:`-prefixed message is distinguishable from a digest-mismatch message in `cloudsync/status`, [else stop]

### Stem Bundle Hydration (STEM)

Added Mon 14 Sep 2026 (ADR-0024): many tracks in a typical library
have a 4-stem demucs bundle on another machine but not on this one, and the loader accepts v1 mp3/flac parts once they exist locally. STEM covers pulling those bundles from
R2 on demand (deck load) and in bulk (CLI/HTTP parity), bounded by the local cache budget, without
ever blocking the track's own audio load.

- [x] **STEM-09** (shipped Mon 14 Sep 2026, ADR-0024): `apps.cloud.stem_index.build_index_from_journal`
  derives a `{stable_id: {filename: sha256}}` map from the existing R2 push rail's journal
  (`data/state/stem-r2-migration.jsonl`, written by `scripts/local_stems_to_r2.py`), the smallest
  correct mapping from a stable_id to its part hashes.
  - [if] the journal has (legacy_key, key) pairs for a stable_id's manifest and parts [then] the
    index maps that stable_id's filenames to their sha256 ⛔️
  - [if] a bundle is re-rendered and journaled again with a new sha256 for the same filename [then]
    the later journal line wins ⛔️
  - [if] the journal's final line is torn (a mid-write crash) [then] the index still builds from
    every earlier well-formed line; if an earlier line is corrupt, building raises rather than
    silently skipping it [⛔️ if a corrupt earlier line is silently dropped]
- [x] **STEM-10** (shipped Mon 14 Sep 2026, ADR-0024): The index publishes to R2 at a fixed,
  non-content-addressed key (`indexes/stem-bundle-index.json`) via `apps.cloud.stem_index.publish_index`
  / `fetch_index`, the one deliberate overwrite-in-place object in an otherwise content-addressed store.
  - [if] the R2 index object does not exist yet [then] publishing creates it ⛔️
  - [if] it already exists [then] publishing replaces its body, not a content-addressed no-op ⛔️
- [x] **STEM-11** (shipped Mon 14 Sep 2026, ADR-0024): A local, on-disk cache of the fetched index
  (`apps.cloud.stem_index.save_cached_index` / `load_cached_index`) lets deck-load and bulk hydration
  answer "is this stable_id in R2" without a network round trip on every check.
  - [if] no local cache file exists [then] it reads as an empty index, not an error ⛔️
  - [if] a local cache file exists but is corrupt or the wrong shape [then ⛔️] `load_cached_index`
    raises `StemIndexError` rather than silently reading as empty
- [x] **STEM-12** (shipped Mon 14 Sep 2026, ADR-0024): `apps.cloud.stem_hydration.hydrate_one` fetches
  a bundle's manifest and parts into the stem_bundle local cache path (atomic tmp-dir-plus-rename),
  and the result is verified by the real, unmocked strict loader
  (`apps.webui.server.stem_artifacts.load_stem_bundle`), never a fake.
  - [if] a bundle is already valid on local disk [then] hydration is a no-op reported `already_local`,
    and no network call is made ⛔️
  - [if] the index has the bundle's manifest and part hashes [then] hydration writes them to disk and
    the strict loader accepts the result ⛔️
  - [if] a part fetch fails partway (a hash the index names is not actually in R2) [then ⛔️] no
    partial bundle directory is left behind
- [x] **STEM-13** (shipped Mon 14 Sep 2026, ADR-0024): Reservation guard, deliberately asymmetric.
  `<data_dir>/state/stem-order-reserved-100.json` (committed copy: `ops/stem-order-test/reserved-100.json`)
  names tracks reserved for in-app ordering tests. `bulk_hydrate` skips them by default; on-demand
  deck-load hydration (`hydrate_one` with its default `skip_reserved=False`) never skips them, because a
  reserved track loaded on a deck still needs its stems.
  - [if] a bulk hydrate request names a reserved id [then] it is skipped, reported reason `reserved`,
    unless `include_reserved=True` is passed explicitly ⛔️
  - [if] the same id is loaded on demand (deck load) [then ⛔️] it is not skipped
- [x] **STEM-14** (shipped Mon 14 Sep 2026, ADR-0024): The local stem_bundle cache is
  bundle-granular LRU-evicted (amended Thu 1 Oct 2026: against the disk-aware budget of STEM-39,
  `apps.cloud.stem_cache_budget.enforce`, which retired the fixed-size
  `apps.cloud.stem_hydration.enforce_budget`), and a bundle open on a deck
  (`OpenDeckRegistry`, refcounted; `POST /tracks/{id}/stems/deck-open` and `/deck-close`) is never
  evicted even when it is the least-recently-used bundle over budget.
  - [if] the cache exceeds its byte budget [then] the least-recently-used bundle (by newest-part
    mtime) is evicted first ⛔️
  - [if] a bundle is marked open on a deck [then ⛔️] it is never evicted regardless of recency
- [x] **STEM-15** (shipped Mon 14 Sep 2026, ADR-0024): The stems manifest route
  (`GET /tracks/{id}/stems`) never blocks a deck load on a full 4-part R2 fetch: a missing-but-indexed
  bundle enqueues background hydration (`ThreadPoolExecutor` + in-flight `Future` registry) and returns
  immediately with `hydrating: true`. The part route (`GET /tracks/{id}/stems/{part}`) is the one that
  waits, bounded by `STEM_PART_HYDRATE_WAIT_S` (30s), because only a part request needs real bytes.
  - [if] a bundle is missing locally but present in the R2 index [then] the manifest GET returns
    immediately with `hydrating: true`, never blocking on the part fetch ⛔️
  - [if] the part GET is made for that same bundle [then] it waits (bounded) and then serves the
    real hydrated bytes ⛔️
  - [if] no R2 credentials/config are bound on `app.state` (local mode) [then ⛔️] both routes behave
    exactly as they did before this feature (unchanged 200 unavailable / 404)
- [x] **STEM-16** (shipped Mon 14 Sep 2026, ADR-0024): Fail loud, never silently empty. When the
  index says a bundle exists but hydration cannot produce it, both the manifest and part routes
  answer HTTP 502 with a distinct code (`STEM_BUNDLE_HYDRATION_FAILED`) on every subsequent request
  until the bundle is fixed, never falling back to the ordinary 200/404 "no bundle" shape that would
  read to the storage/stems view as "no stems" instead of "something is wrong".
  - [if] the index names a bundle whose hydration fails (a part hash never actually pushed to R2)
    [then] the next manifest or part GET answers HTTP 502 `STEM_BUNDLE_HYDRATION_FAILED`, not 200
    unavailable and not 404 ⛔️
  - [if] a bundle is genuinely absent everywhere (not local, not in the R2 index) [then ⛔️] that
    stays the ordinary, cheap 200 unavailable / 404 -- it is never confused with a hydration failure

- [x] **STEM-17** (shipped Mon 14 Sep 2026, ADR-0024): The OpenAPI contract and generated

  - [if] a client reads `StemUnavailableOut` from the generated types [then ⛔️] the `hydrating`

- [x] **STEM-36** (Wed 16 Sep 2026, measured on the test Mac after onboarding run 2): on-device stem separation is only OFFERED when this install can actually spawn its worker. The worker is named by an absolute path anchored on the source tree, and `local_stems_gate()` -- which `GET /api/v1/stems/plan` reports as `local_refusal` -- refuses when that file is absent, so the button renders inert with the reason instead of accepting a job. Before this, the installed app enqueued separation and the job failed 198 ms later with `can't open file '//scripts/stems_local_worker.py'`: the argv was relative, the engine's cwd is `/`, and the payload ships no `scripts/` directory.
  - [if] the local worker script is not present in this install [then] the plan endpoint's `local_refusal` names it and says on-device separation is not installed in this build [⛔️ if the button stays live and the tester presses it into a job that cannot run].

  - [if] the worker IS present, as in a checkout [then] the gate allows it and the argv names it absolutely [⛔️ if the refusal overshoots and silently turns local stems off for every developer, or if the path is still a bet on the spawning cwd].
- [x] **STEM-37** (Thu 24 Sep 2026, stems missing after upgrade): a deck waits through `STEM_BUNDLE_HYDRATING`. On an installed spoke a track's bundle usually lives only in R2, so the first manifest GET starts the download and answers HTTP 200 `hydrating: true` (STEM-15). The deck read that as the settled "no bundle" answer, so stems appeared only when the same track was loaded a second time. `awaitStemArtifact` keeps re-asking (1, 2, 3, then every 5 s, one GET per deck) with the deck in `loading`, stops the moment the deck loads another track, and fails loud as a stems error after 10 minutes.
  - [if] the manifest GET answers `STEM_BUNDLE_HYDRATING` and a later GET answers the manifest [then] the deck lands the stems on that same load ⛔️

  - [if] the bundle is still hydrating after `STEM_HYDRATE_MAX_WAIT_MS` [then] the deck shows a stems error naming the wait, never `unavailable` ⛔️
  - [if] output-stall recovery rebuilds the audio graph while a deck's stems are still `loading` [then] the rebuild restarts the upgrade on the new context and the old task stops silently, so the stems still land on that load ⛔️

The floor is the larger of `floor_gib` (default 20) and `floor_fraction` (default 0.05) of the volume holding the stems directory (changed Thu 1 Oct 2026 from 30 and 0.10: measured need on the 460 GiB preview laptop is about 17 GiB, being 8.2 GiB peak swap, about 7 GiB for one set's stems hydrated back, and under 2 GiB of database working copies, while the old 46 GiB floor read as low disk at 39 GiB free). Settings are stored as overrides only, so a machine that changed one switch still follows a later default; a file that already holds explicit floor values keeps them; the budget is cache plus free minus floor (`apps.cloud.stem_cache_budget`). The engine enforces it on a timer (`StemCacheEnforcer`, default every 300 s, first tick 60 s after boot) and after every hydrate. Supersedes: the fixed 100 GB `enforce_budget` of STEM-14.

- [x] **STEM-40** (Thu 1 Oct 2026): eviction is gated on the R2 stem index. A bundle is removed only when the index lists it with the same file names AND every local file's sha256 equals the index digest, checked at eviction time. A local-only or differing bundle is never evicted: it is recorded in `state/stem-upload-queue.json` and counted on the status route.
  - [if] a bundle is absent from the index and the disk is under the floor [then ⛔️] it stays on disk and its id is queued for upload
  - [if] a local file's bytes differ from the index digest [then ⛔️] the bundle stays on disk with the reason `content_differs`
  - [if] the index cache is missing [then ⛔️] every bundle reads local-only and nothing is evicted
  - [if] a bundle is re-rendered in place with the same file names but new bytes [then] the next timer pass hashes it (its name/size/mtime fingerprint moved), queues it `content_differs` and status counts it local-only, even on a healthy disk where no eviction runs (Fri 2 Oct 2026) ⛔️
  - [if] a bundle's fingerprint has not moved since it last hashed equal to the index [then ⛔️] no pass hashes it again; a timer pass hashes at most 2 GiB of changed bundles and the post-hydrate pass none
  - [if] two passes write the upload queue at once [then ⛔️] neither fails: each write goes through its own temp file
  - [if] a pass that scanned before a bundle appeared saves after a pass that queued it [then ⛔️] the entry stays: each save is serialized and merges the on-disk queue, keeping entries for bundles this pass did not see whose directory still exists (`stem_upload_queue`)
  - [if] a bundle is re-rendered after a pass scanned it and a newer pass judged the new bytes [then] the older pass's save keeps the newer verdict, while a pass whose scan is still current replaces the on-disk one [else stop]
  - [if] the engine timer and a hydrate job in another process save the upload queue at once [then ⛔️] the second waits on an OS file lock beside the queue (`stem-upload-queue.json.lock`) and merges what the first wrote (Sat 3 Oct 2026)
- [x] **STEM-41** (Thu 1 Oct 2026): eviction is minimal and contained. Nothing is evicted while free space is at or above the floor; when under it, least-recently-used bundles go first and eviction stops as soon as the floor is reached. Nothing is evicted when no hydration source is armed (`hydration_not_armed`) or when `auto_evict` is off, because an evicted bundle that cannot be fetched back is a lost bundle. The pass after a hydrate may free at most the bytes that hydrate took.
  - [if] free space is at or above the floor [then ⛔️] zero bundles are evicted, however large the cache
  - [if] the shortfall is one bundle's worth [then ⛔️] exactly one bundle is evicted, the least recently used
  - [if] no hydration source is armed [then ⛔️] zero bundles are evicted and the report names the reason
  - [if] a concurrent pass wins the claim on a bundle this pass picked [then ⛔️] its bytes count toward this pass's shortfall, so two passes never evict twice what the disk needed, including one removed before this pass hashed it
  - [if] a bundle disappears while a pass scans it [then ⛔️] that pass skips it rather than failing, so a post-hydrate pass never turns a good deck load into an error
  - [if] a pass renamed a bundle for eviction but could not delete it [then ⛔️] the next writing pass removes the leftover `.evicting-` directory

  - [if] every indexed bundle is open on a deck [then ⛔️] nothing is evicted and the report says nothing is evictable
  - [if] a deck opens or is served a bundle while a pass is hashing it [then ⛔️] the live registry is asked again just before removal and the bundle stays (Fri 2 Oct 2026)

  - [if] a hydrate runs outside the engine (a hydrate worker or CLI, which cannot see the engine's decks) [then ⛔️] its post-hydrate pass evicts nothing and only refreshes the upload queue; eviction belongs to the engine, which marks itself the deck holder when it arms hydration (Sat 3 Oct 2026)
  - [if] a deck-load hydrate finds the bundle already published by another hydrator [then ⛔️] it still marks the bundle served before returning (Sat 3 Oct 2026)
  - [if] the engine and a hydrate worker hydrate the same id at once [then ⛔️] they take turns on a cross-process lock (`state/stem-hydrate-locks/`, 256 striped files), so neither removes the bundle the other just published (Sat 3 Oct 2026)

- [x] **STEM-47** (Thu 1 Oct 2026, "song has stems - stems buttons here don't do anything"): stems that finish loading while the deck is PLAYING take over without stopping it. Before this a finished bundle was held until the deck next stopped, and under machine pressure its decode was not started at all while any deck played, so a track played straight after loading kept dead stem buttons for its whole play (reproduced on the preview: 197 s with the buttons disabled, ready only after every deck was paused). Now the stems are scheduled to start at one future audio-clock instant at the position the deck will have reached, the mix is stopped at that same instant, and the deck is switched to the stems only after the stems acknowledged (`stem-live-handoff.ts`; the engine side is `_landStems`). A transport command during the handoff wins and the handoff is retried; a deck that stays busy keeps the bundle for its next stop and says so. The pressure hold on a deck's own stem decode (PERFMODE-04 `eager-stem-decode`) is now bounded (6 s here; PERFMODE-18 grades it to 500 ms under the early warning alone and 2 s under real pressure, `EAGER_STEM_DECODE_EARLY_WARNING_DEFER_MS` / `EAGER_STEM_DECODE_MAX_DEFER_MS`) and can be ended at once from the deck (`LOAD NOW`, `stem_load`).
  - [if] the stems start and the mix stops at different instants [then ⛔️] (a gap or a doubled deck)
  - [if] a transport command lands while the stems' schedule is being acknowledged and the deck is switched anyway [then ⛔️]
  - [if] a transport command sent after the switch but before the handoff instant reaches the stems while the mix is still audible [then ⛔️] (it waits for the instant)
  - [if] scheduling the stems fails [then] the playing mix is never stopped or retired ⛔️
  - [if] the handoff waits on a flag only the presentation (rAF) loop clears [then ⛔️] (a backgrounded window would never land stems)
  - [if] a pressure hold outlives its bound [then ⛔️]
  - [if] the stems' schedule is acknowledged after the handoff instant [then] they are never connected to the deck, so they are never heard beside the mix ⛔️
  - [if] `LOAD NOW` on a held bundle fails to land [then] the deck reads a retryable error, never `switching` until the track is reloaded ⛔️
  - [if] `LOAD NOW` on one deck starts another deck's held decode [then ⛔️]
  - [if] `LOAD NOW` for a deck's new track starts the old track's held decode [then ⛔️]
  - [if] a held decode's load goes stale before its hold ends [then] it never decodes ⛔️
  - [if] the mix refuses its stop [then] it stays audible until the stems start, then is retired and the error is logged ⛔️
  - [if] the mix's stop is still unacknowledged when the stems start [then] the mix is retired then, never left under the stems ⛔️

  - [if] a track has no bundle locally or in the cloud [then] hovering a stem chip says so ⛔️

- [x] **CLOUDSYNC-29** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026, ADR: NEW deletes-stay-deleted, wire v7): A track tombstone outranks every synced write to that `tracks` row that is not a later explicit restore, whatever the `updated_at` ordering. Hub and spoke compare a lifecycle key (the later of `deleted_at` and `restored_at`) before last-writer-wins; when a live row loses to a stored tombstone the hub re-logs the tombstone so the sender pulls it and converges. The hub's only hard delete of a `tracks` row (identity collapse) refuses unless `sync_identity_remap` names the row as a collapsed loser. Rollout order: hub first, then spokes; a v6 peer is refused with the update-required answer. Not covered: a stale copy that holds the recording under a different `stable_id` than the tombstone. A library whose deletes predate tombstones, where the hub holds nothing to win with, is CLOUDSYNC-30. Proof: `tests/cloudsync/test_tombstone_wins.py`.
  - [if] a machine restored from an old copy pushes a live row whose stamp is newer than the hub's tombstone [then] the hub keeps the tombstone and the machine's next pull removes the track locally [⛔️ if the track is live on any machine]
  - [if] a restore stamped after the tombstone is pushed [then] the track is live on every machine [⛔️ if the tombstone still wins]

- [x] **CLOUDSYNC-30** (Thu 1 Oct 2026, ADR: NEW deletes-stay-deleted "Stale copies"): A stale or copied library cannot bring back tracks the fleet dropped, tombstone or not. A live `tracks` row whose `origin_device_id` names a machine registered on the hub other than the pushing machine, and for whose `stable_id` the hub holds no row and no identity remap, is refused: the spoke asks `POST /api/v1/sync/stale-check` before it pushes and stops with `SyncStaleTracks`, naming every such track and the remedy, and `POST /push` answers 409 `SYNC_STALE_TRACKS` as a backstop. After a settled `tracks` digest mismatch the spoke asks about its whole library, so a copy that kept its source's watermark is named stale rather than corrupt. `python -m apps.sync_hub stale-tracks` lists them (exit 3), `--remove` tombstones them locally so the next sync puts the deletion on the hub, and `--keep` claims them as the machine's own writes so they return to the fleet. The machine's own tracks, tombstones, and a sync that saw the hub go backwards (`reseed`) pass; a track whose author the hub does not know is counted and not decided. Proof: `tests/cloudsync/test_stale_copy_guard.py`.
  - [if] a copy of a library taken before the fleet dropped a track runs its first sync [then] it raises `SyncStaleTracks` naming the track and the hub's changelog does not grow [⛔️ if the track, a field row, a vendor id or a playlist membership of it reaches the hub or another machine]
  - [if] the copy kept its source's sync watermark [then] the `tracks` digest mismatch is raised as `SyncStaleTracks` [⛔️ if it surfaces only as `SyncDigestMismatch`]
  - [if] `stale-tracks --remove` runs and the copy syncs again [then] the sync completes and the hub holds a tombstone for the track [⛔️ if the track is live on any machine]
  - [if] `stale-tracks --keep` runs and the copy syncs again [then] the track is live on the hub and on every machine that syncs [⛔️]
  - [if] a new machine with only tracks it wrote runs its first sync against a populated hub [then] it completes and its tracks arrive [⛔️ if it is refused]
  - [if] the hub went backwards and a spoke re-offers rows the hub forgot [then] they are accepted [⛔️ if the re-seed is refused]
  - [if] a push carries an orphan without the spoke's own check [then] the hub answers 409 `SYNC_STALE_TRACKS` and applies nothing in the batch [⛔️]
- [x] **CLOUDSYNC-31** (Fri 2 Oct 2026, ADR: NEW deletes-stay-deleted "Removed and re-added copies"): A track the user removed and then added back by dropping the same file again stays two rows on every machine: the removed one tombstoned, the re-add live. A removed `tracks` row takes no part in content-identity collapse (CLOUDSYNC-07) on either side of the match, and an incoming row whose own primary key is stored removed and outranks it is refused by the lifecycle rule (CLOUDSYNC-29) before content identity is consulted. Before this the re-offered tombstone lost the collapse to the re-add, the sender hard-deleted the removed row, the watched-folder rescan re-inserted it live about 18 s later, and every sync after ended `accepted 0, rejected N`, INCONCLUSIVE. A spoke already in that state converges on its next sync: on each push the hub retires every identity remap whose loser it stores as a tombstone and re-logs that tombstone, and the spoke's stale-remap recovery retires its own copy. A push answer names each rejected row (`rejected_rows`: table, key, reason `not_newer`, `removed_on_hub` or `identity_loser`, at most 100 per answer), the client logs each one, keeps them on `SyncResult.rejected_rows`, prints them from `python -m apps.sync_hub sync`, and names the first five in the CloudSync status journal message. A genuine duplicate the collapse drops and the rescan re-inserts no longer pins the push fence: CLOUDSYNC-32. Proof: `tests/cloudsync/test_tombstone_identity_collapse.py`.

  - [if] a spoke is stuck with the removed track live and a remap holding it out [then] the next sync leaves it removed on spoke and hub and a later sync pushes nothing [⛔️ if the hub keeps rejecting rows]
  - [if] two LIVE copies of one recording sync [then] they still collapse to one track and the remap survives later pushes [⛔️]
  - [if] the hub rejects an offered row [then] the sync result names its table, key and reason [⛔️ if only a count is reported]

Loading a track it has no copy of answers 404 `AUDIO_NOT_ON_THIS_MACHINE` with the sentence "This file isn't on this computer.", and the deck shows that sentence after the track title, where it used to show the raw `CLOUD_POLICY_UNCONFIGURED: no sync_policies row for machine ... refusing to assume a mode` text, an instruction a DJ cannot act on mid-set. `resolve_policy` still refuses to assume a mode (`PolicyUnconfigured`); only playback resolution treats the missing row as local-only, so an unconfigured machine never streams or hydrates and still plays every copy it has. That includes rekordbox's own FolderPath for the track when its own `track_locations` path is gone, because the library listing already counts that file as the track's (the row's own path was gone while rekordbox's file was on disk, so the listing showed it available and the deck refused it). Only `AUDIO_NOT_ON_THIS_MACHINE` gets the plain sentence: `AUDIO_FILE_MISSING` also covers iCloud stubs, unsupported extensions and unresolvable paths, where the file is here, so it keeps its own message. When no copy plays and rekordbox's file is on disk but won't play (a dataless iCloud stub, an unsupported extension), the deck gets that reason instead of "not on this computer"; a working alternate location still plays first. The toast's error report keeps the raw cause. Proof: `tests/cloudsync/test_asset_tier_policy.py`, `tests/webui/test_track_audio_believed_state.py`, `apps/webui/frontend/tests/unit/deck-load-failure-context.test.mjs`.

  - [if] the same machine's own path for a track is gone but rekordbox's FolderPath for it is on disk [then] it plays rekordbox's file [⛔️ if a track the listing shows available refuses to load]

- [x] **CLOUDSYNC-32** (Fri 2 Oct 2026, ADR: NEW deletes-stay-deleted "Settled identity losers"): A content-identity loser the hub has answered for is SETTLED on the spoke, not held. Found during testing: a library holding its own duplicate audio under a watched folder printed a nonzero held count on every sync after the seed and re-offered the same rows forever (rows pushed, none accepted, all rejected), because the seed's collapse dropped each loser, the watched-folder rescan re-inserted it under its old id, the persisted `sync_identity_remap` held it out of the offer, and its changelog entry pinned the push fence. A `tracks` row a persisted hub remap names as a loser, and every child row of it, is still never offered and still out of the digest hash, but it is not counted as held (`excluded: N row(s) held here`, the status page's excluded total), never re-logged after a full offer and never a fence pin, so later syncs push nothing and reject nothing. A loser the hub has NOT answered for (a local election only) is held and pins the fence as before, so it still travels if it stops being a loser first. The loser row stays in the local library, as local duplicates always have. The identity repair's one-row offer of each hub-answered loser is reported as a confirmation (`SyncResult.identity_repairs`, "N identity duplicate collapse(s) confirmed by the hub", logged at info), not as a rejection, so the summary's `rejected` always equals the rows it names; the seed used to say `rejected 0` while its log claimed 152 rejections. The hub retires remaps whose loser it stores as a tombstone (CLOUDSYNC-31) on every `hello` as well as every push, because a spoke whose losers settled may have nothing left to push. An edit made to a settled loser row itself follows its survivor: `prepare_spoke_identity` moves the loser's child rows onto the survivor before every offer, and a moved row keyed by `stable_id` (`track_fields`) now keeps its changelog entry under its new key, so it is offered and accepted; where the survivor already holds that key, the survivor's value stands and the loser's entry is dropped, so nothing is re-offered. Before this the move dropped the entry and logged none, the row sat on the survivor unoffered, and the digest raised `SyncDigestMismatch` (`track_fields/<survivor>/comments row exists locally but not on hub`) on that and every later sync; a CI run hit it when its runner listed `a.wav` before `b.wav`, making `a.wav` the loser the test then edited. Not covered: the loser stays visible in the local library. Proof: `tests/cloudsync/test_settled_identity_losers.py`.
  - [if] a library with duplicate audio under a watched folder seeds, rescans and syncs again [then] no row is counted as held, the push fence reaches the changelog head, and a later sync pushes 0 and rejects 0 [⛔️ if the held count or the re-offer persists]
  - [if] the seed's identity repair offers each loser for confirmation [then] the summary's `rejected` equals the rejected rows it names, and the confirmations are counted separately [⛔️ if the log claims rejections the summary does not count]
  - [if] a real edit or a restore is made after the losers settle [then] it is pushed and accepted, and the sync after it pushes nothing [⛔️ if it is swallowed or re-offered forever]
  - [if] a loser has not been answered by the hub [then] it is still held and pins the fence [⛔️ if it is settled]
  - [if] a row is held for a stamp fault [then] it still pins the fence until repaired [⛔️ if it is settled]

- **PARITY-07**: The parity law gains three net-new clauses beyond the dispatcher rule already in force at `AGENTS.md:128-131`, `CONVENTIONS.md` and PARITY-02. (1) UI-MIRROR STATE: the agent-readable state document must mirror what a human reads off the screen, not a subset of it, so a control that renders but is absent from the mirror is a parity defect (AGENT-02). (2) FULL CLI: every button and dial on the performance surface is reachable from the `opendj` CLI, so a control with no verb is a parity defect (AGENT-05). (3) BEAT-TIME ORDERS: agents can order work sequentially, in parallel, and as transitions expressed in beats, bars and phrases rather than only as one immediate command at a time (AGENT-03, AGENT-04). Rationale and the evidence that these three are net-new and nowhere today: the agent-control and red-team spec, section 1.4.
  - [if] a performance control renders on screen but has no entry in the UI-mirror state document [then] it is a parity defect, exactly as a direct-to-engine control is ⛔️
  - [if] a performance control is on the command bus but `opendj --list-verbs` does not name it [then] it is a parity defect ⛔️
  - [if] an agent can only issue one immediate command at a time on a surface [then] the beat-time order clause is unmet for that surface ⛔️

_Numbered PARITY-07 rather than PARITY-03: PARITY-03 is already taken by a shipped v1
requirement (own-decode waveform peaks for unmapped tracks, shipped Tue 1 Sep 2026), and
a duplicate id would collide in `reqs.json` and the traceability table._

### Instance Link (LINK)

Recorded Sat 12 Sep 2026 (primary use: multiple Open DJ accounts, extra
sync-lane waveform above CH1 showing the shared master beatgrid; one source of
truth, others attached; also two controllers of a server oDJ on the PA, and a
mobile surface controlling the laptop that holds CPU + SoT). Plan only: see
the Instance Link spec. Not implemented this wave. Classic Ableton Link is
groundwork on the same SyncClock, not the primary ship.

- [ ] **LINK-01**: Shared SyncClock. One session object holds tempo, beat, phase,
      quantum (default 4.0, BAR), start/stop intent, SoT instance id, provider
      name, rtt_ms, and a named degraded state. Capture-compute-commit, matching
      Ableton Link's session-state model so a classic Link adapter is a provider
      rather than a fork. Providers, in order: `local_master` (today's elected
      Beat Sync MASTER deck), `odj_wan` (LINK-04), `ableton_link` (LINK-05).
      Presentation clock remains `AudioContext.getOutputTimestamp()` on the
      AUDIO instance; attached UIs and remote engines render the published
      clock and never invent an optimistic playhead. CloudSync is not a
      provider (CLOUDSYNC-08: metadata freeze during Gig; 300s
      scheduler cannot carry beat phase). Spec section 3.2.
  - [if] a session is running [then] `GET /api/v1/sync/clock` and the UI-mirror
        both carry the same SyncClock snapshot
        [⛔️ if the waveform, the mirror, and the CLI disagree on beat or tempo]
  - [if] the provider is `local_master` [then] tempo/beat/phase equal the elected
        Beat Sync MASTER deck's published PQTZ clock
        [⛔️ if a second clock is synthesized beside it]
  - [if] a timestamp is non-finite, negative, or regressing [then] it is
        rejected and `degraded` becomes `lost`
        [⛔️ if the lane freewheels a fake grid]

- [ ] **LINK-02**: Sync-lane waveform above CH1. Extra special row in
      `WaveformStack`, visually above deck 1, showing the session master
      beatgrid for beatmatching. Not a fifth deck: no load, no fader, no play,
      no hot cues, no stems. Same 24s scrolling window and fixed center
      playhead as `WaveRow` so the lane and CH1 share a time base. Distinct
      tint and a `SYNC` (or SoT instance name) label. Renders the published
      SyncClock plus the SoT master's PQTZ only. Dragging the lane does not
      seek. Agent-native: `ui-mirror.sync_lane`, `opendj state --sync-lane`,
      same HTTP document (PARITY-07). Inert chrome carries a `title` saying
      why it is not a deck. Spec section 3.4. Primary UX of the program.
  - [if] Instance Link is on and a SoT master grid exists [then] a sync-lane
        row renders above CH1 with bar-1 emphasis matching the SoT PQTZ
        [⛔️ if the lane is a fifth playable `WaveRow`, or sits below CH1]
  - [if] the lane is visible [then] `ui-mirror.sync_lane` names source
        instance, tempo, beat, quantum, rtt_ms, and degraded
        [⛔️ if the row renders and the mirror omits it]
  - [if] the user drags the sync-lane [then] no deck seeks
        [⛔️ if a remote or local playhead jumps]

- [ ] **LINK-03**: Instance topology and roles. Exactly one source-of-truth
      per session; others are attached. Named topologies: (A) one audio
      engine + N attached surfaces (mobile / second laptop control the PA
      machine; UI-only, AGENT-03 over `MUSIC_DJ_ALLOWED_HOSTS`); (B) N
      engines, one clock SoT (two oDJ apps each with audio, phase-locked;
      sync-lane shows the remote master grid); (C) two controllers of a
      server oDJ on the PA (A with two attached surfaces). Role is a named
      command (`opendj sync role sot|attached`), refused while any deck is
      playing unless the current SoT is `lost` for >5s. Topology A/C
      conflict default: last-writer-wins on the engine command queue, with
      the mirror showing which instance_id last touched each deck/mixer
      scope. Decisions pending (spec D2, D3, D4): attached preview audio
      (default no), per-deck ownership vs last-writer-wins, role-UI
      placement. Spec section 3.5.
  - [if] two instances join one session [then] exactly one reports
        `role=source-of-truth` and the other `role=attached`
        [⛔️ if both claim SoT, or the role is inferred from hostname]
  - [if] topology A [then] the attached surface has no AudioContext and
        every Class A control is an AGENT-03 command at the SoT engine
        [⛔️ if the phone opens a second graph, or Class A waits on a
        CloudSync round]
  - [if] an attached instance tries `opendj sync role sot` while the SoT
        is playing and not `lost` [then] the command is refused with a
        named reason
        [⛔️ if the SoT is stolen silently]

- [ ] **LINK-04**: Clock transport, never CloudSync. Join-time probe, re-probed
      on loss, pick whatever is fastest: (1) same-LAN UDP unicast to the SoT,
      (2) Tailscale UDP, (3) WebRTC datachannel, (4) refuse with a named
      reason. Never silently fall through to CloudSync push/pull. RTT
      compensation (Cristian / NTP-class offset; we do not have NIC PTP).
      Named degraded states published on the mirror: `ok` (<=20ms),
      `lan_ok` (<=40ms), `wan_soft` (<=80ms), `wan_hard` (<=150ms), `lost`
      (no packet within 1s). First implementation measures round-trip time
      between two machines on a local network, and between a local machine
      and a remote host, while a deck is playing and replaces the floor with
      that measurement; a tidy binary in-sync/not is a defective instrument.
      Class A never waits on this plane (LATENCY-01).
      QUANTIZED LAUNCH (LATENCY-02) is how a play on an attached engine
      lands on the shared downbeat despite tens of milliseconds of RTT.
      Sample-accurate audible lock over the public internet is not a v2
      gate; beatmatching the sync-lane plus quantized launch is. Spec
      sections 3.1, 3.3, 5.
  - [if] two oDJ instances join over Tailscale [then] the clock plane is
        UDP (or a measured-faster WebRTC datachannel) and CloudSync
        `/push` `/pull` is not on the path
        [⛔️ if beat phase rides the 300s changelog]
  - [if] RTT p95 crosses a named threshold [then] `degraded` changes and
        the sync-lane chip shows the state and the ms
        [⛔️ if the lane stays solid while packets are 200ms late, or a
        binary in-sync flag hides the ms]
  - [if] the clock peer is lost for 1s [then] the lane grays and attached
        does not freewheel
        [⛔️ if CH1 keeps drawing a guessed remote grid]

      oDJ talks TCP localhost; Carabiner talks over Link's standard
      multicast group. GPL stays outside the app binary. Untracked
      spike at `spikes/carabiner-link/` (Carabiner 1.2.0, protocol probed,

      Link SDK licensing program (Ableton AG) and in-process SDK (needed for App Store if
      Link is inside the binary), (3) GPL the oDJ binary. Do not embed GPL
      in the app binary without that ruling. Classic Link is LAN-only;
      WAN uses LINK-04. Link Audio (Live 12.4, Tue 5 May 2026) is out of
      scope. Mixxx still has no native Link ([#8650](https://github.com/mixxxdj/mixxx/issues/8650)
      OPEN); do not treat Mixxx as a working reference. Spec section 3.6.
  - [if] D1 is unset [then] no Link library is linked into the oDJ binary
        [⛔️ if GPL Link is vendored into the app as a drive-by]
  - [if] the sidecar is running on a LAN with Ableton Live Link-enabled
        [then] Live's timeline follows oDJ tempo and phase at quantum 4
        and a quantized launch in Live lands on oDJ bar 1
        [⛔️ if the only evidence is `peers: 0` against Carabiner]
  - [if] a user enables classic Link over a VPN [then] it is refused with

        [⛔️ if multicast-over-VPN is the product path]

- [ ] **LINK-06**: Clock-provider mod surface. A typed `ClockProvider`

### Stem Artifact Coverage (STEM)

- [x] **STEM-01** (shipped Wed 9 Sep 2026): Ingest coverage, library refresh targeting, and deck stem lookup treat a track as complete when any configured stem root contains a valid bundle; an invalid higher-precedence candidate is logged and cannot shadow a valid lower-precedence bundle.
  - [if] a present track has only a valid RoFormer bundle in the secondary root [then] coverage counts its stems and library refresh does not enqueue separation [⛔️ if it is re-queued]
  - [if] a higher-precedence bundle is invalid and a lower-precedence bundle is valid [then] the deck receives the valid bundle and the rejected root is logged [⛔️ if the deck reports no stems]
  - [if] no configured root has a valid bundle [then] the error names every root searched and the track remains missing [⛔️ if an invalid directory is counted as complete]

- [x] **STEM-02** (shipped Thu 10 Sep 2026): The demucs bundle producer (scripts/stem_bundle_worker.py) consults apps/stems/stem_size_policy.py's source-extension codec policy and per-part size target instead of always writing WAV.
  - [if] the source file is .mp3 or .m4a [then] every stem part is encoded to MP3 at or under the source's own bitrate (LAME 320 CBR when the source is >= 320 kbps, else LAME V0 VBR, with a rung-2 CBR re-encode for any part that still exceeds the source) [⛔️ if a part is written as WAV or FLAC]
  - [if] the source file is .flac, .wav, .aif, or .aiff [then] every stem part is written as 16-bit FLAC [⛔️ if a lossy source is upgraded to a lossless stem]
  - [if] a stem part still lands larger than the source file after the size policy's ladder [then] the file is kept and the overage is recorded in manifest.json, never discarded [⛔️ if an over-budget stem is deleted or the run is aborted]
  - [if] the source extension has no entry in the codec policy [then] the run raises before any GPU spend [⛔️ if an unrecognised extension silently defaults to a codec]

- [ ] **STEM-03** (Mon 14 Sep 2026): v1 stem bundles load MP3 and FLAC parts by their own container.
  - [if] a schema v1 bundle declares .mp3 or .flac parts whose magic bytes match the suffix [then] `load_stem_bundle` validates geometry without WAV parsing and exposes `audio/mpeg` or `audio/flac` through the stems API [⛔️ if the loader raises `StemArtifactError` or hardcodes `audio/wav`]
  - [if] all parts share one container and sample rate and channels match [then] the bundle loads and aligned frame counts use exact equality for WAV/FLAC and `FRAME_MISMATCH_TOL_S` for MP3 padding [⛔️ if mixed containers load or misaligned geometry is accepted]
  - [if] a part's suffix and magic bytes disagree, or a truncated MP3/FLAC part fails declared-length or tail-frame validation [then] the bundle is rejected [⛔️ if garbage or truncated parts load]

Counts use the `present` (materialised local audio) denominator, never all `tracks` rows.

### Lyrics (LYRICS)

- [x] **LYRICS-01**: Fetch free line-synced lyrics for one stable track id through `python -m apps.lyrics fetch <track>`, atomically cache integer-millisecond lines under `data/state/lyrics-cache/<stable_id>.json`, and reject paid providers or word-level karaoke data.
  - [if] the same stable track id is fetched twice [then] the second request reads
    the existing cache and makes no source request ⛔️
  - [if] the free source has no synced line lyrics [then] the command fails plainly
    and writes no fabricated cache entry ⛔️
  - [if] the source exposes enhanced word timestamps [then] the command refuses the
    result rather than storing karaoke data ⛔️
  - [if] consecutive LRC lines share one timestamp, or one line carries several
    stamps (compressed LRC) [then] every stamp is kept, the lines are cached in time
    order, and a line repeated verbatim at one stamp is kept once (amended Mon 14 Sep
    2026: LRCLIB 35886253 failed a library job with "must be strictly increasing") ⛔️
  - [if] a line's earliest stamp is before the previous line's [then] the fetch fails
    with "jump backwards" and writes no cache entry ⛔️
- [x] **LYRICS-05**: The /performance waveform renders cached line-synced lyric text in a track-time lane that scrolls beneath its fixed playhead, hides when the loaded track has no lyrics, and exposes the same cache through `GET /api/v1/tracks/{stable_id}/lyrics`.
  - [if] a cached lyric line starts six seconds after a deck's current track position [then] its lane position is projected from that six-second track-time delta through the same pitch-scaled waveform window as the bands ⛔️
  - [if] playback crosses a cached line timestamp [then] that line becomes the active lyric at the playhead, while earlier and later visible lines continue scrolling on their real timestamps ⛔️
  - [if] the loaded track has no cached lyrics [then] `GET /api/v1/tracks/{stable_id}/lyrics` returns 404 and the performance waveform renders no lyrics lane ⛔️
  - [if] `/performance` loads with no deck track [then] a visible Stage control is present but disabled; [if] a deck has a loaded track [then] Stage opens the existing full-screen karaoke overlay in performance/deck mode ⛔️

- [x] **LYRICS-06**: The performance waveform reads `GET /api/v1/tracks/lyrics-cached-ids` before requesting per-track lyrics and skips `GET /api/v1/tracks/{stable_id}/lyrics` when that stable_id is absent from the index.
  - [if] a loaded track has no cached lyrics [then] the waveform never issues `GET /api/v1/tracks/{stable_id}/lyrics` while still allowing agents to read the explicit 404 cache-miss route ⛔️
  - [if] a stable_id is listed in `GET /api/v1/tracks/lyrics-cached-ids` [then] the waveform issues `GET /api/v1/tracks/{stable_id}/lyrics` and renders the lane when lines exist ⛔️

- [x] **LYRICS-07**: Hub `GET /api/v1/sync/lyrics-asr/{stable_id}` presigns `lyrics-asr/v1/{stable_id}.json` with named 404/502 codes and no client R2 keys; library-jobs `lyrics` lane tries LRCLIB then ASR; terminal `instrumental` / `no_source` outcomes avoid retry loops; ASR transcripts become line-synced cache entries (`source=asr`) that set `lyrics_available` and render with a "transcribed" header; `no_source` retries only when the stem index vocals hash changes.
  - [if] a present track has no LRCLIB lyrics and an R2 transcript exists [then] after one lyrics job the lyrics panel shows timed lines with a "transcribed" header and `lyrics_available` is true ⛔️
  - [if] the R2 transcript is absent [then] the job records `no_source` with the hub 404 reason and retries only when the vocals hash changes ⛔️
  - [if] the transcript has zero words [then] the track is recorded `instrumental` with no cache entry ⛔️
  - [if] the hub is unreachable [then] the job fails loudly with the hub error text and nothing is cached ⛔️

- [x] **LYRICS-08** (Thu 24 Sep 2026): a lyrics run that reaches a track before the spoke has fetched its stem index from the hub does not record `no_source`. A missing index cache reads as empty, and a `no_source` verdict with no vocals hash stays terminal (LYRICS-07), so those tracks were never asked about again. The fetch now fails retryable with `LYRICS_STEM_INDEX_NOT_LOADED` and writes nothing.
  - [if] a hub transport is configured and the stem index cache is absent [then] no verdict and no cache entry are written, and the item fails with `LYRICS_STEM_INDEX_NOT_LOADED` ⛔️
  - [if] no hydration transport is configured (local mode) [then] `no_source` is still recorded ⛔️
- [x] **LYRICS-09** (Thu 24 Sep 2026): the deck's lyrics parser accepts consecutive lines with the same `start_ms`, as the server cache does since the LYRICS-01 amendment of Mon 14 Sep 2026. Before this, a cached track with a doubled line rendered as a lyrics load error on the deck.
  - [if] two consecutive lines share `start_ms` [then] the deck shows both ⛔️
  - [if] a line starts before the previous one [then] the deck still rejects the response ⛔️
  - [if] two lines share `start_ms` [then] the waveform lyrics lane draws them as ONE entry reading `first / second`, never two spans stacked at one position, and the line panel keys its rows by position ⛔️
- [x] **LYRICS-10** (built Thu 1 Oct 2026): on the waveform line lane a lyric line is drawn from its start time rightwards, so the start of its text meets the playhead when the line begins (before, the middle of the text did). Each line is capped to the distance to the next line and ends in an ellipsis when it does not fit, so lines cannot overlap, and each sits on a backing mixed at least 80% from the app background. Still open: word-by-word accuracy on tracks without aligned words, which the line lane cannot give.
  - [if] a line starts at the playhead time [then] its left edge is at 50% of the lane
  - [if] two lines follow each other [then] the first line's left edge plus its width never passes the second line's left edge
  - [if] a line is the last one [then] it has no width cap
- [x] **LYRICS-11** (remainder; built Thu 1 Oct 2026): the karaoke word lane gets the same treatment as the line lane: each word sits on an 85 percent opaque backing and is capped in width at the next word on its row, with an ellipsis, so words no longer run over each other.

Lyrics are NOT a bulk local corpus. LYRICS-01's cache is fetched one stable track id at
a time, on demand, from LRCLIB only, so there is no ambient coverage to measure
against the whole library. The coverage denominator is whatever
`tracks_on_disk()` in `apps/webui/server/routes/ingest_job.py` currently resolves
(materialised audio files, minus streaming-only rows) and the numerator is
whatever `valid_lyrics_ids()` finds cached under `data/state/lyrics-cache/` -
the same two functions the shipped lyrics-completion health dot already uses,
so this reuses that population rather than defining a second one. On this dev/CI checkout
the honest answer is 0 of 0: `data/state/state.db`
ships empty and gitignored, and no `lyrics-cache` directory exists on disk. The
real fraction for the user's library can only be read by running that same health-dot
path against the user's real `state.db` and `lyrics-cache/`, which this worktree does not
have access to. `apps/lyrics/search_contract.py` records the typed boundary
(`LyricSearchDocument`, `build_search_document`) that later parts (background
index, and search UI) consume; neither an index nor a search UI is
built here.

- [x] **LYRICS-02**: Lyric-search result latency is a
  measured KPI, not an assumed one - p95 under 50ms for a substring scan
  (`apps.lyrics.search_contract.find_matches`) across a PARITY-01-sized (2,314
  document) corpus, enforced by `tests/lyrics_search/test_search_contract.py`
  measuring the real reference scan rather than asserting a number.
  - [if] the reference scan runs 60 trials across a 2,314-document corpus [then]
    the test computes p95 from real `time.perf_counter` samples and fails if it
    is not under the budget in `search_contract.SEARCH_RESULT_LATENCY_P95_MS_MAX` ⛔️
  - [if] a `LyricSearchDocument` is built from a `Lyrics` cache entry with no
    lines [then] the boundary raises rather than returning an empty, silently
    unsearchable document ⛔️
  - [if] Parts 2 or 3 need the lyric-search data shape [then] they import
    `LyricSearchDocument` / `build_search_document` from `apps.lyrics.search_contract`
    rather than re-deriving a second flattening of `Lyrics.lines` ⛔️

- [x] **LYRICS-03**: Lyric-search hits come from a durable checkpointed background index over the Part 1 documents, built one bounded batch per poll so it pauses within one poll of the UI becoming active, resumes from the on-disk checkpoint once idle, and never keeps the incomplete index in RAM.
  - [if] the UI becomes active while the indexer is building [then] indexing pauses
    within one poll and resumes only after the UI is idle again ⛔️
  - [if] indexing is interrupted mid-corpus [then] the committed batches survive on
    disk and the next run resumes past them without re-indexing ⛔️
  - [if] a cache entry is added or removed [then] the next batch indexes or drops
    exactly that document ⛔️
  - [if] a lyric term is searched against the built index [then] matching stable ids
    come back from the on-disk FTS5 store, not from a RAM-resident index copy ⛔️

- [x] **LYRICS-04**: Lyric-only search results render below a labeled divider after the primary metadata results, fetched lazily and debounced only once the primary search has settled, with a contextual matched-phrase snippet rather than the whole transcript or a bare title.
  - [if] a whole-collection search is typed [then] title/artist results render
    immediately and lyric-only results are fetched only after that search settles ⛔️
  - [if] a lyric hit renders [then] it shows a labeled divider above it and the
    matching lyric line in context, never the full transcript or a bare title ⛔️
  - [if] no lyric hits exist for the query [then] no divider renders - an honest
    empty, not a stale or placeholder section ⛔️
  - [if] a query is superseded by a newer one before its lyric fetch resolves
    [then] the stale response is dropped and never renders ⛔️

- [x] **OBS-02** (Sentry setup review Mon 21 Sep 2026): No event leaves for Sentry while any deck is playing or audible. A browser error carries the page's own `any_deck_live` flag (`anyDeckPlaying`: playing OR audible; `null` when no probe is registered, never "idle") and that flag is authoritative when it is a bool; an engine exception, and an opt-in transaction, asks the registered probe, which the engine entry point wires to the UI mirror's `decks[*].playing|audible` and refuses when `received_at` is older than 15 s. The local JSONL sink and the daily client log are written BEFORE the gate, held events spend no quota, and a missing or raising probe reads NOT live so a broken gate fails toward sending. ADR-NEW-sentry-live-gate-and-opt-in-tracing.
  - [if] a client error arrives with `any_deck_live: true` [then] it is in the daily log and no envelope reaches the Sentry transport ⛔️
  - [if] a client error arrives with `any_deck_live: false` while the engine's mirror says a deck is playing [then] it is sent (the page's read outranks the mirror) ⛔️
  - [if] an engine exception fires while the mirror (fresher than 15 s) shows a deck playing [then] no envelope reaches the transport, and the next exception after transport stops does ⛔️
  - [if] the mirror shows a deck playing but `received_at` is 60 s old [then] the engine reads NOT live and sends ⛔️
  - [if] the registered probe raises [then] the engine reads NOT live, sends, and logs the probe fault once ⛔️

- [x] **OBS-03** (Sentry setup review Mon 21 Sep 2026): Request tracing is off by default and opt-in per process through `SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE` (a number in [0, 1]; unset or 0 is errors only; anything else fails startup loud, naming the variable, even when telemetry is off). Transactions pass `before_send_transaction`, which applies the OBS-02 live-set gate and the same scrub as an error: span descriptions and the transaction name are path- and token-scrubbed, span `data` and `tags` are allowlisted. Profiling, session replay, logs and metrics have no switch and stay off; the org-side Loader Script toggles were switched off on the preview key because no loader script exists in the app. ADR-NEW-sentry-live-gate-and-opt-in-tracing.

  - [if] tracing is on and a span description carries a library path and its data a `track_title` [then] the delivered transaction ends the description in `<path.mp3>` and the data reads `[redacted]`, with `deck_id` intact ⛔️
  - [if] tracing is on and a deck is live [then] the transaction never reaches the transport ⛔️

- [x] **OBS-04** (Mon 21 Sep 2026): The dmg ships Sentry. `scripts/build_engine_payload.py` requests the `observability` extra so `sentry-sdk` is in the payload and the payload's own interpreter must import it or the build fails; `scripts/payload_telemetry.py` bakes the ship DSN from `OPENDJ_SENTRY_DSN_BACKEND_SHIP` (env, else the project's secret store; never the build host's preview `SENTRY_DSN`) into `telemetry.json` at the payload root, verified by the build and checked by `scripts/dmg_preflight.sh`; the launcher exports its path as `OPENDJ_BUNDLED_TELEMETRY`; `decide_telemetry` turns a PACKAGED build with a DSN ON when `OPENDJ_TELEMETRY` is unset (a checkout stays off), and a tester opts out by creating `telemetry-opt-out` in the engine data directory (`OPENDJ_TELEMETRY=0` still wins over everything; `=1` wins over the marker). A payload that lost its SDK or its bundle logs loudly and keeps running. ADR-NEW-sentry-live-gate-and-opt-in-tracing (clause 6).
  - [if] the payload build runs without `OPENDJ_SENTRY_DSN_BACKEND_SHIP` in env or the secret store [then] it fails naming the variable and writes no telemetry.json ⛔️
  - [if] only `SENTRY_DSN` (the preview key) is set at build time [then] the bake refuses rather than shipping the preview key ⛔️
  - [if] the payload's interpreter cannot import `sentry_sdk` [then] `assert_verify_report` fails the build naming OBS-04 ⛔️
  - [if] a packaged engine boots with the bundled file and no env vars [then] telemetry is on under the bundled DSN, environment `ship`, release the build sha ⛔️
  - [if] `telemetry-opt-out` exists in the data directory [then] a packaged build boots with telemetry off and the reason names the marker ⛔️
  - [if] the launcher names a bundled file the engine cannot read [then] the engine logs `[ERROR] bundled telemetry unreadable` and boots with telemetry off ⛔️

- [x] **OBS-05** (Mon 21 Sep 2026): Test-user consent gates every Sentry send. A build that turned telemetry on by itself (OBS-04, `explicit=False`) holds errors, forwarded browser errors and transactions in the local sink until `<data-dir>/telemetry-consent.json` says `accepted` for the CURRENT `TERMS_VERSION` (`apps/shared/telemetry/consent.py`); an operator-explicit `OPENDJ_TELEMETRY=1` is never held. `GET/PUT /api/v1/telemetry/consent` reads and records the decision and flips the in-process gate without a restart; `declined` is remembered and read as an opt-out on the next boot; acceptance of an older terms version reads as `undecided` so the tester is asked again. The page asks once, after the boot window, only when the engine reports `consent_required` (the OBS-04 `explicit=False` case; an operator-explicit boot never asks) AND there is something an acceptance would turn on (`telemetry_active` or a replay loader URL); the dialog text is `docs/legal/test-user-terms.md`. ADR-NEW-sentry-live-gate-and-opt-in-tracing (clause 7).
  - [if] a packaged build boots with no consent file [then] a captured exception is in the local sink and no envelope reaches the transport ⛔️
  - [if] `PUT /api/v1/telemetry/consent` records `accepted` with the current terms version [then] the next captured exception is sent, with no restart ⛔️
  - [if] `PUT` carries an older terms version with `accepted` [then] the response is 409 naming the current version and the stored decision is unchanged ⛔️
  - [if] the stored acceptance is for an older terms version [then] `GET` reports `undecided` (with the old version) and sends stay held ⛔️
  - [if] `OPENDJ_TELEMETRY=1` was set by an operator [then] no consent is required and the first exception is sent ⛔️
  - [if] `GET` reports `undecided` with `telemetry_active: false` and no loader URL [then] the page does not ask ⛔️
  - [if] `GET` reports `consent_required: false` (operator-explicit boot) with a loader URL [then] the page does not ask and starts the replay on the stored acceptance only ⛔️

The engine derives the Sentry Loader Script URL from the frontend DSN (`OPENDJ_SENTRY_DSN_FRONTEND` baked into `telemetry.json` for a dmg, `SENTRY_FRONTEND_DSN` for a checkout; `js-<region>.sentry-cdn.com/<key>.min.js`, region from the ingest host) and serves it on `GET /api/v1/telemetry/consent` with `replay_session_sample_rate` (`SENTRY_REPLAY_SESSION_SAMPLE_RATE`, default 1.0) and `replay_on_error_sample_rate` 1.0. A poll every 2 s reads `anyDeckPlaying` and stops the replay while any deck is playing or audible, restarting after two idle ticks. The open-dj-fe key's loader options in the org were set to replay only (tracing, debug, feedback, logs off). ADR-NEW-sentry-live-gate-and-opt-in-tracing (clause 7).
  - [if] the tester accepts [then] exactly one script tag for the loader URL is appended and `sentryOnLoad` initializes with the masking options above ⛔️
  - [if] the stored decision is `declined` or `undecided` [then] no loader script is fetched ⛔️
  - [if] a deck becomes live [then] the replay is stopped once, and restarted only after two consecutive idle polls ⛔️
  - [if] a loader-SDK event carries `/Users/x/Music/Artist - Title.mp3` [then] the sent event reads `<path.mp3>` and app routes such as `/performance` survive ⛔️
  - [if] a track title is on screen (table text and `title` attributes) while a replay segment uploads [then] the decoded rrweb recording, its `ui.click` breadcrumb selectors included, does not contain that title ⛔️
  - [if] the payload build has no `OPENDJ_SENTRY_DSN_FRONTEND` [then] it fails naming the variable ⛔️
