### Analysis JIT Cache Safety (JIT)

librosa marks several of its hot paths
`@numba.guvectorize(..., cache=True)`, so they compile on first call and write
`.nbi`/`.nbc` artifacts into ONE shared on-disk cache. Concurrent
`apps.analysis.run` processes meeting a COLD cache interleave those writes, the
index and the object file stop agreeing, and from then on every process that
LOADS the result dies at a NULL instruction pointer with no traceback and no
Python exception. Neither `fork` nor thread oversubscription is involved
(both were investigated and ruled out): it reproduces at `--workers 1`, with no
child process at all.

- [x] **JIT-01**: `apps.analysis.run` compiles the backend's cached JIT paths once, in the parent process, before it creates the worker pool, for every worker count including `--workers 1`.
  - [if] a run uses `--workers 2` [then] every worker reports that the warm-up marker already existed when it ran, and names the driver's pid as its author ⛔️
  - [if] a run uses `--workers 1` [then] the warm-up still runs, because the corruption needs two processes and not two workers ⛔️
  - [if] the warm-up call is removed from `run.py` [then] the ordering test fails, rather than passing on a log line that proves only what was printed first ⛔️
- [x] **JIT-02**: The warm-up is skipped only while the on-disk cache is byte-for-byte what the last successful serial warm-up left, checked by fingerprinting every `*.nbi`/`*.nbc` artifact under the backend's declared cache roots against a stamp written inside the lock.
  - [if] anything writes to the cache after a warm-up [then] the next run warms again instead of trusting it ⛔️
  - [if] the backend declares no cache roots, or a root cannot be walked [then] the run warms unconditionally rather than reporting an unmeasured cache as fine ⛔️
  - [if] the cache is untouched since the last serial warm-up [then] the run skips the compile and says `skipped=1` ⛔️
- [x] **JIT-03**: The cold-compile window is held under an advisory `fcntl.flock` lock keyed on the cache location, so two invocations meeting a cold cache compile one after the other and never together. This is what covers the webui refresh route, which shells out to `apps.analysis.run --workers 2` per chunk and can have several chunks in flight at once.
  - [if] four processes warm at once [then] no two are inside the compile at the same moment, and the run spans at least the sum of their holds ⛔️
  - [if] the same probe runs WITHOUT the lock [then] it does overlap, so the exclusion assertion above is known to be capable of failing ⛔️
  - [if] two processes would write different caches [then] they take different locks; if they would share one cache they take the same lock ⛔️
- [x] **JIT-04**: Two concurrent cold-cache `apps.analysis.run --workers 2` invocations over real audio both exit 0, and a third run against the cache they left also exits 0.
  - [if] a cold concurrent invocation exits 139 or dies of SIGSEGV [then] the acceptance test fails and names the exit code ⛔️
  - [if] the pair of runs writes no JIT artifacts at all [then] the test fails rather than passing against a cache that was never populated ⛔️
- [x] **JIT-05**: `python -m apps.analysis.jit_warmup [--purge]` is the single entry point CI uses to repair and warm the cache, and it exits non-zero when a backend that declares cache roots ends with zero artifacts on disk. The e2e gate purges and warms; the pytest lanes warm only.
  - [if] a warm-up writes nothing onto disk [then] the command exits 1 rather than reporting a green step that guaranteed nothing ⛔️
  - [if] a purge runs [then] the stamp goes with the artifacts, so the next warm-up cannot skip against a fingerprint of a cache that no longer exists ⛔️
  - [if] a CI job reimplements the purge or the warm-up inline [then] the workflow test fails, because CI must not drift from the warm-up that ships ⛔️
- [x] **JIT-06**: The warm-up's compile lock and stamp live in a private 0700 directory under the temp root, or by explicit opt-in in an existing directory named by `MDT_NUMBA_WARMUP_DIR` that the operator controls; the lock file is opened without following symlinks and used only when it is a regular file this process may own; nothing is chmodded to 0o666; and a warm-up that cannot establish such a lock is refused rather than run unlocked against a cold cache.
  - [if] a symlink is planted at the lock path [then] the warm-up refuses to follow it, leaves the target's mode untouched, and compiles nothing ⛔️
  - [if] the lock file is not a regular file this process may own, or cannot be opened [then] the warm-up is refused rather than compiling without the cross-process lock ⛔️
  - [if] the private lock directory is missing, a symlink, or another user's [then] the warm-up is refused rather than run through a directory it does not own ⛔️
  - [if] the lock path is a healthy regular file in a 0700 directory this user owns [then] the warm-up locks and compiles, and never fchmods the lock file ⛔️
  - [if] `MDT_NUMBA_WARMUP_DIR` names an existing directory [then] it is used as-is; if it does not exist, the warm-up is refused rather than silently created ⛔️

### By-Ear Level Meter Calibration (METERCAL)

Tue 8 Sep 2026: the first song played straight into red and stayed there. Measured
cause: trim defaults to unity and EQ is flat, so the post-EQ/pre-fader tap sees each
file raw - most sampled library tracks lit all ten segments at unity gain (median
true peak +1.0 dBTP). The fixed scale was calibrated for a mixing desk where the
operator rides trim; nothing here gives the user a reason to. Decision already made:
a static master gain ceiling, not a look-ahead limiter - no limiter exists anywhere
in this codebase and adding one is a separate, contentious DSP commitment.

- [x] **METERCAL-01**: The clip latch only repaints red segments that are currently lit, not all three regardless of level, AND owns a dedicated top-segment indicator so a brief overshoot stays readable after the level falls back below red.
  - [if] the latch has no indicator of its own [then] a transient clip is unreportable once the level drops and the latch is decorative ⛔️
  - [if] the tap clips once and the level then falls back to green [then] the latch still shows for its hold window, but only the segments the CURRENT level lights render at full opacity ⛔️
  - [if] the meter is continuously clipping [then] it reads permanently red, which is correct - the defect was clipping painting all three red segments AT ANY level, including green ⛔️
  - [if] `.clipped .rb-channel-level-meter-segment.red` is matched without `.lit` in the selector [then] this requirement is not met ⛔️
- [x] **METERCAL-02**: `ChannelLevelMeter.svelte` shifts its segment thresholds through `segmentThresholdsForRed(red_enabled ? red_dbfs : null)` and lights segments by recomputing against that calibrated set, not the tap's default-scale count.
  - [if] `level_calibration.red_enabled` is false [then] the meter reads exactly as the fixed default scale (regression guard already covers `segmentThresholdsForRed(null)`) ⛔️
  - [if] `red_enabled` is true and a track hits the captured `red_dbfs` level [then] that track lights the first red segment, not 10/10 ⛔️
  - [if] a quieter track plays after calibration [then] it reads visibly lower than a loud one, i.e. the scale still discriminates ⛔️
  - [if] a low `red_dbfs` calibration shifts a threshold below `METER_FLOOR_DBFS` [then] `segmentThresholdsForRed` clamps it at the floor and `segmentsLitFromDbfs` reads exactly 0 at true silence for every `red_dbfs` the UI permits, never lighting a segment with no signal present (fixing a correctness bug that shipped earlier) ⛔️
- [x] **METERCAL-03**: A capture at the meter floor is REFUSED (a stopped deck reads -60 dBFS; arming that ceiling applies a 0.001 master multiplier and one click silences the output), and calibration disk writes are SERIALIZED so the last click is the last write. R and M icons top-left of each channel strip capture the channel's current tap level (dBFS) and arm `red_dbfs`/`ceiling_dbfs` independently; toggling either off clears only its `*_enabled` flag, keeping the captured number for a later re-arm. Persisted through `PUT /api/v1/ui-prefs` (`level_calibration`), following the existing `auto_sync` nested-object pattern in `prefs.svelte.ts`.
  - [if] R is clicked while a track plays [then] `red_dbfs` becomes that instant's tap reading and `red_enabled` becomes true, both persisted to disk and localStorage ⛔️
  - [if] M is clicked on a silent or stopped channel [then] nothing is captured and no ceiling is armed ⛔️
  - [if] two calibration clicks land in quick succession [then] exactly one write is in flight at a time and the final write carries the final state ⛔️
  - [if] a calibration write and an unrelated pref write (e.g. `setTheme`) land in the same tick [then] they share ONE disk-write queue and are still serialized, not just calibration writes against each other (fixing a BLOCKING gap that shipped earlier: only calibration writes were chained, every other setter in `prefs.svelte.ts` bypassed the queue) ⛔️
  - [if] an already-armed R is clicked [then] `red_enabled` becomes false and `red_dbfs` is unchanged ⛔️
  - [if] a client PUTs `level_calibration` with an `*_enabled: true` and no captured level [then] the backend's existing 422 (`ui_prefs.py::_parse_level_calibration`) still fires - a lit toggle never does nothing ⛔️
  - [if] LESS deck-layout mode is active [then] the R/M icons remain fully visible and clickable, never clipped by `.rb-mixer`'s `overflow: hidden` (the LESS deck-area floor undercounted `.strip-head`'s real height by 1px, widened 400px -> 401px rather than hiding the controls) ⛔️

- [x] **METERCAL-04**: M enforcement is a static master gain ceiling applied at `_masterGain` in `audio-engine.svelte.ts`: when `ceiling_enabled`, master gain is attenuated so 0 dBFS never exceeds the captured `ceiling_dbfs`; disabling removes the attenuation exactly. No limiter, no signal-dependent gain reduction anywhere in this path.
  - [if] M is enabled with a captured ceiling below 0 dBFS [then] the master `GainNode`'s value is the fader position times a fixed multiplier derived only from the captured level, never from the live signal ⛔️
  - [if] M is disabled [then] the multiplier is exactly 1 and master gain returns to the fader's own value ⛔️
  - [if] `audio-engine.svelte.ts` is touched for this [then] it gains zero new top-level imports - it is a hotspot file already at `frontend.max_fan_out`'s ceiling, so the calibrated value is pushed in from `Mixer.svelte` (which already imports both `audio-engine.svelte` and `prefs.svelte`) via a primitives-only `setLevelCeiling(dbfs, enabled)` method ⛔️

- [x] **METERCAL-05** (Sat 12 Sep 2026): Each deck's channel meter taps post-trim, post-EQ, and post-channel-fader on the same `fader` AudioNode the channel-volume slider drives, so the slider and indicator always describe the same audible channel level.
  - [if] a playing deck's channel fader is reduced [then] its visible level meter falls with the post-fader channel audio [⛔️ if the slider changes sound while its own indicator stays unchanged].
  - [if] the channel fader is closed [then] the channel meter reaches its silent floor on the next meter observation, while trim and EQ remain upstream contributors when the fader is open [else stop].
  - [if] a constant test signal runs through the production channel graph with unity fader then fader 0.5 [then] the half-gain reading is approximately 6 dB below unity within +/- 1 dB (`meter-artifact.spec.ts` via `channel-meter-browser-entry.ts`) [else stop].
  - [if] the master meter tap or its post-master-gain source changes as a side effect of this work [then] fail; the master meter must still follow `_masterGain` only (`master-output-meter.test.mjs`, `meter-artifact.spec.ts`) [else stop].

### Daemon security (SEC)

- [x] **SEC-01**: The webui daemon rejects requests whose `Host` is not in the configured allowlist (`127.0.0.1` / `localhost` / `::1`, `MUSIC_DJ_SHARE_HOST`, `MUSIC_DJ_ALLOWED_HOSTS`) and rejects mutating HTTP methods when a foreign `Origin` is present. Non-loopback binds without `MUSIC_DJ_ALLOWED_HOSTS` fail at startup.
  - [if] `GET /api/...` with `Host: evil.example` returns 2xx [then] fail; expect 403 with `HOST_NOT_ALLOWED` ⛔️
  - [if] a mutating request with `Origin: https://evil.example` and a loopback Host returns 2xx [then] fail; expect 403 `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED` ⛔️
  - [if] a mutating request from the real UI origin or with no Origin header fails [then] fail (no regression) ⛔️
  - [if] share-host requests change behavior [then] fail; `share_gate` semantics stay intact ⛔️
  - [if] the packaged Tauri shell engine origin can no longer load the UI [then] fail ⛔️
  - [if] the daemon starts on a non-loopback `--host` with an empty allowlist [then] it must exit non-zero with an explicit message ⛔️
- [x] **SEC-02** (ADR-0043): `docs/security/security.md` shows EXACTLY what the security review system does today. Its status table is generated from repo files by `scripts/security/security_status.py`, and its SWOT is pinned to the table it was written against.
  - [if] the committed status table differs from what the repo files imply [then] fail; `tests/test_security_status_doc.py` goes red ⛔️
  - [if] the table changes and the SWOT is not re-acknowledged (`--ack-swot`) [then] fail ⛔️
  - [if] a check is reported WIRED when no workflow, hook or config runs it [then] fail; an empty repo reports nothing WIRED ⛔️
- [ ] **SEC-03** (ADR-0043): Agents merge to a private repo without security gates; code reaches the public repo only through a promotion job that pushes a private `main` SHA whose every required CI and security job completed with `success`. Design: `docs/security/merge-and-promotion.md`.
  - [if] a SHA with any required job cancelled, skipped, queued or absent is promoted [then] fail ⛔️
  - [if] promotion would need a non-fast-forward push [then] it must exit non-zero, never force-push ⛔️
  - [if] a self-hosted runner is registered on the public repo [then] fail ⛔️
- [ ] **SEC-04** (ADR-0043): A weekly AI security review reads the high-risk paths listed in `ops/security/weekly-security-review.md` and replaces the body of the rolling `security: weekly review` issue.
  - [if] a run reports no findings without listing the files it read and the `main` SHA it reviewed [then] fail ⛔️
  - [if] the routine pushes, opens a PR or edits files [then] fail; it is read-only ⛔️
  - [if] the prompt file changes but the status table still shows the old routine [then] fail ⛔️

The label is shown in EVERY auth state (regression, fixed): the top bar passes `showLabel` unconditionally, never a signed-in expression, so the signed-out bar still reads "Sign in with Google" beside the gray bauble.

### Headphone Cue Output Routing (CUEOUT)

Added Fri 11 Sep 2026 from headphone-cue research (README + part 2 + eight cited
source reports). Findings that shape these ids: (1) picking a
second output device is the easy half, clock drift between two independently clocked devices
is the real problem (at 100 ppm the cue slides past the 15-20 ms DJ-detectable offset in about
2.5 minutes); (2) only VirtualDJ and Mixxx do true two-device cue, both natively; rekordbox,
Serato, Traktor and djay Pro on Mac require one multi-channel interface, an Aggregate Device
or a mono split cable, and no incumbent supports Bluetooth cueing or ships latency
compensation; (3) the shipped `player/headphones.ts` bridge (cue bus -> MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode
-> detached `<audio>` -> `setSinkId`) is architecturally right but WebKit only fixed
"`setSinkId()` reporting success without switching output for a single-track MediaStream" in
Safari Technology Preview 251 (Wed 26 Aug 2026), so on the shipping WKWebView it likely reports
`active: true` while playing out of the system default; (4) Chrome has already been observed
clamping a 4-out DDJ-400 to `maxChannelCount = 2`, so the controller phones jack is not
reachable from Web Audio until a spike proves otherwise. The product modes below are named so
they stop being conflated: practice (headphones only), split cable, two outputs, controller
soundcard, external mixer.

- [x] **CUEOUT-02**: Split-cable mode. `output_mode = split_cable` sends a mono downmix of master to the LEFT channel and a mono downmix of the cue bus to the RIGHT channel of the single main output (the djay / Serato / VirtualDJ split-cable contract), with MIX and per-channel CUE still live on the right leg. The UI states plainly that the room feed is mono in this mode and that a true DJ splitter cable, not a Y cable, is required.
  - [x] [if] `split_cable` is active [then] L carries only master (mono sum) and R carries only cue (mono sum); a stereo test tone panned hard left on a cued deck with fader down is audible on R and silent on L ⛔️
  - [x] [if] `split_cable` is active and no channel has CUE on [then] R is silent ⛔️
  - [x] [if] the mode switches back to `practice` or `two_outputs` [then] the main output returns to stereo master within one parameter-smoothing window, with no click (setTargetAtTime, not a hard set) ⛔️
- [x] **CUEOUT-03**: Two-outputs hardening. In `two_outputs` mode the headphone bus has a manual head delay in milliseconds (Mixxx "Head Delay" contract, 0-500 ms, persisted with the mixer config) applied as a delay line on the monitor path, and the UI shows a standing warning that two independently clocked devices drift and that Bluetooth as the monitor leg is for auditioning, not beatmatching.
  - [if] head delay is set to N ms [then] the monitor output lags the cue bus by N ms within one buffer of tolerance, measured by a loopback test against a click train ⛔️
  - [if] head delay is set outside 0-500 or non-finite [then] the setter throws and the previous value stands ⛔️
  - [if] the selected monitor device's label matches a Bluetooth transport (enumerated device label or CoreAudio transport type where exposed) [then] the warning names Bluetooth explicitly ⛔️
  - [if] the app restarts [then] the head delay value is restored from persisted mixer config ⛔️
- [x] **CUEOUT-04**: Agent-native parity for every headphone control. `apps/webui/server` exposes HTTP endpoints mirroring the in-page performance IPC for `headphone_mix`, `headphone_level`, `channel_cue`, `output_mode`, `head_delay_ms`, `headphone_outputs_refresh`, `headphone_output_select`, plus a read endpoint returning the full `HeadphoneState`, so a CLI or agent can drive the same flows without a live page context.
  - [if] `POST /api/v1/performance/headphones/mix {"value":0.25}` is sent while the webview is attached [then] `mixerState.headphones.mix` reads 0.25 within 250 ms and the GET reflects it ⛔️
  - [if] a value outside 0..1 (or an unknown `output_mode`) is posted [then] the endpoint returns 4xx with the same error text the IPC throws, and state is unchanged ⛔️
  - [if] no webview is attached [then] the endpoint returns 503 naming the missing page rather than 200 with a stale state ⛔️

- [x] **CUEOUT-15** (shipped this PR): Library preview on the cue bus. Clicking any mini-waveform in the library plays THAT track from THAT point through the headphone cue, without loading it onto a deck and without touching the room mix. It is the app's fifth voice and the only one that is not a deck: it joins the graph at `cueSum`, the single node every channel CUE already joins, so it inherits the whole CUEOUT routing policy unchanged in all three output modes (`two_outputs` to the cue sink, `split_cable` to the right leg, `practice` to the MAIN output through `practiceCueMix`) and CUEOUT-09's P0 that the MAIN speaker line is never interrupted still holds, because the preview makes no second `setSinkId` call and no connection to the master bus. A click on a mini-waveform NEVER seeks a deck any more: it used to seek every deck holding that `stable_id` with no check on `playing` and none on `is_master`, so browsing could jump a deck that was live on air while `_loadOntoDeck` immediately below it revalidates the master three separate ways. the user chose the replacement semantics (ADR-0075 decision 4): the browser is a monitoring surface, never a transport control, so the click previews even when a deck holds the same track, is playing, and is the elected master, and stopping a preview never touches a deck either. A streaming row (no local audio) and a missing-file row (broken link) are refused with a toast before any decode, the same refusal a deck load gives. Audio is sourced with `decodeAudioData` into an `AudioBufferSourceNode`, the decoder the four decks already use, so the preview's format support is exactly theirs; a media element was tried first and abandoned on evidence (see ADR-0075 decision 2). Exactly ONE track is decoded at a time and its PCM is released on stop and before decoding a replacement. A preview that could not be heard is refused with the named cause (no audio graph, a selected cue device that is not playing, a cue path at zero gain) and never started into silence; a barely audible one plays with a warning; practice mode says out loud that it is on the MAIN output. `mixerState.headphones.supported` is deliberately NOT consulted, because it only records that the I/O menu has enumerated devices and practice and split-cable previews need no device selection at all. Agent parity: IPC `preview_cue` / `preview_stop` with the HTTP mirror `POST /api/v1/performance/headphones/preview` and `.../preview/stop` (CUEOUT-04 pattern); a refusal is a 400 carrying the operator-facing reason, never a 200 over a preview that never started; and `PerformanceState.preview` carries the live stable id, playing flag, position, duration and route, so an agent that can start a preview can also read one.
  - [if] a library mini-waveform is clicked at 50% while a cue device is selected [then] that track plays from near its half-way point on the cue bus and nothing of it reaches the MAIN output ⛔️
  - [if] a library mini-waveform is clicked while that track is also loaded on a deck that is playing and is the elected master [then] the click previews that track on the cue bus and the deck does not seek, keeps playing, and stays master (e2e `preview-cue-library.spec.ts`, real pointer click on the row's `preview-strip`) ⛔️
  - [if] a second mini-waveform is clicked [then] the first preview stops, its decoded PCM is released, and exactly one preview playhead is shown in the table ⛔️
  - [if] the same mini-waveform is clicked again [then] the track is not decoded a second time ⛔️
  - [if] the cue path gain is zero (MIX fully at the master end, or GAIN at zero) [then] the click is refused naming the knob to raise, rather than appearing to start ⛔️
  - [if] the operator has never opened the I/O menu [then] a practice-mode preview still plays, with a warning that it is on the MAIN output ⛔️
  - [if] the stop control on the previewing row is pressed [then] audio on `cueSum` returns to silence and the preview playhead disappears ⛔️
  - [if] a preview is stopped while its track is live on a deck [then] that deck's position, playing flag and master flag are untouched (e2e `preview-cue-library.spec.ts`, via the row's STOP PREVIEW button) ⛔️
  - [if] `POST /api/v1/performance/headphones/preview` is issued while the cue path is silent [then] it answers 400 with the same wording the operator would have seen, not 200 ⛔️
  - [if] the track's file is missing on disk, or it is a streaming URI with no local audio [then] the click is refused with a toast naming the cause before any decode is attempted (implemented in `BrowserPanel.svelte` `previewSeek`; no automated test yet as of Wed 16 Sep 2026) ⛔️

- [ ] **CUEOUT-22** (built, awaiting Mac hands; IOPIN-05; ADR-NEW-native-cue-sink-in-the-mac-shell): Two-device headphone cue in the installed macOS app. WKWebView has no `setSinkId`, so the CUEOUT-09 route (a second `AudioContext` pinned to the headphones) cannot exist in the shipped app. The desktop shell serves a token-guarded loopback WebSocket (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/cue_sink.rs`, announced to the page as `globalThis.OPENDJ_CUE_SINK`) and plays the cue bus from a CoreAudio AUHAL output unit bound to the chosen HEADPHONE CUE device. The page keeps the whole monitor graph (MIX, GAIN, HEAD DELAY, calibration chirp) and only the last hop changes: the existing cue-bridge sender worklet's PCM is relayed by a dedicated web Worker (`cue-native-sink.worker.ts`) over that socket into a lock-free ring that holds the same target fill as the in-page bridge and corrects clock drift by at most one dropped or repeated frame per render callback, decided on a smoothed fill so relay burstiness never reads as drift. The room mix never leaves the webview, so master latency is unchanged. A selected MAIN in the packaged app records `routes.master` as `selected` after the native pin succeeds (2026-10-05: the native branch of `_applyMasterSink` returned before that write, so calibration refused a chosen MAIN as capability `default`). Clearing MAIN returns the route to `default`. Outputs are listed by the shell (ids `native:<CoreAudio UID>`), so the output pickers fill without a microphone prompt. Inputs (AUDIO IN, the calibration mic) still come from the webview: when it withholds their names the panel reads `permission_needed`, not `listed`, and its grant button asks the webview for the microphone once, so AUDIO IN and cue calibration can pick a mic. MASTER/MAIN in the Mac app is the macOS default output (that is where the webview plays): an unpinned MASTER auto-pins to the CURRENT default output rather than a guessed speaker, unless that default is the cue device, and while a cue device is open the shell puts the default back on the pinned MASTER if macOS moves it (headphone plug, Bluetooth reconnect), extending CUEOUT-09's P0 to the Mac app. A vanished cue device stops the native output and never falls back to another device. Chrome keeps the CUEOUT-09 route unchanged.

- [x] **CUEOUT-18** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026, measured on the live preview): `GET /api/v1/performance/headphones` answers from the best-informed open page, not the last page to publish. Every page names itself with a `client_id` in its mirror publish, and the engine keeps each client's latest headphone report (`apps/webui/server/headphone_reports.py`). A report whose device lists were read (`device_access.status` = `listed`) is not replaced by a report from a different client whose lists were not; between equals the most recent wins; a client's own later report always replaces its own earlier one; a client silent for 90 s (`HEADPHONE_REPORT_STALE_S`) expires, and a page that closes is forgotten at once. The payload keeps every earlier field and adds `reporting_client_id` and `report_age_ms`. Found because an automation tab with the microphone denied published `permission_denied` with 1 output over the operator tab's `listed` state with 9 outputs. The UI mirror document itself, and which page claims an agent command, are still shared by all open pages.
  - [if] one client reports `listed` with 9 outputs and a different client then reports `permission_denied` or `not_checked` [then] GET returns the `listed` state and names that client [⛔️ if the later report replaces it].
  - [if] the `listed` client itself later reports `permission_denied` [then] GET returns `permission_denied` [⛔️ if its earlier state is kept].
  - [if] two clients both report `listed` [then] the most recent report is returned [⛔️ if the older one is].
  - [if] the `listed` client sends nothing for more than 90 s while another client keeps reporting [then] the other client is returned [⛔️ if a closed tab's state is served indefinitely].
  - [if] a page publishes with no `client_id` [then] GET answers 200 with every earlier field and `reporting_client_id` "anonymous" [⛔️ if the route rejects it or drops a field].
  - [if] any state is returned [then] `report_age_ms` is the real age of that client's report [⛔️ if it is absent or zeroed for an old report].

### Comment-pin requirements: Mixtour and audio I/O (IOPIN)

Recorded Tue 22 Sep 2026. Every item below is tagged `source: comment-pin`.
The immutable intake record carries full pin text, timestamp, source build,
device hostname, route and attachment. Delivery/verification tasks are tracked
separately.
These requirements refine the earlier CUEOUT and controller requirements; they do
not declare their implementations or physical acceptance complete.

- [x] **IOPIN-01** (source: comment-pin): Centralized browser input ownership. MIDI browse always advances the track selection with directional scroll lookahead, irrespective of earlier mouse/keyboard focus, except while a context menu owns navigation. Keyboard arrows and WASD move selection when no text input owns the keys; left/right traverse playlist, track and deck-load focus. Enter chooses the focused target; double Enter follows the existing double-click load behavior with its master-deck protection. Research official controller conventions and retain the explicit Open DJ decisions.
  - [if] MIDI/keyboard selection moves beyond the visible rows [then] the selected row and directional lookahead become visible, including virtualized lists ⛔️
  - [if] a text input or context menu owns navigation [then] its keystrokes do not accidentally browse or load a track; exiting restores the documented owner ⛔️
  - [if] the browse encoder turns after another control had focus [then] selection advances once per decoded step without mutating an unrelated control ⛔️

- [ ] **IOPIN-02** (source: comment-pin): Corresponding deck and mixer channel share a clear hover/focus treatment, with consistent color and emphasis for all four decks.
  - [if] either a deck or its mixer channel is hovered/focused [then] both identify the same deck without highlighting a different channel ⛔️
  - [if] hover/focus ends [then] transient emphasis clears without losing playback or selection state ⛔️

- [ ] **IOPIN-03** (source: comment-pin): The audio I/O trigger shows a compact quick-settings explanation after 100 ms and hides it immediately on pointer leave. Clicking opens a separate persistent panel with visible X and Esc dismissal and the hint "Esc or X to dismiss". Optional BOOTH and advanced channel assignment show disabled "Coming soon" rows above the three device selectors.
  - [if] the pointer briefly crosses or leaves the trigger [then] no sticky or oversized hover panel remains ⛔️
  - [if] I/O is clicked, dismissed or reopened [then] device choices remain accurate and audio is uninterrupted ⛔️
  - [if] a future routing row is clicked [then] it cannot alter any output; already implemented split-cable/controller modes remain available ⛔️

- [ ] **IOPIN-04** (source: comment-pin): Move practice/main/split/two-output configuration, capability explanations and routing feedback inside I/O. Use one accessible headphones/Bluetooth/speaker trigger and headphone icons on MIX and VOL. Delay guidance explains relative master/cue latency with a compact visual and keyboard/scroll instructions. Transient action failures/results use existing toasts; persistent capability context sits beside the relevant selector.
  - [if] I/O is closed [then] persistent warnings and routing mode controls do not occupy mixer space ⛔️
  - [if] routing is unsupported or fails [then] the applicable option explains why inside I/O and the failure is surfaced once without changing a healthy master path ⛔️

- [ ] **IOPIN-05** (source: comment-pin; v1 priority): The installed macOS shell supports separately selected master and headphone devices through a proved platform route. Research WKWebView and Core Audio capabilities, implement the smallest suitable native route when required, and verify actual output separation. This extends CUEOUT-07/09/12/14; Mixtour channel-pair routing is a separate supported topology. Built as CUEOUT-22 (native CoreAudio cue sink in the shell); awaiting the installed-app check on a Mac.
  - [if] native two-device support is claimed [then] two physical output devices carry independent master/cue audio in the installed shell, including reconnect, with recorded device/build identities ⛔️

- [ ] **IOPIN-06** (source: comment-pin; pickup policy confirmed Tue 22 Sep 2026): After software changes an absolute MIDI-controlled dial/fader, show its last observed hardware position as a ghost and prevent value jumps until hardware crosses the current software value. Default to pickup and expose an explicit Jump override; relative encoders remain immediate. Retain per-device/per-control/per-deck ownership through bank changes and reconnect.
  - [if] hardware is away from a software-edited value [then] ghost feedback shows the last observed hardware position and movement cannot jump the software value before pickup ⛔️
  - [if] hardware crosses the target in either direction, or software is moved back to hardware [then] control resumes without an extra jump ⛔️

Do not blame room noise without evidence. Retain selectable chirp and the existing alternate probe (identify from research/code; do not guess). Place the calibration view below device selection so both stay visible.

The label distinguishes a measured application signal from proof that the physical speaker emitted it. Input capture obeys permission/lifecycle and avoids unintended Bluetooth hands-free switching.

Key compatibility follows existing Camelot rules; a row receives combined green emphasis only when both match.
  - [if] master tempo changes [then] BPM cell severity and compatibility refresh using the closest raw/half/double relationship ⛔️
  - [if] either key or tempo is unknown/incompatible [then] the row is not marked jointly compatible ⛔️

- [x] **IOPIN-12** (source: live observation, Fri 25 Sep 2026 21:27 UTC; shipped; installed-shell hardware acceptance pending): A connected Mixtour Pro map redirects the page into `?djio=master12-cue34` once. When the selected output exposes fewer than 4 channels (`AudioDestinationNode.maxChannelCount`), the graph plays ordinary stereo master with cue 3/4 off instead of throwing, raises a click-to-copy warn toast naming the channel count and the fix (one on screen at a time: a rebuild while it shows counts on it instead of stacking another, and a rebuild after it expires raises it again), shows the same message inline in the I/O headphone section with a hover title for the count, and publishes it to agents as `output_topology` in the ui-mirror. Any failure while building the audio graph discards the half-built context and every deck node already built on it, so the next deck load builds a fresh graph with every deck wired; when that build ran inside a headphone or master output selection, the selection rejects with the build's own error and the I/O panel shows it. The output-stall rebuild (a new context with the loaded decks re-attached) follows the same rule: when it fails (its new graph cannot be built, the old graph's teardown rejects, or a deck's processor cannot be re-attached) the graph state is still reset, each deck left without a processor is unloaded with `audio graph recreate failed, reload the track: <cause>` on the deck instead of showing a track that cannot play, and every deck it did re-attach keeps playing. Every graph reset, successful rebuilds included, unregisters the context it drops, so library mode does not count a replaced context as leaked. A page that already carries `djio` (including a fallback page), an explicit empty `djio`, or `extroute` is never redirected, so the reload cannot loop. In the installed shell, a page that is leaving for `djio` never keeps native MIDI live: a MIDI boot that runs again before the redirect lands neither reloads a second time nor subscribes, and a page that had already subscribed (the Mixtour plugged in after boot, or an in-app navigation whose plain link dropped `djio`) stops its hot-plug poll and waits for the Tauri unlisten to land before its one reload, so no press arrives twice after it. An in-app navigation that drops `djio` therefore costs one reload back into it; carrying `djio` across in-app links is not done. Selecting the macOS output device from the app (`setSinkId`) is out of scope: WKWebView lacks it and it would override the saved MASTER selector.
  - [if] djio is requested on a 2-channel output [then] every deck loads and plays through stereo master, the destination stays at 2 channels, and the fallback is visible in the toast, the I/O panel and the ui-mirror ⛔️
  - [if] djio is requested on a 4-channel output [then] master still routes to 1/2 and cue to 3/4, with no fallback shown ⛔️
  - [if] a graph build throws partway [then] no deck is left without a graph: the failed context is closed and the next load wires all decks on a fresh context with no cross-context connections ⛔️
  - [if] the controller map is seen again on a page whose URL carries `djio` (the redirect's target, or a fallback page) [then] the page is not reloaded ⛔️
  - [if] the redirect fires on a page already subscribed to native MIDI (a hot-plug, or an in-app navigation that dropped `djio`) [then] the hot-plug poll stops and the Tauri unlisten lands before the one `location.replace` ⛔️
  - [if] the MIDI boot runs twice before the redirect lands [then] `location.replace` fires once and no native MIDI listener is registered on the leaving page ⛔️
  - [if] the graph build fails inside a headphone or master output selection [then] the selection error and the I/O panel error name the build's own cause, not a stale-operation error ⛔️
  - [if] the fallback graph is rebuilt while its toast is on screen [then] exactly one fallback toast shows, with its repeat count ⛔️
  - [if] an output-stall rebuild cannot build its new graph or close the old one [then] no deck keeps a track it cannot play: each deck left without a processor is unloaded with the cause on the deck, and the next load builds a fresh graph ⛔️
  - [if] an output-stall rebuild succeeds, or re-attaches some decks before failing [then] every re-attached deck keeps its track and plays, and only the live context stays registered ⛔️
  - [if] an output selection is parked on `setSinkId` across an output-stall rebuild [then] it rejects as stale and publishes nothing ⛔️
  - Evidence (Thu 1 Oct 2026): proved in a real browser by `tests/e2e/iopin-12-real-audio.spec.ts` (djio on a 2-channel output loads two decks, plays audibly at the destination and shows the fallback; a successful output-stall rebuild moves a playing deck to a new context, audible) and `tests/e2e/audio-output-topology.spec.ts` (master 1/2 and cue 3/4 routing on a real four-channel graph). The node suites `iopin-12-*.test.mjs` run on a recording stand-in for Web Audio and are wiring checks, not acceptance evidence. The criteria above that still have only wiring checks (a build that throws partway, a failed or partial stall rebuild, a selection parked on `setSinkId`, the single counted toast, the I/O panel notice, djio active in the app on a 4-channel device) are tracked as follow-up debt.

- [x] **IOPIN-13** (source: engine test failure on the Preview branch, Thu 1 Oct 2026; shipped; hardware acceptance pending): The built-in controller maps load in the Rust audio engine, so `?engine=rust` has controller support. The classic Mixtour `nameMatch` excludes the Mixtour Pro with an alternation instead of a negative lookahead, because the engine compiles patterns with `regex_lite`, which has no lookaround. The ten Mixtour Pro actions that read page-owned state (`deck_sync_toggle`, `deck_key_sync_toggle`, `deck_auto_loop_toggle`, `deck_manual_loop_cycle`, `deck_loop_scale`, `deck_key_nudge`, `deck_tempo_nudge`, `deck_stem_eq_toggle`, `controller_pad_mode`, `controller_pad`) are forwarded by the engine to the page, like `deck_hot_cue`, instead of refusing the whole export.
  - [if] the engine loads the exported built-in maps [then] every map compiles and none is refused for an unknown action type or an unsupported pattern ⛔️
  - [if] a classic Mixtour port name is resolved by the page matcher or the engine matcher, in either map order [then] it selects the classic map and never the Pro map ⛔️
  - [if] a Mixtour Pro port name is resolved by either matcher, in either map order [then] it selects the Pro map and never the classic map ⛔️
  - [if] an exported `nameMatch` uses syntax `regex_lite` rejects [then] the page-side and engine-side tests both fail ⛔️
  - [if] Mixtour Pro SYNC is pressed under the Rust engine [then] the engine forwards `deck_sync_toggle` to the page rather than applying or dropping it ⛔️

- [x] **IOPIN-14** (source: operator report, Thu 1 Oct 2026; real-hardware and installed-shell acceptance pending): The audio I/O panel never draws a device list it could not read as an empty one. The page reads the device list at boot, again each time I/O opens, and on every `devicechange`. The output list always carries a selectable `System default output`; the browser's unnamed placeholder entries (empty id) are never drawn as rows. The outcome of the read is published as `mixer.headphones.device_access` with one of seven named states (`not_checked`, `listed`, `permission_needed`, `permission_denied`, `api_missing`, `enumeration_failed`, `timeout`), a message, and an action; the panel shows the message with a `Grant access to list devices` or `Retry device check` button, and `GET /api/v1/performance/headphones` returns the same lists and state to agents. What opening I/O may ask for is one build switch, `VITE_IO_DEVICE_ACCESS_ON_OPEN`, set in `apps/webui/frontend/vite.config.ts`: the dev server is `request`, so when the browser has never been asked (permission state `prompt`) opening I/O requests microphone access, stops the stream as soon as it opens, and lists again, which costs one prompt per origin because the browser keeps the grant; every built app is `button`, so opening never requests and only the grant button does. Mounting never requests in either mode, a granted or denied origin is never asked on open, and the request selects no device. A standalone test-harness vite config that does not set the switch reads as `button`; a set value that is neither word throws. A shell that cannot pin an output device (no `setSinkId`) says so and disables the MASTER and CUE selects instead of showing empty menus. The MASTER and CUE picks are saved by device id and name; when a saved device is not in a fully listed set the panel names it and says the system default output is in use. A saved device is not re-selected automatically.
- [x] **IOPIN-15** (Thu 1 Oct 2026; `apps/webui/frontend/tests/unit/performance-ui-command-result.test.mjs`, 5 tests, each guard mutated in both directions; the bare `catch {}` at the UI command boundary is what hid the IOPIN-14 regression): `runPerformanceCommandFromUi` never drops a failure in silence and never rejects. It resolves a typed result: `{ ok: true }`; `{ ok: false, reason: 'no_session' }` when no command session is current (the route has not started one yet, or has torn it down), which is the one expected refusal and is logged at debug only, with no toast and no error row; or `{ ok: false, reason: 'failed' }` for everything else, which is always on screen and in the console by the time the caller sees it. A failure the dispatcher already toasted is not toasted twice, a load that suppressed its toast still writes a console error, and a failure the dispatcher did not persist (it lands after its session was torn down) is toasted at the boundary.
  - [if] the page boots and nobody has opened I/O [then] `device_access.status` has left `not_checked` and the output list is not empty ⛔️
  - [if] I/O is opened on a machine with an audio output [then] MASTER and CUE each offer `System default output` with a non-empty label, and no option has an empty value or label ⛔️
  - [if] the browser withholds device names [then] the state is `permission_needed` or `permission_denied`, never `listed`, and the panel shows a message and an action button ⛔️
  - [if] the device API is missing, rejects, or does not answer in time [then] the state is `api_missing`, `enumeration_failed`, or `timeout` respectively, each with a retry action and the system default output still listed ⛔️
  - [if] every device is named [then] the state is `listed`, no action button is shown, and the parity route returns the same outputs and inputs the panel shows ⛔️
  - [if] I/O opens in a `request` build with permission state `prompt` [then] exactly one stream is opened and stopped, the state becomes `listed`, and later opens open no stream ⛔️
  - [if] I/O opens in a `request` build and the operator refuses [then] the state is `permission_denied` with how to re-allow, no error is raised, and later opens do not ask ⛔️
  - [if] I/O opens in a `button` build, or the page merely mounts in any build [then] no stream is opened ⛔️
  - [if] a saved MASTER or CUE device is absent from a `listed` set [then] a notice names it and the system default fallback; on a withheld list no such notice is raised ⛔️

  cue surface. Unknown status families and unbound wires learn-log as unmapped and
  never run a command. Hardware capture is out of this PR.
  - [if] a fake WebMIDI device named DDJ-FLX4 is connected with the map registered
    [then] the map is selected and the binding count is logged
  - [if] a bound FLX4 control is sent [then] the matching engine command runs
  - [if] an unknown control or status family is sent [then] it is logged as
    unmapped (or out of P0 scope) and no command runs

- [x] **CTRL-02** (shipped this PR, follow-on work): Agent-native live MIDI
  capture probe, the onboarding tier T3 instrument that adjudicates the
  theory-first map against real hardware. `uv run tools/controller-probe/capture.py`
  exposes `ports`, `sniff`, `capture` and `diff`: it opens the CoreMIDI source by
  name substring, decodes every non-realtime inbound message, reverse-looks-up
  each (status, code) against `tools/controller-probe/flx4_expected_map.json`,
  walks a filtered set of expected controls one at a time while writing a
  crash-safe JSON record on every step, and grades that record with a nonzero
  exit on any mismatch. It is the CLI equivalent of the in-app learn wizard, so an agent adjudicates the map
  before that UI exists.
  - [if] the port name substring matches zero or more than one CoreMIDI source
    [then] the probe exits nonzero listing every candidate rather than guessing
  - [if] a control sends a wire pair absent from the expected map [then] the
    sniff line reads UNMAPPED and `diff` lists that pair as EXTRA
  - [if] any captured control never sent its expected (status, code) [then]
    `diff` exits 1, and a control that sent nothing at all is `skipped` rather
    than counted as a mismatch

- [x] **CTRL-04** (shipped; decision in ADR-NEW-fractional-beat-loops; physical pad and audible acceptance pending; CTRL-03 is in progress): Beat loops accept fractional lengths. `beat_loop` takes any finite positive beat count through the shared command and the installed MIDI-map schema, so the Mixtour Pro Auto Loop pads (1/4 to 32 beats) and Bounce Loop pads (1/32 to 4 beats) engage the length printed on the pad. The loop starts on a real PQTZ beat; a fractional end is interpolated between the two measured beat timestamps around it, never from nominal BPM, and a whole-beat end stays the exact recorded timestamp. The on-screen loop-length selector stays whole-beat.
  - [if] a half-beat loop is engaged on a deck with a beatgrid [then] it ends halfway between the two measured beats around its end point rather than at a nominal-BPM offset ⛔️
  - [if] a whole-beat loop is engaged [then] its end is the exact recorded beat timestamp, unchanged by the fractional path ⛔️
  - [if] the beat count is zero, negative or not finite [then] the command is refused with an explicit error and no loop is engaged ⛔️
  - [if] the grid has too few beats to cover a fractional range [then] the loop is refused rather than estimated ⛔️
  - [if] a fractional beat loop is scheduled [then] it is not re-snapped to the manual 1/4/8-beat grid and stays within the track's real duration ⛔️
- [x] **CTRL-05** (shipped; decision in `docs/decisions/ADR-NEW-independent-stem-controls-for-controller-pads.md`; physical pad acceptance pending): Bass and other stems are controlled independently. Mute, solo and gain exist for `bass` and `other` alongside vocal, instrumental and drums; instrumental stays the parent of the two (gains multiply, either mute silences the branch, mute wins over solo). The Mixtour Pro Neural Mix pads select drums, bass, other and vocal, with an exclusive solo that clears every other solo in one engine update. The independent controls are kept in query state and in session and rescue snapshots, and are restored only once the deck's stems have finished loading.
  - [if] bass is muted on a deck with a ready four-part bundle [then] other keeps playing, and instrumental gain still scales both ⛔️
  - [if] a Neural Mix pad is pressed on a deck whose stems are two-part, loading or absent [then] the pad warns and stays inert rather than acting on a control that does not exist ⛔️
  - [if] an exclusive solo is dispatched [then] every other stem solo is cleared in the same update, while a non-exclusive solo from the UI keeps its previous behavior ⛔️
  - [if] a session or rescue snapshot saved before these controls existed is restored [then] bass and other start unmuted, unsoloed and at unity ⛔️
  - [if] a snapshot holds a mute, solo or non-default gain for a stem the loaded bundle does not offer [then] restore fails with an explicit error rather than dropping the saved effect ⛔️
  - [if] the deck is reloaded or its stems fail while a restore is waiting [then] the restore stops with an explicit error and sends no stem command to the new load ⛔️

### Beatgrid flag (GRIDFLAG)

Recorded Thu 1 Oct 2026, aligned with the deck beatgrid source ADR: decks stay on rekordbox's grid for v1, so the flag says Beat Sync may wander on the track, never that the track is broken.

- [x] **GRIDFLAG-01** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026): One beatgrid-quality rule, shared by the deck
  warning and the library flag. `apps/analysis_beatgrid/grid_quality.py` is the reference and
  `GridQualityThresholds` its single config; `src/lib/rb/grid-quality.ts` mirrors it and is pinned
  to it by `tests/fixtures/grid_quality_conformance.json`. A grid is flagged when any beat interval
  sits more than 3 ms off the median interval. A flagged grid is `suspect` (uneven grid over steady
  music) when its constant-tempo regions (25 ms, 16 beats) cover at least 50% of the beats and at
  least 70% of the beats sit on the longest region's line, else `variable_tempo`. Fewer than two
  beats, a missing or unreadable analysis file, no rekordbox grid, or a track not yet scanned is
  `unknown`, which is never shown as ok or as a flag.
  - [if] a steady track carries an uneven grid [then] it is `suspect` with the count of uneven
    intervals, the worst deviation in ms and where it is
  - [if] the tempo really changes (a ramp, two tempos) [then] it is `variable_tempo`, not `suspect`
  - [if] a threshold changes [then] the rule version changes and both languages follow the fixture
  - [if] a track is remapped to a different ANLZ file with the same size and mtime [then] the stored verdict is not current and the scan re-parses the new file [else stop]
- [x] **GRIDFLAG-02** (shipped Thu 1 Oct 2026): Verdicts are computed once per grid version and

  - [if] a scan repeats over unchanged grids [then] nothing is parsed and nothing is written
  - [if] a grid file changes [then] the next scan replaces its verdict

    side as `FILTER_HP_FLOOR_HZ = 30` up to `FILTER_HP_CEILING_HZ = 6300` on an

### Native Audio Engine (NAE)

Recorded Thu 24 Sep 2026. The engine is additive: the app keeps playing through the Web Audio engine until the shadow null tests pass.

- [x] **NAE-01** (shipped this PR): `odj-audio`, a standalone Rust engine process (`apps/audio-engine/`) that owns playback state behind one mailbox. Protocol v1 is newline-delimited JSON on stdio; command names and fields are the audio subset of the page's `PerformanceCommand` in the same 0..1 knob units, and every command gets a `result` echoing its id.
  - [if] a command the page owns (`browser_select_playlist`) or an unknown type is sent [then] the result is `ok: false` with code `unsupported` ⛔️
  - [if] an engine command this build does not do yet (`stem_mute`, `key_sync`) is sent [then] the result is `not_implemented` naming the plan that brings it, never a silent no-op ⛔️
  - [if] such a command is malformed as the page's parser sees it (an unexpected field, a missing or mistyped field, a value outside the page's set) [then] it is `invalid`, as the page refuses it; only a well-formed one is `not_implemented` ⛔️
  - [if] an optional field the page reads is present but `null` or the wrong type (`load.stems`, `load.suppressCommandErrorToast`, `load.stable_id`, `play.quantize`, `play.start_at_context_sec`, `beat_loop.start_ms`, and the engine's own `load.bpm`, `engine_advance.ms` and a beatgrid entry's `n`) [then] the command is `invalid`, as the page's parser refuses it, rather than read as absent or as `not_implemented`; leaving the field out is how to send it absent ⛔️
  - [if] a knob value is outside 0..1 [then] the result is `invalid` naming the field, and nothing is clamped ⛔️
  - [if] a file's decoded sample rate changes part-way through [then] the load fails with `decode` rather than relabel the audio before the change ⛔️
  - [if] no packet of a file decodes (every one a decode error) [then] the load fails with `decode` rather than load the file as silence; a corrupt packet among good ones still plays as silence of its own length ⛔️
  - [if] `engine_advance` gives both `ms` and `frames`, or a load both `beatgrid` and `beatgrid_ms` [then] it is `invalid` rather than use one and drop the other ⛔️
  - [if] a `beat_loop` has a `start_ms` below 0 [then] it is `invalid`, as the page's parser refuses it, rather than start the loop on the first beat ⛔️
  - [if] a `beat_jump` lands past the decoded audio on a grid with no beat at or before its end [then] it is `invalid` and the playhead stays, as the page's `beatJumpTargetWithinDurationMs` refuses it ⛔️
  - [if] a message, a command or an object nested in one (a loop's bounds, a beat of a grid) carries a field the page's `_exactKeys` would not accept, such as a misspelled `quantise` [then] it is `invalid`, naming the unexpected fields, and nothing plays; the page-only `suppressCommandErrorToast` and `persist` are accepted and change nothing in the engine ⛔️
  - [if] a `beat_loop` or `beat_jump` reaches a deck with no real beatgrid, even one loaded with a tag `bpm` [then] it is `no_beatgrid` and nothing moves, as the page's `requireBeatGrid` refuses both; the tag BPM still times plan events and the tempo readout ⛔️
  - [if] a load's beatgrid has a time before 0, fewer than 2 beats, or beat numbers `n` that do not count 1, 2, 3, 4 around the bar [then] the load is `invalid`, as the page's `validateBeatGrid` refuses it; a track with no grid is loaded by leaving the grid out ⛔️
  - [if] a message's `id` is a number [then] its result carries the same number, not a string of it; [if] the `id` is a boolean, an object or an array [then] the message is `invalid` with a null id and the command does not run; no id or a null one answers with a null id ⛔️
  - [if] a `load` or `unload` carries `refuseIfMaster: true` [then] it is `not_implemented`, since the engine has no sync master to protect yet; `false` or leaving it out is the plain command ⛔️
  - [if] a track is loaded over a deck with a changed tempo [then] it starts at tempo 1 with the pitch range, Quantize and channel strip kept; [if] a deck is unloaded [then] tempo is 1 and Quantize is back on at grid 1, as the page's empty deck ⛔️
  - [if] a `tempo` or a loop exit (`loop: null`) is sent to an empty deck [then] it is refused as `no_track` before its value is looked at, as the page's `setTempoRatio` and `setLoop` refuse it, so no tempo is shown that the next load would set back to 1; [if] a `seek` asks for a position before 0 [then] it is refused as invalid when parsed, whatever is loaded, as the page's parser refuses it ⛔️
  - [if] a loop wraps at fractional read positions (a 44.1 kHz track at 48 kHz), including a loop whose ends fall between frames [then] the frames around the wrap interpolate only audio inside the loop, and audio before a loop the playhead has not reached is untouched ⛔️
  - [if] Quantize is on (the default, grid 1) and the deck has a beatgrid [then] a pause or the first paused CUE stores the cue on the nearest grid point (a downbeat for grid 4, every other downbeat for grid 8, the earlier on a tie) without moving the playhead, and a paused CUE jump goes where a `seek` to the cue would (snapped, refused past the decoded end, leaving a loop it lands outside); CUE while playing pauses at the cue and leaves an engaged loop engaged. A `seek` lands on the nearest grid point (exiting an engaged loop when that point is outside it, refused when it is past the decoded end) and a `loop`'s ends each snap to theirs (refused when both land on one point), as the page's `quantizedSeek` and `setLoop` do; beat loops and beat jumps keep their exact grid beats. `quantize` and `quantize_grid` set it per deck, `quantize_grid` 'phase' is `not_implemented`, and the state feed carries it ⛔️
  - [if] CUE is pressed while playing and the stored cue lies past the end of the decoded audio (a pause near the end snapped it to a later grid beat) [then] it is `invalid` and the deck keeps playing where it was, as the page's `normalizeScheduledTransportEntrySec` refuses it; a cue at or before the end is returned to and paused on ⛔️
- [x] **NAE-02** (shipped this PR): The engine's mixer uses the page engine's laws exactly: EQ shelves and peak at 250/1200/5000 Hz with the -26..+6 dB knob law, TRIM 0..2x, linear channel fader, equal-power crossfader with A/B/THRU (decks start on the page's default sides, odd decks A and even decks B), the two-biquad filter with its dead zone, and 10 ms parameter smoothing (EQ gains ramp linearly over 10 ms as `applyEqRamp` does; master mute is a hard switch, as the page's mute gain is). Lowpass and highpass read Q in dB as Web Audio does. Glides follow Web Audio frame by frame: a change plays its start value on the frame it lands on, and a moving filter takes new coefficients every frame in direct form I, as Chromium's a-rate biquad does.
  - [if] the low EQ knob is at 0 [then] a 100 Hz tone drops by more than 20 dB; [if] it is at 0.5 [then] the tone is within 0.1 dB of flat ⛔️
  - [if] a stopped deck is crossfaded out and then started [then] its first 10 ms are already silent: a stopped deck's parameters keep moving and its filters ring out on silence, as a Web Audio channel's do ⛔️
  - [if] master mute is engaged while a deck plays [then] the next frame is exactly silent, and unmuting restores full level on its first frame; master volume still glides ⛔️
  - [if] the filter knob moves while a deck plays [then] the output matches a reference built from Web Audio's rules (glide from the next frame, per-frame coefficients, direct form I) to within 1e-6; a 16-frame coefficient update or a glide starting on the event frame fails it ⛔️
  - [if] an EQ knob moves [then] its gain reaches the target in a straight line in dB 480 frames later at 48 kHz ⛔️
  - [if] the 20-05 null test harness renders single knob moves on both engines [then] trim, fader, crossfader and EQ moves null at the WAV decoder floor (-93 dB) against Chromium
- [x] **NAE-03** (shipped this PR): Three clocks drive the same engine. `serve --clock fake` moves time only on `engine_advance` and renders as fast as the CPU allows; `--clock wall` paces a null sink in real time; `--clock device` (build feature `device`) runs in the output device callback. The state feed carries per-deck `position_ms`, `rate`, `playing`, the engaged loop in the page's `LoopState` shape (`in_ms`, `out_ms`, `engaged`, and `beat_length`, null for a loop set by bounds), the engine frame and `engine_time_ns`, about 30 times a second on the threaded clocks. On the threaded clocks each state also carries `host_time_ns` (when its position is heard, on the engine's private monotonic clock), `sent_ns` (that clock as the line is written) and `heard_in_ns`, their difference, which a receiver adds to its own clock at receipt. Every state carries `state_seq`, and every `engine_state` `ok` carries the `state_seq` it was given (1, 2, 3 and on, per session): the state that answers a request is the first whose `state_seq` is at least the request's, since states carry no request id and the periodic feed keeps flowing around requests. The `ok` is written before the engine can answer the request, so its answer never precedes it. `engine_advance` moves at most an hour at a time, and a `--record` session no further than one WAV file holds.
  - [if] a deck plays at tempo 1.1 on the fake clock and 1000 ms is advanced [then] the state reads position 1100 ms and frame 48000 at 48 kHz ⛔️
  - [if] `engine_advance` is sent to a wall-clock engine [then] the result is `wrong_clock` ⛔️
  - [if] `engine_advance` asks for more than an hour (or `frames` near 2^64) [then] the result is `invalid` and nothing is rendered ⛔️
  - [if] a wall-clock state arrives [then] `heard_in_ns` equals `host_time_ns - sent_ns` and is within 100 ms ⛔️
  - [if] a buffer plays a deck's last frame [then] the deck is stopped at the end in the state read after that buffer, not a buffer later; a loop ending at the track end wraps and plays on ⛔️
  - [if] the supervisor closes stdin [then] the engine exits
  - [if] the engine's stdout closes while stdin stays open (the supervisor's reader died) [then] on the wall and device clocks the engine stops its audio and exits with an error, rather than keep applying commands whose results nobody reads; a result lost as the engine stops (the reply to `engine_shutdown`, or a last state or result written while it drains) ends it with that error too, never with success ⛔️
  - [if] the default output device, or its rate, changes between the device clock's probe and its stream opening [then] the stream still opens the device that was probed, found again by its id (not whatever is the default by then); if that device is gone, or now runs at another rate, the engine refuses it with a message (naming both rates for a rate change) and exits with an error, rather than render at one rate into a stream at another ⛔️
  - [if] a threaded-clock engine's stdout closes while lines it has already read wait to be handled (a flooding supervisor whose reader died) [then] none of them is applied: the closure is noticed before the next line, whichever thread's write met it first, and those lines get no result, which nobody could read ⛔️
  - [if] `engine_state` is answered ok on a threaded clock while stdout is slow and the state queue is full [then] the requested state still follows once there is room, and only once; requests made before one block takes them share that block's one state, which is taken after all of them and after every command sent before any of them ⛔️
  - [if] `engine_state` arrives while a block renders, or while commands sent before it wait on a full result queue [then] the state that answers it comes from a later block that has applied those commands, never one from before the request; periodic states published meanwhile, including ones written after the request's `ok`, carry an earlier `state_seq`, so none is taken for the answer. The request waits for the commands sent before it and no more: [if] commands sent after it keep the queue busy [then] it is still answered once those before it have applied ⛔️
  - [if] `engine_state` is acknowledged on a threaded clock and shutdown or EOF follows at once [then] its state is still written before the engine exits, bounded by the 2 s drain, including when the block that takes the request finds the state queue full and must try again; with no request pending the engine stops at once ⛔️
  - [if] `engine_state` follows commands still waiting on a deck's load (`load`, then `play` on that deck) [then] it is asked of the engine only once that work has gone ahead on every such deck, including a later load queued there, or failed; with no load pending it is asked at once ⛔️
  - [if] a track is decoded and loaded (any clock, or a render) [then] its samples are held once: the decoder's buffer is shared as it is, never copied into a second allocation first ⛔️
  - [if] a supervisor writes commands faster than a threaded-clock engine handles them (stdout stalled) [then] the engine stops reading stdin at 1024 lines or 32 MiB not yet handled, so the pipe holds the supervisor back, and reads on once they are handled, every line still getting its result; a line refused as too long counts as a line not yet handled until its refusal is written ⛔️
  - [if] a line on stdin is longer than 8 MiB (any clock) [then] it is skipped without being held whole and refused with a null id; the next line is read as usual ⛔️
  - [if] a line on stdin is not UTF-8 (any clock) [then] it is refused as invalid with a null id and the session reads on, as for a line that is not JSON; it neither ends the session nor stops the audio ⛔️
  - [if] a deck's load is still decoding [then] up to 1023 commands for that deck wait behind it, in order, so they and the load itself fit the engine's 1024-slot mailbox together once the load is done; each one past that is refused at once as a full mailbox, as the engine's own mailbox refuses one ⛔️
  - [if] loads accepted on a threaded clock that the audio side has not yet taken (decoding, parked behind a pending load, or waiting in the mailbox) hold 64 MiB of paths and beatgrids [then] the next load that would pass that is refused at once as the engine being full, unless nothing else is held, so any load a line can carry still goes alone; each load gives its share back when its result is out ⛔️
  - [if] loads on a threaded clock have decoded, and hold 1 GiB of decoded audio between them, whose results are not yet out (the output stalled, so a decoded track waits in the mailbox and the one it replaces waits for its result to be written) [then] no further load starts decoding until results flow again and give room back; such loads wait, in order, rather than being refused, and a decode starts whenever nothing is held, so any one file still loads ⛔️
  - [if] a progressive load's head has gone to its deck while the rest of its file still decodes [then] that rest counts against the same 1 GiB from the head on, at the length the file states (at least ten minutes when it states none), and at what its buffer has actually allocated whenever that is more, as it grows, until it reaches the deck or is dropped, so rapid loads on every deck, hour-long files with no stated length included, cannot grow whole-track buffers past it unseen ⛔️
  - [if] reading stdin fails on a threaded clock (an I/O error, not end of input) [then] the engine finishes what it had read, as at EOF, and then exits with an error naming the failed read, never with success ⛔️
  - [if] a command's string id is longer than 256 bytes (any clock) [then] it is refused with a null id before the command runs, as an id of the wrong type is ⛔️
  - [if] other decks' traffic fills the mailbox when a deck's load finishes decoding [then] the load and every command accepted behind it wait, in order, and go as the audio side drains, new commands for that deck and an `engine_state` waiting behind them; none is refused after it was accepted, and at shutdown or EOF the drain sends them on too ⛔️
  - [if] any engine (fake, wall or device clock) loads and unloads many files [then] it holds only the files some deck holds now (decks on one file share one copy, whichever of them loaded it last, and a load of a file still decoding waits for that decode and shares it), and frees a file once no deck holds it ⛔️
  - [if] a fake-clock session runs with `--record R` and a load names R (by any spelling, symlink or hard link) [then] the load is `invalid` and R is untouched until the recording is written there at the end ⛔️
  - [if] a render's output or a `--record` file has become, by the time it is written, the plan or a track the run read (swapped or relinked while it ran), or has become a file the run read after that file was renamed away and something else put at its path [then] the command fails naming what it would overwrite and writes nothing there; the check is made on each output as opened, against each input's path and against each input file as the run opened it, and the output is then written through that open file. [if] the command is refused after some outputs were claimed [then] it removes only the files and directories it created itself, as the volume answered an exclusive create, so an output another run created first in a race is left alone, and only while its path still names what it created: one another run removed and replaced since is left alone too ⛔️
- [x] **NAE-04** (shipped this PR): `odj-audio render --plan P --out O.wav` renders a plan offline. Events fire at absolute times or when a deck's playhead reaches a bar, beat or track time on its own grid; ramps move a knob over ms, beats or bars. The summary reports frames, sha256, fired-event frames, and the real-time factor.
  - [if] the same plan renders twice, or with a different block size [then] the sha256 and every fired frame are identical ⛔️
  - [if] an event waits for bar 5 of a 120 BPM deck at tempo 1.05 [then] it fires on frame ceil(384000 / 1.05) at 48 kHz ⛔️
  - [if] a plan's end is never reached [then] the render stops at `max_ms` with an error rather than hanging ⛔️
  - [if] the end cannot come from the current state and every pending event waits on a deck that cannot get there or falls due after `max_ms` [then] the render fails at once rather than render silence to `max_ms`; an event due exactly at `max_ms` still fires ⛔️
  - [if] the end is deck-relative and out of reach, and the only pending work cannot move that deck or a deck it waits on (a master mute, a fader, a crossfader or tempo ramp, a tempo change, another deck nothing waits on) [then] the render fails at once rather than render silence until that work is done; work that starts, stops, seeks, cues, loops or jumps the end's deck, or a deck an event on it waits for, keeps the render going ⛔️
  - [if] a plan time or ramp length names more than one field (`bar` and `beat`, `frame` and `ms`, `beats` and `bars`) [then] the plan is `invalid` rather than render at the first field's place ⛔️
  - [if] a command sets a knob a ramp is moving (or a load or unload resets the deck's tempo during a tempo ramp) [then] the ramp ends and the command's value stays, in plan order on the same frame; a ramp after the command, or a command on another knob, leaves the ramp running ⛔️
  - [if] a render returns per-deck outputs [then] the mix and the deck outputs share what one WAV file holds, so each deck output shortens the longest render allowed, and an absolute end past that is refused before anything is decoded ⛔️
  - [if] a plan decodes tracks [then] every distinct decoded track counts against the same one-WAV-file budget as the rendered buffers (a file loaded twice counts once, and each at what its buffer retains, spare capacity included), so long sources shorten the longest render allowed; the decoding stops at the track that leaves no room, and an absolute end past the shortened ceiling fails on the load that shortened it. Each load is told the room left (the budget less the tracks so far and the frames the render needs) and stops decoding once a file passes it, so a track that does not fit is never held whole; a file already decoded shares its samples and always loads, however the plan spells its path (`a.wav`, `sub/../a.wav`, a symlink) ⛔️
  - [if] `render --out` names the same file as a `--decks-out` deck output, or any output names the plan or a track the plan loads [then] the render is refused before anything is rendered or written, naming both; paths are compared where they really lead, including through directories the render would create (`missing/../out`) ⛔️
  - [if] an output is a hard link to a track the plan loads, to the plan, or to another output [then] the render is refused before anything is written, as a second spelling of that file would be (compared by file identity: device and inode on Unix, volume serial and file index on Windows) ⛔️
  - [if] an output is a symlink, even a dangling one, whose target is another output, the plan or a track [then] the render is refused before anything is written, since the write would follow the link ⛔️
  - [if] two outputs are spelled differently but the volume holds them as one file (`--out DIR/Deck1.wav` beside `--decks-out DIR` on a case-insensitive volume, or two Unicode forms of one name on a normalizing one) [then] the render is refused before any output is written, naming both, and the files and directories it made to ask are removed again; on a volume that tells the spellings apart both render. The render opens every output first and compares what the volume opened (device and inode on Unix, volume serial and file index on Windows), so no rule on names stands in for the volume ⛔️
  - [if] an existing output is longer than what the render writes there [then] it is replaced whole; outputs are emptied only once every one is known apart ⛔️
  - [if] a plan or a session loads one file under two names (a hard link, a symlink, `sub/../a.wav`) [then] both loads share one decode and a render's budget counts the file once (keyed by device and inode on Unix, volume serial and file id on Windows, the resolved path elsewhere, all read from the open file that is then decoded, so a path renamed or repointed during a load never files one file's samples under another's key); [if] the file was rewritten in place since [then] it decodes afresh, on Unix even when the rewrite keeps its length and puts its modification time back (`cp -p`, `rsync -t`), since the key holds the file's change time; on Windows the key holds the change time NTFS and ReFS keep beside the resolved path, so the same holds there (exFAT keeps none, so there a rewrite that keeps length and modification time still shares the old decode); a copy is a file of its own ⛔️
  - [if] a plan's `max_ms` is negative [then] the plan is refused when read; 0 and above are accepted ⛔️
  - [if] a ramp length gives `deck` beside `ms` or `frames` [then] the plan is refused when read, since an absolute length is the same on every deck; `deck` goes with `beats` or `bars` ⛔️

  - [if] a render or a decode fills its buffers [then] each buffer's allocated capacity, spare room included, stays within the frames the budget charged it, while growth below that stays geometric ⛔️
  - [if] a plan, an event, a time, a ramp or a length carries a field nothing reads [then] the plan is refused when read, naming the field, rather than render something it did not mean ⛔️
  - [if] a plan's absolute end (in ms or frames) is past `max_ms` or past what one WAV file holds (4 h at 48 kHz) [then] it is refused before anything is decoded or rendered ⛔️

The summary echoes the plan verbatim with its sha256, says `master_tempo` (true once any deck turned Master Tempo on, so a tempo change no longer moved its pitch), lists each deck's tempo and local BPM from each tempo change, and gives a timeline of which decks are heard (loaded, playing, and trim x fader x crossfader at or above -60 dB) with every overlap and the solo span either side of it. `--decks-out DIR` also writes each loaded deck's own audio, after its channel strip and before the master gain, as `deckN.wav`.

- [x] **NAE-07** (shipped this PR): `odj-audio serve --clock wall|device --ws 127.0.0.1:0` also serves protocol v1 on a loopback WebSocket at `/api/v1/ws`, where the renderer, agents and Python are equal clients of the one mailbox. A command's `result` goes only to the client that sent it; `state` goes to every client. The stdout `hello` names the socket's URL as `ws`. Every socket client presents the token from `ODJ_AUDIO_WS_TOKEN` as `?token=`.
  - [if] a socket client connects without the token, with a wrong one, or on another path [then] the handshake answers 401 or 404 and the client never reaches the mailbox ⛔️
  - [if] `--ws` names a non-loopback address, the token is missing or shorter than 32 characters, or the clock is `fake` [then] the engine refuses to start and says why ⛔️
  - [if] socket A sends a command [then] its result reaches A only, and B and stdio see the state it produced ⛔️
  - [if] a socket client sends `engine_shutdown` [then] the result is `unsupported`; only the supervisor's stdio stops the engine ⛔️
  - [if] MIDI produces a `midi_action` or `midi_unmapped` line [then] every client receives it, like `state`; the `midi_ports` line and the `midi-N` results of the engine's own MIDI commands go to stdio, and a `midi_inject` result goes to its sender only ⛔️

  - [if] the engine's hello is not protocol v1 [then] the status is `failed` and it is not restarted ⛔️
  - [if] the engine is stopped [then] it exits on stdin EOF with code 0, or is terminated if it ignores that, and the status is `stopped`, not a crash ⛔️
  - [if] `ODJ_AUDIO_ENGINE` holds any other value [then] the Python engine refuses to boot ⛔️
