- [x] **NAE-19** (shipped this PR, into main-electron-rust): continuous phase lock for Beat Sync followers in Rust engine mode. A join used to set a follower's tempo and phase once, so any small tempo mismatch (grid BPM against the audio's real tempo, a stretcher's rate error, a windowed tempo on a variable grid) drifted without bound: 0.05% is 150 ms after five minutes. On every engine state frame (30 Hz) the page now measures each locked, playing follower's beat-phase error against the master through each deck's own grid and sends a small tempo trim on top of the join's base tempo: nothing under 2 ms, a proportional nudge over 4 master beats capped at 0.3% of the base and inside the pitch range, the exact base again once the error is back under 1 ms, and a re-join (a seek) when the error passes a quarter beat or 15 ms, whichever is smaller (a capped trim corrects only 3 ms/s, so a larger error is re-joined rather than walked back audibly for up to ~34 s). (Amended Thu 1 Oct 2026 by BEATSYNC-JITTER-01..04: an uneven grid is read smoothed and its local tempo followed, and the re-join now waits for 3 consecutive ticks past the line and 8 s since the join.) In simulation a 0.05% rate error stays within 1.9 ms for five minutes (150 ms without the lock) and 0.15% within 3.1 ms, at about two tempo commands a second. The Web Audio engine (the default) runs the same decision from its presentation frame, throttled to 30 Hz of AudioContext time, on positions projected from its own schedule on the audio clock; a trim is a tempo-only schedule revision relative to the base `_synchronizeFollowers` recorded, and a lost lock re-runs `_synchronizeFollowers`. In simulation through that bookkeeping a 0.05% error stays under 5 ms for five minutes. `src/lib/rb/phase-lock.ts`, `src/lib/audio-engine/rust-transport.ts` (`phaseLockTick`), `src/lib/rb/phase-lock-webaudio.ts`. Lifecycle hardening (adversarial findings F1, F2, F5, F6, F8, F9): a double-tempo follower's phase is wrapped to its own phase points (min(1, 1/N) master beats), so an odd-anchored in-phase 2x follower is no longer re-seeked every frame; an AUTOMATIC master handoff (master paused, CUE'd, faded out, played out or unloaded) re-joins the playing Beat Sync followers to the new master in both engines, as the manual master switch does, while a locked master that stops hands nothing off; a partially failed Web Audio sync still records the lock of every follower that did sync (none when the master's own schedule failed); a lock dropped mid-trim sends the base tempo back once, only while the deck still plays the lock's track and the lock's own last tempo and is not now the master, and never to a stopped Web Audio deck; and the off-tempo readout (`isTempoLockedToMaster`, jog dial) allows 0.1 BPM plus the 0.3% trim cap of the folded master BPM, so an ordinary trim no longer reads "Off tempo" while a 1 BPM mismatch at 128 BPM still does. Follow-up (adversarial findings F3, F4, F7): a beat jump on a PLAYING deck (transport running or scheduled) moves exactly the asked number of grid beats and keeps its fractional beat phase, through the target beat's own interval, and is not re-snapped to the deck's 1/4/8-beat quantize grid, in both engines; a paused deck, a jump off the grid's interior, and every other quantized seek (CUE, hot cue, waveform click, IPC jump, Rust-mode seek) still snap as before. The phase lock's base tempo follows a tempo change inside either grid: each lock tick takes the ratio both grids ask for over four master beats centered on the playheads (at the master's tempo and the lock's 0.5x/1x/2x fold, inside the pitch range), moved only past half the trim cap so millisecond-rounded beat times never move it, and the trim corrects the residual; in simulation a 124 to 128 BPM ramp and a 3% step hold with no re-seek. A synced join while the master is still before its first grid beat (an intro) extrapolates the master's grid backwards at its first interval in BEAT mode, so the follower meets the master's first beat in phase; BAR mode still refuses an extrapolated anchor, and a master past its last beat is still refused. `src/lib/rb/beat-sync-math.ts` (`beatJumpSeekPlan`, `computeFollowerSyncPlan`), `src/lib/rb/phase-lock.ts` (`phaseLockFeedForwardBase`), `apps/audio-engine/src/deck.rs` (`beat_jump`). Click and hot-cue phase (Thu 1 Oct 2026): a waveform click, hot cue or CUE jump on a SYNCED, PLAYING follower lands on the clicked or cued beat plus the master's current beat phase, so it is in phase with the master in one move. Before, the re-join picked the nearest landing, which put the follower a beat early when the master was past mid-beat. In BAR mode it lands on the beat nearest the click that shares the master's beat number, so bar alignment holds. Both engines do this (`anchorOnBeat` on `computeFollowerSyncPlan`, from Web Audio `quantizedSeek` and Rust-mode `_seek`). A click or hot cue on the master, on a paused deck, or on a deck with Beat Sync off snaps exactly as before, and a beat jump keeps its exact F3 landing. Round 2 (adversarial e2e on real own beatgrids): a pitch fader no longer costs one group re-lock per message. Every queued tempo command takes a ticket, and a queued tempo that a newer tempo for the same deck has overtaken runs as a no-op when its turn comes (`TempoCoalescer` in `src/lib/rb/tempo-coalesce.ts`, used by the performance dispatcher, so both engines), so nothing is reordered, intermediate fader values are dropped and the deck always ends on the last one. Only a contiguous run of tempos coalesces: a command queued between two tempos whose queue scopes overlap theirs (play, seek, a master or sync change) is a barrier, so the tempo queued before it still runs and that command acts at the pitch the DJ had set when pressing it. Measured on a synced 128 BPM master with one follower: 30 messages 10 ms apart settled 25.4 s after the sweep ended before, 0.8-1.5 s after. A quantized seek (waveform click, CUE, hot cue) or a beat jump on a PLAYING deck now lands on the deck's own beat phase at the instant the schedule actually lands, in the Web Audio engine on both the BeatSyncMax master path and the free path: a click lands on the clicked beat at the beat fraction the playhead is at when it lands, a jump moves exactly the asked beats from there, and a landing off the grid or past the decoded audio falls back to the fixed target (`phaseKeepingLandingSec`, `src/lib/rb/beat-sync-math.ts`). Before, the target was a fixed second decided earlier than it landed, and the master skipped part of a beat: 165.2 ms on a +4 jump and 169.6 ms on a click with BeatSyncMax on, 8.7 ms and 117.5 ms off. A paused deck, a seek off the grid's interior, a follower seek and a Rust-mode seek are unchanged.
  - [if] a pitch fader sends many tempo messages to a synced master faster than each re-lock completes [then] every overtaken queued tempo is a no-op, and the deck ends on the fader's last value ⛔️
  - [if] a play, seek or master command is queued between two tempos for a deck [then] the earlier tempo still runs before it and only tempos with no such command between them coalesce ⛔️
  - [if] another command is submitted between two tempos [then] it still runs between them: nothing is reordered and no non-tempo command is skipped ⛔️
  - [if] a quantized click or beat jump lands on a playing master later than it was decided [then] the master lands on its own beat phase at the landing instant (rhythm slip under 5 ms) and a synced follower stays under 15 ms of phase error, with BeatSyncMax on and off ⛔️
  - [if] a locked follower drifts more than 2 ms off the master's beat phase [then] it gets a tempo trim of the sign that closes the gap, never more than 0.3% of its base and never outside its pitch range ⛔️
  - [if] the error is back under 1 ms [then] the follower plays its exact base tempo again, so no trim becomes a permanent tempo change ⛔️
  - [if] the error passes a quarter beat [then] the follower is re-joined (seeked onto the master's phase), unless it is in its own engaged loop ⛔️
  - [if] Beat Sync goes off, the master changes or moves its tempo, the follower pauses or loads another track [then] that lock is dropped and sends nothing more until the next join ⛔️
  - [if] the Web Audio engine is playing a locked follower [then] the phase lock runs at most 30 times per second of audio-clock time, measuring both decks' positions from the engine's schedule projection at one shared AudioContext time ⛔️
  - [if] either deck has a queued, pending or unpresented schedule revision, a re-anchor ramp in force or an armed quantized launch [then] the Web Audio lock sends nothing that tick and keeps its base, so a trim never races a sync or a ramp ⛔️
  - [if] the Web Audio engine trims a follower [then] the trim is a tempo-only schedule revision at the base `_synchronizeFollowers` recorded times (1 + trim), never compounded on an earlier trim ⛔️
  - [if] a Web Audio follower's tempo was written by anything but its lock (a re-sync, a ramp) or a sync starts for it [then] the old lock is dropped, and a completed sync records a new base ⛔️
  - [if] a Web Audio follower's lock is lost by more than a quarter beat [then] it is re-joined through `_synchronizeFollowers` once, not trimmed and not re-seeked again while that join is in flight ⛔️
  - [if] the Web Audio master moves automatically (unload, pause, played out, faded off air) [then] the followers' re-join runs under every deck's scope plus `sync`, queued behind the command that moved it, so a load, seek or tempo sent after that command waits for the re-join and is never overwritten by it ⛔️
- [x] **NAE-25** (shipped this PR, into main-electron-rust; renumbered from NAE-23, which main now uses for the m4a beatgrid/key engine decode, and before that from NAE-21, which main uses for decode fingerprint v2; ADR-NEW-progressive-deck-load): a Rust engine deck load answers, and the deck can play, as soon as the head of the track is decoded (at least 8 s, and at least 1/40 of the stated length so a long mix's head outlasts the rest of its decode), instead of after the whole file. The rest decodes behind it on the same load thread and the whole track is swapped in on the audio thread without a seam: the head is the whole decode's first frames sample for sample (one decode pass, and the sample-rate conversion now streams packet by packet behind the decoder with output identical to the whole-file form), so playhead, cue, loop, tempo, key lock and the channel strip carry on untouched. Measured Thu 1 Oct 2026 on a 4-core cloud VM (whole decodes there take about twice the 0.60 s the 20-05 report measured on a Mac), into a 48 kHz engine, 8 rounds each: the 6-minute 320 kbps MP3 from the 20-05 null test (48 kHz) was playable after 29-48 ms against a whole decode of 1.19-1.73 s; the same audio encoded at 44.1 kHz, so resampled, after 25-44 ms against 1.10-1.48 s; a 30-minute 44.1 kHz mix of it after 149-344 ms against 5.9-8.7 s. While the rest decodes, seeks, cues and loops are bounded by the length the container states (exact for WAV, FLAC, MP4 and a tagged MP3, estimated for an untagged CBR MP3), the deck plays silence past what is decoded and keeps time, and the state feed carries `decoded_ms` per deck beside `duration_ms`. A `set_beatgrid` sent while the rest decodes is kept on the whole track. The engine already runs at the output device's own rate and converts only files at another rate (NAE-11); that is unchanged.
  - [if] the rest of the file fails to decode after its head was loaded and answered ok [then] the deck is emptied and every client gets a `load_failed` line naming the deck and the error; a track cut short is never left playing as if whole.
  - [if] that `load_failed` reaches the page while a load on the same deck is still in flight there [then] it is held until the load settles: it ends the new load when it names that load's file, is dropped when it names the earlier file the new load replaced, and ends the earlier track still shown when the new load fails ⛔️
  - [if] another load or an unload reaches the deck before the rest of the file is decoded [then] the rest is dropped and never lands on the newer track.
  - [if] the stated length was an estimate and the whole track is shorter than the playhead or a loop's end [then] the deck stops at the real end and the loop is let go; a loop within the track is kept.
  - [if] a second deck loads a file another deck is still decoding [then] it waits for that decode and shares it whole, as before.
  - [if] a file is shorter than the head [then] it loads whole, exactly as before.
  - [if] a newer load on the deck fails while an earlier load's head is still playing there [then] the earlier load's rest still lands on its head, so it plays to its real end.
  - [if] a third load reaches a deck while its current load and one earlier load's rest are both still decoding [then] it waits for that rest to finish before its own decode starts, so a deck never runs more than two decodes at once.

Beats the shift moves before 0 are dropped. The served grid offset moves from +15 ms to -10 ms, the same fit on the new reference, and the beat grid producer goes to 1.5.0 so stored grids re-run (1.6.0 where the Preview integration also carries NATIVE-19's default fit).
- [x] **NAE-24** (shipped this PR; extends NAE-20's edit-list trim): an AAC m4a with no MP4 edit list but iTunes gapless metadata (the `iTunSMPB` freeform tag under `moov/udta/meta/ilst`) is trimmed by that tag: its priming delay is dropped from the front and its original sample count kept, on every engine decode, playback and analysis alike, and the streaming decode (stems, vocals) cuts at that exact length rather than keeping the straddling packet whole as it does for an edit list. Why: Apple's encoders (iTunes, Music, afconvert) commonly write only that tag, so those files decoded with 2112 priming frames in front and played and analyzed 47.9 ms late at 44.1 kHz. An edit list, when the file has one, still wins.
  - [if] an m4a's sound track has no edit list and its `iTunSMPB` states a delay and a length [then] the engine drops the delay and keeps the length, so a click encoded at 0.25 s decodes at frame 11025 ⛔️
  - [if] the file has both an edit list and an `iTunSMPB` tag [then] the edit list decides the trim ⛔️
  - [if] the tag is missing, unparsable, outside the `com.apple.iTunes` namespace, or states an implausible delay (over 480000 frames) or length (over 2^40 frames) [then] the file decodes untrimmed, as before, rather than failing ⛔️
  - [if] a stale tag's delay is longer than the decoded stream [then] the streaming decode ignores it and writes the untrimmed audio, as the deck does, rather than fail with no audio ⛔️

## v3 Requirements

Deferred past v2. Each entry here is a roadmap scope decision (who moved it,
when, and why), not an architecture change; the underlying ADR, if any, is
unchanged.

### Library Management (LIBM)

- [ ] **LIBM-120** (decided ADR-0023): v1's stated scale target is 10k tracks; the measured floor against that target is the open half. The flip is measured against a budget of 500 ms target / 1 s acceptable for the 10k-track full library listing and playlist-detail paths (Tue 29 Sep 2026), on the user's clock, for both the first rows and the full fill. Related items already shipped as LIBM-130/LIBM-131 (Fri 25 Sep 2026); the remaining blocker is that the full-listing walk measures well over this budget (6.5 s server-side alone on the latest re-measure, `docs/perf/performance-register.md`), the PLAY IT page's whole-playlist read does too (4.5 s), and the library browser's paginated playlist fill is not yet measured. Reconciled Wed 30 Sep 2026: `docs/decisions/ADR-NEW-libm120-10k-budgets.md` adopts this budget verbatim (rows L1, L2, L4, L12) and holds the full flip rule (rows L1-L12 within Acceptable on main at one SHA, with retained raw samples; an unmeasured row blocks). Moved to v3 Thu 1 Oct 2026; chain-tip re-measure recorded the misses: L2 6.3-6.9 s, L4 16-18 s and L12 3.9-4.5 s against the 1 s acceptable budget, L8 readiness stalls, and six user-clock rows UNKNOWN because no render harness exists yet.

### Performance Modes & Machine Tiers (PERFMODE)

- [ ] **PERFMODE-17**: Separate native menubar gig-helper app: Gig posture offers to enable the helper; the helper is a Butler-like native menubar process (not browser or web UI) that can hide unrelated OS menubar items, tracks system performance and pressure on Mac and PC, and automatically manages load so the machine stays below high load and system pressure and avoids occasional lags (real OS-level load shedding or throttling, not an in-app warning only). v1 **PERFMODE-16** already ships the in-app ask-once prompt, helper-on indicator, and once-per-episode pressure toast inside the web UI; it does not hide menubar items, does not run as a native menubar app, and does not throttle or shed load on the host.

### Command Bar (CMDK)

- [x] **CMDK-01** (Fri 2 Oct 2026): Cmd-K (Ctrl-K off macOS) on /performance opens a command bar over the browser that lists the open playlist and narrows it as you type, matching every typed word in any order against title, artist, genre and key, in the page with no request per keystroke. Tab widens the search to the whole library (the browser's whole-collection FTS5 search) and back. Escape or a click outside closes it.
- [x] **CMDK-02** (Fri 2 Oct 2026): in the command bar, Up/Down pick a track and Left/Right pick the deck (opening on the lowest empty deck, else the lowest deck that is not the live master); Enter loads the track there through the browser's own deck-load path, so the same refusals (missing file, live master, streaming) and load settings apply as for a double-click.
- [x] **CMDK-03** (Fri 2 Oct 2026): the command bar loads vocals-only on Shift+Enter, or for every load while its "Vocals only" toggle (Alt+V) is on, by soloing the deck's vocal stem once its stems finish loading (never on a deck that has moved to another track); a track with no stem bundle loads as the full mix with a warning saying so.

- [x] **NAE-20** (shipped this PR; research `research/audio-decode/2026-10-01-packaging-audio-decode.md`, ADR-NEW-analysis-decodes-with-the-engine): the bundled engine decodes for analysis, so an installed app needs no user-installed ffmpeg to read a track. `odj-audio decode PATH [--rate HZ] [--mono] [--format f32le|s16le]` streams little-endian PCM on stdout and ends with one JSON summary line on stderr (`sample_rate`, `channels`, `frames`, `format`); `odj-audio probe PATH` prints the playable length as JSON (`source: header` when the container states it, `decode` when it does not). An MP4 edit list is applied on every engine decode, playback included: symphonia 0.6 parses `elst` but does not apply it, so an AAC m4a decoded with its encoder priming frames in front (1024 from ffmpeg's encoder, 2112 from Apple's) and played and analyzed 23 to 48 ms late. Analysis admission (`apps/analysis/queue_targets.py`) reads a folder-imported track's length through the engine (`apps/shared/engine_decode.py`), and asks ffmpeg only where no engine build exists. Measured Thu 1 Oct 2026 against ffmpeg 6.1: WAV, AIFF, FLAC and ALAC bit-identical; MP3 and Vorbis same length and alignment with a null under -120 dB; AAC m4a aligned after the edit fix.
  - [if] an installed app with no ffmpeg admits a folder-imported track with no stored length [then] its length is the engine's reading, not `duration_unknown` ⛔️
  - [if] an AAC m4a carries an edit list [then] the engine drops its priming frames and keeps only the edit's playable length, so a click encoded at 0.25 s decodes at frame 11025, not 1024 frames later ⛔️
  - [if] the file is not a regular file (a pipe) or its MP4 header cannot be read [then] it decodes as before, with no edit, and the load does not fail for it ⛔️
  - [if] an MP3 carries a leading ID3v2 tag larger than symphonia's 1 MiB probe depth (several MB of embedded artwork) [then] it still opens, for playback and analysis, because the probe scans past the tag; before, it failed with "no suitable format reader found" while ffmpeg read it (a real 320k MP3, found by the Platinum Notes thread) ⛔️
  - [if] `decode` cannot read the file [then] it exits non-zero with a reason and writes no PCM a reader could take for a decode ⛔️
  - [if] `ODJ_AUDIO_BIN` is set but is not executable [then] analysis names it as unavailable rather than falling back to a repo build ⛔️
  - Not yet: the canonical decode fingerprint, waveform, loudness, key, Beat This! and stems still decode through ffmpeg. Their move is ordered in the research doc (fingerprint first, then one decode shared by every lane). The fingerprint moved in NAE-21.

- [x] **NAE-21** (shipped this PR; ADR-NEW-decode-fingerprint-v2-on-the-engine): decode fingerprint v2. Every own record's `decode_fingerprint` is the sha256 of `odj-audio decode --rate 44100 --mono --format s16le` (the app's own engine: symphonia, MP4 edit list applied, rubato `FftFixedIn` with 4096-frame chunks), no longer of ffmpeg with `soxr`. Why: the shipped app bundles `odj-audio` and no ffmpeg, and Homebrew's default macOS ffmpeg has no libsoxr, so an installed app could take no fingerprint and wrote no own beatgrid, key or waveform record (Open DJ 0.1.5, Fri 2 Oct 2026: bpm `?` on every deck, engine log "ffmpeg is not on PATH"). The beatgrid, key and waveform lanes check the decoder once per run, before any track, by decoding a 48 kHz WAV through the canonical command and asserting exactly the expected 44.1 kHz byte count.
  - [if] a host has `odj-audio` (bundled, or a repo build) and no ffmpeg [then] the beatgrid and key lanes take the fingerprint and do not refuse as "canonical decode fingerprint cannot be taken" ⛔️
  - [if] the same samples arrive in two containers (16-bit and 24-bit WAV) [then] the fingerprints are equal; [if] the audio differs [then] they differ ⛔️
  - [if] the engine is missing, cannot decode, or decodes to the wrong length (a build that does not resample) [then] the lane refuses once for the host, naming why, rather than once per track ⛔️
  - [if] a key record runs against a beatgrid record still stamped with a v1 (ffmpeg) fingerprint [then] its segments report a stale dependency until the beatgrid is re-analyzed, as for any changed decode ⛔️
  - Not yet: the own waveform lane still decodes its bands through ffmpeg (research doc step 4, owned by the waveform thread), and own loudness keeps its own ffmpeg fingerprint until its `ebur128` move (step 5). Beat This! still reads the file with torchaudio, so an m4a has no beatgrid without ffmpeg until the runner is handed the engine's decode (step 3, NAE-23).

- [x] **NAE-23** (shipped this PR; ADR-NEW-analysis-decodes-with-the-engine; research `research/audio-decode/2026-10-01-packaging-audio-decode.md` step 3): an m4a gets an own beatgrid and key with no ffmpeg. For a container libsndfile cannot read (anything but WAV, AIFF, FLAC, Ogg and MP3), the beatgrid lane hands Beat This! the engine's decode as a float WAV, and the key lane reads the engine's mono float decode instead of librosa's. Why: Beat This! reads through torchaudio, soundfile and madmom, and the key lane through librosa and audioread, and each opens an m4a only through ffmpeg, which the shipped app does not bundle. The engine's decode applies the MP4 edit list, so the AAC priming frames are gone (librosa through ffmpeg kept them).
  - [if] a host has `odj-audio` and no ffmpeg [and] the track is an m4a [then] the beatgrid and key lanes analyze it rather than recording it unreadable ⛔️
  - [if] the same m4a is analyzed twice [then] the runner reads it from the same path, so its activation file is the same file, and the decoded WAV is deleted after each run ⛔️
  - [if] two runs analyze the same m4a at once [then] the second is retried later rather than writing the WAV under the first; a lock left by a crashed run is taken over once it is older than the runner and decode timeouts ⛔️
  - [if] the decode fails, stalls or the disk fills [then] no partial WAV is left behind; a stalled engine is killed at the decode timeout ⛔️
  - [if] the engine cannot decode the file, or its output is shorter than the frames it states [then] that one track is unreadable; [if] the engine itself is missing [then] the lane stops for the host ⛔️
  - [if] the track is WAV, AIFF, FLAC, Ogg or MP3 [then] the lanes read it exactly as before ⛔️
  - Not yet: HE-AAC and other containers symphonia does not decode (Opus, WMA) wait on the OS-decoder fallback in the research doc.

## Out of Scope

| Feature                                     | Reason                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Audio DSP / mixing engine                   | We orchestrate controllers; we don't replace them               |
| DRM-protected streaming playback            | Cataloging Spotify/TIDAL URIs yes; playback no (ToS + DRM)      |
| Phase-one cross-platform                    | macOS only during MVP; all current DB paths are `~/Library/...` |
| Reverse-engineering beyond read+write needs | Ethical line - no cracking we didn't earn                        |
| Becoming a new controller hardware vendor   | We integrate, not manufacture                                   |
| Ableton Link Audio (PCM over Link)          | Clock + control is the v2 ask; oDJ already owns the audio graph. Revisit only if a peer must hear oDJ audio inside Live without a cable. |
| Classic Ableton Link over VPN / internet    | Ableton: Link does not work over a VPN; multicast 224.76.78.75:20808 does not route. WAN uses the oDJ-WAN clock plane (LINK-04). |
| Embedding GPL Link in the oDJ app binary    | Decision LINK-05 / D1, same class as AGENT-07. Default plan is out-of-process Carabiner. |
